reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.BindingWa.summary: Struct BindingWatchBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What When.Binding(binding) returns: names the blocks that run when a LiveRebind() binding's object or availability changed. public readonly struct BindingWatchBuilder Expand Details ... Examples Guard = Bind.Object().LiveRebind(); When.Binding(Guard).Changed(Swaps.Add(1)); When.Binding(Guard).Unavailable(Alarm.Set(true)); Remarks The runner reconciles a LiveRebind() binding before the script's update, and this watch runs after the update, in the same frame, the way every When.* watch does. A replacement that happens between two updates is one change: Changed runs once, and Unavailable does not run, because the binding holds an object again. The object the binding holds when the script becomes ready is its starting state and is not a change. Methods Changed(params Block[]) Registers the blocks that run when the binding now holds a different object, or became unavailable, since the last time this watch ran. public void Changed(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. Examples When.Binding(Guard).Changed(Swaps.Add(1)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException blocks is null or contains null. Unavailable(params Block[]) Registers the blocks that run when the binding changed and now holds no object. public void Unavailable(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Block.htm.title: Class Block | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Block.htm.summary: Class Block Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One step of behaviour in a script. A block object is created once, when its script type is built, and is then shared by every object running that script; the per-object state it reads and writes lives in slots on the ScriptInstance passed to Execute(ScriptInstance). public abstract class Block : IScriptNode Expand Details ... Inheritance object Block Implements IScriptNode Derived ActionBlock ActivateObjectBlock AssetLoadBlock AssetReleaseBlock CreateObjectBlock CreatePrefabObjectBlock DeactivateObjectBlock DespawnObjectBlock DestroyObjectBlock FileLoadBlock SceneLoadBlock SceneUnloadBlock SpawnObjectBlock Examples public sealed class SetNumberBlock : Block { private readonly NumberSlot m_Slot; public override void Execute(ScriptInstance instance) => instance.SetNumber(m_Slot, 1.0); } Remarks Every field of every block is readonly, and a structural test enforces it, because one tree serves every object running the script and a mutable field would be shared state across all of them. AGENTS.md rule 22. A block holds slot handles, literals and child block arrays, and nothing else: no List, no Dictionary, no cached host and no cached component. Constructors Block(SourceLocation) Creates a block that knows where it was authored. protected Block(SourceLocation location = default) Parameters Type Name Description SourceLocation location Where the factory that built it was called, or Unknown when the builder is an operator that cannot capture one. The parameter is optional so that a block whose builder has no location to give needs no constructor initialiser at all. Fields None An empty block list. A shared readonly array, so an If with no Else costs no allocation and needs no null check on the run-time path. public static readonly Block[] None Field Value Block[] Remarks A field rather than a static auto-property, because Unity's lifecycle analyzer asks every type with a static auto-property to carry an [AutoStaticsCleanup] or [NoAutoStaticsCleanup] attribute, and a zero-length shared array needs neither. Properties Contexts Legacy custom nodes are runtime-only until explicitly declared shared or Editor-only. public virtual ScriptContexts Contexts { get; } Property Value ScriptContexts Examples public override ScriptContexts Contexts => ScriptContexts.Shared; Location Where in the user's script this block was authored, captured when it was built. public SourceLocation Location { get; } Property Value SourceLocation Examples var where = block.Location.Describe(); // "Assets/Scripts/CountdownScript.cs:12" Remarks This is the only place a block's own source line can come from. A block is composed inside Build() and executed much later by ScriptRunner, so at the moment it logs or throws the user's line is not on the call stack at all; the factory method that built it captured the line with [CallerFilePath] and [CallerLineNumber] and handed it here. SourceLocation states what that costs, which is one reference and one int per block and no allocation. A block built by a C# operator, such as the NumberArithmeticBlock behind health + 1.0, carries Unknown: an operator cannot declare the optional parameters the caller attributes need. The block that consumes such an expression carries the location instead. RequiredServices Services this node requires in addition to its children's requirements. public virtual ScriptServices RequiredServices { get; } Property Value ScriptServices Examples public override ScriptServices RequiredServices => ScriptServices.Clock; Methods AdvanceContained(ActionBlock, ScriptInstance) Advances one action inside the same per-action containment boundary ExecuteAll(Block[], ScriptInstance) uses, and hands its result back to the routine or group that owns it. public static ActionResult AdvanceContained(ActionBlock action, ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ActionBlock action The action to advance once. ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Returns ActionResult What the action reported. Examples var result = Block.AdvanceContained(child, instance); Remarks A result and a failure are different things and this is where they separate: an action reports Failed through its own specified domain-failure behaviour, while an exception thrown out of it is attributed here and propagated to the runner's boundary, which stops the instance. docs/execution-model.md, "Contained action failures". DescribeChildren(NodeDescription) Declares composed children during Build. Custom composite nodes override this method. public virtual void DescribeChildren(NodeDescription description) Parameters Type Name Description NodeDescription description Examples description.Add("Child", child); Execute(ScriptInstance) Runs this block against one object's state. Called once per event per instance and must allocate nothing after warm-up; AGENTS.md rule 29. public abstract void Execute(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. ExecuteAll(Block[], ScriptInstance) Runs a list of blocks in order. The one place every composite block iterates its children, so that iteration is written once for all of them. public static void ExecuteAll(Block[] blocks, ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks to run, in order. ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Examples Block.ExecuteAll(m_ThenBlocks, instance); Remarks Event lists and composite child lists use the same per-action containment boundary. An action failure stops the instance at its runner boundary; prior writes are retained. Operators implicit operator Block((Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth, Block Seventh, Block Eighth, Block Ninth)) Nine blocks written as a tuple, as one sequence: Sequence(...) with the same blocks. It runs them in the order they are written and does what they would do written out in its place. public static implicit operator Block((Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth, Block Seventh, Block Eighth, Block Ninth) blocks) Parameters Type Name Description (Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth, Block Seventh, Block Eighth, Block Ninth) blocks The blocks, in the order they run. Returns Block The sequence, as one block. Examples var steps = (Step.Set(1), Wait(1), Step.Set(2), Wait(1), Step.Set(3), Wait(1), Step.Set(4), Wait(1), Step.Set(0)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException A block is null, or the tuple was converted outside Build(). implicit operator Block((Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth, Block Seventh, Block Eighth)) Eight blocks written as a tuple, as one sequence: Sequence(...) with the same blocks. It runs them in the order they are written and does what they would do written out in its place. public static implicit operator Block((Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth, Block Seventh, Block Eighth) blocks) Parameters Type Name Description (Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth, Block Seventh, Block Eighth) blocks The blocks, in the order they run. Returns Block The sequence, as one block. Examples var steps = (Step.Set(1), Wait(1), Step.Set(2), Wait(1), Step.Set(3), Wait(1), Step.Set(4), Wait(1)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException A block is null, or the tuple was converted outside Build(). implicit operator Block((Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth, Block Seventh)) Seven blocks written as a tuple, as one sequence: Sequence(...) with the same blocks. It runs them in the order they are written and does what they would do written out in its place. public static implicit operator Block((Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth, Block Seventh) blocks) Parameters Type Name Description (Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth, Block Seventh) blocks The blocks, in the order they run. Returns Block The sequence, as one block. Examples var count = (Step.Set(1), Wait(1), Step.Set(2), Wait(1), Step.Set(3), Wait(1), Step.Set(0)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException A block is null, or the tuple was converted outside Build(). implicit operator Block((Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth)) Six blocks written as a tuple, as one sequence: Sequence(...) with the same blocks. It runs them in the order they are written and does what they would do written out in its place. public static implicit operator Block((Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth) blocks) Parameters Type Name Description (Block First, Block Second, Block Third, Block Fourth, Block Fifth, Block Sixth) blocks The blocks, in the order they run. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.BodyFacto.summary: Struct BodyFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Body surface inside Build(): observations of what physics actually did to the object this script runs on, and the switch of its Rigidbody between kinematic and dynamic. public readonly struct BodyFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.FixedUpdate(Travelled.Set(Body.PositionDelta)); On.Spawned(Body.MakeDynamic()); On.FixedUpdate(If(Expired).Then(Body.MakeKinematic())); Remarks A script type that never reads PositionDelta stores no previous position and is not walked after a physics step. Round 05 gated this observation at build time. MakeKinematic(string, int) and MakeDynamic(string, int) run in On.FixedUpdate, and also in On.Created, On.Spawned, On.Ready, On.Enabled, On.Disabled and On.Despawned, which run once per lifecycle change. Both leave the body with no velocity. An object with no Rigidbody warns once per incarnation and nothing is switched. Properties PositionDelta This body's world position after the last physics step, minus its world position after the step before that. Includes collision and other forces. Not the requested MoveBy vector. public Vector3ValueBlock PositionDelta { get; } Property Value Vector3ValueBlock Examples On.FixedUpdate(Travelled.Set(Body.PositionDelta)); Remarks Legal after a fixed step has run. The first observation after spawn is zero. A script type that never reads this value is not an observer. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This surface was read outside Build(). Methods MakeDynamic(string, int) Makes the object's Rigidbody dynamic, and then clears its linear and angular velocity, so it starts from rest under forces, gravity and contacts. public Block MakeDynamic(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block The finished block. Examples On.Spawned(Body.MakeDynamic()); Remarks Runs in On.FixedUpdate, On.Created, On.Spawned, On.Ready, On.Enabled, On.Disabled and On.Despawned; written in any other event it is reported once and ignored. A body that is already dynamic also loses its velocity. An object with no Rigidbody warns once per incarnation. On.Spawned is where a pooled object that a previous use made kinematic gets its dynamic body back, before anything else reads it. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This surface was read outside Build(). MakeKinematic(string, int) Makes the object's Rigidbody kinematic, so forces, gravity and contacts stop moving it and only a kinematic move such as Motion.MoveBy does. A dynamic body first loses its linear and then its angular velocity, while it is still dynamic, so it stops where it is. Its collider stays enabled, so it still blocks and touches other bodies. public Block MakeKinematic(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block The finished block. Examples On.FixedUpdate(If(Expired).Then(Body.MakeKinematic())); Remarks Runs in On.FixedUpdate, On.Created, On.Spawned, On.Ready, On.Enabled, On.Disabled and On.Despawned; written in any other event it is reported once and ignored. A body that is already kinematic stays kinematic and gets no velocity write. An object with no Rigidbody warns once per incarnation. A pool resets no native state, so a script whose pooled object becomes kinematic writes MakeDynamic(string, int) in its On.Spawned. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This surface was read outside Build().

Examples On.FixedUpdate(Collision.BoxCast().Size(1, 1, 1).InLocalSpace().Into(Sight)); Remarks World space is the default. Do not pass one: it records the authored line a diagnostic names. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns BoxCastBuilder This query, which takes further clauses. Examples On.Update(Collision.BoxCast().Size(1, 1, 1).Along(Camera.ScreenRay(point.Value)).Into(Hover)); Remarks Along(ray) is From(ray.Origin).Towards(ray.Direction) with one camera read, so it is written without From, Offset and Towards, and a screen ray is a world ray, so the query is not in local space. A ray the camera could not compute, for a position outside the view or without a camera, runs no query and clears the result. Length bounds the travel from the near plane. It hides UnityEngine.Camera inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. public readonly struct CameraFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Camera.For(ChaseRig).Follow()); Remarks A rig is an authored Cinemachine configuration and this surface does not replace it. Framing, damping, noise and collision stay in the rig the author set up; what a script writes is which objects the rig tracks. That is what the captain's answer on the camera family requires: the camera is routed through Cinemachine rather than reimplemented over it. Follow and look-at are two targets, not one. A chase camera keeps its position relative to the car it follows and aims at the corner ahead of it, so a rig carries both and each is written on its own. This surface's shape is provisional, for the reason ViewFactory states: it implements the recorded recommendation of the open decision contract-view-routing. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CameraGat.summary: Class CameraGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The core's one entry point to the camera. Owns the ICameraProvider, passes each authored operation to it, and reports a refused one once. public sealed class CameraGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object CameraGateway Examples runner.CameraGateway.UseProvider(new FakeCameraProvider()); Remarks This is the camera counterpart of NetworkGateway and InputGateway and is the same shape for the same reason: the core may not reference Cinemachine, so the core owns an interface and a separate, package-gated assembly implements it. With no provider installed, a camera block writes nothing and says so once. That is what the accepted design asks of an absent optional adapter: a diagnostic, and no block executes. A project without the Cinemachine package therefore still builds, still runs and still passes its tests; the camera operations do nothing and the reason is in the Console. A refusal is reported once per operation per object pair. These operations are normally authored in On.Ready, but nothing stops one appearing in On.Update, and a Console line per frame would bury the one that matters. The bookkeeping allocates only on the failure path, which is not the steady state. Properties HasProvider Whether a camera adapter has been installed. False means every camera operation writes nothing. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool Methods ChangeTargetGroup(Object, CameraTargetOperation, Object, double, double, string, string) Changes a rig's group of tracked objects, reporting a refusal once. public CameraOperationResult ChangeTargetGroup(Object rig, CameraTargetOperation operation, Object target, double weight, double radius, string call, string scriptTypeName) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The camera rig. CameraTargetOperation operation What to do to the group. Object target The object the operation acts on. double weight How much it pulls the framing. double radius How much room to leave around it. string call How the authored call is written, for the diagnostic. The block passes the constant it was built with; composing one here allocated three events per call on the frame path, which AGENTS.md rule 29 forbids and ExecutionCoreAllocationTests.EveryBlock_AllocatesNothingWhenItRuns caught. string scriptTypeName Whose script asked, for the diagnostic. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Examples gateway.ChangeTargetGroup(rig, CameraTargetOperation.Add, avatar, 1.0, 0.5, "Camera.For(...).Targets.Add", "ArenaScript"); SetTracking(Object, CameraTracking, Object, string, string) Writes one of a rig's two tracking targets, reporting a refusal once. public CameraOperationResult SetTracking(Object rig, CameraTracking tracking, Object target, string call, string scriptTypeName) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The camera rig. CameraTracking tracking Which of the two. Object target The object to track, or null to stop tracking. string call How the authored call is written, for the diagnostic. The block passes the constant it was built with, so nothing here composes a string on the frame path. string scriptTypeName Whose script asked, for the diagnostic. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Examples gateway.SetTracking(rig, CameraTracking.Follow, avatar, "Camera.For(...).Follow", "ChaseScript"); SetViewCamera(Object, Object, string) Makes a view render one camera rig, reporting a refusal once. public CameraOperationResult SetViewCamera(Object view, Object rig, string scriptTypeName) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view the author assigned. Object rig The rig to make active. string scriptTypeName Whose script asked, for the diagnostic. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Examples gateway.SetViewCamera(view, rig, "ChaseScript"); SetViewport(Object, double, double, double, double, string) Sets the fraction of the screen a view occupies, reporting a refusal once. public CameraOperationResult SetViewport(Object view, double x, double y, double width, double height, string scriptTypeName) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view the author assigned. double x The left edge. double y The bottom edge. double width How much of the width. double height How much of the height. string scriptTypeName Whose script asked, for the diagnostic. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Examples gateway.SetViewport(view, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 0.5, "SplitScreenScript"); UseProvider(ICameraProvider) Installs the backend. public void UseProvider(ICameraProvider provider) Parameters Type Name Description ICameraProvider provider The backend. Null is the caller's mistake. Examples runner.CameraGateway.UseProvider(new FakeCameraProvider()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The provider is null.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CameraGro.title: Struct CameraGroupFollowBuilder | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CameraGro.summary: Struct CameraGroupFollowBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Camera.FollowGroup() returns: a rig's target group that follows every local player's object, finished with For(ObjectBinding), optionally limited with Bounds(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock) first. public readonly struct CameraGroupFollowBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Camera.FollowGroup().For(Rig)); On.Ready(Camera.FollowGroup().Bounds(20, 12).For(Rig)); Remarks Who is in the group. The object Object.Create(prefab).ForPlayer(n) or Object.Spawn(pool).ForPlayer(n) produced, and an object whose LunyScript Behaviour's Local Player field names n, while local player n is paired, the object exists and it is active. Membership is brought up to date once per frame, after the frame's objects were created and destroyed. What it writes. Each member goes into the rig's Cinemachine target group with weight 1 and its footprint as its radius, and comes out when it leaves the group. Targets the scene authored stay. The rig's own Follow, LookAt, framing and damping stay as authored, so the rig has to follow its target group for the group to move it. How long. The registration belongs to the instance that ran the block, ends when that instance ends, and ends when a Camera.For(rig).Targets write reaches the same rig. Running the block again updates it. Ending it writes nothing to the rig. docs/proposals/group-follow-bounds-and-near-player.md is the contract. Methods Bounds(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock) Limits how far apart the group's players can walk: the group's full extent, from its outermost footprint edges, stays within width on world X and height on world Z. public CameraGroupBoundsBuilder Bounds(NumberValueBlock width, NumberValueBlock height) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock width The group's largest extent on world X, in scene units. NumberValueBlock height The group's largest extent on world Z, in scene units. Returns CameraGroupBoundsBuilder A builder whose For(ObjectBinding) produces the block. Examples On.Ready(Camera.FollowGroup().Bounds(20, 12).For(Rig)); Remarks It constrains Motion. Every Motion.MoveBy and Motion.MoveTo of a member, in any event, is applied together with the others at the end of the tick pass, an outward step shortened to what keeps the group inside. A group walking the same way moves as one, and a player who does not move stays where it is. A Transform write, a teleport or a placement is not constrained; a group found wider than its Bounds is reported once, and Motion then lets its players close up and never spread further. The rectangle is centred on the group and moves with it. One group Bounds is in force at a time. Both numbers are evaluated where the block runs. One that is not a finite number above zero is reported then and nothing is registered; a literal one is refused when the script type is built. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException A number is null, a literal number is not a finite number above zero, or the builder is a default one. Bounds(Vector2ValueBlock) Limits how far apart the group's players can walk, with the width and height as one value: X on world X and Y on world Z. Bounds(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock) states what the limit does. public CameraGroupBoundsBuilder Bounds(Vector2ValueBlock size) Parameters Type Name Description Vector2ValueBlock size The group's largest extent: X on world X and Y on world Z, in scene units. Returns CameraGroupBoundsBuilder A builder whose For(ObjectBinding) produces the block. Examples On.Ready(Camera.FollowGroup().Bounds(new Vector2(20, 12)).For(Rig)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The value is null, a literal value is not a finite number above zero on both axes, or the builder is a default one. For(ObjectBinding) Builds a block that makes rig's target group follow every local player's object. public Block For(ObjectBinding rig) Parameters Type Name Description ObjectBinding rig The declared object input holding the rig, which carries a Cinemachine target group. While the input is unavailable the block does nothing. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Ready(Camera.FollowGroup().For(Rig)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle is one Build() never assigned, or the builder is a default one.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CameraOpe.summary: Enum CameraOperationResult Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What happened when the camera gateway asked its provider to do something. public enum CameraOperationResult Expand Details ... Fields Done = 0 The provider did it. NoProvider = 1 No camera adapter is installed, so nothing was done. NoSuchTarget = 5 The object the operation names is not in the rig's target group. NoTarget = 6 The operation needs an object to act on and was given none. NoTargetGroup = 4 The rig carries no target group, so the group operation had nothing to act on. NotACameraRig = 3 The object given as the camera rig is not one, so nothing was done. NotAView = 2 The object given as the view is not one, so nothing was done. NotOnThisViewsChannel = 7 The rig is on an output channel this view does not listen to, so selecting it would not change what the view renders. Examples if (result != CameraOperationResult.Done) Report(...); Remarks Every value but Done is reported once, naming the operation and the object, and nothing is written. A camera operation is refused rather than approximated, because a view pointed at the wrong rig is a defect a player sees and cannot explain.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Cinemachi.title: Class CinemachineCameraProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Cinemachi.summary: Class CinemachineCameraProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Cinemachine Assembly ApiSource.dll The camera backend that drives Cinemachine. The one place in the product that references the Cinemachine package. public sealed class CinemachineCameraProvider : ICameraProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object CinemachineCameraProvider Implements ICameraProvider Examples runner.CameraGateway.UseProvider(new CinemachineCameraProvider()); Remarks This assembly compiles only when the Cinemachine package is installed. Its assembly definition carries a version define, LUNY_CINEMACHINE from com.unity.cinemachine 3.0.0 or newer, and a matching define constraint, which is the same arrangement CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode uses for Netcode for GameObjects and CodeSmile.LunyScript.Services uses for Unity Gaming Services. With the package absent the assembly is not compiled, nothing references this type, and the core's CameraGateway has no provider, so every camera block writes nothing and says so once. Nothing here reimplements a camera. Framing, damping, noise, blending and collision stay in the rig the author configured; this provider writes which rig a view renders and what a rig tracks, and Cinemachine does the rest. That is what the captain's answer on the camera family requires. Selecting a rig is Prioritize(), which keeps the authored blend. Cinemachine's brain renders the highest-priority camera on an output channel it listens to, and the transition into it is the blend the author configured. A rig on a channel the view's brain does not listen to is reported rather than silently having no effect. Methods ChangeTargetGroup(Object, CameraTargetOperation, Object, double, double) Changes a rig's group of tracked objects. public CameraOperationResult ChangeTargetGroup(Object rig, CameraTargetOperation operation, Object target, double weight, double radius) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The camera rig. CameraTargetOperation operation What to do to the group. Object target The object the operation acts on, ignored by Clear. double weight How much the object pulls the framing towards itself, used by Add and SetWeight. double radius How much room the framing leaves around the object, used by Add and SetRadius. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. SetTracking(Object, CameraTracking, Object) Writes one of a rig's two tracking targets. public CameraOperationResult SetTracking(Object rig, CameraTracking tracking, Object target) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The camera rig. CameraTracking tracking Which of the two to write. Object target The object to track, or null to stop tracking. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. SetViewCamera(Object, Object) Makes a view render one camera rig. public CameraOperationResult SetViewCamera(Object view, Object rig) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view, as the author assigned it. Object rig The camera rig to make active for that view. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Nothing is written unless this is Done. SetViewport(Object, double, double, double, double) Sets the fraction of the screen a view occupies, which is how a split screen is laid out. public CameraOperationResult SetViewport(Object view, double x, double y, double width, double height) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view, as the author assigned it. double x The left edge, 0 at the left of the screen and 1 at the right. double y The bottom edge, 0 at the bottom of the screen and 1 at the top. double width How much of the screen's width the view takes. double height How much of the screen's height the view takes. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened.

Each start is one attempt on an operation handle, bound with .As(handle), which is required; the outcome arrives through When.Cloud(handle) and When.Operation(handle). Examples On.Ready(Cloud.Load(Career).As(Downloading)); On.Message(RunEnded, Cloud.Save(Career).As(Uploading)); Remarks A document is one stored value under its name, the layout Progress writes. Requests for one document run one at a time in the order their blocks ran; LunyScript sets no deadline, because the provider owns the timing. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CloudSave.title: Class CloudSaveGateway | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CloudSave.summary:
Class CloudSaveGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Owns every cloud upload, download and delete of a document one ScriptRunner's scripts start: signs in when the first request arrives, queues requests in the order their blocks ran, sends one request per document at a time, polls each operation once per frame, and completes each request's attempts with its classified outcome. No script and no block ever sees a Task or an exception type; AGENTS.md section 12. public sealed class CloudSaveGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object CloudSaveGateway Examples var runner = new ScriptRunner(); runner.CloudGateway.UseProvider(new FileCloudSaveProvider(directory)); Remarks Order and coalescing, stated exactly. Requests for one document run one at a time, in the order their blocks ran, so a download after an upload reads what the upload stored; uploads, downloads and deletes share that order, and requests for different documents do not wait for each other. A request is sent once the one before it for the same document has ended, whatever that ending was, with the values it captured when its block ran; a failed request is never sent again. An upload that finds the same object's upload of the same document still waiting replaces its captured values and joins its attempt; a download or a delete joins a waiting one of the same kind. That is the settled cloud-document-request-order A and the round 05 answer "queued requests continue". A waiting request is removed without being sent when every attempt bound to it was cancelled before it started, which is what handle.Cancel() does; a download is also removed when none of its attempts is pending any more, and a download or a delete when its object despawned. An upload whose object despawned is still sent, because its values were captured. Timing belongs to the provider. The gateway sets no deadline; the captain's words of 2026-09-26 are "we do not implement timeout ourselves, this is all handled by unity services package". A failed sign-in fails every queued request once, and every request made after it fails immediately with the sign-in's classified reason; there is no retry in this version, and docs/slice-decisions.md D5.3 records that decision. The pending path allocates nothing per frame. A request allocates when its block runs and when it starts, which is the boundary AGENTS.md rule 31 names; a tick that only polls allocates nothing, and a tick with no request returns on its first line. Properties HasProvider Whether a provider has been named. Requests made while this is false are queued, not thrown; AGENTS.md rule 51. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool IsReady Whether sign-in has completed successfully, so requests dispatch immediately. public bool IsReady { get; } Property Value bool Methods Tick() Polls once. Called by TickFrameUpdate() before any instance runs, so a completion is observed in the same frame the watches that react to it run in. With no request this returns on its first line and allocates nothing. public void Tick() Examples gateway.Tick(); Remarks A throwing provider cannot leave this method. Every call this gateway makes into ICloudSaveProvider and into the operations a provider returns is guarded, and a caught exception becomes OperationFailure.Unknown on the request it belongs to, logged once with the original exception text. A provider that returns no operation is classified the same way; docs/slice-decisions.md D5.12 and D5.16. UseProvider(ICloudSaveProvider) Names the backend this gateway talks to. Called once, by whoever owns the runner, before or after the first request; requests made before it are queued and dispatched once sign-in completes. public void UseProvider(ICloudSaveProvider provider) Parameters Type Name Description ICloudSaveProvider provider The backend. Examples LunyScriptRuntime.DefaultRunner.CloudGateway.UseProvider(new UgsCloudSaveProvider()); Remarks The only provider code this method calls is Describe(), to name the provider in its log line and in that exception's message, and it is guarded: a provider whose Describe throws is named by its type instead, and the exception does not leave this method.

The supplied provider is replaced. With the Cloud Save package installed, the default runner starts with UgsCloudSaveProvider, unless the project settings turn it off. A provider named here replaces it until it starts signing in, which it does at the first cloud request; requests queued before then go to the replacement. docs/proposals/supplied-providers.md is the contract.

Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException provider is null. LunyScriptUsageException A provider was already named, other than a supplied one that has not started signing in. A gateway talks to one backend for its lifetime; with domain reload disabled the default runner and its gateway are reset between Play sessions, so each session names its provider once.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Collectio.title: Struct CollectionResult | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Collectio.summary: Struct CollectionResult Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The read-only, named outcome of one synchronous collection call. Declared with Define.CollectionResult(nameof(X)) inside Build() and produced by exactly one Slots.TryAdd(item).As(X). Used as a condition, it stands for Succeeded. public readonly struct CollectionResult Expand Details ... Examples public CollectionResult Added { get; private set; } // Inside Build(): Added = Define.CollectionResult(nameof(Added)); On.Ready( Slots.TryAdd(item).As(Added), If(Added).Then(Hits.Add(1.0))); Remarks It starts not-run, with Succeeded and Failed both false. Each time the bound call runs, it stores that call's own outcome, which the result keeps across frames until the bound call runs again. Every object running the script has its own result, and a pooled object that is reused starts not-run again. Reading the result performs no collection call, so a read placed before the bound call in the same event sees the previous outcome. A loop that runs the bound call leaves its last outcome; a loop that never runs it leaves the outcome it had before. This is a synchronous result, which is a different category from Operation: the call has finished when the block that runs it returns, so there is no pending state, no deadline, no generation and no When.* watch. Properties Failed True when the latest run of the bound call was refused and left the collection unchanged. False before the bound call has run. public ConditionBlock Failed { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Update(If(Added.Failed).Then(ShowFull.Set(true))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle is one Build() never assigned, or it belongs to another script. IsDeclared False for a handle Build() never assigned. public bool IsDeclared { get; } Property Value bool Examples var declared = Added.IsDeclared; // true after Define.CollectionResult Name The name the script declared. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Examples var label = Added.Name; // "Added" Succeeded True when the latest run of the bound call changed the collection. False before the bound call has run. public ConditionBlock Succeeded { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Update(If(Added.Succeeded).Then(Hits.Add(1.0))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle is one Build() never assigned, or it belongs to another script. Methods ToString() The name, for a diagnostic. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "Added". Operators implicit operator ConditionBlock(CollectionResult) Reads the result as its Succeeded condition, so If(Added) branches on the latest outcome of the bound call. public static implicit operator ConditionBlock(CollectionResult result) Parameters Type Name Description CollectionResult result The declared result. Returns ConditionBlock The Succeeded condition of result. Examples On.Ready(Slots.TryAdd(item).As(Added), If(Added).Then(Hits.Add(1.0))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle is one Build() never assigned, or it belongs to another script.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Collectio.title: Struct CollectionTryBuilder | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Collectio.summary: Struct CollectionTryBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Slots.TryAdd(item) returns: one synchronous collection call whose own outcome is read. It has two kinds of consumer and takes exactly one: If(Slots.TryAdd(item)), or ElseIf(Slots.TryAdd(item)) in an If chain, branches on the outcome, and As(CollectionResult, string, int) stores it in a CollectionResult. public readonly struct CollectionTryBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(If(Slots.TryAdd(item)).Then(Hits.Add(1.0)).Else(ShowFull.Set(true))); On.Ready(Slots.TryAdd(item).As(Added), If(Added).Then(Hits.Add(1.0))); Remarks Nothing runs while Build() runs. The block the consumer produces evaluates the item once and performs the mutation once each time it executes, and the outcome it reads is the Boolean that one call returned. It is never inferred from the collection-wide Failed() flag, which the call still updates the way every collection call does. The try is restricted on purpose. There is no conversion to a block and no condition operator on this type, so it cannot be placed in an event list on its own or combined with &, | or !, where a condition could be evaluated more than once or not at all. A refusal writes no log, because the branch or the bound result is where the script handles it. What the compiler cannot see is checked while Build() runs and when it finishes: a try that is never consumed, a try consumed twice, a consumer whose block is placed nowhere, a result that has no producer or two, and an As block placed a second time, which would be a second producer. Each is refused naming the line. An If over a try placed a second time is a second call, exactly as writing it again would be. Methods As(CollectionResult, string, int) Binds this call's outcome to a declared result. The block this returns performs the call each time it runs and then stores Succeeded or Failed in result. public Block As(CollectionResult result, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description CollectionResult result The handle Define.CollectionResult returned. One result has one producer. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in one event list, once. A second place would run a copy of it, which would be a second producer of result, so Build() refuses it. Examples On.Ready(Slots.TryAdd(item).As(Added), If(Added).Then(Hits.Add(1.0))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This builder is a default, it was already consumed, result was never declared or belongs to another script, or another call already produces result.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Color.htm.title: Struct Color | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Color.htm.summary: Struct Color Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A colour: red, green, blue and alpha channels, each from 0 to 1, as Unity's Color holds them. [Serializable] public struct Color Expand Details ... Examples var amber = new Color(1, 0.6, 0.1); var glass = new Color(0.3, 0.6, 1, 0.5); On.CollisionEnter(Object.SetColor(amber)); Remarks The name is Unity's, and the namespace is LunyScript's. This type is CodeSmile.LunyScript.Color, kept apart from UnityEngine.Color by its namespace, for the reason Vector3 gives: a script imports no engine namespace, so Color in a script names this type. A file that imports both CodeSmile.LunyScript and UnityEngine writes UnityEngine.Color for Unity's type. The channels are public fields that Unity saves. The type carries [Serializable], so a Color field of a ScriptableObject, a MonoBehaviour or a [Serializable] struct is saved with the asset or scene and shown in the Inspector as four numbers. The captain selected public writable fields for engine-free value types on 2026-09-28. The channels are Double. A script writes colour.R = 0.5 and new Color(1, 0.5, 0) with no f suffix and no narrowing conversion error, which is what AGENTS.md rule 12 promises for every number a script writes. Each channel is narrowed to Unity's Single once, where the colour is written into Unity, which is rule 13's seam. A channel is not clamped. A value above 1 is kept, because an HDR colour property uses it as intensity. A write that reaches Unity refuses a channel that is negative, not a number, or beyond the largest Single, and says so once; the colour itself stores what it was given. Constructors Color(double, double, double) Builds an opaque colour from three channels, each from 0 to 1. Alpha is 1, as Unity's new Color(r, g, b) gives. public Color(double red, double green, double blue) Parameters Type Name Description double red The red channel. double green The green channel. double blue The blue channel. Examples var amber = new Color(1, 0.6, 0.1); Color(double, double, double, double) Builds a colour from four channels, each from 0 to 1. public Color(double red, double green, double blue, double alpha) Parameters Type Name Description double red The red channel. double green The green channel. double blue The blue channel. double alpha The alpha channel: 1 is opaque. Examples var glass = new Color(0.3, 0.6, 1, 0.5); Fields A The alpha channel, from 0 to 1: 1 is opaque and 0 is transparent on a material that blends. public double A Field Value double Examples var glass = Color.White; glass.A = 0.5; B The blue channel, from 0 to 1. public double B Field Value double Examples var tint = new Color(1, 0.5, 0); tint.B = 1; Black Opaque black, (0, 0, 0, 1). public static readonly Color Black Field Value Color Examples On.Message(Burnt, Object.SetColor(Color.Black)); Blue Opaque blue, (0, 0, 1, 1). public static readonly Color Blue Field Value Color Examples On.Message(Frozen, Object.SetColor(Color.Blue)); Clear Transparent black, (0, 0, 0, 0), which is also what default(Color) holds. public static readonly Color Clear Field Value Color Examples On.Message(Vanish, Object.SetColor(Color.Clear)); G The green channel, from 0 to 1. public double G Field Value double Examples var tint = new Color(1, 0.5, 0); tint.G = 0.25; Gray Opaque middle grey, (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1). public static readonly Color Gray Field Value Color Examples On.Message(Disabled, Object.SetColor(Color.Gray)); Green Opaque green, (0, 1, 0, 1). public static readonly Color Green Field Value Color Examples On.TriggerEnter(Object.SetColor(Color.Green)); R The red channel, from 0 to 1. public double R Field Value double Examples var tint = new Color(1, 0.5, 0); tint.R = 0.8; Red Opaque red, (1, 0, 0, 1). public static readonly Color Red Field Value Color Examples On.CollisionEnter(Object.SetColor(Color.Red)); White Opaque white, (1, 1, 1, 1). public static readonly Color White Field Value Color Examples On.Message(Healed, Object.SetColor(Color.White)); Methods Equals(Color) Whether two colours have the same four channels. public bool Equals(Color other) Parameters Type Name Description Color other The colour to compare against. Returns bool True when every channel matches exactly. Examples var unchanged = tint.Equals(Color.White); Equals(object) Whether this is an equal colour. public override bool Equals(object obj) Parameters Type Name Description object obj What to compare against. Returns bool True when it is a Color with the same four channels. Examples var same = tint.Equals((Object)other); GetHashCode() A hash of the four channels. public override int GetHashCode() Returns int The hash. Examples var hash = tint.GetHashCode(); ToString() The four channels, written with a full stop as the decimal separator whatever the machine's culture, so a comma between channels is never also a decimal comma. public override string ToString() Returns string The channels, for example RGBA(1, 0.5, 0, 1). Examples var described = tint.ToString();

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Compariso.title: Enum ComparisonOperator | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Compariso.summary: Enum ComparisonOperator Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which comparison a CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberComparisonBlock performs. public enum ComparisonOperator Expand Details ... Fields Equal = 4 Left equals right. Compares two Double values exactly; see docs/execution-model.md on why exact comparison is what the API offers and what a user should write instead when a tolerance is wanted. Greater = 0 Left is greater than right. GreaterOrEqual = 1 Left is greater than or equal to right. Less = 2 Left is less than right. LessOrEqual = 3 Left is less than or equal to right. NotEqual = 5 Left does not equal right. Remarks The operator is a literal field on the block rather than six separate block types, because "compare two numbers" is one behaviour with a parameter; AGENTS.md rule 22 allows a literal as a block field.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Condition.title: Class ConditionBlock | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Condition.summary: Class ConditionBlock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A block that answers true or false for one object. Passed to If(...) and combined with &, | and !. public abstract class ConditionBlock : IScriptNode Expand Details ... Inheritance object ConditionBlock Implements IScriptNode Examples If(health > 10 & Alive).Then(...) If(health > 10 && Alive).Then(...) Remarks operator true and operator false return false, in every build. C# implements && and || with those operators. Returning false makes both sides of those spellings run, so they construct the same AND and OR nodes as & and |. Evaluation still short-circuits at run time. AGENTS.md rule 39. A C# if or while around a condition block still throws, in release builds too: that path uses the implicit conversion to bool, which always raises LunyScriptUsageException. There is no #if DEBUG anywhere in this file. AGENTS.md rule 38. The release-gate player asserts that throw. Fields OperatorMisuseMessage The message the implicit bool conversion carries. Named so a test can assert on it without repeating the wording. public const string OperatorMisuseMessage = "a LunyScript condition block was used in a C# if or while. Pass it to If(...) instead, combine conditions with &, |, && or ||, and negate one with !." Field Value string Properties Contexts Legacy custom nodes are runtime-only until explicitly declared shared or Editor-only. public virtual ScriptContexts Contexts { get; } Property Value ScriptContexts Examples public override ScriptContexts Contexts => ScriptContexts.Shared; RequiredServices Services this node requires in addition to its children's requirements. public virtual ScriptServices RequiredServices { get; } Property Value ScriptServices Examples public override ScriptServices RequiredServices => ScriptServices.Clock; Methods DescribeChildren(NodeDescription) Declares composed children during Build. Custom composite nodes override this method. public virtual void DescribeChildren(NodeDescription description) Parameters Type Name Description NodeDescription description Examples description.Add("Child", child); Evaluate(ScriptInstance) Answers the condition for one object. Called once per evaluation per instance and must allocate nothing after warm-up; AGENTS.md rule 29. public abstract bool Evaluate(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Returns bool What the condition says about this object right now. Operators operator &(ConditionBlock, ConditionBlock) Builds a condition that is true when both are true. public static ConditionBlock operator &(ConditionBlock left, ConditionBlock right) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock left The first condition. ConditionBlock right The second condition. Returns ConditionBlock A block evaluating both. Examples If(health > 10 & alive.IsTrue()).Then(...) operator |(ConditionBlock, ConditionBlock) Builds a condition that is true when either is true. public static ConditionBlock operator |(ConditionBlock left, ConditionBlock right) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock left The first condition. ConditionBlock right The second condition. Returns ConditionBlock A block evaluating both. Examples If(health < 1 | alive.IsFalse()).Then(...) operator false(ConditionBlock) Always false. Present for the same reason as operator true; C# requires the pair, and && and || are implemented with this one. public static bool operator false(ConditionBlock condition) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The block C# asked about. Not used. Returns bool False. implicit operator bool(ConditionBlock) Always throws. Present so that a condition block used in a C# if or while fails loudly instead of testing as false. public static implicit operator bool(ConditionBlock condition) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The block C# tried to test. Returns bool Never returns. Examples if (health > 10) { } // throws LunyScriptUsageException If(health > 10).Then(...) // the supported form Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Always, in every build configuration. operator !(ConditionBlock) Builds a condition that is true when this one is false. public static ConditionBlock operator !(ConditionBlock condition) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The condition to invert. Returns ConditionBlock A block evaluating the inverse. Examples If(!(health > 10)).Then(...) operator true(ConditionBlock) Always false. Present so && and || construct both sides. public static bool operator true(ConditionBlock condition) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The block C# asked about. Not used. Returns bool False, so C# always evaluates the other operand and calls & or |. Examples If(health > 10 && Alive).Then(...)

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CreateBui.title: Struct CreateBuilder | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CreateBui.summary: Struct CreateBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Object.Create(prefab) returns: a fresh copy of a prefab with no placement yet. Add At(Vector3ValueBlock), ChildOf(string, int), Into(OwnedObject, string, int), ForPlayer(int, string, int) and SurvivesCaller(string, int) in any order, or use it as a block, which creates the copy at the prefab's own pose. public readonly struct CreateBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry)); On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry).At(new Vector3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)).ChildOf().Into(Guard)); Remarks The three builder structs are a typestate: this one offers At and no frame modifier, CreatePlacedBuilder offers the two frame modifiers and no second At, and CreateFramedBuilder offers neither. So Object.Create(p).InWorldSpace() and Object.Create(p).At(a).At(b) and Object.Create(p).At(a).InWorldSpace().InLocalSpace() are all compile errors rather than run-time checks; AGENTS.md rule 41 and the settled semantics-t08 answer, which asks for conflicting space clauses to be unavailable in typestate. The copy is owned by the instance that created it, with or without Into: it is destroyed when that instance ends. SurvivesCaller(string, int) hands it to the scene instead. The implicit conversion is what AGENTS.md rule 42 asks for: every builder either converts to a block or registers its finish action before Build() returns, so an unfinished chain cannot silently drop its behaviour. Methods At(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock) Names where the produced object goes as three numbers, leaving its rotation as the prefab's. public CreatePlacedBuilder At(NumberValueBlock x, NumberValueBlock y, NumberValueBlock z) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock x The x of where the produced object goes. NumberValueBlock y The y of that position. NumberValueBlock z The z of that position. Returns CreatePlacedBuilder A builder that can still take a frame, a parent and a name. Examples On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry).At(Column, 0.0, Row)); Remarks The same placement as At(position), with the three numbers as the position's X, Y and Z. They are evaluated where this block runs, and they are the parent's coordinates until InWorldSpace() says otherwise. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Any number is null, or this builder is a default that no Object.Create(prefab) call produced. At(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, RotationValueBlock) Names where the produced object goes as three numbers, and how it is turned. public CreatePlacedBuilder At(NumberValueBlock x, NumberValueBlock y, NumberValueBlock z, RotationValueBlock rotation) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock x The x of where the produced object goes. NumberValueBlock y The y of that position. NumberValueBlock z The z of that position. RotationValueBlock rotation How the produced object is turned. Returns CreatePlacedBuilder A builder that can still take a frame, a parent and a name. Examples On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry).At(0.0, 1.0, 0.0, Rotation.Euler(0.0, 90.0, 0.0))); Remarks The same placement as At(position, rotation), with the three numbers as the position's X, Y and Z. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Any argument is null, or this builder is a default that no Object.Create(prefab) call produced. At(Vector3ValueBlock) Names where the produced object goes, leaving its rotation as the prefab's. public CreatePlacedBuilder At(Vector3ValueBlock position) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3ValueBlock position Where the produced object goes. Returns CreatePlacedBuilder A builder that can still take a frame, a parent and a name. Examples On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry).At(new Vector3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0))); Remarks The expression is evaluated where this block runs, not where the runner applies the create, so a position read from a variable is that variable's value at the authored line. The coordinates are the parent's until InWorldSpace() says otherwise; with no parent the two are the same coordinates. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException position is null, or this builder is a default that no Object.Create(prefab) call produced. At(Vector3ValueBlock, RotationValueBlock) Names where the produced object goes and how it is turned. public CreatePlacedBuilder At(Vector3ValueBlock position, RotationValueBlock rotation) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3ValueBlock position Where the produced object goes. RotationValueBlock rotation How the produced object is turned. Returns CreatePlacedBuilder A builder that can still take a frame, a parent and a name. Examples On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry).At(Vector3.Zero, Rotation.Euler(0.0, 90.0, 0.0))); Remarks Both expressions are evaluated where this block runs. The coordinates and the rotation are the parent's until InWorldSpace() says otherwise. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Either expression is null, or this builder is a default that no Object.Create(prefab) call produced. ChildOf(OwnedObject, string, int) Parents the produced object to an object this script owns. public CreateBuilder ChildOf(OwnedObject parent, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description OwnedObject parent The owned object Define.Object() declared. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns CreateBuilder A builder that can still take a placement and an owned object to hold it in. Examples On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry).ChildOf(Turret)); Remarks The parent is an owned object this script produced, by Object.Create or Object.Spawn with Into. A parent whose slot is empty when the create is applied leaves the produced object at the scene root and reports it. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException parent is not an owned object this script declared, this chain already names a parent, or this builder is a default. ChildOf(string, int) Parents the produced object to the object this script runs on. public CreateBuilder ChildOf(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns CreateBuilder A builder that can still take a placement and an owned object to hold it in. Examples On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry).ChildOf()); Remarks ChildOf cannot parent to itself. ChildOf(OwnedObject, string, int) parents it to an object this script owns instead. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This chain already names a parent, or this builder is a default. ForPlayer(int, string, int) Binds every script the produced object starts to one local player, so its player-less input reads, Input.Vector2("Move"), Input.IsPaired and When.Player(), read that player. public CreateBuilder ForPlayer(int localPlayer, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayer The local player number, from 0. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns CreateBuilder A builder that can still take the clauses it could take before. Examples When.Player(1).Paired(Object.Create(Avatar).At(Pad).ForPlayer(1)); Remarks It overrides the Local Player field the prefab's LunyScriptBehaviour carries, for every script Instantiate starts during this create, children included. The binding lasts for that incarnation. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException localPlayer is negative, this chain already names a player, or this builder is a default. Into(OwnedObject, string, int) Holds the produced object in one of this script's declared owned objects, so later blocks can address it. public CreateBuilder Into(OwnedObject target, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description OwnedObject target The owned object Define.Object() declared. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns CreateBuilder A builder that can still take a placement and a parent. Examples Guard = Define.Object(); On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry).Into(Guard)); Remarks The owned object is an address and nothing else. A copy is owned by the instance that created it whether or not Into is written; Into only lets later blocks name it, for example Object.Destroy(Guard). A prefab copy keeps the name the prefab gives it in the scene. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException target is not an owned object this script declared, this chain already names one, another call already produces it, or this builder is a default. NearPlayer(int, NumberValueBlock, string, int) Places the object near the object local player player controls, on the floor, facing the way that object faces. public CreateFramedBuilder NearPlayer(int player, NumberValueBlock radius, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description int player The local player whose object the new one goes near. NumberValueBlock radius How far from that object, in metres, evaluated where the block runs. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns CreateFramedBuilder A builder that takes the remaining clauses; At and a frame do not follow. Examples When.Player(2).Paired(Object.Create(Avatar).NearPlayer(1, 2).ForPlayer(2).Into(Guest2)); Remarks Decided where the create is applied, after the event that ran it, so a host and a guest who pair in the same frame both get their object. Up to 16 points are drawn uniformly over the disk of radius around the player's object on world X and Z; the first one whose floor, passing through players and triggers, is at the player's own floor height within 0.25 metres is used, clamped first into the room a group Bounds leaves a new member. When none is, the object goes where the player's object stands. No clearance is tested and nothing waits for space. The player's object is the one ForPlayer(player) produced or whose Local Player field names the player. No such object, no floor under it, or a radius that is not a finite number above zero is reported as an error naming this call, and nothing is created. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The player number is negative, the radius is null or a literal that is not a finite number above zero, or this builder is a default. SurvivesCaller(string, int) Lets the produced object outlive the instance that created it: it ends with its scene, or when something ends it, rather than when this instance ends. public CreateBuilder SurvivesCaller(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns CreateBuilder A builder that can still take the clauses it could take before. Examples On.Update(If(Health <= 0).Then(Object.Create(Reward).SurvivesCaller(), Object.Destroy())); Remarks Without it, the copy is owned by this instance and destroyed when the instance ends, with or without Into(OwnedObject, string, int). With it, the scene the copy is in holds that obligation, and Into(OwnedObject, string, int) still lets this script address the copy while this instance runs. A copy that survives the caller cannot be a child of the caller, because a child is destroyed with its parent, so ChildOf() with this clause is refused while the script type is built. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This chain already says it, or this builder is a default. Operators implicit operator Block(CreateBuilder) Finishes a create that states no placement, so the produced object keeps the pose the prefab carries. public static implicit operator Block(CreateBuilder builder) Parameters Type Name Description CreateBuilder builder The builder to finish. Returns Block The finished block. Examples Block block = Object.Create(Sentry); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException builder is a default that no Object.Create(prefab) call produced.

Into(OwnedObject, string, int) Holds the produced object in one of this script's declared owned objects, so later blocks can address it. public CreatePlacedBuilder Into(OwnedObject target, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description OwnedObject target The owned object Define.Object() declared. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns CreatePlacedBuilder A builder that can still take a placement and a parent. A prefab copy keeps the name the prefab gives it in the scene. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException target is not an owned object this script declared, this chain already names one, another call already produces it, or this builder is a default. SurvivesCaller(string, int) Lets the produced object outlive the instance that created it: it ends with its scene, or when something ends it, rather than when this instance ends. public CreatePlacedBuilder SurvivesCaller(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns CreatePlacedBuilder A builder that can still take the clauses it could take before. A copy that survives the caller cannot be a child of the caller, because a child is destroyed with its parent, so ChildOf() with this clause is refused while the script type is built. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CreatePre.summary: Class CreatePrefabObjectBlock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Object.Create(prefab) and its chain build: produces a fresh copy of a declared prefab input, places it, parents it, and holds it in an owned-object slot when the chain named one. public sealed class CreatePrefabObjectBlock : Block, IScriptNode Expand Details ... Inheritance object Block CreatePrefabObjectBlock Implements IScriptNode Inherited Members Block.Contexts Block.Location Block.ExecuteAll(Block[], ScriptInstance) Block.AdvanceContained(ActionBlock, ScriptInstance) Block.None Examples On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry).At(new Vector3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)).ChildOf().Into(Guard)); Remarks The block records the create; the runner applies it after the current dispatch. A prefab can carry a LunyScriptBehaviour, and producing such an object runs its Awake inside the call, which re-enters ScriptRunner.Spawn. The runner refuses to be re-entered during dispatch, so an authored create takes effect between event invocations, which is also what the settled contract-dispatch-order answer asks for. The placement expressions are evaluated here, not when the create is applied. A position read from a variable is that variable's value at the line the author wrote. This block itself allocates nothing. It writes one struct into the runner's request list; the object, and everything the prefab carries, is allocated when the runner applies the request, which is AGENTS.md rule 31's first boundary. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.DebugFact.summary: Struct DebugFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Debug surface: blocks that write a line to the Console when they run. Examples On.Ready(Debug.Log("ready"), Debug.Log(Health)); On.Update(If(Health < 20).Then(Debug.Warn("low health", Health))); Remarks It hides UnityEngine.Debug inside a script the same way Time hides UnityEngine.Time: inside a Script or an EditorScript, Debug means this one. Each call builds a block, and the block writes each time it runs. A variable's value is read then, for the object the block runs on, so Debug.Log(Health) placed in On.Update writes that object's health on every frame. The line is the message and value, then (Script: <script>, Object: <object>), then the line the block was written on as a link: Health = 15 (Script: PlayerScript, Object: Player). A variable shows its declared name; an expression such as Health + 5 has none and shows its value alone. Text is quoted. The blocks write only where DEBUG is defined: the Editor and every development player. In a player built without it they read nothing and write nothing. An error line is a message, not a failure: the script keeps running. Debug.Log("HP: " + Health) compiles, because C# joins any value to a string, and the string is made once while the script type is built, from the handle's description. Write Debug.Log("HP", Health) to log the value. Methods Error(ConditionBlock, string, int) Builds a block that writes a condition's current value as an error. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.DefineFac.summary: Struct DefineFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Define surface inside Build(): declares a script's variables, operations and collection results, and hands back the typed handles the blocks are built from. public readonly struct DefineFactory Expand Details ... Examples Health = Define.Number(nameof(Health), 100); TeamScore = Define.Number(nameof(TeamScore), 0).Shared(); MatchData = Define.Store(); LevelKills = Define.Number(nameof(LevelKills), 0).Shared(MatchData); Remarks Object-local has no modifier. .Shared() with no argument is the default store. A declared store is .Shared(MatchData), after MatchData = Define.Store();. Nested Define.Shared.Number is not this surface. Explicit Var.Define remains supported. Methods Choice(string, int) Declares a choice: the name Choose(handle) opens one scored selector under. The declaration starts no selector. public Choice Choice(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Choice The handle, which waits for its name. Examples Needs = Define.Choice(); On.Ready(Choose(Needs).Highest(Option(WorkScore).Then(Work), Option(RestScore).Then(Rest))); Remarks A hand-written property names it with .As(nameof(Property)). docs/proposals/declared-identity-handles.md is the contract. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This surface was read outside Build(). CollectionResult(string, string, int) Declares a collection result: the outcome of one synchronous collection call, which a try call binds with .As(result) and If(result) reads. It starts not-run, with Succeeded and Failed both false. public CollectionResult CollectionResult(string name, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name, which should come from nameof. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns CollectionResult The handle .As binds and If reads. Examples Added = Define.CollectionResult(nameof(Added)); On.Ready(Slots.TryAdd(item).As(Added), If(Added).Then(Hits.Add(1.0))); Remarks A collection result is not an Operation: the call it stores has finished when its block returns, so it has no pending state, deadline, generation or watch. This call performs no collection call. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The name is empty or already used, or this surface was read outside Build(). Color(string, Color, string, int) Declares a Color variable. There is no Shared form and no synchronised form in this version. public Var<Color> Color(string name, Color defaultValue = default, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name, which should come from nameof. Color defaultValue What every instance starts from. Color.Clear, all four channels 0, when omitted. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Var<Color> The handle. Examples Gold = Define.Color(nameof(Gold), new Color(1.0, 0.8, 0.2)); Data<TValue, THandle>(ILunyScriptData<TValue, THandle>, string, int) Declares this script's own copy of a LunyScriptDataAttribute struct: one variable per field, named after the declaration and the field, such as Stats.Damage, each starting from value. public DataDefineBuilder<TValue, THandle> Data<TValue, THandle>(ILunyScriptData<TValue, THandle> value, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) where TValue : struct where THandle : struct, ILunyScriptDataVariables Parameters Type Name Description ILunyScriptData<TValue, THandle> value The values every object starts from. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns DataDefineBuilder<TValue, THandle> A declaration that is complete once it is assigned or named with As. Type Parameters TValue The schema struct, inferred from value. THandle Its generated Variables, inferred from value. Examples Stats = Define.Data(new WeaponStats { Damage = 10, Cooldown = 0.4 }); On.Ready(Stats.Damage.Add(5)); Remarks Every object running the script starts from value, and a pooled object starts from it again. Asset.Load(file).Into(data) fills the variables from a JSON file: each load starts from value, overlays the fields the file names and discards the rest. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException value is null or is not a [LunyScriptData] struct. Document(string, string, int) Declares a document: a named, versioned list of this script's variables that Progress or Settings keeps in the user's local storage. List its fields with Field, then assign the result to a LunyScript.Document property. public DocumentDefineBuilder Document(string name, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name, which should come from nameof. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.DocumentF.summary: Class DocumentFields Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The stored fields of one document while a DocumentMigration step converts them. Names are case sensitive. A name written by a step uses letters, digits, dash and underscore, 1 to 64 of them, the rule Define.Document(...).Field applies; any other name throws, and the load fails as Unsupported. Properties Count How many fields the document holds now. public int Count { get; } Property Value int Examples var empty = fields.Count == 0; Methods Contains(string) Whether a field of this name exists, whatever it holds. public bool Contains(string name) Parameters Type Name Description string name The field name. Returns bool True when the field exists. Examples if (fields.Contains("legacy")) fields.Remove("legacy"); DefaultBindings(string) Adds a player's bindings field holding no bindings when the field is absent. Returns bool True when the field was added. Examples fields.DefaultFlag("Unlocked", false); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The name is not a storable field name. Returns bool True when the field was added. Examples fields.DefaultNumber("Coins", 0); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The name is not a storable field name. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.DocumentM.title: Class DocumentMigration | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.DocumentM.summary: Class DocumentMigration Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One consecutive step of a document's schema: converts a stored document of FromVersion into version FromVersion + 1. Written in C#, registered in Build() with Define.Document(...).Migration(step). public abstract class DocumentMigration Expand Details ... Inheritance object DocumentMigration Examples public sealed class CareerVersion1To2 : DocumentMigration { public override Int32 FromVersion => 1; public override MigrationResult Migrate(DocumentFields fields) { fields.Rename("best", "BestWave"); fields.DefaultFlag("Unlocked", false); return MigrationResult.Converted; } } Remarks A load of a document stored at an older version runs every step from that version to the declared one, in order, on a copy of the stored fields. Migrate(DocumentFields) sees only that copy, through DocumentFields: no script variable changes until the whole chain has run and the result holds every declared field in a form it can hold. A step that returns Rejected(string) or throws fails the load as OperationFailure.Unsupported, and nothing is written, including the stored file. Migration never writes the upgraded document back; the next save does. A step is shared by every object running the script and may run for several loads, so it keeps no state of its own between calls. Properties FromVersion The stored version this step converts. It produces FromVersion + 1. public abstract int FromVersion { get; } Property Value int Examples public override Int32 FromVersion => 1; Methods Migrate(DocumentFields) Converts the fields of a version FromVersion document in place into the fields of the next version. public abstract MigrationResult Migrate(DocumentFields fields) Parameters Type Name Description DocumentFields fields A copy of the stored fields, as the previous step left them. Returns MigrationResult Converted, or Rejected(string) with the reason when this document cannot be converted. Examples public override MigrationResult Migrate(DocumentFields fields) { if (fields.TryGetNumber("seconds", out var seconds) == false) return MigrationResult.Rejected("the save has no play time"); fields.SetNumber("minutes", seconds / 60.0); fields.Remove("seconds"); return MigrationResult.Converted; } ToString() The step's type and versions, for a diagnostic. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "CareerVersion1To2 (version 1 to 2)".
