reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Easing.ht.title: Enum Easing | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Easing.ht.summary: Enum Easing Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The curve an eased timed move follows: how far along its path the object is at each point of the duration. Written in Ease(...) after Over(amount), or after its unit call such as Over(amount).Seconds(), on Motion.MoveTo and Motion.RotateTo. public enum Easing Expand Details ... Fields InBack = 22 Moves about 10 percent of the path behind the start, then travels to the destination. InBounce = 28 Bounces off the start with growing height, then travels to the destination. InCirc = 19 Starts slowly along a quarter circle. InCubic = 7 Starts slowly: progress is elapsed cubed. InElastic = 25 Swings around the start with growing amplitude, then leaves for the destination. InExpo = 16 Starts very slowly and ends very fast: progress doubles every tenth of the duration. InOutBack = 24 Moves behind the start at the beginning and past the destination near the end, then settles on it. InOutBounce = 30 Bounces off the start, crosses, and bounces at the destination. InOutCirc = 21 Starts and ends slowly along two quarter circles. InOutCubic = 9 Starts and ends slowly with the cubed curve. InOutElastic = 27 Swings around the start, crosses quickly, and swings around the destination. InOutExpo = 18 Starts and ends very slowly with the exponential curve. InOutQuad = 6 Starts and ends slowly with the squared curve. InOutQuart = 12 Starts and ends slowly with the fourth-power curve. InOutQuint = 15 Starts and ends slowly with the fifth-power curve. InOutSine = 3 Starts and ends slowly along a half sine wave. InQuad = 4 Starts slowly: progress is elapsed squared. InQuart = 10 Starts slowly: progress is elapsed to the fourth power. InQuint = 13 Starts slowly: progress is elapsed to the fifth power. InSine = 1 Starts slowly along a quarter sine wave. Linear = 0 Constant speed. The same positions as a timed move with no Ease while nothing blocks the object and the destination does not move. OutBack = 23 Travels about 10 percent of the path past the destination, then returns to it. OutBounce = 29 Reaches the destination and bounces back short of it three times with shrinking height. OutCirc = 20 Slows to a stop along a quarter circle. OutCubic = 8 Slows to a stop: the mirror of InCubic. OutElastic = 26 Reaches the destination quickly and swings around it with shrinking amplitude. OutExpo = 17 Starts very fast and ends very slowly: the mirror of InExpo. OutQuad = 5 Slows to a stop: the mirror of InQuad. OutQuart = 11 Slows to a stop: the mirror of InQuart. OutQuint = 14 Slows to a stop: the mirror of InQuint. OutSine = 2 Slows to a stop along a quarter sine wave. Examples On.FixedUpdate(Motion.MoveTo(Pad).Over(2).Ease(Easing.InOutSine)); Remarks The curve turns elapsed time, 0 at the start and 1 at the end of the duration, into progress along the path: 0 is where the object was when the move started and 1 is the destination. Every curve is exactly 0 at the start and exactly 1 at the end, so an eased move still lands on its destination when the duration ends. These are the 31 standard easing curves. In starts slowly and speeds up, Out starts quickly and slows down, and InOut does both, reaching half the path at half the duration. The families differ in how strongly they bend: Sine, Quad, Cubic, Quart, Quint and Expo in increasing order, and Circ along a quarter circle. Three families turn back on purpose. Back goes about 10 percent of the path behind the start (InBack) or past the destination (OutBack) before it arrives. Elastic swings past its end several times with shrinking amplitude. Bounce reaches its end and falls back short of it three times, like a dropped ball. A move with these curves travels outside the straight segment between start and destination, or back along it, while it runs. A rotation follows the same curve along the shortest arc between the two orientations.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Event.htm.summary: Struct Event Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll An event a script sends: a notification that something happened on its object, which every local script listening to it hears at once. public readonly struct Event Expand Details ... Examples Opened = Define.Event(); On.Request(Open, IsOpen.Set(true), SendEvent(Opened)); Remarks Opened = Define.Event(); declares one, and SendEvent(Opened) sends it; a script sends only its own events. A listener names it through the generated descriptor, DoorScript.Events.Opened, in On.Event(DoorScript.Events.Opened).Do(...), and hears every local sender of that declaration unless From(target) selects one. docs/proposals/script-communication.md is the contract. Properties IsDeclared Whether this handle names a declared event. public bool IsDeclared { get; } Property Value bool Examples if (Opened.IsDeclared) { } Name The name the event was declared with, or null before it has one. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Examples var name = Opened.Name; Methods As(string, string, int) Names an event a hand-written property holds, which the generator does not name. public Event As(string name, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name; use nameof of the property. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Event The named event. Examples Opened = Define.Event().As(nameof(Opened)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(), on an event that already has a name, or with an empty name or one this script already uses. ToString() How a diagnostic names this event: DoorScript.Opened. public override string ToString() Returns string The declaring script and the name.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeCamer.title: Class FakeCameraProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeCamer.summary: Class FakeCameraProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A camera backend that records what it was asked to do, with no Cinemachine package, no camera and no scene. public sealed class FakeCameraProvider : ICameraProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object FakeCameraProvider Implements ICameraProvider Examples var provider = new FakeCameraProvider(); provider.RegisterView(view); provider.RegisterRig(rig); Remarks This is a second real implementation rather than a test mock, in the same way FakeNetworkProvider is: it applies the same rules the Cinemachine adapter applies - a view must be a view, a rig must be a rig, a group operation needs a group - and it keeps the resulting state so a test can read it back. It is what makes every camera block testable in Edit Mode, which is also what proves the blocks build and run with Cinemachine absent. It decides what an object is by what the test registered, through RegisterView(Object), RegisterRig(Object) and RegisterTargetGroup(Object). An object nothing registered is neither, which is how the refusals are exercised. Methods ActiveRigOf(Object) Which rig a view was last pointed at, or null. public Object ActiveRigOf(Object view) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view. Returns Object The active rig. Examples Assert.That(provider.ActiveRigOf(view), Is.SameAs(rig)); ChangeTargetGroup(Object, CameraTargetOperation, Object, double, double) Changes a rig's group of tracked objects. public CameraOperationResult ChangeTargetGroup(Object rig, CameraTargetOperation operation, Object target, double weight, double radius) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The camera rig. CameraTargetOperation operation What to do to the group. Object target The object the operation acts on, ignored by Clear. double weight How much the object pulls the framing towards itself, used by Add and SetWeight. double radius How much room the framing leaves around the object, used by Add and SetRadius. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. FollowOf(Object) What a rig was last told to follow, or null. public Object FollowOf(Object rig) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The rig. Returns Object The followed object. Examples Assert.That(provider.FollowOf(rig), Is.SameAs(avatar)); LookAtOf(Object) What a rig was last told to look at, or null. public Object LookAtOf(Object rig) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The rig. Returns Object The object it aims at. Examples Assert.That(provider.LookAtOf(rig), Is.SameAs(target)); RegisterRig(Object) Declares that an object is a camera rig. public void RegisterRig(Object rig) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The object. Examples provider.RegisterRig(rig); RegisterTargetGroup(Object) Declares that a camera rig carries a target group. A rig without one refuses every group operation, which is what a Cinemachine camera without a target group does. public void RegisterTargetGroup(Object rig) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The rig. Examples provider.RegisterTargetGroup(rig); RegisterView(Object) Declares that an object is a view this provider can render with. public void RegisterView(Object view) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The object. Examples provider.RegisterView(view); SetTracking(Object, CameraTracking, Object) Writes one of a rig's two tracking targets. public CameraOperationResult SetTracking(Object rig, CameraTracking tracking, Object target) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The camera rig. CameraTracking tracking Which of the two to write. Object target The object to track, or null to stop tracking. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. SetViewCamera(Object, Object) Makes a view render one camera rig. public CameraOperationResult SetViewCamera(Object view, Object rig) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view, as the author assigned it. Object rig The camera rig to make active for that view. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Nothing is written unless this is Done. SetViewport(Object, double, double, double, double) Sets the fraction of the screen a view occupies, which is how a split screen is laid out. public CameraOperationResult SetViewport(Object view, double x, double y, double width, double height) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view, as the author assigned it. double x The left edge, 0 at the left of the screen and 1 at the right. double y The bottom edge, 0 at the bottom of the screen and 1 at the top. double width How much of the screen's width the view takes. double height How much of the screen's height the view takes. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. TargetsOf(Object) A rig's target group as it stands now. public IReadOnlyList<FakeCameraProvider.TargetGroupEntry> TargetsOf(Object rig) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The rig. Returns IReadOnlyList<FakeCameraProvider.TargetGroupEntry> The entries, in the order they were added. Empty for a rig with no group. Examples Assert.That(provider.TargetsOf(rig).Count, Is.EqualTo(2)); ViewportOriginOf(Object) The left and bottom edges a view was last given, as the first two components. public Vector3 ViewportOriginOf(Object view) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view. Returns Vector3 The origin, or the zero vector when the view was never sized. Examples Assert.That(provider.ViewportOriginOf(view).Y, Is.EqualTo(0.5f)); ViewportSizeOf(Object) The width and height a view was last given, as the first two components. public Vector3 ViewportSizeOf(Object view) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view. Returns Vector3 The size, or the zero vector when the view was never sized. Examples Assert.That(provider.ViewportSizeOf(view).X, Is.EqualTo(1.0f));

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeInput.title: Class FakeInputProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeInput.summary: Class FakeInputProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll An input backend that holds its actions and their values in memory, with no device, no window and no Input System package. public sealed class FakeInputProvider : IInputProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object FakeInputProvider Implements IInputProvider Examples var provider = new FakeInputProvider(); provider.AddAction(0, "Fire", InputValueKind.Button); provider.Raise(0, "Fire", InputPhase.Performed); Remarks This is a second real implementation rather than a test mock, in the same way FakeNetworkProvider is: it answers every member of IInputProvider with the same rules the Input System adapter answers them with, occurrences aside, which is what makes the input tests runnable in Edit Mode and what lets a project without the package still run a script that reads input. A test configures it the way an action asset is configured - name the actions and their kinds - and then drives them: SetNumber(int, string, double), SetVector(int, string, double, double, double) and SetPressed(int, string, bool) write the last value an action received, which every read returns in every event until the test writes another, and Raise(int, string, InputPhase) marks an occurrence as having happened in the frame that is running. EndFrame() clears the occurrences, which is what a real backend's next frame does. The adapter records an occurrence as it arrives and hands it to the next frame update in BeginFrame(); here a test places it in a frame directly, so BeginFrame() changes nothing. Bindings are one path per action and one per part. AddAction(int, string, InputValueKind, bool, string) takes the path the action asset would give the action, and AddPart(int, string, string, string) adds a composite part with its own path. A rebind, a reset and a load change the override that sits on top of each, which is what BoundControl reads and a Settings document saves; the key of an override is the action's name, or action/part for a part. Players are fixed until UseLocalPlayers(int) is called. By default the first SetLocalPlayerCount(int) numbers are present from the start and pairing is refused, which is what the Input System adapter's one-player setup does. After UseLocalPlayers(int) nobody is present, and a test pairs players with the same rules the adapter applies: PressDevice(string) is a button press on a named device, DisconnectDevice(string) and ReconnectDevice(string) unplug and replug it, and every change is applied by UpdatePairing(), which the gateway calls once per frame. The solo start, until pairing first opens. The first press makes the host, who then holds every device: the host reads its actions, holds the pointer and is never lost. The first OpenPairing() ends it: the host keeps the participant and holds no device, and the next device pressed is the host's, whether or not pairing is still open. docs/proposals/local-player-pairing.md, "The solo start", is the contract. After UseLocalPlayers(int), numbers 0 and 1 both name the host. The first device paired is the host's, and later devices pair guests 2, 3 and so on. An action added for number 0 or 1 is the host's one action, so a test adds it once, under either number, and every member that takes a local player number reads and writes it through both. Fields KeyboardAndMouse The device name that stands for the keyboard and mouse: after UseLocalPlayers(int), the player holding a device of this name holds the pointer, as the Input System adapter's keyboard-and-mouse player does. public const string KeyboardAndMouse = "KeyboardAndMouse" Field Value string Examples provider.PressDevice(FakeInputProvider.KeyboardAndMouse); Properties IsPairingOpen Whether a button press on a device no local player holds currently pairs it. public bool IsPairingOpen { get; } Property Value bool LocalPlayerCapacity How many local player numbers this backend can hold, from 0. A one-player backend answers 1. A backend that pairs its own players answers one more than the players it can hold, because numbers 0 and 1 both name its host. public int LocalPlayerCapacity { get; } Property Value int Remarks The gateway reads the pairing state of every number below this once per frame, so it must allocate nothing. LocalPlayerCount How many local players this backend currently has. Zero is a valid answer and is not a failure. public int LocalPlayerCount { get; } Property Value int Remarks While players are fixed, the number SetLocalPlayerCount(int) set. After UseLocalPlayers(int), how many numbers are paired. PointerHolder While players are fixed, the one local player number that holds the pointer, or -1 for none. 0 by default, because the Input System adapter's one-player setup gives player 0 every device. After UseLocalPlayers(int) it is ignored, and the player holding KeyboardAndMouse holds the pointer. public int PointerHolder { get; set; } Property Value int Examples provider.PointerHolder = 2; Methods AddAction(int, string, InputValueKind, bool, string) Configures one action, the way an action asset configures one. public void AddAction(int localPlayerIndex, string name, InputValueKind kind, bool composite = false, string defaultPath = null) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player the action belongs to. string name The action's name. InputValueKind kind What it produces. bool composite True when the action's binding is a composite, whose whole rebind is refused. AddPart(int, string, string, string) also makes an action a composite. string defaultPath The control path the action asset gives the action, which BoundControl reads while no override is applied, or null for none. Examples provider.AddAction(0, "Fire", InputValueKind.Button, defaultPath: "<Keyboard>/space"); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException That player already has an action of that name. After UseLocalPlayers(int), numbers 0 and 1 are the host's one set of actions. AddPart(int, string, string, string) Adds one part to an action's composite binding, the way a W A S D composite's Up is configured, and makes the action a composite. public void AddPart(int localPlayerIndex, string action, string part, string defaultPath) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player the action belongs to. string action The action's name. string part The part's name. string defaultPath The control path the action asset gives the part. Examples provider.AddPart(0, "Move", "Up", "<Keyboard>/w"); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The action is missing, or already has that part. ApplyOverrides(int, List<InputBindingOverride>, List<InputBindingOverride>) Replaces every binding override of one local player's actions with overrides: removes them all, then applies each entry whose key names a binding of that player's actions. public bool ApplyOverrides(int localPlayerIndex, List<InputBindingOverride> overrides, List<InputBindingOverride> stale) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. List<InputBindingOverride> overrides The overrides to apply. List<InputBindingOverride> stale Receives each entry whose key names no binding, or whose path is empty; those are not applied. Returns bool False when this backend has no actions for that local player; nothing changes then. BeginFrame() Starts the occurrences of a new frame: from this call until the next one, Occurred(int, InputPhase) answers whether the action received that occurrence between the previous call and this one. Called once per frame by the gateway, before any script instance runs. Must allocate nothing. public void BeginFrame() Remarks Several input updates can fall between two calls, such as several fixed steps of one frame when the backend processes its input before each fixed step; all of them belong to the frame that starts here, and one occurrence received in two of them is delivered once. BoundPath(int, int) The control path one binding uses now: its override when one is applied, the action asset's path otherwise. Must allocate nothing, because a settings row reads it every frame. public string BoundPath(int actionId, int partId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. int partId A part's identifier, or Unresolved for the action's first binding that is not part of a composite. Returns string The path, or null when the action has no such binding. BoundPath(int, string) The override path last applied to that action, or null when none has been. public string BoundPath(int localPlayerIndex, string name) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex string name Returns string Examples Assert.That(provider.BoundPath(0, "Fire"), Is.EqualTo("<Keyboard>/e")); CancelAllRebinds() Stops every in-flight capture. A provider that is about to be replaced or dropped must call this so a RebindingOperation does not stay subscribed to Input System updates. public void CancelAllRebinds() CancelRebind(int) Stops one capture without applying an override. A missing or already-terminal identifier is a no-op. public void CancelRebind(int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int rebindId The identifier StartRebind(int, int, out int) produced. CancelRebind(int, string) Completes a pending capture as Canceled, which is what Escape does. public void CancelRebind(int localPlayerIndex, string name) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex string name Examples provider.CancelRebind(0, "Fire"); ClosePairing() Stops pairing new players. A player whose device is lost still takes the next device pressed. public InputPairingResult ClosePairing() Returns InputPairingResult Applied, or why this backend pairs nothing. CompleteRebind(int, string, string, string) Completes a pending capture as success, applying path as the live override, or as Denied when another action of that player already uses that path, or, for a part, another part of the same composite does. public void CompleteRebind(int localPlayerIndex, string name, string path, string part = null) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player. string name The action's name. string path The control the user pressed. string part The part the capture is for, or null for the whole action. Examples provider.CompleteRebind(0, "Fire", "<Keyboard>/e"); DenyRebind(int, string) Completes a pending capture as Denied without applying an override. public void DenyRebind(int localPlayerIndex, string name) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex string name Examples provider.DenyRebind(0, "Fire"); DeviceOf(int) The device a local player number holds, or null for nobody. Numbers 0 and 1 both answer the host's device. public string DeviceOf(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number. Returns string The device name, or null. Examples Assert.That(provider.DeviceOf(2), Is.EqualTo("Pad2")); DisconnectDevice(string) Unplugs the named device: the player holding it stays paired and their device is lost until ReconnectDevice(string) or another device replaces it. public void DisconnectDevice(string device) Parameters Type Name Description string device The name PressDevice(string) paired. Examples provider.DisconnectDevice("Pad2"); EndFrame() Clears every occurrence, which is what a real backend's next frame does. Values are left alone, because a held button is still held next frame. public void EndFrame() Examples provider.EndFrame(); HasPendingRebind(int, string) Whether a capture is listening for that action. public bool HasPendingRebind(int localPlayerIndex, string name) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex string name Returns bool Examples Assert.That(provider.HasPendingRebind(0, "Fire"), Is.True); HoldsPointer(int) Whether the player on one local player number holds the pointer device: the mouse, which pairs together with the keyboard and belongs to one player at a time. The interaction family's focuser uses the pointer for that player and the centre of the view for every other. Must allocate nothing, because the gateway asks once per frame per focuser. public bool HoldsPointer(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns bool True while that player's devices include a pointer that is not lost. Remarks A one-player backend answers true for its player when a pointer device is connected. A backend answers true for at most one player; when two answer true, the interaction family uses the lowest number and reports it once. IsCapturingPart(int, string, string) Whether the pending capture of that action is for the named part. public bool IsCapturingPart(int localPlayerIndex, string name, string part) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex string name string part Returns bool Examples Assert.That(provider.IsCapturingPart(0, "Move", "Up"), Is.True); IsLost(int) Whether the device the player on that number is paired with has disconnected. False for nobody. Must allocate nothing. public bool IsLost(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns bool True while that player's device is lost. Remarks The host of the solo start holds every device, so the host is never lost while it lasts. IsPressed(int) Whether the action was held down when it last received input. Must allocate nothing; AGENTS.md rule 29. public bool IsPressed(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. Returns bool True while the last input the action received holds the control pressed. Leave(int) Asks to release one local player's devices and free the number. The release is applied by the next UpdatePairing(). public InputPairingResult Leave(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns InputPairingResult Applied, NoPlayer when nobody holds the number, HostStays for numbers 0 and 1 while the host holds them, or why this backend pairs nothing. Remarks Numbers 0 and 1 name the host, who stays: their leave answers HostStays and changes nothing. Occurred(int, InputPhase) Whether one occurrence was handed to the frame that is running by the last BeginFrame(). Must allocate nothing. public bool Occurred(int actionId, InputPhase phase) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. InputPhase phase Which occurrence to ask about. Returns bool True when the action received it before this frame began and after the frame before began. OpenPairing() Starts pairing: from now on a button press on a device no local player holds pairs it with the host while nobody holds the host, and with the lowest free guest number after that. public InputPairingResult OpenPairing() Returns InputPairingResult Applied, or why this backend pairs nothing. Remarks The first open ends the solo start: a host who paired keeps the participant and holds no device until the next device pressed. PartPath(int, string, string) The override path last applied to one part, or null when none has been. public string PartPath(int localPlayerIndex, string name, string part) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex string name string part Returns string Examples Assert.That(provider.PartPath(0, "Move", "Up"), Is.EqualTo("<Keyboard>/i")); ParticipantAt(int) The backend's identity of the person on one local player number, or 0 when nobody holds it. Must allocate nothing. public long ParticipantAt(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns long The identity, 0 for nobody and for a number the backend cannot hold. Remarks The identity changes when a different person takes the number, and stays the same when the same person's device is lost and regained or re-paired, which is what the settled contract-player-identity answer asks of a participant. A backend must not hand out the same identity to two people during its lifetime; the gateway maps it to a counter of its own, so two backends may use the same numbers. Two numbers that answer the same identity name one person. A backend that pairs its own players answers its host's identity on numbers 0 and 1, and the gateway then gives both numbers one participant and counts that person once. PollRebind(int) Asks whether one capture has finished. Must allocate nothing while pending. public InputRebindPoll PollRebind(int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int rebindId The identifier StartRebind(int, int, out int) produced. Returns InputRebindPoll Pending while listening, then a terminal outcome. Examples provider.PressDevice("Pad1"); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Players are still fixed, or device is null or empty. Raise(int, string, InputPhase) Marks one occurrence as having happened during the frame that is running. public void Raise(int localPlayerIndex, string name, InputPhase phase) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player. string name The action's name. InputPhase phase Which occurrence. Examples provider.Raise(0, "Fire", InputPhase.Performed); ReadNumber(int) The last one-component value the action received. Must allocate nothing. public double ReadNumber(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. Returns double The value, which is 0 at rest and before the action received anything. ReadOverrides(int, List<InputBindingOverride>) Adds every binding override one local player's actions carry to into, in the backend's own order. public bool ReadOverrides(int localPlayerIndex, List<InputBindingOverride> into) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. List<InputBindingOverride> into The list to add to. The gateway clears it first. Returns bool False when this backend has no actions for that local player; nothing is added then. Remarks An override whose path is the action's or the part's own configured path is not reported, because it binds nothing the asset does not already bind. ReadVector(int, out double, out double, out double) The last spatial value the action received, with unused components zero. Must allocate nothing. public void ReadVector(int actionId, out double x, out double y, out double z) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. double x The first component. double y The second component. double z The third component, zero for a two-component action. ReconnectDevice(string) Plugs the named device back in: the player it was lost from has it again. public void ReconnectDevice(string device) Parameters Type Name Description string device The name DisconnectDevice(string) unplugged. Examples provider.ReconnectDevice("Pad2"); ResetBinding(int, int) Removes the override of one part, or of every binding of the action, so the action asset's paths return. public void ResetBinding(int actionId, int partId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. int partId A part's identifier, or Unresolved for every binding of the action, its composite parts included. Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) Finds the configured action one declaration names, and hands back the identifier every later read uses. public InputActionResolution Resolve(int localPlayerIndex, string actionName, InputValueKind kind, out int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player's actions to look in. string actionName The action's name, as the script declared it. InputValueKind kind What the declaration says the action produces. int actionId The identifier the four reads take, meaningful only when this returns Resolved. Returns InputActionResolution Whether the action was found, and why not when it was not. Remarks Called once per declaration rather than once per read, so an implementation may do the string work here and must do none of it afterwards. ResolvePart(int, string, out int) Finds one part of a composite binding of a resolved action, by the part's name in the action asset, compared ordinally. The first composite part of that name is the one. public InputActionResolution ResolvePart(int actionId, string partName, out int partId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced for the action. string partName The part's name, such as Up. int partId The identifier the binding members take for this part, meaningful only when this returns Resolved. Remarks Called once per part declaration, as Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) is once per action declaration, so an implementation may do the string work here and none afterwards. SetBoundPath(int, string, string) Sets the live override path a conflict check reads, without starting a capture. public void SetBoundPath(int localPlayerIndex, string name, string path) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex string name string path Examples provider.SetBoundPath(0, "Fire", "<Keyboard>/space"); SetLocalPlayerCount(int) Says how many local players this backend has, so that a test can exercise the missing-player refusal without configuring devices. public void SetLocalPlayerCount(int count) Parameters Type Name Description int count How many local players are present. Examples provider.SetLocalPlayerCount(2); SetNumber(int, string, double) Writes a one-component action's value. public void SetNumber(int localPlayerIndex, string name, double value) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player. string name The action's name. double value What it holds. Examples provider.SetNumber(0, "Throttle", 0.5); SetPressed(int, string, bool) Holds a button down or lets it up. public void SetPressed(int localPlayerIndex, string name, bool pressed) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player. string name The action's name. bool pressed True to hold it down. Examples provider.SetPressed(0, "Fire", true); SetVector(int, string, double, double, double) Writes a spatial action's value. public void SetVector(int localPlayerIndex, string name, double x, double y, double z) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player. string name The action's name. double x The first component. double y The second component. double z The third component, ignored by a two-component action. Examples provider.SetVector(0, "Move", 1.0, 0.0, 0.0); StartRebind(int, int, out int) Starts an interactive capture for one resolved action, or for one part of its composite. The gateway allows one in-flight capture per local player; this method starts the backend listening. public InputRebindStart StartRebind(int actionId, int partId, out int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. int partId The identifier ResolvePart(int, string, out int) produced, or Unresolved to capture for the whole action. int rebindId The identifier later poll and cancel take, meaningful only when this returns Started. Returns InputRebindStart Whether the capture started, and why not when it did not. UpdatePairing() Applies every pairing change requested or detected since the last call. Called once per frame by the gateway before any script instance runs, so every script sees the same players during one frame. Must allocate nothing when nothing changed. public void UpdatePairing() Remarks Leaves are applied first and then presses, in the order the test made them. A press on a device a player holds does nothing. Otherwise the device goes to the lowest-numbered player whose device is lost, who keeps their participant, then to the host who holds no device since the solo start ended. After that, during the solo start, it makes the host when nobody holds the host yet; after the solo start, while pairing is open, it goes to the host when nobody holds the host yet, and to the lowest free guest number after that, as a new participant. UseLocalPlayers(int) Switches to paired players: nobody is present, and up to capacity players pair through PressDevice(string). The first press makes the host, whom numbers 0 and 1 both name, with pairing open or not; the others are guests 2 up to capacity, who pair while pairing is open. This is what new InputSystemProvider(actions, capacity) does. public void UseLocalPlayers(int capacity) Parameters Type Name Description int capacity How many players can be paired, the host included. Examples provider.UseLocalPlayers(4); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException capacity is below 1.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeNavig.summary: Class FakeNavigationProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A navigation backend with no navigation mesh: each registered actor has a position, a speed and a stopping distance, and moves in a straight line to the end of the route a test chose. public sealed class FakeNavigationProvider : INavigationProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object FakeNavigationProvider Implements INavigationProvider Examples var navigation = new FakeNavigationProvider(); navigation.AddAgent(actor, new Vector3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), 2.0); navigation.SetRoute(island, NavigationRouteState.Partial, shore); runner.NavigationGateway.UseProvider(navigation); Remarks This is a second real implementation rather than a test mock, in the same way FakeCameraProvider is: it answers every member of INavigationProvider with the rules the NavMesh adapter answers them with, and it is what makes every navigation block testable in every gate with no navigation mesh. A test decides what the world is. AddAgent(Object, Vector3, double, double) registers an actor; an object nothing registered carries no agent. SetRoute(Vector3, NavigationRouteState, Vector3) decides which route a destination gets and where that route ends; a destination with no rule gets a complete route that ends at the destination. PendingReads is how many polls a new route stays pending. Advance(double) moves every actor that follows a known route and is not held, which is the part of a frame Unity's agent does by itself. An actor's transform follows its agent, as a NavMeshAgent's does: registering an actor and moving it write its world position, so a Follow or Lead run reads the actor where the agent is. Properties PendingReads How many polls a route stays pending after Start(Object, Vector3). Zero, the default, means the first poll already sees the route. public int PendingReads { get; set; } Property Value int Examples navigation.PendingReads = 2; RefusesDestinations Makes Start(Object, Vector3) refuse every destination, as a backend does that can map no destination onto its navigation surface. public bool RefusesDestinations { get; set; } Property Value bool Examples navigation.RefusesDestinations = true; Methods AddAgent(Object, Vector3, double, double) Registers an actor with a navigation agent standing on the navigation surface. public void AddAgent(Object actor, Vector3 position, double speed = 1, double stoppingDistance = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The object a script names as the actor, or runs on. Vector3 position Where it stands. double speed How far it moves per second of Advance(double). double stoppingDistance How far from a route's end it stops. Examples navigation.AddAgent(actor, new Vector3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), 2.0); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException actor is null, or speed or stoppingDistance is negative. Advance(double) Moves every actor that follows a complete or partial route, is not held and has not reached the end, by its speed times seconds, straight toward the end. public void Advance(double seconds) Parameters Type Name Description double seconds How much time passes. Examples navigation.Advance(0.5); Check(Object) Reports whether the actor can navigate. The gateway asks before every start and every control. public NavigationAgentState Check(Object actor) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The actor, as the author assigned it or as the script's own object. Returns NavigationAgentState Ready, or why it cannot. Clear(Object) Clears the actor's route, so it stops following it. The position the actor reached is kept. public void Clear(Object actor) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The actor. Remarks An actor that cannot navigate is left as it is. ClearCount(Object) How many times an actor's route was cleared. public int ClearCount(Object actor) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor A registered actor. Returns int The count. Examples Assert.That(navigation.ClearCount(actor), Is.EqualTo(1)); Describe() Names the backend for the one log line UseProvider(INavigationProvider) writes. Called once, so it may allocate. public string Describe() Returns string For example: "Unity NavMesh". DestinationOf(Object) The destination of the latest Start(Object, Vector3) on an actor. public Vector3 DestinationOf(Object actor) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor A registered actor. Returns Vector3 The destination. Examples Assert.That(navigation.DestinationOf(actor), Is.EqualTo(pad)); Hold(Object, bool) Holds the actor where it is, or releases it. A held actor keeps its route and moves along it again when it is released. public void Hold(Object actor, bool hold) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The actor. bool hold True to hold, false to release. Remarks An actor that cannot navigate is left as it is. IsHeld(Object) Whether an actor is held in place. public bool IsHeld(Object actor) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor A registered actor. Returns bool True while held. Examples Assert.That(navigation.IsHeld(actor), Is.True); PositionOf(Object) Where an actor stands. public Vector3 PositionOf(Object actor) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor A registered actor. Returns Vector3 Its position. Examples Assert.That(navigation.PositionOf(actor).X, Is.EqualTo(4.0)); Read(Object, Vector3) Reports the actor's route toward destination, its movement and its end as they stand now. public NavigationReading Read(Object actor, Vector3 destination) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The actor. Vector3 destination The destination the latest Start(Object, Vector3) asked for. A backend that moves a destination onto its navigation surface reports a route that ends away from this point as Partial, because it does not reach the destination. Returns NavigationReading The reading. Remarks The route is the one SetRoute(Vector3, NavigationRouteState, Vector3) chose for the destination Start(Object, Vector3) was given, so destination is not read. RouteOf(Object) The route an actor follows, as the next poll would report it apart from a pending count. public NavigationRouteState RouteOf(Object actor) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor A registered actor. Returns NavigationRouteState The route. Examples Assert.That(navigation.RouteOf(actor), Is.EqualTo(NavigationRouteState.None)); SetEnabled(Object, bool) Disables or enables an actor's agent, which a disabled component or an inactive object does in Unity. public void SetEnabled(Object actor, bool enabled) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor A registered actor. bool enabled False to disable. Examples navigation.SetEnabled(actor, false); SetOnSurface(Object, bool) Takes an actor off the navigation surface or puts it back on. public void SetOnSurface(Object actor, bool onSurface) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor A registered actor. bool onSurface False to take it off. Examples navigation.SetOnSurface(actor, false); SetRoute(Vector3, NavigationRouteState, Vector3) Decides the route a destination gets. A later rule for the same destination replaces the earlier one. public void SetRoute(Vector3 destination, NavigationRouteState route, Vector3 end) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3 destination The destination, compared exactly. NavigationRouteState route Complete, Partial or Invalid. Vector3 end Where the route ends. Read only for a partial route; a complete route ends at the destination, and an invalid one ends nowhere. Examples navigation.SetRoute(island, NavigationRouteState.Partial, shore); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException route is not one of the three resolved states. Start(Object, Vector3) Asks for a route from the actor's position to a destination and starts following it once it is known. A route the actor already follows is replaced. The gateway calls it only for an actor Check(Object) reported ready. public bool Start(Object actor, Vector3 destination) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The actor. Vector3 destination The destination in world space. The gateway passes finite components only. Returns bool True when the route was requested. False when the backend can request no route to destination at all, which the gateway reports as an invalid route; nothing changed. StartCount(Object) How many times a route was started for an actor. public int StartCount(Object actor) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor A registered actor. Returns int The count. Examples Assert.That(navigation.StartCount(actor), Is.EqualTo(1));

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeNetwo.title: Class FakeNetworkProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeNetwo.summary: Class FakeNetworkProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A netcode backend that runs entirely in this process, with no network, no Editor and no Netcode for GameObjects. Two instances are paired with Pair(out FakeNetworkProvider, out FakeNetworkProvider) and each one's sends arrive in the other's queues. public sealed class FakeNetworkProvider : INetworkProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object FakeNetworkProvider Implements INetworkProvider Examples FakeNetworkProvider.Pair(out var host, out var client); gateway.UseProvider(host); host.StartHost(); Remarks This is a second real implementation, not a mock. It is the netcode counterpart of FileCloudSaveProvider, which AGENTS.md rule 52 makes a first-class part of the product because it is how every branch is tested without a service. The message and cadence tests run against this provider with no network and no Editor session, and the same behaviour is exercised against NgoNetworkProvider where a real session is available. TestKit.NetworkProviderConformance is the one list of assertions both providers are held to, so that the double cannot drift from the backend without a test saying so. Authority here is ownership, which is the distributed-authority meaning. Each object is owned by exactly one peer, set with SetAuthority(int, int). That is the default topology under AGENTS.md rule 44, and a script written against Net.HasAuthority reads the same under either. Delivery is immediate and ordered. A send lands in the peer's queue before the call returns, so a test observes it on the next drain with no waiting and no frames. That makes the tests deterministic; it also means this provider cannot reproduce a latency or reordering defect, and a test that needs those needs the real provider. Fields NoPracticalLimit What MaximumTransformStreamBytes reports unless a test lowers it. Large enough that a thousand objects fit in one stream. public const int NoPracticalLimit = 1048576 Field Value int Properties IsHost True when this peer is the host. False for a client and for no session at all. Exposed because rule 45 forbids hiding it, and because "works as host, breaks as client" is the defect that hiding it produces. public bool IsHost { get; } Property Value bool MaximumTransformStreamBytes How many payload bytes of transform stream this backend can carry in one send. The runner splits a tick's stream into as many sends as it needs to stay inside it. public int MaximumTransformStreamBytes { get; set; } Property Value int Remarks A transport carries a bounded message. One stream per authority per tick is what AGENTS.md rule 47 requires and it stays true here: the tick still produces one stream, and this is how many bytes of it fit in one message. A hundred objects sending all three channels is about 1800 bytes, which is past what Netcode for GameObjects carries unfragmented, so this is not a limit only an unusual session meets. Splitting rather than asking the backend to fragment is deliberate. Each piece carries the stream's own 3-byte header and is decoded on its own, so a piece costs about 3 bytes plus whatever the backend's own per-message header is; a fragmented message costs the backend's fragment headers and its reassembly state instead, and leaves the stream depending on a feature that differs between backends. PeerCount How many peers are in the session, including this one. Zero when offline. public int PeerCount { get; } Property Value int PeerId Which peer this is. The host is 0 and the joining peer is 1, fixed so a test can name an owner without first reading it back. public int PeerId { get; } Property Value int RoundTripMilliseconds Round trip time to the host in milliseconds, or 0 when offline or when this peer is the host. Latency is a state a script may read, not an error; AGENTS.md rule 45. public double RoundTripMilliseconds { get; } Property Value double Remarks Zero unless this peer is in a session and is not the host, which is the same shape NgoNetworkProvider reports: a peer with no session has no round trip to report, and the host's round trip to itself is zero. SimulatedRoundTripMilliseconds How many milliseconds this provider reports as round trip time. Settable so a test can assert that a script reads latency as a state rather than as an error; it does not delay anything, because delivery here is immediate. public double SimulatedRoundTripMilliseconds { get; set; } Property Value double State What the session is doing right now. Never throws and is meaningful before any session has been started. public SessionState State { get; } Property Value SessionState TransformStreamBytesSent How many payload bytes those delivered streams carried in total. Returned to zero by EndSession() with TransformStreamsSent. public long TransformStreamBytesSent { get; } Property Value long TransformStreamsSent How many transform streams this peer has delivered since the session started. EndSession() returns it to zero, so it reads per session and not per instance. public int TransformStreamsSent { get; } Property Value int Remarks Counted here rather than only in a test, because the number of streams and the bytes in them are what AGENTS.md rule 47 is about, and a figure that can only be measured with a network is a figure nobody measures. These two count the stream's own payload; what a real backend adds around it is measured at the transport, which is what docs/netcode-bandwidth.md records. Only a delivered stream is counted, which is what NgoNetworkProvider counts too: a call made while this provider has no session, or with no connected peer to receive it, is not a send and does not move either figure. The two providers implement one documented property and a reading that meant different things on each would be worse than either meaning. Methods Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines, so a reader of the Console can tell a real session from the in-process one. Allocates; called only at state transitions, never per tick. public string Describe() Returns string For example: "Netcode for GameObjects, host on port 7777", or "in-process provider, 2 peers". EndSession() Ends the session and returns to Offline. Called again on an already-offline provider, it does nothing, so that a restart is EndSession then StartHost without the caller tracking state. public void EndSession() HasAuthority(int) Whether this peer may write the state of one object. public bool HasAuthority(int objectId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The networked object, as the gateway numbers it. Returns bool True when this peer owns the object under distributed authority, or is the server under client-server. False when offline, because an offline peer has no authority to speak of and a script that guards on authority then does nothing rather than misbehaving. Pair(out FakeNetworkProvider, out FakeNetworkProvider) Builds two providers that deliver to each other, one host and one client, both still offline until their session is started. public static void Pair(out FakeNetworkProvider host, out FakeNetworkProvider client) Parameters Type Name Description FakeNetworkProvider host The peer that will host. Peer id 0. FakeNetworkProvider client The peer that will join. Peer id 1. SendToAuthority(int, int) Sends one message to whichever peer holds authority over the object. The message has a name and no payload in this milestone. public void SendToAuthority(int objectId, int messageId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the message is about. int messageId The message, interned by the gateway so no string crosses this call. Remarks Delivered only while this peer is in a session, and to another peer only while that peer is in one too, which is what NgoNetworkProvider does: it refuses an unconnected session and then sends over a transport that reaches connected clients only. A message left in an unstarted peer's queue would run the moment it joined, which no real session does. SendTransformStream(byte[], int) Sends one authority's whole transform stream for one network tick. public void SendTransformStream(byte[] payload, int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The buffer the runner encoded the stream into. The provider must copy what it needs before returning, because the runner reuses this buffer next tick. int length How many bytes of it the stream occupies. Remarks One call per authority per tick, carrying every object that authority has something to send for, rather than one call per object. AGENTS.md rule 47 requires that shape, because one message per object per tick spends about as many bytes on framing as a half-precision position costs. SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) Sends one variable's value to every other peer. Called only by the authority, and only when the variable's cadence says to send. public void SendVariable(int objectId, int variableIndex, in NetworkValue value) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the variable belongs to. int variableIndex Which synchronised variable, numbered by the order the script declared it in. See VariableIndex for why this is not a slot index. NetworkValue value The value to send. Remarks Delivered only to a peer that is in a session, which is the condition SendToAuthority(int, int) and SendTransformStream(byte[], int) apply too, and the one NgoNetworkProvider applies to all three of its send paths. An update handed to a peer that has not joined would be drained by it the moment it did, delivering a value no real session would have carried and hiding whether the join resend that is supposed to carry it works. SetAuthority(int, int) Says which peer owns one object, on both providers at once so the two never disagree about authority. public void SetAuthority(int objectId, int ownerPeerId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object. int ownerPeerId Which peer owns it. StartClient(string) Joins a session. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running. public void StartClient(string address) Parameters Type Name Description string address Where to connect. An implementation that needs no address ignores it. StartHost() Starts hosting. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running, so an implementation may assume it is offline. public void StartHost() TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage) Takes one received message off the queue, if there is one. The gateway drains this until it returns false, once per tick. public bool TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage message) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkMessage message The message, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks A TryDequeue rather than a returned collection, because the gateway drains it every tick and a returned collection would allocate every tick; AGENTS.md rule 29. TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int) Takes one "a peer joined" notification off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). public bool TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int peerId) Parameters Type Name Description int peerId The peer that joined, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks This is what makes SyncCadence.Once work for a peer that was not there when the value was first set. Without it, a name chosen by the host before anyone joined would never be sent, because Once sends once and a late joiner missed it. The authority answers a join by marking every synchronised variable unsent, so the next tick sends the current value of all of them. The resend goes to every peer, not only to the one that joined. This milestone has no per-peer addressing: SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) is a broadcast. The cost is one redundant copy of each synchronised variable per peer per join, which is bounded by the number of joins rather than by the frame rate. Per-peer addressing is part of the transform stream milestone, where rule 47's bandwidth budget makes it load-bearing. TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[], out int, out int) The next transform stream that arrived, as a view into a buffer the provider owns. The view is valid until the next stream arrives. public bool TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[] payload, out int offset, out int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The provider's buffer. int offset Where the stream starts in it. int length How many bytes it occupies. Returns bool False when none is waiting. Remarks A view rather than an array, because a peer that is not the authority receives a stream on every tick and returning a fresh array would allocate on every one of them. TransformStreamInbox is the implementation both providers use. TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate) Takes one received variable update off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). public bool TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate update) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkVariableUpdate update The update, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeScene.title: Class FakeSceneProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeScene.summary: Class FakeSceneProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll An in-memory scene backend: a list of scene paths that count as in the build, a list of loaded scene instances, and loads and unloads that complete when the gateway ticks or when a test says so. It reports the native Loaded and Unloaded phases the way Unity's callbacks do. public sealed class FakeSceneProvider : ISceneProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object FakeSceneProvider Implements ISceneProvider Examples var scenes = new FakeSceneProvider(); scenes.AddToBuild("Assets/Scenes/Menu.unity", "Assets/Scenes/Arena.unity"); scenes.MarkLoaded("Assets/Scenes/Menu.unity"); runner.SceneGateway.UseProvider(scenes); Remarks It exists so every scene-flow behaviour can be tested without a scene on disk. The same role FakeAssetLoadProvider has for asset loads. It follows the Unity provider's rules: a path that is not in the build fails as NotFound, a replacement unloads every loaded instance before the destination is loaded, and the last loaded scene cannot be unloaded. With CompletesOnTick true, the default, everything started before a gateway tick completes at the start of that tick, which is the frame a Unity load of a small scene completes in. Set it false to hold operations pending and complete them with CompletePending(). Properties CompletesOnTick Whether operations complete at the start of the next gateway tick. True by default. public bool CompletesOnTick { get; set; } Property Value bool Examples scenes.CompletesOnTick = false; LoadedSceneCount How many scene instances are loaded now. public int LoadedSceneCount { get; } Property Value int PendingCount How many operations have started and not completed. public int PendingCount { get; } Property Value int Examples Assert.That(scenes.PendingCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); Methods AddToBuild(params string[]) Makes scene paths loadable, the way adding them to the build does. public void AddToBuild(params string[] scenePaths) Parameters Type Name Description string[] scenePaths The scene asset paths. Examples scenes.AddToBuild("Assets/Scenes/Arena.unity"); CompletePending() Completes every pending operation in the order they started, reporting each native phase as it happens. public void CompletePending() Examples scenes.CompletePending(); CountLoaded(string) How many loaded scene instances were loaded from this asset path. public int CountLoaded(string scenePath) Parameters Type Name Description string scenePath The scene asset's path. Returns int Zero when none is loaded. Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines. Allocates; called only when the provider is installed. public string Describe() Returns string For example: "Unity SceneManager" or "in-memory scene provider". FailPending(OperationFailure) Completes every pending operation as a classified failure, loading and unloading nothing. public void FailPending(OperationFailure failure) Parameters Type Name Description OperationFailure failure The classified reason. Not None. Examples scenes.FailPending(OperationFailure.Unknown); IsLoaded(string) Whether a scene instance of this path is loaded now. public bool IsLoaded(string scenePath) Parameters Type Name Description string scenePath The scene asset path. Returns bool True when at least one is. Examples Assert.That(scenes.IsLoaded("Assets/Scenes/Arena.unity"), Is.True); Load(string, bool) Starts loading one scene asset. A replacement load releases every loaded scene; an additive load releases none. public ISceneLoadOperation Load(string scenePath, bool additive) Parameters Type Name Description string scenePath The scene asset's path. bool additive True to load alongside the loaded scenes. Returns ISceneLoadOperation The operation the gateway polls. A scene that is not in the build completes at once as OperationFailure.NotFound, and nothing starts. LoadedScenePathAt(int) The asset path of one loaded scene instance. public string LoadedScenePathAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index From zero to LoadedSceneCount minus one. Returns string The path. May allocate; the gateway reads it only when a replacement load starts. MarkLoaded(string) Records one scene instance as already loaded, the way the scene a game starts in is. Reports nothing. public void MarkLoaded(string scenePath) Parameters Type Name Description string scenePath The scene asset path. Examples scenes.MarkLoaded("Assets/Scenes/Menu.unity"); Unload(ISceneLoadOperation) Starts unloading the exact instance one completed additive load produced. This is how a load whose requester stopped waiting is cleaned up. public IAsyncOperation Unload(ISceneLoadOperation load) Parameters Type Name Description ISceneLoadOperation load An operation this provider's Load(string, bool) returned, completed successfully. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FileCloud.title: Class FileCloudSaveProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FileCloud.summary: Class FileCloudSaveProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The file-based Cloud Save provider: one file per document, under a directory the caller names. A first-class part of the product, not a test fixture; AGENTS.md rule 52. It is how every failure branch is tested without a network, and what makes the automated suite runnable with no credentials. public sealed class FileCloudSaveProvider : ICloudSaveProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object FileCloudSaveProvider Implements ICloudSaveProvider Examples runner.CloudGateway.UseProvider(new FileCloudSaveProvider(Path.Combine(tempDirectory, "saves"))); Remarks Every operation does its work inside the provider call. By default the gateway observes the outcome on its next per-frame poll, so a script sees the same event sequence it sees against a real service, one or more frames later rather than hundreds; DelayCompletion(int) holds each outcome back for a number of polls, which is how a test or a demonstration sees a request stay pending across frames. A document is stored as the JSON text the gateway hands over, UTF-8 without a byte order mark, in a file named after its key with the .json extension. Keys are case sensitive, on every file system. Save("Level1", ...) and Save("level1", ...) hold two separate documents and Load("Level1") returns the first, on Windows and macOS as well as on Linux, which is how Unity Cloud Save behaves; docs/slice-decisions.md D5.14 records the decision and the file name it produces. Constructors FileCloudSaveProvider(string) Creates a provider storing its files under one directory. public FileCloudSaveProvider(string directory) Parameters Type Name Description string directory Where the files live. Created by SignIn() when it does not exist. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException directory is null or whitespace. Methods DelayCompletion(int) Makes every later operation report that it is complete only after the gateway has polled it polls times, which the gateway does once per frame. The work itself still happens inside the provider call, the way a service can store a document before its answer arrives. 0, the default, reports each outcome on the first poll. public void DelayCompletion(int polls) Parameters Type Name Description int polls How many polls report the operation as still pending. Examples provider.DelayCompletion(30); // each request stays pending for 30 frames Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException polls is negative. Delete(string) Starts removing the document stored under a key. public IAsyncOperation Delete(string key) Parameters Type Name Description string key The document's name. Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. It succeeds when no document is stored under the key afterwards, whether or not one was stored before. Remarks Succeeds when no file is left for the key, whether or not one existed. Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines, so that a reader of the Console can tell a real service round trip from a file-based one. Allocates; called only at state transitions, never per frame. public string Describe() Returns string For example: "Unity Cloud Save, signed in as player abc123", or "file-based provider at C:/saves". FailNext(OperationFailure) Makes the next operation, whichever it is, complete with failure instead of doing its work. This is how a test reaches every failure branch without a network, which is the reason this provider exists; AGENTS.md rule 52. public void FailNext(OperationFailure failure) Parameters Type Name Description OperationFailure failure The classified reason the next operation reports. Examples provider.FailNext(OperationFailure.RateLimited); Load(string) Starts reading the document stored under a key. public ICloudLoadOperation Load(string key) Parameters Type Name Description string key The document's name. Returns ICloudLoadOperation The operation the gateway polls. A key with no stored document completes with OperationFailure.NotFound. Save(string, string) Starts storing one document under its key, replacing any copy stored before. public IAsyncOperation Save(string key, string document) Parameters Type Name Description string key The document's name. The script's build validated it; a provider may refuse a key it cannot store with OperationFailure.Denied. string document The whole document as JSON text. Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. SignIn() Starts signing in. Called by the gateway once, when the first request arrives. A provider that needs no sign-in returns an already-completed operation. public IAsyncOperation SignIn() Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. Remarks Creates the directory. There is no account, so "signing in" is only that.

Returns Block A block to place in an event list. It has no slot, reads the same value on every object, and a write to it is refused while the script type is built. public static implicit operator Flag(bool value) Parameters Type Name Description bool value The constant. Returns Flag The constant input. Examples Flag Always = true; operator !=(Flag, Flag) Builds a condition that is true when the two flags differ. public static ConditionBlock operator !=(Flag left, Flag right) Parameters Type Name Description Flag left A flag variable or constant. Flag right A flag variable or constant. Returns ConditionBlock A condition block. Examples On.Update(If(Open != Wanted).Then(Moving.Set(true))); operator !(Flag) Builds a condition that is true when this flag is false. UgsCloudSaveProvider in CodeSmile.LunyScript.Services wraps Unity Gaming Services. A document is one stored value under its key, the settled answer "One stored value for the whole document". The value is the document's JSON text in the layout Progress writes; a provider stores and returns it and never interprets its fields. A key is case sensitive, and every implementation must hold it that way. Level1 and level1 are two keys carrying two values, which is how Unity Cloud Save behaves; docs/slice-decisions.md D5.14 records the decision and what FileCloudSaveProvider does to keep it on a case-insensitive file system. The provider owns request timing. The gateway sets no deadline; a provider that gives up on a request completes its operation with OperationFailure.Timeout.
