reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.IInputPro.title: Interface IInputProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.IInputPro.summary: Interface IInputProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What an input backend provides to the InputGateway: the resolution of a declared action name to something the backend can read, the four value reads, the start of each frame's occurrences and the three occurrence tests, interactive rebind start, cancel and poll, the bound control path, binding reset, the binding overrides a Settings document saves and loads, and local player pairing. Script code never sees this type; it sees the Input surface, When.Input, When.Player, handle.Rebind().As, handle.BoundControl, handle.ResetBinding() and .Bindings(Input.ForPlayer(n)). Cursor lock and visibility are not on this interface. public interface IInputProvider Expand Details ... Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new FakeInputProvider()); Remarks Two implementations exist and the tests that matter run against both. FakeInputProvider is a second real implementation rather than a mock, in the same way FakeNetworkProvider is: it holds declared actions and the values a test gives them, which is what makes every input test runnable in Edit Mode with no device and no window. InputSystemProvider in CodeSmile.LunyScript.Input is the Input System one, the only LunyScript assembly that references that package; it translates to LunyInput's LocalInput, which records the actions, pairs the devices and captures the rebinds, and which C# beside the scripts can read too. A value read returns the last value the action received. The backend keeps a copy of each resolved action's value and press state, written while the backend processes its input, and a read returns that copy without asking a device. The same copy answers in On.FixedUpdate, in On.Update and in every other event, whichever of those phases the backend processes its input in. An action that has received nothing reads its resting value. An occurrence is delivered once, in the first frame update after it was received, and is never replayed. The backend records the occurrences each action receives, and BeginFrame() hands everything received since the previous call to the frame that is starting. An occurrence the scripts of that frame did not ask about is gone, which is what the accepted design requires of input while a menu is open. Nothing here throws because a device is absent. A player with no paired device reads the resting value of every action, the way an offline INetworkProvider reports no authority: a missing device is a state, not an exception. Properties IsPairingOpen Whether a button press on a device no local player holds currently pairs it. bool IsPairingOpen { get; } Property Value bool LocalPlayerCapacity How many local player numbers this backend can hold, from 0. A one-player backend answers 1. A backend that pairs its own players answers one more than the players it can hold, because numbers 0 and 1 both name its host. int LocalPlayerCapacity { get; } Property Value int Remarks The gateway reads the pairing state of every number below this once per frame, so it must allocate nothing. LocalPlayerCount How many local players this backend currently has. Zero is a valid answer and is not a failure. int LocalPlayerCount { get; } Property Value int Methods ApplyOverrides(int, List<InputBindingOverride>, List<InputBindingOverride>) Replaces every binding override of one local player's actions with overrides: removes them all, then applies each entry whose key names a binding of that player's actions. bool ApplyOverrides(int localPlayerIndex, List<InputBindingOverride> overrides, List<InputBindingOverride> stale) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. List<InputBindingOverride> overrides The overrides to apply. List<InputBindingOverride> stale Receives each entry whose key names no binding, or whose path is empty; those are not applied. Returns bool False when this backend has no actions for that local player; nothing changes then. BeginFrame() Starts the occurrences of a new frame: from this call until the next one, Occurred(int, InputPhase) answers whether the action received that occurrence between the previous call and this one. Called once per frame by the gateway, before any script instance runs. Must allocate nothing. void BeginFrame() Remarks Several input updates can fall between two calls, such as several fixed steps of one frame when the backend processes its input before each fixed step; all of them belong to the frame that starts here, and one occurrence received in two of them is delivered once. BoundPath(int, int) The control path one binding uses now: its override when one is applied, the action asset's path otherwise. Must allocate nothing, because a settings row reads it every frame. string BoundPath(int actionId, int partId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. int partId A part's identifier, or Unresolved for the action's first binding that is not part of a composite. Returns string The path, or null when the action has no such binding. CancelAllRebinds() Stops every in-flight capture. A provider that is about to be replaced or dropped must call this so a RebindingOperation does not stay subscribed to Input System updates. void CancelAllRebinds() CancelRebind(int) Stops one capture without applying an override. A missing or already-terminal identifier is a no-op. void CancelRebind(int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int rebindId The identifier StartRebind(int, int, out int) produced. ClosePairing() Stops pairing new players. A player whose device is lost still takes the next device pressed. InputPairingResult ClosePairing() Returns InputPairingResult Applied, or why this backend pairs nothing. HoldsPointer(int) Whether the player on one local player number holds the pointer device: the mouse, which pairs together with the keyboard and belongs to one player at a time. The interaction family's focuser uses the pointer for that player and the centre of the view for every other. Must allocate nothing, because the gateway asks once per frame per focuser. bool HoldsPointer(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns bool True while that player's devices include a pointer that is not lost. Remarks A one-player backend answers true for its player when a pointer device is connected. A backend answers true for at most one player; when two answer true, the interaction family uses the lowest number and reports it once. IsLost(int) Whether the device the player on that number is paired with has disconnected. False for nobody. Must allocate nothing. bool IsLost(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns bool True while that player's device is lost. IsPressed(int) Whether the action was held down when it last received input. Must allocate nothing; AGENTS.md rule 29. bool IsPressed(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. Returns bool True while the last input the action received holds the control pressed. Leave(int) Asks to release one local player's devices and free the number. The release is applied by the next UpdatePairing(). InputPairingResult Leave(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns InputPairingResult Applied, NoPlayer when nobody holds the number, HostStays for numbers 0 and 1 while the host holds them, or why this backend pairs nothing. Occurred(int, InputPhase) Whether one occurrence was handed to the frame that is running by the last BeginFrame(). Must allocate nothing. bool Occurred(int actionId, InputPhase phase) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. InputPhase phase Which occurrence to ask about. Returns bool True when the action received it before this frame began and after the frame before began. OpenPairing() Starts pairing: from now on a button press on a device no local player holds pairs it with the host while nobody holds the host, and with the lowest free guest number after that. InputPairingResult OpenPairing() Returns InputPairingResult Applied, or why this backend pairs nothing. ParticipantAt(int) The backend's identity of the person on one local player number, or 0 when nobody holds it. Must allocate nothing. long ParticipantAt(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns long The identity, 0 for nobody and for a number the backend cannot hold. Remarks The identity changes when a different person takes the number, and stays the same when the same person's device is lost and regained or re-paired, which is what the settled contract-player-identity answer asks of a participant. A backend must not hand out the same identity to two people during its lifetime; the gateway maps it to a counter of its own, so two backends may use the same numbers. Two numbers that answer the same identity name one person. A backend that pairs its own players answers its host's identity on numbers 0 and 1, and the gateway then gives both numbers one participant and counts that person once. PollRebind(int) Asks whether one capture has finished. Must allocate nothing while pending. InputRebindPoll PollRebind(int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int rebindId The identifier StartRebind(int, int, out int) produced. Returns InputRebindPoll Pending while listening, then a terminal outcome. ReadNumber(int) The last one-component value the action received. Must allocate nothing. double ReadNumber(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. Returns double The value, which is 0 at rest and before the action received anything. ReadOverrides(int, List<InputBindingOverride>) Adds every binding override one local player's actions carry to into, in the backend's own order. bool ReadOverrides(int localPlayerIndex, List<InputBindingOverride> into) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. List<InputBindingOverride> into The list to add to. The gateway clears it first. Returns bool False when this backend has no actions for that local player; nothing is added then. ReadVector(int, out double, out double, out double) The last spatial value the action received, with unused components zero. Must allocate nothing. void ReadVector(int actionId, out double x, out double y, out double z) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. double x The first component. double y The second component. double z The third component, zero for a two-component action. ResetBinding(int, int) Removes the override of one part, or of every binding of the action, so the action asset's paths return. void ResetBinding(int actionId, int partId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. int partId A part's identifier, or Unresolved for every binding of the action, its composite parts included. Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) Finds the configured action one declaration names, and hands back the identifier every later read uses. InputActionResolution Resolve(int localPlayerIndex, string actionName, InputValueKind kind, out int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player's actions to look in. string actionName The action's name, as the script declared it. InputValueKind kind What the declaration says the action produces. int actionId The identifier the four reads take, meaningful only when this returns Resolved. Returns InputActionResolution Whether the action was found, and why not when it was not. Remarks Called once per declaration rather than once per read, so an implementation may do the string work here and must do none of it afterwards. ResolvePart(int, string, out int) Finds one part of a composite binding of a resolved action, by the part's name in the action asset, compared ordinally. The first composite part of that name is the one. InputActionResolution ResolvePart(int actionId, string partName, out int partId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced for the action. string partName The part's name, such as Up. int partId The identifier the binding members take for this part, meaningful only when this returns Resolved. Returns InputActionResolution Resolved, or NoSuchPart. Remarks Called once per part declaration, as Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) is once per action declaration, so an implementation may do the string work here and none afterwards. StartRebind(int, int, out int) Starts an interactive capture for one resolved action, or for one part of its composite. The gateway allows one in-flight capture per local player; this method starts the backend listening. InputRebindStart StartRebind(int actionId, int partId, out int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. int partId The identifier ResolvePart(int, string, out int) produced, or Unresolved to capture for the whole action. int rebindId The identifier later poll and cancel take, meaningful only when this returns Started. Returns InputRebindStart Whether the capture started, and why not when it did not. UpdatePairing() Applies every pairing change requested or detected since the last call. Called once per frame by the gateway before any script instance runs, so every script sees the same players during one frame. Must allocate nothing when nothing changed. void UpdatePairing()

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.INavigati.summary: Interface INavigationProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What a navigation backend provides to the NavigationGateway: sending an actor toward a destination, reading its route and movement, holding it in place, and clearing its route. Script code never sees this type; it sees the Navigation surface. public interface INavigationProvider Expand Details ... Examples runner.NavigationGateway.UseProvider(new FakeNavigationProvider()); Remarks The shipped backend is Unity's NavMesh. NavMeshNavigationProvider in CodeSmile.LunyScript.Navigation is the one real implementation and the only place in the product that names NavMeshAgent. FakeNavigationProvider is a second real implementation with no navigation mesh, which is what makes every navigation block testable in every gate. The settled contract-targeting-navigation answer asks for "an explicitly configured navigation capability" and no "implicit provider choice", so the C# code that owns the runner installs one with UseProvider(INavigationProvider). An actor is a UnityEngine.Object. The core cannot name Unity's object model outside GameObjectHost, AGENTS.md rule 24, so an actor reaches the provider as the object a declared input resolved to, or as the object the script runs on, and the provider is what knows whether that object carries an agent. A GameObject, a Transform and any component of the actor are all the same actor. The gateway owns the attempts; the provider owns none. Which operation drives an actor, what a partial route means for it, and when an attempt ends are decided in the gateway, so every backend applies the same rules. The provider only answers what the backend knows. Every member but Describe() runs on the frame path and must not allocate once an actor has been seen, AGENTS.md rule 29. Methods Check(Object) Reports whether the actor can navigate. The gateway asks before every start and every control. NavigationAgentState Check(Object actor) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The actor, as the author assigned it or as the script's own object. Returns NavigationAgentState Ready, or why it cannot. Clear(Object) Clears the actor's route, so it stops following it. The position the actor reached is kept. void Clear(Object actor) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The actor. Remarks An actor that cannot navigate is left as it is. Describe() Names the backend for the one log line UseProvider(INavigationProvider) writes. Called once, so it may allocate. string Describe() Returns string For example: "Unity NavMesh". Hold(Object, bool) Holds the actor where it is, or releases it. A held actor keeps its route and moves along it again when it is released. void Hold(Object actor, bool hold) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The actor. bool hold True to hold, false to release. Remarks An actor that cannot navigate is left as it is. Read(Object, Vector3) Reports the actor's route toward destination, its movement and its end as they stand now. NavigationReading Read(Object actor, Vector3 destination) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The actor. Vector3 destination The destination the latest Start(Object, Vector3) asked for. A backend that moves a destination onto its navigation surface reports a route that ends away from this point as Partial, because it does not reach the destination. Returns NavigationReading The reading. Start(Object, Vector3) Asks for a route from the actor's position to a destination and starts following it once it is known. A route the actor already follows is replaced. The gateway calls it only for an actor Check(Object) reported ready. bool Start(Object actor, Vector3 destination) Parameters Type Name Description Object actor The actor. Vector3 destination The destination in world space. The gateway passes finite components only. Returns bool True when the route was requested. False when the backend can request no route to destination at all, which the gateway reports as an invalid route; nothing changed.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.INetworkP.title: Interface INetworkProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.INetworkP.summary: Interface INetworkProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What a netcode backend provides to the NetworkGateway: a session to start and end, the connection facts a script is allowed to read, and two queues the gateway drains once per tick. Script code never sees this type; it sees the Net and Sync surfaces. AGENTS.md rule 49. public interface INetworkProvider Expand Details ... Examples runner.NetworkGateway.UseProvider(new FakeNetworkProvider()); Remarks Two implementations exist, and the tests that matter run against both. FakeNetworkProvider runs two peers in one process with no network and no Editor, which is what makes the message and cadence tests runnable in Edit Mode; it is a second real implementation rather than a mock, in the same way FakeHost is for blocks. NgoNetworkProvider in CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode is the Netcode for GameObjects one, and it is the only place in the product that references that package. Authority, not "server". HasAuthority(int) answers for one object and means owner under distributed authority and server under client-server, which is why a script written against it runs unchanged in either topology. AGENTS.md rule 44. Nothing here throws because a session is not running. A provider with no session reports Offline, zero peers and no authority. Connection state is a state a script reads, not an exception it handles; AGENTS.md rule 45. Properties IsHost True when this peer is the host. False for a client and for no session at all. Exposed because rule 45 forbids hiding it, and because "works as host, breaks as client" is the defect that hiding it produces. bool IsHost { get; } Property Value bool MaximumTransformStreamBytes How many payload bytes of transform stream this backend can carry in one send. The runner splits a tick's stream into as many sends as it needs to stay inside it. int MaximumTransformStreamBytes { get; } Property Value int Remarks A transport carries a bounded message. One stream per authority per tick is what AGENTS.md rule 47 requires and it stays true here: the tick still produces one stream, and this is how many bytes of it fit in one message. A hundred objects sending all three channels is about 1800 bytes, which is past what Netcode for GameObjects carries unfragmented, so this is not a limit only an unusual session meets. Splitting rather than asking the backend to fragment is deliberate. Each piece carries the stream's own 3-byte header and is decoded on its own, so a piece costs about 3 bytes plus whatever the backend's own per-message header is; a fragmented message costs the backend's fragment headers and its reassembly state instead, and leaves the stream depending on a feature that differs between backends. PeerCount How many peers are in the session, including this one. Zero when offline. int PeerCount { get; } Property Value int RoundTripMilliseconds Round trip time to the host in milliseconds, or 0 when offline or when this peer is the host. Latency is a state a script may read, not an error; AGENTS.md rule 45. double RoundTripMilliseconds { get; } Property Value double State What the session is doing right now. Never throws and is meaningful before any session has been started. SessionState State { get; } Property Value SessionState Methods Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines, so a reader of the Console can tell a real session from the in-process one. Allocates; called only at state transitions, never per tick. string Describe() Returns string For example: "Netcode for GameObjects, host on port 7777", or "in-process provider, 2 peers". EndSession() Ends the session and returns to Offline. Called again on an already-offline provider, it does nothing, so that a restart is EndSession then StartHost without the caller tracking state. void EndSession() HasAuthority(int) Whether this peer may write the state of one object. bool HasAuthority(int objectId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The networked object, as the gateway numbers it. Returns bool True when this peer owns the object under distributed authority, or is the server under client-server. False when offline, because an offline peer has no authority to speak of and a script that guards on authority then does nothing rather than misbehaving. SendToAuthority(int, int) Sends one message to whichever peer holds authority over the object. The message has a name and no payload in this milestone. void SendToAuthority(int objectId, int messageId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the message is about. int messageId The message, interned by the gateway so no string crosses this call. SendTransformStream(byte[], int) Sends one authority's whole transform stream for one network tick. void SendTransformStream(byte[] payload, int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The buffer the runner encoded the stream into. The provider must copy what it needs before returning, because the runner reuses this buffer next tick. int length How many bytes of it the stream occupies. Remarks One call per authority per tick, carrying every object that authority has something to send for, rather than one call per object. AGENTS.md rule 47 requires that shape, because one message per object per tick spends about as many bytes on framing as a half-precision position costs. SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) Sends one variable's value to every other peer. Called only by the authority, and only when the variable's cadence says to send. void SendVariable(int objectId, int variableIndex, in NetworkValue value) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the variable belongs to. int variableIndex Which synchronised variable, numbered by the order the script declared it in. See VariableIndex for why this is not a slot index. NetworkValue value The value to send. StartClient(string) Joins a session. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running. void StartClient(string address) Parameters Type Name Description string address Where to connect. An implementation that needs no address ignores it. StartHost() Starts hosting. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running, so an implementation may assume it is offline. void StartHost() TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage) Takes one received message off the queue, if there is one. The gateway drains this until it returns false, once per tick. bool TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage message) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkMessage message The message, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks A TryDequeue rather than a returned collection, because the gateway drains it every tick and a returned collection would allocate every tick; AGENTS.md rule 29. TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int) Takes one "a peer joined" notification off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). bool TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int peerId) Parameters Type Name Description int peerId The peer that joined, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks This is what makes SyncCadence.Once work for a peer that was not there when the value was first set. Without it, a name chosen by the host before anyone joined would never be sent, because Once sends once and a late joiner missed it. The authority answers a join by marking every synchronised variable unsent, so the next tick sends the current value of all of them. The resend goes to every peer, not only to the one that joined. This milestone has no per-peer addressing: SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) is a broadcast. The cost is one redundant copy of each synchronised variable per peer per join, which is bounded by the number of joins rather than by the frame rate. Per-peer addressing is part of the transform stream milestone, where rule 47's bandwidth budget makes it load-bearing. TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[], out int, out int) The next transform stream that arrived, as a view into a buffer the provider owns. The view is valid until the next stream arrives. bool TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[] payload, out int offset, out int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The provider's buffer. int offset Where the stream starts in it. int length How many bytes it occupies. Returns bool False when none is waiting. Remarks A view rather than an array, because a peer that is not the authority receives a stream on every tick and returning a fresh array would allocate on every one of them. TransformStreamInbox is the implementation both providers use. TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate) Takes one received variable update off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). bool TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate update) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkVariableUpdate update The update, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.IScenePro.summary: Interface ISceneProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What a scene backend provides to SceneGateway: starting a load of one scene asset, ending one loaded instance, and reporting which scene instances are loaded. Script code never sees this type; it sees Scene.Load, Scene.Unload and When.Operation. public interface ISceneProvider Expand Details ... Examples runner.SceneGateway.UseProvider(new FakeSceneProvider()); Remarks Two implementations exist. UnitySceneProvider calls Unity's SceneManager and is what the default runner uses. FakeSceneProvider is an in-memory list of scenes for tests, the same role FakeAssetLoadProvider has for asset loads. An Addressables scene provider would be a third, behind the same gateway. A scene is named by its asset path, for example Assets/Scenes/Arena.unity, because that is what the Inspector stores for a scene input and what Unity loads by. The provider never receives a scene's file name alone. The native Loaded and Unloaded phases do not come from the provider. Unity reports them through SceneManager.sceneLoaded and sceneUnloaded whichever call started the load, and the runner's driver forwards those two callbacks to the gateway. Properties LoadedSceneCount How many scene instances are loaded now. int LoadedSceneCount { get; } Property Value int Methods CountLoaded(string) How many loaded scene instances were loaded from this asset path. int CountLoaded(string scenePath) Parameters Type Name Description string scenePath The scene asset's path. Returns int Zero when none is loaded. Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines. Allocates; called only when the provider is installed. string Describe() Returns string For example: "Unity SceneManager" or "in-memory scene provider". Load(string, bool) Starts loading one scene asset. A replacement load releases every loaded scene; an additive load releases none. ISceneLoadOperation Load(string scenePath, bool additive) Parameters Type Name Description string scenePath The scene asset's path. bool additive True to load alongside the loaded scenes. Returns ISceneLoadOperation The operation the gateway polls. A scene that is not in the build completes at once as OperationFailure.NotFound, and nothing starts. LoadedScenePathAt(int) The asset path of one loaded scene instance. string LoadedScenePathAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index From zero to LoadedSceneCount minus one. Returns string The path. May allocate; the gateway reads it only when a replacement load starts. Unload(ISceneLoadOperation) Starts unloading the exact instance one completed additive load produced. This is how a load whose requester stopped waiting is cleaned up. IAsyncOperation Unload(ISceneLoadOperation load) Parameters Type Name Description ISceneLoadOperation load An operation this provider's Load(string, bool) returned, completed successfully. Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. Unload(string) Starts unloading the one loaded instance of this asset path. The gateway calls it only after CountLoaded(string) returned one. IAsyncOperation Unload(string scenePath) Parameters Type Name Description string scenePath The scene asset's path. Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. When that instance is the only loaded scene, it completes at once as OperationFailure.Denied, because a game always has one scene loaded.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.IScriptAs.title: Interface IScriptAssetInputs | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.IScriptAs.summary: Interface IScriptAssetInputs Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The part of a host that carries the assets an author assigned to one object, so that two objects running the same script can hold different assets. public interface IScriptAssetInputs Expand Details ... Examples var assigned = (host as IScriptAssetInputs)?.AssignedAsset(nameof(GateScript.OpenSound)); Remarks It is a second interface rather than a member on IScriptHost for the reason IScriptObjectLifetime is one: a host that carries no assignments answers nothing to every name, and a member every implementation could only answer null to would be a member every implementation has to carry. A host that does not implement this is a host that assigns nothing, which resolves every input to its declared source or its type's asset placeholder rather than failing. A value is matched to an input by the input's declared name. That is the settled api-asset-inspector-binding-mechanism-identity answer of 2026-09-12: the name is the durable identity, so the order the inputs are declared in can change and a stored value still reaches the same input. It names no GameObject, Transform or Component, so the type ban of AGENTS.md rule 24 still holds. UnityEngine.Object is what an asset is, and it is what the host component serializes. Methods AssignedAsset(string) The asset this object has stored under one declared input name, or null when it stores none. Object AssignedAsset(string declaredName) Parameters Type Name Description string declaredName The input's declared name. Returns Object The stored asset, or null. Remarks Called once per declared input when the object spawns, and never afterwards. The caller checks the type, so an implementation returns what it holds rather than testing it.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.IScriptHo.title: Interface IScriptHost | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.IScriptHo.summary: Interface IScriptHost Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The object a script runs on, as the blocks see it. Blocks reach the object through this interface and never through a GameObject, a Transform or a Component. public interface IScriptHost Expand Details ... Examples var host = new FakeHost(instanceId: 1); var instance = runner.Spawn(program, host); Remarks Game scripts use GameObjectHost. Explicit editor workflows use the scene-free host owned by EditorScriptSession, which refuses spatial access. FakeHost remains a test double. AGENTS.md rule 53 and docs/editor-foundation.md define the capability boundary. Properties IsAlive False once the underlying object no longer exists. The Editor and DEBUG frame loop polls this to report lifecycle violations. Explicit Ready validation and network transform access guards read this in every build. bool IsAlive { get; } Property Value bool Remarks AGENTS.md rule 20 states the contract and what it does not promise. Detection is best-effort. MotionBodyIsActive Whether the object's GameObject is active in the hierarchy. Physical Motion inputs on an inactive body are refused. bool MotionBodyIsActive { get; } Property Value bool Methods AudioIsPlaying() Whether the bound AudioSource is playing. False while it is paused, stopped, or missing. bool AudioIsPlaying() Returns bool Describe() Names this host for a diagnostic message. Allocates, and is called only where LunyScript is reporting a failure, by throwing or by logging, never on the succeeding run-time path. string Describe() Returns string Something a user can find in the scene, for example a GameObject name, where the implementation can still read one. Remarks GameObjectHost retains the name and EntityId in DEBUG or when LUNYSCRIPT_CAPTURE_HOST_NAMES is defined. Rename updates that capture after the native name is written. Without capture a destroyed host returns a fixed description. docs/proposals/review-proposals.md states the capture and native-rename boundaries. HasParent(TransformRelation, int) Whether the named object has a parent. bool HasParent(TransformRelation relation, int childIndex) Parameters Type Name Description TransformRelation relation Which object to ask about. int childIndex The child index, used only for Child. Returns bool True when it is parented to another object rather than sitting at the scene root. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The named object does not exist. LookAt(TransformRelation, int, double, double, double, double, double, double) Turns the named object to face a world point, about a stated up direction. bool LookAt(TransformRelation relation, int childIndex, double x, double y, double z, double upX, double upY, double upZ) Parameters Type Name Description TransformRelation relation Which object to turn. int childIndex Its child index, used only for Child. double x The world x of the point to face. double y The world y. double z The world z. double upX The x of the up direction to keep the object's up axis nearest. double upY The y of that direction. double upZ The z of that direction. Returns bool False when the facing is undefined, in which case nothing was written: the point is where the object already stands, or the direction to it is parallel to the up direction, and there is no rotation the two describe. True when the object was turned. Remarks An undefined facing writes nothing rather than inventing a direction, which is the captain's answer to API-semantics row T04 on 2026-09-13. The object's forward axis ends up pointing at the point and its up axis is kept as near the up direction as the facing allows. Must allocate nothing; AGENTS.md rule 29. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The named object does not exist. MotionAddExplosion(double, double, double, double, double, double, bool) One explosion force or impulse on a dynamic body, through the engine's own explosion call: Unity's Rigidbody.AddExplosionForce with ForceMode.Force or ForceMode.Impulse. The engine measures the distance from the centre to the body's colliders, scales the strength down linearly to zero at radius, and leaves a body farther away than that untouched. void MotionAddExplosion(double strength, double centerX, double centerY, double centerZ, double radius, double upwardsModifier, bool impulse) Parameters Type Name Description double strength The force, or the impulse, at the centre. double centerX The explosion centre's world x. double centerY The explosion centre's world y. double centerZ The explosion centre's world z. double radius World units from the centre at which the strength reaches zero. Greater than 0. double upwardsModifier World units below the centre that the push direction is measured from; the centre and the radius stay where they are. 0 pushes straight away from the centre. bool impulse True for an impulse, false for a force. MotionAddForce(double, double, double, TransformSpace, bool) A force or impulse on a dynamic body. Local space is the body's physics orientation. void MotionAddForce(double x, double y, double z, TransformSpace space, bool impulse) Parameters Type Name Description double x double y double z TransformSpace space bool impulse MotionFaceTowards(double, double, double, double) Turns toward a world point by at most maxDegrees without overshoot. A point the object already stands on, or a direction parallel to world up, writes nothing. void MotionFaceTowards(double targetX, double targetY, double targetZ, double maxDegrees) Parameters Type Name Description double targetX double targetY double targetZ double maxDegrees MotionMoveBy(double, double, double, TransformSpace) One Motion.MoveBy displacement. A dynamic body also clears both velocities. A kinematic body receives a pose write and no velocity setter. void MotionTeleport(double x, double y, double z) Parameters Type Name Description double x double y double z MotionTeleport(double, double, double, double, double, double, double) Places the object and writes this orientation. A dynamic body also clears both velocities. A kinematic body receives a pose write and no velocity setter. void MotionTeleport(double x, double y, double z, double rotationX, double rotationY, double rotationZ, double rotationW) Parameters Type Name Description double x double y double z double rotationX double rotationY double rotationZ double rotationW MoveBy(double, double, double) Adds to the object's world-space position. AGENTS.md rules 12 and 13. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Input.Inp.title: Class InputSystemProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Input.Inp.summary: Class InputSystemProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Input Assembly ApiSource.dll The input backend that reads Unity's Input System, through LunyInput's LocalInput. The one LunyScript assembly that references that package and LunyInput. public sealed class InputSystemProvider : IInputProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object InputSystemProvider Implements IInputProvider Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new InputSystemProvider(actions)); runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new InputSystemProvider(actions, 4)); Remarks This assembly compiles only when the Input System package is installed. Its assembly definition carries a version define, LUNY_INPUTSYSTEM from com.unity.inputsystem 1.8.0 or newer, and a matching define constraint, which is the same arrangement CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode uses for Netcode for GameObjects, and LunyInput's assembly carries the same pair. The core stays package-independent. LunyInput does the work; this type translates. A LocalInput finds and records the actions, pairs the devices, captures rebinds and lists the binding overrides, and C# beside the scripts can read the same players through Input and LocalPlayer(int). This type maps a script's declaration to a LunyInput record and back to the numbers InputGateway keeps, maps the enums, and adds what is LunyScript's own: the two numbers of the host, the frame window and pairing at the runner's frame start. Assets/CodeSmile/LunyInput/README.md states the boundary. Numbers 0 and 1 both name the host. With players the LocalInput pairs, LunyScript's local player numbers 0 and 1 are LunyInput's player 0, the host, and number n from 2 up is LunyInput's player n - 1, so LocalPlayerCapacity is one more than the players it can hold. docs/proposals/local-player-pairing.md is the contract. In the other two setups a number is the player index unchanged. The three occurrences are handed to the next frame update. Started, Performed and Canceled are the action's own phases; the record collects the ones received since the gateway's last BeginFrame(), which hands them to the frame that is starting and drops the ones the previous frame held. Several input updates in one frame deliver one occurrence, and an occurrence nobody read in its frame is not delivered later. The gateway also applies pairing at its frame start, through UpdatePairing(), so every script of one frame sees the same players. Three setups, chosen by the constructor. new InputSystemProvider(actions) is one player: local player 0 is present from the start on every device and pairing is refused. new InputSystemProvider(actions, 4) pairs up to four local players itself, with the solo start LocalInput describes. With PlayerInput components in the scene and no local player count, their players are observed and PlayerInputManager owns the pairing. InputSystemProvider.For(input) reads a LocalInput the caller made and keeps. Constructors InputSystemProvider() Creates a provider that reads whichever PlayerInput components are present, and nothing else. public InputSystemProvider() Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new InputSystemProvider()); Remarks Use this when the project pairs its players with PlayerInput. A local player with no PlayerInput resolves nothing and every action of that player is reported once and reads its resting value. InputSystemProvider(InputActionAsset) Creates a provider with one action asset to fall back on for local player 0. public InputSystemProvider(InputActionAsset actions) Parameters Type Name Description InputActionAsset actions The action asset for local player 0, or null for none. Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new InputSystemProvider(actions)); Remarks A PlayerInput for a local player always wins, because that is where the Input System keeps that player's paired devices. The asset is what a single-player project uses, where there is nothing to pair and a PlayerInput component would be ceremony. The asset is enabled here, because an action that is not enabled reads its resting value forever and that reads exactly like a wrong binding. A PlayerInput's own actions are left alone: that component enables and disables them itself. InputSystemProvider(InputActionAsset, int) Creates a provider that pairs up to localPlayers local players itself. Nobody is present until someone presses a button. public InputSystemProvider(InputActionAsset actions, int localPlayers) Parameters Type Name Description InputActionAsset actions The action asset each local player's copy is made from. int localPlayers How many local players can pair, the host included, from 1. Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new InputSystemProvider(actions, 4)); Remarks The first player to pair is the host, and local player numbers 0 and 1 both name the host for as long as this provider lives: a leave of either changes nothing. Every later player is a guest on the lowest free number from 2 up to localPlayers. The solo start. Until a script first opens pairing, the first button press on a device the asset can use makes the host, and the host's actions read every device, so a game for one player needs no pairing line. Opening pairing for the first time ends it: the host keeps their InputUser and their participant, their actions read no device, and the next device pressed becomes the host's, with pairing open or not. A guest pairs only while pairing is open, and opening pairing again later keeps the host's device. Each player gets its own copy of actions, so the actions of two players are different InputAction objects and one gamepad cannot drive both. PlayerInput components are not read by this setup: it owns the pairing, and a scene that pairs with PlayerInputManager uses the other constructors. Call Dispose(), or install another provider, which disposes this one, to release the copies and the InputUsers. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException actions is null or localPlayers is below 1. Properties Input The LocalInput this provider reads, so C# beside the scripts reads the same players. Player n there is LunyScript's local player n, except with players it pairs, where LunyScript's numbers 0 and 1 are its player 0 and number n from 2 up is its player n - 1; LocalPlayer(int) does that arithmetic. public LocalInput Input { get; } Property Value LocalInput Examples var pause = provider.Input.Player(0).Button("Pause"); IsPairingOpen Whether a button press on a device no local player holds currently pairs it. public bool IsPairingOpen { get; } Property Value bool LocalPlayerCapacity How many local player numbers this backend can hold, from 0. A one-player backend answers 1. A backend that pairs its own players answers one more than the players it can hold, because numbers 0 and 1 both name its host. public int LocalPlayerCapacity { get; } Property Value int Remarks The gateway reads the pairing state of every number below this once per frame, so it must allocate nothing. LocalPlayerCount How many local players this backend currently has. Zero is a valid answer and is not a failure. public int LocalPlayerCount { get; } Property Value int Remarks With a local player count, how many players are paired, the host counted once. Otherwise the number of PlayerInput components present, or 1 when this provider was given an action asset and no PlayerInput exists. Methods ApplyOverrides(int, List<InputBindingOverride>, List<InputBindingOverride>) Replaces every binding override of one local player's actions with overrides: removes them all, then applies each entry whose key names a binding of that player's actions. public bool ApplyOverrides(int localPlayerIndex, List<InputBindingOverride> overrides, List<InputBindingOverride> stale) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. List<InputBindingOverride> overrides The overrides to apply. List<InputBindingOverride> stale Receives each entry whose key names no binding, or whose path is empty; those are not applied. Returns bool False when this backend has no actions for that local player; nothing changes then. Remarks Removes every override of that player's actions, then finds each entry's binding by the binding id, the last segment of its key, and applies the path to it; the order Unity's LoadBindingOverridesFromJson uses. An id the actions do not have is stale. BeginFrame() Starts the occurrences of a new frame: from this call until the next one, Occurred(int, InputPhase) answers whether the action received that occurrence between the previous call and this one. Called once per frame by the gateway, before any script instance runs. Must allocate nothing. public void BeginFrame() Remarks Several input updates can fall between two calls, such as several fixed steps of one frame when the backend processes its input before each fixed step; all of them belong to the frame that starts here, and one occurrence received in two of them is delivered once. BoundPath(int, int) The control path one binding uses now: its override when one is applied, the action asset's path otherwise. Must allocate nothing, because a settings row reads it every frame. public string BoundPath(int actionId, int partId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. int partId A part's identifier, or Unresolved for the action's first binding that is not part of a composite. Returns string The path, or null when the action has no such binding. Remarks For a whole action, the first binding that is neither a composite nor one of its parts. Reads InputBinding.effectivePath, a string the binding already holds. CancelAllRebinds() Stops every in-flight capture. A provider that is about to be replaced or dropped must call this so a RebindingOperation does not stay subscribed to Input System updates. public void CancelAllRebinds() Remarks Cancels the captures this provider started; a capture C# started on the same LocalInput keeps listening. CancelRebind(int) Stops one capture without applying an override. A missing or already-terminal identifier is a no-op. public void CancelRebind(int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int rebindId The identifier StartRebind(int, int, out int) produced. ClosePairing() Stops pairing new players. A player whose device is lost still takes the next device pressed. public InputPairingResult ClosePairing() Returns InputPairingResult Applied, or why this backend pairs nothing. Dispose() Stops copying input into the records this provider resolved, which then read their resting values, and releases every local player's InputUser and action copy, by disposing the LocalInput it made. A LocalInput the caller gave it is left working, and only the rebinds this provider started are canceled. UseProvider(IInputProvider) calls it when another provider replaces this one, and ReleaseProvider(IInputProvider) when the game takes it out. public void Dispose() Examples provider.Dispose(); For(LocalInput) Creates a provider that reads a LocalInput the caller made, so the scripts and the C# beside them read the same players, the same pairing and the same rebound controls. public static InputSystemProvider For(LocalInput input) Parameters Type Name Description LocalInput input The LocalInput to read; it must not be disposed. Returns InputSystemProvider The provider, to install with UseProvider(IInputProvider). Examples m_Input = new LocalInput(m_Actions, 4); LunyScriptRuntime.DefaultRunner.InputGateway.UseProvider(InputSystemProvider.For(m_Input)); Remarks The caller keeps the LocalInput and disposes it: releasing or replacing this provider leaves it working. While this provider is installed, the runner applies the LocalInput's pairing at its frame start, so every script of one frame sees the same players; C# reads after that start see them too. With players the LocalInput pairs, numbers 0 and 1 both name its player 0, the host, and number n from 2 up is its player n - 1. A method rather than a fourth constructor, because the C# compiler reads every constructor's parameter types to choose one, so a constructor taking a LocalInput would make every assembly that calls new InputSystemProvider(actions) reference LunyInput's assembly. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException input is null or was disposed. HoldsPointer(int) Whether the player on one local player number holds the pointer device: the mouse, which pairs together with the keyboard and belongs to one player at a time. The interaction family's focuser uses the pointer for that player and the centre of the view for every other. Must allocate nothing, because the gateway asks once per frame per focuser. public bool HoldsPointer(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns bool True while that player's devices include a pointer that is not lost. Remarks A one-player backend answers true for its player when a pointer device is connected. A backend answers true for at most one player; when two answer true, the interaction family uses the lowest number and reports it once. IsLost(int) Whether the device the player on that number is paired with has disconnected. False for nobody. Must allocate nothing. public bool IsLost(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns bool True while that player's device is lost. Remarks True while the player's InputUser holds a lost device: one that was paired and has since been removed from the Input System, which is what unplugging a gamepad does. The host of the solo start reads every device and is never lost while it lasts. IsPressed(int) Whether the action was held down when it last received input. Must allocate nothing; AGENTS.md rule 29. public bool IsPressed(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. Returns bool True while the last input the action received holds the control pressed. Remarks Returns the pressed state the action last received; asks no device. Leave(int) Asks to release one local player's devices and free the number. The release is applied by the next UpdatePairing(). public InputPairingResult Leave(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns InputPairingResult Applied, NoPlayer when nobody holds the number, HostStays for numbers 0 and 1 while the host holds them, or why this backend pairs nothing. Remarks Numbers 0 and 1 name the host, who stays: their leave answers HostStays and keeps the host's devices. LocalPlayer(int) The LunyInput player a script reads as Input.ForPlayer(n), so C# beside the scripts names the player by the script's number. public InputPlayer LocalPlayer(int localPlayerNumber) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerNumber A script's local player number, from 0. Returns InputPlayer The player, a view that allocates nothing. Examples var guestFire = provider.LocalPlayer(2).Button("Fire"); // the player a script reads as Input.ForPlayer(2) Remarks With players the LocalInput pairs, numbers 0 and 1 both give its player 0, the host, and number n from 2 up gives its player n - 1. In the other two setups the number is the player index unchanged. A number beyond the players the setup holds gives a player nobody holds, whose finds answer NoSuchPlayer. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException localPlayerNumber is negative. Occurred(int, InputPhase) Whether one occurrence was handed to the frame that is running by the last BeginFrame(). Must allocate nothing. public bool Occurred(int actionId, InputPhase phase) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. InputPhase phase Which occurrence to ask about. Returns bool True when the action received it before this frame began and after the frame before began. Remarks Started, Performed and Canceled are the action's own phases of the same names, as its interactions report them: a Hold interaction starts on the press and performs when the hold time is reached, and a pass-through action performs on every change and never starts. OpenPairing() Starts pairing: from now on a button press on a device no local player holds pairs it with the host while nobody holds the host, and with the lowest free guest number after that. public InputPairingResult OpenPairing() Returns InputPairingResult Applied, or why this backend pairs nothing. Remarks The first open ends the solo start: the host keeps their InputUser and their participant, their devices are unpaired so their actions read none, and the next device pressed becomes the host's. ParticipantAt(int) The backend's identity of the person on one local player number, or 0 when nobody holds it. Must allocate nothing. public long ParticipantAt(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. Returns long The identity, 0 for nobody and for a number the backend cannot hold. Remarks The identity changes when a different person takes the number, and stays the same when the same person's device is lost and regained or re-paired, which is what the settled contract-player-identity answer asks of a participant. A backend must not hand out the same identity to two people during its lifetime; the gateway maps it to a counter of its own, so two backends may use the same numbers. Two numbers that answer the same identity name one person. A backend that pairs its own players answers its host's identity on numbers 0 and 1, and the gateway then gives both numbers one participant and counts that person once. PollRebind(int) Asks whether one capture has finished. Must allocate nothing while pending. public InputRebindPoll PollRebind(int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int rebindId The identifier StartRebind(int, int, out int) produced. Returns InputRebindPoll Pending while listening, then a terminal outcome. ReadNumber(int) The last one-component value the action received. Must allocate nothing. public double ReadNumber(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. Returns double The value, which is 0 at rest and before the action received anything. Remarks Returns the value the action last received; asks no device. A button reads its analogue press, which is 1 for a key that is down. ReadOverrides(int, List<InputBindingOverride>) Adds every binding override one local player's actions carry to into, in the backend's own order. public bool ReadOverrides(int localPlayerIndex, List<InputBindingOverride> into) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number, from 0. List<InputBindingOverride> into The list to add to. The gateway clears it first. Returns bool False when this backend has no actions for that local player; nothing is added then. Remarks Every binding of every action map of that player's actions whose overridePath is set and differs from its asset path, keyed map/action/binding-id. An override to the asset's own path binds nothing the asset does not, and is not reported. ReadVector(int, out double, out double, out double) The last spatial value the action received, with unused components zero. Must allocate nothing. public void ReadVector(int actionId, out double x, out double y, out double z) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. double x The first component. double y The second component. double z The third component, zero for a two-component action. Remarks Returns the value the action last received; asks no device. ResetBinding(int, int) Removes the override of one part, or of every binding of the action, so the action asset's paths return. public void ResetBinding(int actionId, int partId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. int partId A part's identifier, or Unresolved for every binding of the action, its composite parts included. Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) Finds the configured action one declaration names, and hands back the identifier every later read uses. public InputActionResolution Resolve(int localPlayerIndex, string actionName, InputValueKind kind, out int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player's actions to look in. string actionName The action's name, as the script declared it. InputValueKind kind What the declaration says the action produces. int actionId The identifier the four reads take, meaningful only when this returns Resolved. Returns InputActionResolution Whether the action was found, and why not when it was not. Remarks Called once per declaration rather than once per read, so an implementation may do the string work here and must do none of it afterwards. ResolvePart(int, string, out int) Finds one part of a composite binding of a resolved action, by the part's name in the action asset, compared ordinally. The first composite part of that name is the one. public InputActionResolution ResolvePart(int actionId, string partName, out int partId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced for the action. string partName The part's name, such as Up. int partId The identifier the binding members take for this part, meaningful only when this returns Resolved. Returns InputActionResolution Resolved, or NoSuchPart. Remarks Called once per part declaration, as Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) is once per action declaration, so an implementation may do the string work here and none afterwards. StartRebind(int, int, out int) Starts an interactive capture for one resolved action, or for one part of its composite. The gateway allows one in-flight capture per local player; this method starts the backend listening. public InputRebindStart StartRebind(int actionId, int partId, out int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. int partId The identifier ResolvePart(int, string, out int) produced, or Unresolved to capture for the whole action. int rebindId The identifier later poll and cancel take, meaningful only when this returns Started. Returns InputRebindStart Whether the capture started, and why not when it did not. Remarks A whole action is captured with no target binding, so Unity applies the override to every binding of the action; a part is captured with its binding as the target, which also makes the control the capture waits for the part's own kind, a key for a 2D vector part. UpdatePairing() Applies every pairing change requested or detected since the last call. Called once per frame by the gateway before any script instance runs, so every script sees the same players during one frame. Must allocate nothing when nothing changed. public void UpdatePairing() Remarks Leaves first, then every button press on a device nobody held, in the order the Input System reported them; LocalInput states where each press goes.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputActi.title: Enum InputActionResolution | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputActi.summary: Enum InputActionResolution Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Why an input action declaration did or did not resolve to a configured action. public enum InputActionResolution Expand Details ... Fields NoProvider = 1 No input backend is installed, so nothing can be resolved. NoSuchPart = 5 The action exists and has no composite part of the declared name. NoSuchPlayer = 4 The local player the declaration names is not present. NotFound = 2 The configured action asset has no action of that name for that local player. Resolved = 0 The backend has an action of that name and of the declared kind. WrongValueKind = 3 An action of that name exists but produces a different kind of value. Examples if (resolution != InputActionResolution.Resolved) Report(...); Remarks A declaration that does not resolve reads its kind's resting value - not pressed, zero, the zero vector - and is reported once, naming the script and the action. The object still spawns: an action name a project has not configured yet is a wiring mistake the author fixes in the action asset, and refusing every object of that script would hide every other thing the script does.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputFact.title: Struct InputFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputFact.summary: Struct InputFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Input surface inside Build(): names the local player whose actions this script reads. It hides UnityEngine.Input inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. public readonly struct InputFactory Expand Details ... Examples var move = Input.ForPlayer(0).Vector2("Move"); var fire = Input.Button("Fire"); On.Ready(Input.Pairing.Open(), Input.Cursor.Lock(), Input.Cursor.Hide()); Remarks Action reads are always one local player's input, never the machine's. There is no member here that reads a key or a device: an action is resolved for one local player, so a four-player split screen reads four players and not one global read that every player shares. That is what the accepted design means by not deriving local players from global device polling. The player is named with ForPlayer(int, string, int), or left out, in which case it is the player bound to the object the script runs on: Input.Vector2("Move") is the settled contract-input-actions answer's default form, and Input.ForPlayer(n) its explicit form. AnyPlayer(string, int) is a shared button. The machine's own state is the exception: Cursor is one lock and one visibility flag, and Pairing and PlayerCount are the machine's local players. Which backend supplies the actions is a runner service, not a script's business. The Input surface names no package. CodeSmile.LunyScript.Input is the Input System adapter, over LunyInput's LocalInput, and the only LunyScript assembly that references that package; with no adapter installed every action reads its resting value and says so once. Properties Cursor The machine cursor: lock and visibility as two independent writes. public CursorInputFactory Cursor { get; } Property Value CursorInputFactory Examples On.Ready(Input.Cursor.Lock(), Input.Cursor.Hide()); Remarks Four local players share one cursor. This is not a member of Input.ForPlayer. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). IsLost True while the device of the local player bound to the object is disconnected. That player's actions read resting values meanwhile. public ConditionBlock IsLost { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Update(If(!Input.IsLost).Then(Transform.MoveBy(1.0, 0.0, 0.0))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The factory is a default one. IsPaired True while a participant holds the local player bound to the object. False for an object bound to nobody. public ConditionBlock IsPaired { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Update(If(Input.IsPaired).Then(Transform.MoveBy(1.0, 0.0, 0.0))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The factory is a default one. Pairing The machine's pairing window: Open, Close and IsOpen. public PairingInputFactory Pairing { get; } Property Value PairingInputFactory Examples On.Ready(Input.Pairing.Open()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). PlayerCount How many local player numbers a participant holds during this frame. public NumberValueBlock PlayerCount { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.Update(If(Input.PlayerCount >= 2.0).Then(Input.Pairing.Close())); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Methods AnyPlayer(string, int) A shared button: read across every local player number the backend holds. public AnyPlayerInputFactory AnyPlayer(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns AnyPlayerInputFactory A builder whose Button declares the shared button. Examples var pause = Input.AnyPlayer().Button("Pause"); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Button(string, string, int) Declares a pressed-or-not action of the local player bound to the object the script runs on. public InputButton Button(string name, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The action's name, as the configured action asset spells it. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns InputButton The handle its two readings come from. Examples var fire = Input.Button("Fire"); Remarks The object is bound by Object.Create(prefab).ForPlayer(n), Object.Spawn(pool).ForPlayer(n) or by the Local Player field on its LunyScriptBehaviour. An object bound to nobody reads resting values, which is the settled answer's "an instance without a participant gets an unavailable binding and neutral value; it does not borrow another player". Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The name is null or whitespace, this script already declares that action as another kind, or the factory is a default one. ForPlayer(int, string, int) Names the local player whose actions the declarations that follow belong to. public PlayerInputFactory ForPlayer(int localPlayerIndex, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player, from 0. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns PlayerInputFactory A builder whose four methods declare one action each. Examples var fire = Input.ForPlayer(0).Button("Fire"); Remarks A local player is numbered from 0, which is the first player on this machine. In a backend that pairs local players, numbers 0 and 1 both name that first player, the host, and the guests are 2 up. The number is what the configured backend pairs a device with; the person holding it is a participant, and a guest's number is reused after that person leaves. A named player is not accepted here yet: Define has no player kind, and the participant reference kind the settled contract-player-identity answer describes is not built. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns InputNumber The handle its reading comes from. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputGate.title: Class InputGateway | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputGate.summary: Class InputGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The core's one entry point to player input. Owns the IInputProvider, resolves each program's declared actions once, and answers the value reads and the occurrence tests the input blocks make. public sealed class InputGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object InputGateway Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new FakeInputProvider()); Remarks This is the input counterpart of NetworkGateway and is deliberately the same shape, because it has the same problem: the core may not reference the Input System package, so the core owns an interface and a separate, package-gated assembly implements it. The ownership board's P01 row is what authorises that adapter, which is the only LunyScript assembly that names the package; it reads the players through LunyInput's LocalInput, a separate module that ships beside LunyScript. Resolution happens once per program, not once per object. A declaration carries a local player index and a name, both written in Build(), so every object running the script resolves to the same configured action. ResolutionsFor(ScriptProgram) returns the one array of backend identifiers that program's instances share; the array is re-resolved in place when the provider changes, so an instance that already holds it keeps reading the right actions. Nothing here is per frame except the reads and the start of each frame's occurrences. Each read is one array index and one call into the backend, which returns the last value the action received, and allocates nothing; AGENTS.md rule 29. CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputGateway.Tick() calls BeginFrame() once per frame, so the occurrences the backend received since the previous frame are the ones this frame's watches read. A declaration that does not resolve is reported once and reads its resting value. The report names the script, the declaration and why, at error severity, once per declaration per program, for the reason the asset inputs report once: the mistake is in the script's wiring or in the action asset, so a thousand objects say so once. Pairing changes are applied once per frame, in CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputGateway.Tick(), before any instance runs. The gateway asks the backend to apply what it queued, then reads the identity on every local player number and maps each new one to a participant counter of its own that is never reused, which is what the settled contract-player-identity answer asks of a participant. Two numbers with the same backend identity get the same participant, which is how numbers 0 and 1 both name the host of a backend that pairs its own players. When.Player(n) watches compare against those participants; docs/proposals/local-player-pairing.md is the contract. Fields Unresolved The identifier a declaration that did not resolve carries. Every read of it produces the resting value of its kind. public const int Unresolved = -1 Field Value int Properties HasProvider Whether an input backend has been installed. False means every action reads its resting value and every occurrence test is false. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool IsLocked Whether the last cursor lock write was Lock. False after Unlock and after Confine. public bool IsLocked { get; } Property Value bool IsPairingOpen Whether a button press on a device nobody holds pairs it now. public bool IsPairingOpen { get; } Property Value bool Examples var open = gateway.IsPairingOpen; IsVisible Whether the last cursor visibility write was Show. public bool IsVisible { get; } Property Value bool LocalPlayerCount How many local players the backend has, or zero when there is none. public int LocalPlayerCount { get; } Property Value int PairedCount How many participants hold a local player number during this frame, each counted once, so the host that numbers 0 and 1 both name counts as one. What Input.PlayerCount reads. public int PairedCount { get; } Property Value int Examples var players = gateway.PairedCount; Methods IsLost(int) Whether the player on one local player number has a lost device during this frame. False for nobody. public bool IsLost(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number. Returns bool True while that player's device is disconnected. Examples var lost = gateway.IsLost(1); IsPressed(int) Whether one resolved action was held down when it last received input. public bool IsPressed(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier, or Unresolved. Returns bool False for an unresolved action, for no provider and under an Input gate. Examples var pressed = gateway.IsPressed(actionId); Occurred(int, InputPhase) Whether one resolved action received one occurrence that was handed to this frame. public bool Occurred(int actionId, InputPhase phase) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier, or Unresolved. InputPhase phase Which occurrence to ask about. Returns bool False for an unresolved action and for no provider. Examples var fired = gateway.Occurred(actionId, InputPhase.Performed); ParticipantAt(int) The participant on one local player number during this frame: a number the gateway never gives to a second person, or 0 for nobody. public long ParticipantAt(int localPlayerIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player number; a negative number is nobody. Returns long The participant, or 0. Examples var paired = gateway.ParticipantAt(1) != 0; ReadNumber(int) The last one-component value one resolved action received. public double ReadNumber(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier, or Unresolved. Returns double Zero for an unresolved action, for no provider and under an Input gate. Examples var throttle = gateway.ReadNumber(actionId); ReadVector(int) The last spatial value one resolved action received. public Vector3 ReadVector(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier, or Unresolved. Returns Vector3 The zero vector for an unresolved action, for no provider and under an Input gate. Examples var move = gateway.ReadVector(actionId); ReleaseProvider(IInputProvider) Takes the installed backend back out, so that nothing reads it after the objects it reads are gone. Every declared action goes back to Unresolved and reads the resting value of its kind. public bool ReleaseProvider(IInputProvider provider) Parameters Type Name Description IInputProvider provider The provider to take out. A provider that is not the installed one changes nothing, so one scene's teardown cannot take another scene's backend away. Returns bool True when that provider was the installed one, false otherwise. Examples runner.InputGateway.ReleaseProvider(m_Provider); Remarks This is the counterpart of UseProvider(IInputProvider), and what a game whose backend reads objects of one scene calls when that scene ends. The runner outlives a scene, so a backend left installed keeps reading what that scene owned: an action asset the scene destroyed resolves as no local player, and the gateway then reports every action the scripts of that scene declared. PlayerCameraDemo is the demonstration that does this, and its OnDestroy releases before it destroys the asset it built. Releasing reports nothing. A declaration that stops resolving because the game ended its own backend is not a mistake in a script, which is what separates this from UseProvider(IInputProvider): there, an action the new backend does not have is reported. The already-reported flags are cleared as well, so a backend installed later reports what it finds missing. A provider that is System.IDisposable is disposed here, as a replaced one is in UseProvider(IInputProvider): InputSystemProvider holds Input System users, action copies and a device listener, and those are what releasing gives back. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InstanceL.summary: Class InstanceLayout Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll How many slots of each kind one instance of a program owns, and what value each slot starts from. Built once per script type and never changed afterwards. public sealed class InstanceLayout Expand Details ... Inheritance object InstanceLayout Examples var layout = program.Layout; // one Double and one Boolean: 8 + 8 = 16 payload bytes in 2 arrays Remarks The layout is what makes a spawn's cost predictable: it names every array a ScriptInstance allocates and how many bytes of payload each one carries, so the allocation test can assert an exact figure rather than a ceiling. See AGENTS.md rule 31, boundary 1, and docs/execution-model.md. Byte counts here are payload only. A managed array also carries a header whose size differs between Mono and CoreCLR, so the layout deliberately does not include it; the allocation test measures the header on the runtime it is running on and adds SlotArrayCount of them. A header size baked in here would be right on one runtime and wrong on another. Fields Empty An empty layout: no slots, no arrays, no payload.
