reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LifetimeR.summary: Enum LifetimeRequest Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What an authored Object.Activate(), Object.Deactivate(), Object.Destroy() or Object.Despawn() asked the runner to do to the object a script runs on. public enum LifetimeRequest Expand Details ... Fields Activate = 1 Activate the object the script runs on. Deactivate = 2 Deactivate the object the script runs on. Despawn = 4 End the incarnation and return its object to the pool it came from. Destroy = 3 End the incarnation and destroy its object. A pooled object leaves its pool. None = 0 Nothing was requested. Examples instance.RequestLifetime(LifetimeRequest.Deactivate); Remarks The request is recorded on the instance and applied by ScriptRunner after its current dispatch finishes, never inside the block that made it. Two reasons, and both are hard ones: a real SetActive or Destroy reaches LunyScriptBehaviour.OnDisable and OnDestroy synchronously, and those call back into the runner, which refuses to be re-entered during dispatch; and the settled contract-dispatch-order answer asks for these changes to be delivered between event invocations.

After the script ended, a read through the reference throws, the way C# throws when it reads a destroyed Unity object or component; IsRunning answers whether a read will succeed. docs/proposals/typed-instance-view.md states the whole contract. Code in another CodeSmile.* namespace writes the full name. Inside a namespace such as CodeSmile.MyGame, the name LunyScript is the namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript, so LunyScript.Find fails with CS0234 when using CodeSmile.LunyScript; is at the top of the file. An object is assigned to a script, not a script to an object. One ScriptProgram is built per script type and shared by every object assigned to it; what belongs to the object is its ScriptInstance, which holds the slots. AGENTS.md rule 21 and docs/execution-model.md. The object is managed by LunyScript from here on. Calling Object.Destroy, SetActive or AddComponent on it from outside LunyScript is outside the contract, and where LunyScript observes it, it throws. AGENTS.md rule 20 states the contract in full, including what it does not promise. Choose Script To Run in the Inspector. The selected managed reference is serialized with the scene or prefab and copied by Instantiate. The built script is held separately, so execution never writes to the serialized reference. The assets a script declares are assigned here too, one field per declared input, below the script. That is the settled api-asset-inspector-location answer: the host Inspector is where an author assigns them, one object at a time. An input this object leaves empty resolves to the input's own declared source or to the asset placeholder for its type, and that resolution is reported. The driver object carries HideFlags.HideAndDontSave, which Unity does not destroy when Play Mode ends in the Editor, so the object is still there when the next session starts, with its runner and every backend that session installed on it. The statics of LunyScriptRuntime are reset between sessions, so that type no longer names this driver, and that is what tells an ended session's driver from the current one. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.title: Class LunyScriptException | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Class LunyScriptException Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The root of every exception LunyScript throws. Catch this to catch everything the product raised and nothing else. public abstract class LunyScriptException : Exception Expand Details ... Inheritance object Exception LunyScriptException Derived LunyScriptContractException LunyScriptInternalException LunyScriptUsageException Examples try { runner.TickFrameUpdate(); } catch (LunyScriptException exception) { /* everything LunyScript raised */ } Remarks This type exists to be the one interception point. Before it, LunyScriptUsageException and LunyScriptContractException were both sealed and both derived from InvalidOperationException, so they were siblings whose only shared ancestor also catches framework failures that have nothing to do with LunyScript. A debugger filter, a catch block or a diagnostic layer could not select "everything LunyScript threw"; now one type name does it. The .NET argument types are deliberately not kept. C# has single inheritance, so an exception cannot be both an ArgumentNullException and a LunyScriptException, and the choice between them was made in favour of the base class: a user of a scripting API is not writing general .NET code against these types and should almost never catch one at all, because they name a mistake to fix rather than a condition to handle. Recorded in docs/api-changes.md. An exception that knows the authored location presents it as the topmost stack frame. A block is composed inside Build() and executed much later, so the user's script line is not on the call stack when the block fails. A throw out of Build() carries the location from its own call site; a throw while a block runs is given the running block's location by ScriptRunner.ReportBlockFailure, through AttachBlockContext, because the checks that raise it are too far from the block to name it themselves; which of the two wins, and when there is neither, is docs/console-navigation.md's "Which authored location a diagnostic carries". StackTrace prepends Location in Unity's own stack-frame format, which is what UnityEngine.StackTraceUtility.ExtractStringFromExceptionInternal reads through this virtual property, so the Console prints the user's own line as the topmost frame. It does not navigate there. A Console entry's double-click target is the file and line Unity fills in from the live call stack when the entry is written; where that lands differs by path and is measured in docs/console-navigation.md. See SourceLocation for how the location is captured. Constructors LunyScriptException(string) Creates an exception that names no script, no block and no location. protected LunyScriptException(string message) Parameters Type Name Description string message What went wrong, and what to do instead. LunyScriptException(string, string, string, SourceLocation) Creates an exception carrying the context a debugging window reads. protected LunyScriptException(string message, string scriptTypeName, string blockTypeName, SourceLocation location) Parameters Type Name Description string message What went wrong, and what to do instead. string scriptTypeName The script type's name, or null. string blockTypeName The block type's name, or null. SourceLocation location Where the block was authored, or Unknown. Properties BlockTypeName The name of the block type this concerns, or null. public string BlockTypeName { get; } Property Value string Location Where in the user's script the block was authored, captured at build time. public SourceLocation Location { get; } Property Value SourceLocation ScriptTypeName The name of the Script subclass this concerns, or null. public string ScriptTypeName { get; } Property Value string StackTrace The runtime stack, with the authored location prepended as its topmost frame when this exception has one. public override string StackTrace { get; } Property Value string Examples // CountdownScript:Build() (at Assets/Scripts/CountdownScript.cs:12) // CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptRunner:TickFrameUpdate() (at ...) Remarks The added line is Unity's own frame format, Type:Method() (at path:line), which is what StackTraceUtility produces, so a reader of the Console text sees the user's own line first. Nothing is removed: the real frames follow, so the failure is still diagnosable by a maintainer. This changes what the entry prints and not where a double-click on it goes. Unity chooses that target from the live call stack at log time rather than from this string. docs/console-navigation.md records the measurement. Where that target lands depends on who wrote the entry, and this property moves it on neither path. Where ScriptRunner.ReportBlockFailure reports the failure, LunyScript writes the entry itself, so it navigates to the line that reported the exception. Where the exception escapes instead - out of ScriptRunner.RaiseReady into LunyScriptBehaviour.Start, or out of Build() - LunyScript writes no entry and no error line at all, so there is no link of ours: Unity logs it, and the entry opens whatever called into the code that threw. The frame this property prepends is printed either way, and Unity links every printed frame that carries source information. Methods ToLogRecord() This exception as the same structured record the logging surface carries, so a debugging window reads a failure and a log entry through one shape. public LunyScriptLogRecord ToLogRecord() Returns LunyScriptLogRecord The record, at Error. Examples LunyScriptLog.Write(exception.ToLogRecord());

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.title: Class LunyScriptInternalException | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Class LunyScriptInternalException Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Thrown when LunyScript's own invariant was broken on a path a user cannot reach: a null or an impossible value inside the product's internals. public sealed class LunyScriptInternalException : LunyScriptException Expand Details ... Inheritance object Exception LunyScriptException LunyScriptInternalException Inherited Members LunyScriptException.ScriptTypeName LunyScriptException.BlockTypeName LunyScriptException.Location LunyScriptException.StackTrace LunyScriptException.ToLogRecord() Examples LunyScriptContract.NotNull(x, nameof(x)); // throws LunyScriptInternalException when x is null Remarks A user should never see one of these. If they do, it is a LunyScript defect and not something they did. Every concrete block type is internal with an internal constructor, built by the factories and never by user code, so a null argument there is the product's mistake; that is the audience split AGENTS.md rule 71 records, and it is why these do not share a type with the mistakes a user can make. Most of these are raised through CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScriptContract, whose guards are compiled out when DEBUG is not defined, so those cost a release build nothing and can be met only in the Editor and in a development player. Two sites are not those, and throw this type in every build: CompletedOperation.Failed and CompletedLoadOperation.FailedLoad. A guard is allowed to be conditional only where the failure its removal gives up is loud; breaking those two makes IsSuccess true on a failed cloud call, which is a silent wrong value rather than a crash. Do not read this type as impossible in a release build. Constructors LunyScriptInternalException(string) Creates the exception with a message naming the broken invariant. public LunyScriptInternalException(string message) Parameters Type Name Description string message Which invariant, and where. LunyScriptInternalException(string, string, string, SourceLocation) Creates the exception with the context a debugging window reads. public LunyScriptInternalException(string message, string scriptTypeName, string blockTypeName, SourceLocation location) Parameters Type Name Description string message Which invariant, and where. string scriptTypeName The script type's name, or null. string blockTypeName The block type's name, or null. SourceLocation location Where the block was authored, or Unknown.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.title: Class LunyScriptLog | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Class LunyScriptLog Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The one place LunyScript writes to the Unity console. Unity log lines are formatted here; the LunyScript console reads the retained structured fields. public static class LunyScriptLog Expand Details ... Inheritance object LunyScriptLog Examples LunyScriptLog.Warning(LunyScriptLogAreas.Cloud, "the save failed as Offline"); Remarks No code outside this class calls UnityEngine.Debug.Log, LogWarning, LogError or LogException. Before this class existed the prefix "LunyScript <area> | " was written out again as a string literal at every call site, in ten files, so changing the format meant editing every literal and a missed one was invisible. SourceRuleTests.NoCodeOutsideTheLoggingSurfaceCallsUnityDebugLog is what makes that a failing test rather than a convention. Every method here carries [HideInCallstack], and that attribute is what makes a log entry open the caller's own line. Unity skips a hidden frame both when it prints the stack and when it chooses the entry's double-click target, so the first frame it accepts is the one that called this class. Deleting the attribute was measured moving that target off the caller and into Write(in LunyScriptLogRecord, Object) in this file; docs/console-navigation.md. It hides frames and cannot reveal one, which is why the authored location is carried in the record rather than looked for on the stack; see SourceLocation. The console and runtime debugger share this structured record contract. Write(in LunyScriptLogRecord, Object) takes a LunyScriptLogRecord with the area, the script, the block and the authored location as separate fields, and formatting is the last thing that happens to it. A window that traces calls reads the record; the Console gets the string. Logging allocates and this class does not pretend otherwise. Composing a message builds strings, which AGENTS.md rule 33 forbids on the run-time path. The product's own call sites are failure paths, build-time paths and once-per-operation paths. The one block that logs each time it runs is the author's own Debug.Log, Debug.Warn and Debug.Error, and only in a build that defines DEBUG: that write is the sixth boundary AGENTS.md rule 31 names, and a build without DEBUG compiles it out. Fields Prefix What every LunyScript log line starts with. The product's name, never the repository's; AGENTS.md section 1. public const string Prefix = "LunyScript " Field Value string Separator What separates the area from the message, and one context field from the next. public const string Separator = " | " Field Value string Properties EditorRecords Editor-session diagnostics, retained even with the console window closed. AutoStaticsCleanup resets storage between Play sessions. Players compile no automatic buffer. public static DiagnosticBuffer EditorRecords { get; } Property Value DiagnosticBuffer Examples var records = LunyScriptLog.EditorRecords.Read(); Methods Compose(in LunyScriptLogRecord) Turns a record into the one line the Console shows. public static string Compose(in LunyScriptLogRecord record) Parameters Type Name Description LunyScriptLogRecord record What to say. Returns string The formatted line. Examples var line = LunyScriptLog.Compose(record); // "LunyScript core | a block threw ..." Remarks The shape is LunyScript <area> | <message>, then the script and block names when the record names them, then the authored location when it has one. A line a script's own Debug block wrote has the author's shape instead: <message> (Script: <script>, Object: <object>), then the authored location. The record's Kind is AuthoredLog. The prefix is left off because the line is the author's output, not something LunyScript is reporting. In the Editor the location is written as a Unity rich-text hyperlink. Unity subscribes EditorGUI_OpenFileOnHyperLinkClicked to its own EditorGUI.hyperLinkClicked event for every console message, and that handler opens the href at the line attribute. Writing the authored location as such a link is therefore what makes a click open the user's own script line, per log entry and with nothing to match up afterwards. Outside the Editor the same location is written as plain text, because a player log and a gate log are read as text and the markup would be noise there. Error(string, string, Object) Writes something that failed. public static void Error(string area, string message, Object context = null) Parameters Type Name Description string area Which part of LunyScript is speaking. string message What happened. Object context The object to ping in the Console, or null. Examples LunyScriptLog.Error(LunyScriptLogAreas.Host, "the script could not be assigned"); Exception(Exception, Object) Reports an exception with its own type and its own stack preserved. public static void Exception(Exception exception, Object context = null) Parameters Type Name Description Exception exception The exception to report. Object context The object to ping in the Console, or null. Examples LunyScriptLog.Exception(caught, hostObject); Remarks Forwards the original exception to UnityEngine.Debug.LogException and retains its structured context for the LunyScript console in the Editor. A LunyScriptException presents the authored location as the topmost frame of that stack, so the entry prints the user's own line first. A double-click on that entry opens the line that called this method, not the authored line. Unity chooses a Console entry's target from the live call stack when the entry is written, and [HideInCallstack] skips this method's own frame but cannot reach a frame that has already unwound. The authored location reaches the user through the entry's printed text. docs/console-navigation.md holds the measurement. Info(string, string, Object) Writes something a user may want to see that is not a problem. public static void Info(string area, string message, Object context = null) Parameters Type Name Description string area Which part of LunyScript is speaking. One of LunyScriptLogAreas. string message What happened. Object context The object to ping in the Console, or null. Examples LunyScriptLog.Info(LunyScriptLogAreas.Cloud, "signed in"); Warning(string, string, Object) Writes something a user probably wants to change, which did not stop the operation. public static void Warning(string area, string message, Object context = null) Parameters Type Name Description string area Which part of LunyScript is speaking. string message What happened. Object context The object to ping in the Console, or null. Examples LunyScriptLog.Warning(LunyScriptLogAreas.Cloud, "the save failed as Offline"); Write(in LunyScriptLogRecord, Object) Writes a record at its own severity. public static void Write(in LunyScriptLogRecord record, Object context = null) Parameters Type Name Description LunyScriptLogRecord record What to say. Object context The object the Console should ping and frame when the entry is selected, or null. Examples LunyScriptLog.Write(record);

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.title: Struct LunyScriptReference<TScript> | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Struct LunyScriptReference<TScript> Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One incarnation of a script, referenced from ordinary C# code: its compiled definition, reads of the variables it declared, and observations of their changes. Find<TScript>(LunyScriptBehaviour) returns it. public readonly struct LunyScriptReference<TScript> where TScript : Script Type Parameters TScript The script type the lookup asked for. Expand Details ... Examples var player = LunyScript.Find<PlayerScript>(behaviour); if (player.IsRunning) healthLabel.text = $"{player.Read(player.Definition.Health):0}"; Remarks A reference identifies one incarnation. It records the runner that runs the script and the instance's generation, so a pooled instance respawned onto another object is a different incarnation and this reference never reads it. A read after the script ended throws LunyScriptUsageException, the way C# throws when it reads a destroyed Unity object or component. IsRunning and IsObjectSpawned are the checks a caller makes first; neither throws. There is no write through a reference. A C# caller changes another script's state by asking it to, with Send(in Message). Properties Definition The compiled script object, whose variable properties hold the handles this reference reads. It stays set after the incarnation ends, and is null for a reference that matched no script. public TScript Definition { get; } Property Value TScript Examples var health = player.Read(player.Definition.Health); Remarks It is the object whose Build() ran, which Script also returns after Awake. A new PlayerScript() is not a definition: its properties were never assigned. IsObjectSpawned True while the object this reference's script runs on is spawned or created, and false once the object is despawned or destroyed. public bool IsObjectSpawned { get; } Property Value bool Examples m_HealthBar.SetActive(player.IsObjectSpawned); Remarks Every despawn in this version also destroys the object, so this becomes false at the same moment as IsRunning, on every path. It is false for a reference that matched no script. IsRunning True while the script this reference was taken of runs on its object, from the object's creation until the object is destroyed. Every read and every Observe succeeds while it is true and throws once it is false. public bool IsRunning { get; } Property Value bool Examples if (player.IsRunning) health = player.Read(player.Definition.Health); Remarks It stays true while the object is deactivated and while the game is paused. It becomes false when Unity destroys the object; when an authored Object.Destroy() takes effect, which ends the script and destroys the object, before Unity removes the object at the end of the frame; and when the runner's session ends, which leaving Play Mode does. It stays false after the pooled instance is respawned as a later incarnation. It is false for a reference that matched no script. Methods Equals(LunyScriptReference<TScript>) Two references are equal when they identify the same incarnation. That does not change when the incarnation ends. public bool Equals(LunyScriptReference<TScript> other) Parameters Type Name Description LunyScriptReference<TScript> other The reference to compare against. Returns bool True for the same runner, instance and generation, and for two references that matched nothing. Examples var same = firstLookup.Equals(secondLookup); Equals(object) Indicates whether this instance and a specified object are equal. public override bool Equals(object obj) Parameters Type Name Description object obj The object to compare with the current instance. Returns bool true if obj and this instance are the same type and represent the same value; otherwise, false. GetHashCode() Returns the hash code for this instance. public override int GetHashCode() Returns int A 32-bit signed integer that is the hash code for this instance. Observe(in Flag, Action<bool>) Calls changed whenever this Flag holds a different value from the one it held at the previous check, until the observation ends. public ScriptObservation Observe(in Flag variable, Action<bool> changed) Parameters Type Name Description Flag variable A handle from Definition. Action<bool> changed Called with the new value, and not for the current one. Returns ScriptObservation The observation, which the caller disposes. It ends by itself when the incarnation ends. Examples m_Watch = player.Observe(player.Definition.Alive, ShowAlive); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The script is no longer running, which IsRunning reports first; the reference matched no script; the handle was not declared by this reference's script type; or changed is null. Observe(in Number, Action<double>) Calls changed whenever this Number holds a different value from the one it held at the previous check, until the observation ends. public ScriptObservation Observe(in Number variable, Action<double> changed) Parameters Type Name Description Number variable A handle from Definition. Action<double> changed Called with the new value. It is not called for the current value; read that with Read(in Number). Returns ScriptObservation The observation, which the caller disposes. It ends by itself when the incarnation ends. Examples m_Watch = player.Observe(player.Definition.Health, ShowHealth); Remarks The check runs once per frame, after every script's On.LateUpdate. When changed is a method of a Unity object that has since been destroyed, the observation ends instead of calling it. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The script is no longer running, which IsRunning reports first; the reference matched no script; the handle was not declared by this reference's script type; or changed is null. Examples m_Watch = player.Observe(player.Definition.Facing, ShowFacing); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The script is no longer running, which IsRunning reports first; the reference matched no script; the handle was not declared by this reference's script type; or changed is null. Examples m_Watch = player.Observe(player.Definition.Stick, ShowStick); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The script is no longer running, which IsRunning reports first; the reference matched no script; the handle was not declared by this reference's script type; or changed is null. Read<TDestination>(in Text, ref TDestination) Copies a text variable of this incarnation into a caller-provided fixed string. Allocates nothing. public CopyError Read<TDestination>(in Text variable, ref TDestination destination) where TDestination : unmanaged, INativeList<byte>, IUTF8Bytes Parameters Type Name Description Text variable A handle from Definition. TDestination destination Where the text is written. Its previous content is replaced. Returns CopyError CopyError.None, or CopyError.Truncation when the destination is too small, in which case the destination is unchanged. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.title: Class LunyScriptRuntime | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Class LunyScriptRuntime Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Holds the one ScriptRunner that LunyScriptBehaviour components share, and the hidden object that ticks it once per frame. public static class LunyScriptRuntime Expand Details ... Inheritance object LunyScriptRuntime Examples var runner = LunyScriptRuntime.DefaultRunner; Remarks This is the one mutable static in the runtime core, and it carries the attribute that resets it. AGENTS.md rule 17 forbids mutable static state and rule 18 names [AutoStaticsCleanup] as the mechanism for the unavoidable one: with domain reload disabled, a static keeps its value from the previous Play session, and this attribute is what puts it back. Gate 3 in docs/gates.md measured the attribute working on this editor version. The type is partial because Unity's code generator emits a second partial declaration holding the generated reset method; a non-partial declaration fails to compile with error CS0260. A test that wants its own runner creates one directly with new ScriptRunner() and never touches this type. Nothing here is needed to run blocks. Fields DriverObjectName Name of the hidden GameObject that ticks the default runner. public const string DriverObjectName = "LunyScript Runner" Field Value string Properties DefaultRunner The runner every LunyScriptBehaviour in the scene uses. Created the first time it is asked for, together with the hidden object that ticks it. Creating it reads the project's LunyScriptSettings asset once and, in Play Mode and in a player, seeds its random draws and installs every provider the installed packages' adapters supply and that asset leaves on. public static ScriptRunner DefaultRunner { get; } Property Value ScriptRunner Examples var program = LunyScriptRuntime.DefaultRunner.GetOrBuildProgram(script); HasDefaultRunner Whether a default runner exists, without creating one. public static bool HasDefaultRunner { get; } Property Value bool Examples Assert.That(LunyScriptRuntime.HasDefaultRunner, Is.False); Methods NotifyDriverDestroyed(LunyScriptDriverBehaviour) Drops the default runner, but only when the driver being destroyed is still the current one. Called by LunyScriptDriverBehaviour from its OnDestroy. public static void NotifyDriverDestroyed(LunyScriptDriverBehaviour driver) Parameters Type Name Description LunyScriptDriverBehaviour driver The driver that is being destroyed. Examples private void OnDestroy() => LunyScriptRuntime.NotifyDriverDestroyed(this); Reset() Drops the default runner and destroys its driver object and the objects of the singleton scripts it ran, so the next caller gets a fresh runner. A test calls this between cases; the driver calls NotifyDriverDestroyed(LunyScriptDriverBehaviour) rather than this, so that destroying an old driver cannot drop a runner created after it. public static void Reset() Examples LunyScriptRuntime.Reset();

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Class LunyScriptSingletonCatalog Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The singleton scripts a player starts, which the build writes into its first scene on a hidden object. [AddComponentMenu("")] public sealed class LunyScriptSingletonCatalog : MonoBehaviour Expand Details ... Inheritance object Object Component Behaviour MonoBehaviour LunyScriptSingletonCatalog Examples Build a player whose production assemblies declare a singleton script; its first scene carries one hidden object with this component. Remarks This is how a player finds its singletons without reflection. The Editor build step reads the list from the Editor's type cache and stores one script object per singleton type here; Unity's serializer recreates them when the scene loads, and its Awake hands them to CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScriptSingletons before the game start reads the list. Nothing adds this component by hand, and a scene in the project never holds one: the build step adds it to the copy of the scene the build writes. docs/proposals/singleton-scripts.md is the contract. Fields ObjectName Name of the hidden object the build step adds to the first scene. public const string ObjectName = "LunyScript Singletons" Field Value string

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Struct LunyScriptTarget Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which object a read of another script, a request or an event filter is about: a declared object binding, an object this script holds under a name, the script that sent the request running now, the object on the other side of the contact event running now, or the script whose create or spawn made this object. public readonly struct LunyScriptTarget Expand Details ... Examples Patient = Bind.Object(); var patient = EnemyScript.At(Patient); var companion = EnemyScript.At(Object.Owned(Companion)); Remarks A script rarely writes this type. A ObjectBinding converts to it, Object.Owned(owned) makes one for an owned object, Other converts to it, and Sender and SpawnedBy are one. The target is resolved each time a block that uses it runs, to the script running on that object at that moment, and only to an incarnation that is still running; a pooled object handed out again is a new incarnation that an old slot no longer names. docs/proposals/script-communication.md is the contract. Properties IsDeclared Whether this names anything: false for a default value. public bool IsDeclared { get; } Property Value bool Examples if (target.IsDeclared) { } Methods ToString() How a diagnostic names the target. public override string ToString() Returns string The binding name, the owned object's name in quotes, Sender, Other or SpawnedBy. Operators implicit operator LunyScriptTarget(ObjectBinding) A declared object binding, as a target. public static implicit operator LunyScriptTarget(ObjectBinding binding) Parameters Type Name Description ObjectBinding binding The binding Bind.Object() declared. Returns LunyScriptTarget The target. Examples LunyScriptTarget target = Patient;

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.title: Class LunyScriptUsageException | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Class LunyScriptUsageException Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Thrown when script code asks LunyScript for something the API does not offer: a C# if around a condition block, an arithmetic operator on a text variable, a builder finished twice. public sealed class LunyScriptUsageException : LunyScriptException Expand Details ... Inheritance object Exception LunyScriptException LunyScriptUsageException Inherited Members LunyScriptException.ScriptTypeName LunyScriptException.BlockTypeName LunyScriptException.Location LunyScriptException.StackTrace LunyScriptException.ToLogRecord() Examples // throws LunyScriptUsageException: a condition block was used in a C# if if (health > 10) { } Remarks Every message names the mistake and the supported alternative, because this exception is read by a user of the product rather than by a maintainer of it. Most of these are raised at build time, which runs once per script type at launch, so a script that can throw one of those throws it on the first run. Seven cases are raised at run time instead, and two of them can fire long after launch. The implicit conversion of a condition block to bool, AGENTS.md rule 38, which throws in release builds too when a C# if or while tests the block. The text-capacity check in ScriptInstance.SetText, reached from SetTextBlock and CopyTextBlock. Build time checks only the 509-byte literal limit and does not know the target variable's TextCapacity, so a 37-byte literal written into a TextCapacity.Bytes32 variable (29 usable bytes) builds clean and throws on the first frame that block executes, which may be long after launch if it sits behind an If. The slot-range check in ScriptInstance, reached from GetNumber, SetNumber, GetFlag, SetFlag and every text accessor. A Var<T> handle carries a slot index and a kind and nothing that identifies its program, so a handle declared by a different script type addresses this script's slot of the same index; where that index is past the end of this instance's array for its kind, the access throws and the message names that cause. It fires on the first frame the block executes, which may be long after launch. docs/slice-decisions.md entries D4.31 and D4.32 record the accepted edge and the shape of the check. ScriptRunner.RaiseReady called twice for one spawn. An invalid Script type selected for serialization. A C# read or Send on LunyScriptBehaviour after the object is destroyed, or before Awake. The message names the object and the call. Other evaluated outside a contact event. The block is built in Build() and runs later, so a read in On.Update throws when that event runs. The message names the call and the six contact events that may use it. This derives from LunyScriptException and no longer from InvalidOperationException. That base is the one interception point a debugger filter or a diagnostic layer uses to select everything LunyScript threw; docs/api-changes.md records the change and why the .NET type was not kept. Constructors LunyScriptUsageException(string) Creates the exception with a message naming the mistake. public LunyScriptUsageException(string message) Parameters Type Name Description string message What the caller did, and what to do instead. LunyScriptUsageException(string, string, string, SourceLocation) Creates the exception with the context a debugging window reads and the authored line the Console shows. public LunyScriptUsageException(string message, string scriptTypeName, string blockTypeName, SourceLocation location) Parameters Type Name Description string message What the caller did, and what to do instead. string scriptTypeName The script type's name, or null. string blockTypeName The block type's name, or null. SourceLocation location Where the block was authored, or Unknown.

Every member returns an expression that is evaluated each time the block holding it runs; none of them writes anything. public readonly struct MathFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Update(Distance.Set(Math.Clamp(Distance + Step, 0.0, 100.0))); Remarks Every function here has a second, writing form on the variable itself. The API semantics board's C01 answer, 2026-09-13, requires both: Math.Abs(Offset) computes a magnitude and leaves Offset alone, while Offset.Abs() writes the magnitude back into Offset. Reach for the expression when the result feeds something else and for the write when the variable is the destination. What this surface holds, and what it deliberately does not. The board's C04 answer is a small core plus named packages: Abs, Min, Max, Clamp, Floor, Ceiling, Truncate, Round and Lerp are the core, and remap, easing, curve, spatial and trigonometric functions live in separate first-party Math packages that this one does not carry. That is an organisation choice rather than a refusal to own them. The five arithmetic operators are not members here. Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and remainder are written + - * / %, which is their expression form; Health.Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide and Remainder are their writing form. A Math.Subtract would be a third spelling of something C# already spells. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.MotionFac.summary: Struct MotionFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Motion surface inside Build(): component-directed movement, force and relocation for the object a script runs on. public readonly struct MotionFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.FixedUpdate(Motion.MoveTo(Pad).AtSpeed(4.0)); On.FixedUpdate(Motion.AddForce(Thrust).InWorldSpace()); On.FixedUpdate(If(Pulse).Then(Motion.AddImpulse(Blast).AsExplosion(Hub, 6.0), Pulse.Set(false))); On.Ready(Motion.TeleportTo(Spawn)); On.LateUpdate(Motion.FlockChildren().Towards(Goal)); Remarks Motion is not Transform. Transform.MoveBy writes pose immediately, with no physics. Motion.MoveBy selects a CharacterController, a kinematic Rigidbody, or a direct transform, and refuses a dynamic Rigidbody. Dynamic bodies use AddForce(Vector3ValueBlock, string, int), AddImpulse(Vector3ValueBlock, string, int), SetVelocity(Vector3ValueBlock, string, int) and StopMotion(string, int), and an explosion is AddForce(strength) or AddImpulse(strength) followed by AsExplosion(center, radius). Relocation that is not traversed movement is TeleportTo(Vector3ValueBlock, string, int). Switching a Rigidbody between kinematic and dynamic is Body.MakeKinematic() and Body.MakeDynamic(). API-semantics M20. Kinematic displacement and a Rigidbody teleport belong in On.FixedUpdate. Every physical input runs in On.FixedUpdate and also in On.Created, On.Spawned, On.Ready, On.Enabled, On.Disabled and On.Despawned, which run once per lifecycle change; a force or impulse added there reaches the body at the next physics step. Written in any other event they are reported once and ignored; they are not transferred to a later step. API-semantics M12, and the captain's answers of 2026-10-02 for the lifecycle events. FlockChildren(string, int) is the one call that moves the object's children rather than the object: it writes their positions once per frame from On.Update or On.LateUpdate, with no physics and no collision. Methods AddForce(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) Applies a continuous force given as three numbers. public MotionForceBuilder AddForce(NumberValueBlock x, NumberValueBlock y, NumberValueBlock z, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock x The frame's X component. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Navigatio.title: Class NavMeshNavigationProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Navigatio.summary: Class NavMeshNavigationProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Navigation Assembly ApiSource.dll The navigation backend that drives Unity's NavMesh. The one place in the product that names NavMeshAgent. public sealed class NavMeshNavigationProvider : INavigationProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object NavMeshNavigationProvider Implements INavigationProvider Examples LunyScriptRuntime.DefaultRunner.NavigationGateway.UseProvider(new NavMeshNavigationProvider()); Remarks This assembly compiles only where Unity's AI module is enabled. Its assembly definition carries a version define, LUNY_NAVIGATION from com.unity.modules.ai 1.0.0 or newer, and a matching define constraint, which is the arrangement CodeSmile.LunyScript.Cinemachine uses for Cinemachine. NavMeshAgent is part of that built-in module. The AI Navigation package, com.unity.ai.navigation, adds the components that bake a navigation mesh; this provider needs a navigation mesh at run time and does not care how it was made. Nothing here finds a route. Unity's agent asks the navigation mesh for the route, follows it with the speed, acceleration, stopping distance and avoidance the author configured, and reports what it knows. This provider translates those reports, which is what the settled contract-targeting-navigation answer asks for: "No new pathfinding engine". An agent that cannot navigate is left alone. Unity writes an error of its own when a script calls SetDestination, ResetPath or isStopped on an agent that is inactive, disabled or off the navigation mesh, so every member checks isActiveAndEnabled and isOnNavMesh first and reports the reason instead. A route reaches the destination, or it is partial. Unity moves a destination that is off the navigation mesh, such as a point inside a wall or on a ledge too small to keep, to the nearest point on the mesh, and calls the route to that point complete. This provider reports such a route as partial, because it does not reach the destination the script asked for, and a RequireComplete() move refuses it. Measured on 6000.7.0b1 in run navigation-smoke-01: a destination on an island top too small for the mesh became a floor point 1.8 units away, and Unity's pathStatus was PathComplete. An end needs a known route and a known distance. The actor is at the end of its route when no route is being calculated, the route is not invalid, and remainingDistance is finite and at most stoppingDistance plus EndTolerance. Unity reports an unknown remaining distance as infinity, and the settled navigation lifecycle answer says that "unknown remaining distance is not a completion signal". reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Navigatio.summary: Class NavigationGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The core's one entry point to navigation. Owns the INavigationProvider, one record per actor with the attempt that drives it and whether it is paused, and polls every driven actor once per frame before any instance runs. One per ScriptRunner. public sealed class NavigationGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object NavigationGateway Examples runner.NavigationGateway.UseProvider(new FakeNavigationProvider()); Remarks This is the navigation counterpart of CameraGateway, and the same shape for the same reason: the core may not reference a navigation package, so the core owns an interface and the gated assembly CodeSmile.LunyScript.Navigation implements it with Unity's NavMesh. docs/proposals/navigation.md is the family. With no provider installed, every Navigation.MoveTo fails as Denied and the gateway says so once. Stop, Pause and Resume do nothing. That is what AGENTS.md section 12 asks of an absent optional adapter: the script still builds, spawns and runs. One actor follows one route. A MoveTo on an actor that another pending attempt drives ends that attempt as cancelled. A MoveTo that repeats the pending request of its own operation - the same actor, destination and RequireComplete choice - coalesces, and any other MoveTo on a pending operation is the retarget the settled api-navigation-lifecycle answer asks for: the pending attempt ends as cancelled and the next generation starts. A navigation attempt has no deadline. The settled deadline answer bounds service operations; a walk is not a request to a service, and its length depends on its route. A record is created the first time an actor navigates, which allocates once. It is reused while the actor exists and freed at the first poll after the actor is destroyed. A coalesced repeat, a retarget, the poll and a report already written allocate nothing; AGENTS.md rule 29. Properties HasProvider Whether a navigation backend has been installed. False means every Navigation.MoveTo fails as Denied. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool Methods Tick() Polls every actor an attempt drives, once. Called by the runner before any instance runs, so an attempt that ended since the last frame has advanced its counters when the watches that react to it run in this same tick. With no actor record this returns after one count check, and a poll allocates nothing. public void Tick() UseProvider(INavigationProvider) Installs the backend. Installing another one replaces it: every navigation attempt still pending ends as cancelled, every actor is released by the previous backend, and every actor record, pause included, is dropped, because the records describe what the previous backend was told. public void UseProvider(INavigationProvider provider) Parameters Type Name Description INavigationProvider provider The backend. Null is the caller's mistake. Examples runner.NavigationGateway.UseProvider(new FakeNavigationProvider()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException provider is null.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetFactor.title: Struct NetFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetFactor.summary: Struct NetFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Net surface a script reads the session through: who has authority, whether there is a session, how many peers, how far behind a value is, and the one way to ask the authority to do something. public readonly struct NetFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Update(If(Net.HasAuthority).Then(Score.Add(1.0))); Remarks Everything here is a state, and none of it throws when there is no session. AGENTS.md rule 45: authority, ownership, connection state and latency are what a networked script gets wrong, and a design that hides them produces the "works as host, breaks as client" defect. An offline peer has no authority, is not connected, has zero peers and a round trip of zero, and a script that guards on any of those then does nothing rather than misbehaving. Authority, not "server". HasAuthority means owner under distributed authority, which is the default topology, and server under client-server. The same script runs unchanged in either; AGENTS.md rule 44. The three session facts are conditions and the two numbers are number expressions. A condition goes into If(...) and is negated with !, the way every other condition in this API is; a number expression is compared and combined the way every other number is. The proposal this milestone was written from wrote If(Net.HasAuthority == false), which would have needed a second way to negate a condition alongside the ! operator that already exists. If(!Net.HasAuthority) is the same sentence with the operator the API already has. Properties HasAuthority True on the peer that may write this object's synchronised variables. public ConditionBlock HasAuthority { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Update(If(Net.HasAuthority).Then(Health.Add(-1.0))); Remarks Owner under distributed authority, server under client-server; false while there is no session, and false on every peer for an object that was never bound to a networked object. This is the guard a write to a synchronised variable belongs behind: without it the write is refused on every peer but one, with the message ScriptInstance raises. IsConnected True while a session is connected, as host or as client. public ConditionBlock IsConnected { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Update(If(!Net.IsConnected).Then(Status.Set("offline"))); Remarks Connecting is not connected, and neither is disconnected. The three are separate states because a script that shows "connecting" and one that shows "offline" are showing a player different things; AGENTS.md rule 45. IsHost True on the peer that is hosting the session. public ConditionBlock IsHost { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Update(If(Net.IsHost).Then(Role.Set("host"))); Remarks Exposed rather than hidden because hiding it is what produces a script that works for whoever is hosting while they test it. It is not the same question as HasAuthority, which is asked per object. PeerCount How many peers are in the session, including this one. Zero while offline. public NumberValueBlock PeerCount { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.Update(If(Net.PeerCount > 1.0).Then(Crowded.Set(true))); RoundTripMilliseconds Round trip time to the host in milliseconds. Zero on the host and while offline. public NumberValueBlock RoundTripMilliseconds { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.Update(If(Net.RoundTripMilliseconds > 200.0).Then(ShowLagWarning.Set(true))); Remarks Latency is a state, not an exception; AGENTS.md rule 45. A script may show it, may refuse to start a timed action above a threshold, and may do neither. Send Where a message to the authority is written. public NetSendFactory Send { get; } Property Value NetSendFactory Examples On.Update(If(!Net.HasAuthority).Then(Net.Send.ToAuthority(RequestReady))); Methods SecondsSinceUpdate(Flag, string, int) How many seconds ago a synchronised flag last arrived from its authority. public NumberValueBlock SecondsSinceUpdate(Flag variable, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Flag variable A synchronised flag variable. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns NumberValueBlock A number expression. Examples On.Update(If(Net.SecondsSinceUpdate(Ready) > 1).Then(Fade.Set(true))); SecondsSinceUpdate(Number, string, int) How many seconds ago a synchronised number last arrived from its authority. public NumberValueBlock SecondsSinceUpdate(Number variable, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Number variable A synchronised number variable. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns NumberValueBlock A number expression. Examples On.Update(If(Net.SecondsSinceUpdate(Health) > 1).Then(Fade.Set(true))); SecondsSinceUpdate(Text, string, int) How many seconds ago a synchronised text variable last arrived from its authority. public NumberValueBlock SecondsSinceUpdate(Text variable, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Text variable A synchronised text variable. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns NumberValueBlock A number expression. Examples On.Update(If(Net.SecondsSinceUpdate(Name) > 1).Then(Fade.Set(true))); SecondsSinceUpdate(TransformChannel, string, int) How many seconds since a value for one transform channel arrived from the authority. Zero on the authority itself, whose transform is the one being sent. public NumberValueBlock SecondsSinceUpdate(TransformChannel channel, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description TransformChannel channel The channel to ask about, which this script must synchronise. string callerFilePath Filled in by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Filled in by the compiler. Returns NumberValueBlock A value block reading the age in seconds. Examples If(Net.SecondsSinceUpdate(TransformChannel.Position) > 0.5).Then(Ghosted.Set(true)) Remarks Latency is a state a script reads rather than an exception it handles; AGENTS.md rule 45. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This script does not synchronise that channel, so nothing ever arrives for it and there is no age to report. SecondsSinceUpdate<T>(Var<T>, string, int) How many seconds ago this peer last received a value for one synchronised variable. Zero on the peer with authority, whose own value is never behind. public NumberValueBlock SecondsSinceUpdate<T>(Var<T> variable, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) where T : struct Parameters Type Name Description Var<T> variable The synchronised variable to ask about. It has to have been declared with Var.DefineSynced or Var.DefineSyncedText in this same script. string callerFilePath Filled in by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Filled in by the compiler. Returns NumberValueBlock A number expression, in seconds. Type Parameters T Number, Flag or Text. Examples On.Update(If(Net.SecondsSinceUpdate(Health) > 1.0).Then(FadeHealthBar.Set(true))); Remarks This is the per-variable half of rule 45's "latency is a state". A rate-capped variable is stale between sends by design and a SyncCadence.Once variable is stale from the moment after it arrives; both are correct, and this is how a script can say by how much rather than assume. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The variable is not one this script synchronises, so there is no arrival for it to be counting from.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetSendFa.title: Struct NetSendFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetSendFa.summary: Struct NetSendFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Net.Send: the one way a peer without authority asks the authority to do something. public readonly struct NetSendFactory Expand Details ... Examples Net.Send.ToAuthority(RequestReady) Remarks There is no "send to everyone" and no "send to one peer" in this milestone. A message goes to the authority over the object it was sent from, because that is the peer allowed to change the object's state, and state reaches the other peers as a synchronised variable rather than as a second message. That keeps one direction of travel: a request goes up to the authority, and state comes back down through the cadences. Methods ToAuthority(Message, string, int) Builds a block that sends one of this script's declared messages to the peer with authority over this object. The message carries its identity and no payload. public Block ToAuthority(Message message, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Message message A message this script declared with Define.Message(). string callerFilePath Filled in by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Filled in by the compiler. Returns Block The block. Examples RequestReady = Define.Message(); On.Update(If(!Net.HasAuthority).Then(Net.Send.ToAuthority(RequestReady))); Remarks Sending while offline does nothing: there is no authority to send to, and that is a state rather than a mistake. Sending on the peer that already has authority delivers the message to itself, so a script does not need two paths for "ask" and "do". Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The message was never declared, has no name yet, or is another script's. A message that no On.Message in this script receives is refused too, at the end of Build() rather than here, because the receive may be written below the send.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode.L.title: Class LunyScriptNetworkBehaviour | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode.L.summary: Class LunyScriptNetworkBehaviour Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode Assembly ApiSource.dll Binds the script instance on this object to the object's network identity, so that its synchronised variables and its messages reach the same object on every peer. [RequireComponent(typeof(LunyScriptBehaviour))] [AddComponentMenu("LunyScript/LunyScript Network Behaviour")] public sealed class LunyScriptNetworkBehaviour : NetworkBehaviour Expand Details ... Inheritance object Object Component Behaviour MonoBehaviour NetworkBehaviour LunyScriptNetworkBehaviour Examples // On a networked object, alongside NetworkObject and LunyScriptBehaviour. gameObject.AddComponent<LunyScriptNetworkBehaviour>(); Remarks This is the whole bridge between Netcode for GameObjects and the LunyScript core. It translates one fact, the network object id, and does nothing else: no state is copied here, no value is serialised here, and the core is told nothing about NGO. AGENTS.md rule 49. The object needs a NetworkObject, a LunyScriptBehaviour that has already been given a script, and this component. The order that matters is that the script is named before LunyScriptBehaviour.Awake runs, which is what spawns the instance. The demo prefab carries its assignment in Script To Run. Despawn unbinds. An id that outlived its object would make an arriving message reach an instance that is no longer the object it names, so the binding ends where the spawn ends rather than where the GameObject is destroyed. Properties LunyScriptObjectId The LunyScript network object id this component binds its instance to. public int LunyScriptObjectId { get; } Property Value int Remarks NGO-ASSUMPTION: NetworkObjectId is a UInt64 that NGO assigns from a counter starting at 1 and increasing, so the value fits an Int32 for any session this product can produce. The narrowing is stated here rather than hidden; a session that spawned more than two billion objects would need INetworkProvider's object id to widen, and the MaxObjectId check below is what would report that rather than silently binding to a wrong id. Methods OnNetworkDespawn() public override void OnNetworkDespawn() OnNetworkSpawn() public override void OnNetworkSpawn()

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode.N.title: Class NgoNetworkProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode.N.summary: Class NgoNetworkProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode Assembly ApiSource.dll The Netcode for GameObjects backend for INetworkProvider: starts and ends a session on NetworkManager, answers the connection facts a script may read, and carries LunyScript's messages and synchronised variables over one named message channel. public sealed class NgoNetworkProvider : INetworkProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object NgoNetworkProvider Implements INetworkProvider Examples runner.NetworkGateway.UseProvider(new NgoNetworkProvider()); runner.NetworkGateway.StartHost(); Remarks This is the only type in the product that references Netcode for GameObjects, and every load-bearing line below carries an NGO-ASSUMPTION comment saying which fact about that package it depends on. AGENTS.md rule 49. The core references neither this assembly nor that package, so replacing the netcode stack is writing a sibling of this file rather than editing everything. One named message channel, not one NetworkVariable per variable and not one RPC per message. Every LunyScript message and every synchronised variable travels as a payload on the channel named ChannelName, tagged with what it is. That is what lets the core decide the cadence and lets this file stay a transport. It is also the shape the transform stream needs, which AGENTS.md rule 47 requires to be one stream per authority per tick rather than one message per object; this milestone does not build that stream, and rule 47's bandwidth benchmark is still owed with it. Topology. HasAuthority(int) reads NetworkObject.HasAuthority, which NGO defines for both topologies, so a script written against Net.HasAuthority is already correct under either; AGENTS.md rule 44. What this milestone assumes is narrower and is stated at each send: the peer with authority is the server, which is the client-server case NGO runs by default. Routing a message to a client that holds authority under distributed authority is the next step and is marked where it belongs. Fields ChannelName The named message channel every LunyScript payload travels on. public const string ChannelName = "LunyScript" Field Value string DefaultPort The port used when an address carries none. public const ushort DefaultPort = 7777 Field Value ushort Properties IsHost True when this peer is the host. False for a client and for no session at all. Exposed because rule 45 forbids hiding it, and because "works as host, breaks as client" is the defect that hiding it produces. public bool IsHost { get; } Property Value bool MaximumTransformStreamBytes How many payload bytes of transform stream this backend can carry in one send. The runner splits a tick's stream into as many sends as it needs to stay inside it. public int MaximumTransformStreamBytes { get; } Property Value int Remarks A transport carries a bounded message. One stream per authority per tick is what AGENTS.md rule 47 requires and it stays true here: the tick still produces one stream, and this is how many bytes of it fit in one message. A hundred objects sending all three channels is about 1800 bytes, which is past what Netcode for GameObjects carries unfragmented, so this is not a limit only an unusual session meets. Splitting rather than asking the backend to fragment is deliberate. Each piece carries the stream's own 3-byte header and is decoded on its own, so a piece costs about 3 bytes plus whatever the backend's own per-message header is; a fragmented message costs the backend's fragment headers and its reassembly state instead, and leaves the stream depending on a feature that differs between backends. PeerCount How many peers are in the session, including this one. Zero when offline. public int PeerCount { get; } Property Value int RoundTripMilliseconds Round trip time to the host in milliseconds, or 0 when offline or when this peer is the host. Latency is a state a script may read, not an error; AGENTS.md rule 45. public double RoundTripMilliseconds { get; } Property Value double State What the session is doing right now. Never throws and is meaningful before any session has been started. public SessionState State { get; } Property Value SessionState TransformStreamBytesSent How many payload bytes those streams carried, before Netcode for GameObjects adds its own message and batch framing around them. public long TransformStreamBytesSent { get; } Property Value long TransformStreamsSent How many transform streams this peer has sent since the session started. The counterpart of FakeNetworkProvider's, and what the bandwidth measurement divides the transport's byte count by. public int TransformStreamsSent { get; } Property Value int Methods Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines, so a reader of the Console can tell a real session from the in-process one. Allocates; called only at state transitions, never per tick. public string Describe() Returns string For example: "Netcode for GameObjects, host on port 7777", or "in-process provider, 2 peers". EndSession() Ends the session and returns to Offline. Called again on an already-offline provider, it does nothing, so that a restart is EndSession then StartHost without the caller tracking state. public void EndSession() HasAuthority(int) Whether this peer may write the state of one object. public bool HasAuthority(int objectId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The networked object, as the gateway numbers it. Returns bool True when this peer owns the object under distributed authority, or is the server under client-server. False when offline, because an offline peer has no authority to speak of and a script that guards on authority then does nothing rather than misbehaving. SendToAuthority(int, int) Sends one message to whichever peer holds authority over the object. The message has a name and no payload in this milestone. public void SendToAuthority(int objectId, int messageId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the message is about. int messageId The message, interned by the gateway so no string crosses this call. SendTransformStream(byte[], int) Sends one authority's whole transform stream for one network tick. public void SendTransformStream(byte[] payload, int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The buffer the runner encoded the stream into. The provider must copy what it needs before returning, because the runner reuses this buffer next tick. int length How many bytes of it the stream occupies. Remarks One call per authority per tick, carrying every object that authority has something to send for, rather than one call per object. AGENTS.md rule 47 requires that shape, because one message per object per tick spends about as many bytes on framing as a half-precision position costs. SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) Sends one variable's value to every other peer. Called only by the authority, and only when the variable's cadence says to send. public void SendVariable(int objectId, int variableIndex, in NetworkValue value) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the variable belongs to. int variableIndex Which synchronised variable, numbered by the order the script declared it in. See VariableIndex for why this is not a slot index. NetworkValue value The value to send. StartClient(string) Joins a session. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running. public void StartClient(string address) Parameters Type Name Description string address Where to connect. An implementation that needs no address ignores it. StartHost() Starts hosting. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running, so an implementation may assume it is offline. public void StartHost() TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage) Takes one received message off the queue, if there is one. The gateway drains this until it returns false, once per tick. public bool TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage message) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkMessage message The message, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks A TryDequeue rather than a returned collection, because the gateway drains it every tick and a returned collection would allocate every tick; AGENTS.md rule 29. TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int) Takes one "a peer joined" notification off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). public bool TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int peerId) Parameters Type Name Description int peerId The peer that joined, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks This is what makes SyncCadence.Once work for a peer that was not there when the value was first set. Without it, a name chosen by the host before anyone joined would never be sent, because Once sends once and a late joiner missed it. The authority answers a join by marking every synchronised variable unsent, so the next tick sends the current value of all of them. The resend goes to every peer, not only to the one that joined. This milestone has no per-peer addressing: SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) is a broadcast. The cost is one redundant copy of each synchronised variable per peer per join, which is bounded by the number of joins rather than by the frame rate. Per-peer addressing is part of the transform stream milestone, where rule 47's bandwidth budget makes it load-bearing. TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[], out int, out int) The next transform stream that arrived, as a view into a buffer the provider owns. The view is valid until the next stream arrives. public bool TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[] payload, out int offset, out int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The provider's buffer. int offset Where the stream starts in it. int length How many bytes it occupies. Returns bool False when none is waiting. Remarks A view rather than an array, because a peer that is not the authority receives a stream on every tick and returning a fresh array would allocate on every one of them. TransformStreamInbox is the implementation both providers use. TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate) Takes one received variable update off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). public bool TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate update) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkVariableUpdate update The update, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetworkGa.title: Class NetworkGateway | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetworkGa.summary: Class NetworkGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The core's one entry point to netcode. Owns the INetworkProvider, refuses the session calls that are a user mistake, and drains the provider's two queues once per tick. AGENTS.md rules 44 to 49. public sealed class NetworkGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object NetworkGateway Examples runner.NetworkGateway.UseProvider(new FakeNetworkProvider()); runner.NetworkGateway.StartHost(); Remarks This is the netcode counterpart of CloudSaveGateway and is deliberately the same shape, because rule 49 poses the same problem rule 52 already solved: the core may not reference the backend, so the core owns an interface and a separate assembly implements it. This type is one of exactly six places the zero-allocation rule relaxes, named as "the services and network gateway" in AGENTS.md rule 31. What that rule permits is narrow: a request may allocate below a stated ceiling, and a pending request must allocate zero per tick. Tick is on the per-frame path and allocates nothing, which is why both queues are drained with TryDequeue rather than by iterating a returned collection. No session method throws because the network is unavailable. They throw only for a user mistake, which is starting a session while one is running. Being offline is a state a script reads through Net.IsConnected; rule 45. Fields DefaultMaximumTransformStreamBytes What a gateway with no provider reports. Chosen to be smaller than what any ordinary transport carries, so that a test running without one still exercises the split. public const int DefaultMaximumTransformStreamBytes = 1024 Field Value int DefaultTicksPerSecond The tick rate a gateway starts with: 30 a second, which is the rate the replaced NetworkTransform runs at. public const double DefaultTicksPerSecond = 30 Field Value double SmallestUsefulTransformStreamBytes The smallest budget that can carry one object: the stream's header and the largest an object's entry can be. public const int SmallestUsefulTransformStreamBytes = 31 Field Value int Properties HasProvider Whether a provider has been set. False means every session call is refused and every state reads as offline. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool IsConnected True when connected as host or client. False with no provider. public bool IsConnected { get; } Property Value bool IsHost True when this peer is the host. False with no provider. public bool IsHost { get; } Property Value bool MaximumTransformStreamBytes How many payload bytes of transform stream one send may carry. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberFun.summary: Enum NumberFunction Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which function a CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberFunctionBlock evaluates, and which write a NumberMutateBlock applies to its slot. public enum NumberFunction Expand Details ... Fields Abs = 0 The magnitude of the first operand, with no sign. Add = 10 The first operand plus the second. Ceiling = 2 The smallest whole number that is not less than the first operand. Clamp = 7 The first operand held between the second and the third. Divide = 13 The first operand divided by the second. Floor = 1 The largest whole number that is not greater than the first operand. Lerp = 8 The first operand moved towards the second by the fraction the third names, with no limit on that fraction. Max = 6 The larger of the first two operands. Min = 5 The smaller of the first two operands. Multiply = 12 The first operand times the second. Remainder = 9 What is left of the first operand after taking out whole multiples of the second. Round = 4 The whole number nearest the first operand, resolving a midpoint by the block's RoundingMode. Subtract = 11 The first operand minus the second. Truncate = 3 The first operand with its fractional part dropped, towards zero. Examples var block = new NumberFunctionBlock(NumberFunction.Abs, value, null, null, RoundingMode.ToEven); Remarks One enum serves both shapes deliberately: every function in the API semantics board's C01 answer has two documented forms, an expression that computes a value and a write that stores the result back into the variable it read, and both forms must mean the same thing. NumberMath is where each one is computed, once. The four arithmetic entries are here as well as on ArithmeticOperator, and the two tables are not redundant. ArithmeticOperator is what the C# operators + - * / % build, where both operands are written at the call site; this table is what a write applies to the variable's own value, where the first operand is the slot and is never written down. Health.Subtract(1.0) and Health.Set(Health - 1.0) reach the same arithmetic through the two tables.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ObjectBin.summary: Struct ObjectBinding Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A handle to one object in a scene that a script binds to: the target Object.For, Camera.For, Audio.For, Particles.For, Panel.For, Navigation.For and a landmark take. Returned by Bind.Object() at build time. public readonly struct ObjectBinding Expand Details ... Examples Witch = Bind.Object(); Guard = Bind.Object().WithTag("Enemy").Named("Guard").LiveRebind(); On.Ready(If(Witch.IsValid).Then(Object.For(Witch).Show())); Remarks Each object running the script resolves the binding for itself when it spawns, in this order: the object its Inspector assigns, then the first object in the spawning object's own scene, inactive objects included, whose name is the declared name. WithTag and Named replace the name search with their own conditions, which must all hold. When nothing is found, the binding is unavailable, and no object is created in its place. An unavailable binding is an ordinary state. IsValid reads it, a write through it does nothing, and a read through it gives that read's documented default. Nothing is logged for it. Two objects that both match a search, and an assigned object that no longer exists, are reported once per incarnation of the object running the script. A bound object ends when it is destroyed or despawned, and the binding is unavailable from then on. LiveRebind() searches again before the script's next update; MustExist() refuses to start the script when the first resolution finds nothing. The two are exclusive. Binding an object grants no lifetime ownership of it. A handle is valid only inside the Build that declared it, for the reason Var<T> states: it carries a slot index and nothing that identifies its program. Properties IsDeclared False for a handle Build() never declared, or one still waiting for its name. public bool IsDeclared { get; } Property Value bool IsValid True while this object's binding holds an object that exists and has not been despawned. public ConditionBlock IsValid { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Ready(If(Witch.IsValid).Then(Object.For(Witch).Show())); Remarks A binding that found nothing, and one whose object ended, answer false. The answer changes only between updates: a LiveRebind() binding searches again before the script's next update, and every block in one update sees the same answer. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(), or on a handle another script declared or Build() never assigned. Name The name the script declared, which is what an Inspector assignment is matched against and, without a filter, the name the scene search looks for. Null until the declaration has its name. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods ToString() The declared name, for a log line or a failure message. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "Witch : object". Returns ObjectBinding The handle. The generated property of the line then gives it the member's name. public static implicit operator ObjectBinding(ObjectBindingBuilder declaration) Parameters Type Name Description ObjectBindingBuilder declaration The chain. Returns ObjectBinding The handle. Examples Witch = Bind.Object(); implicit operator ObjectBinding(RequiredObjectBindingBuilder) Declares the binding a Bind.Object().MustExist() chain describes. public static implicit operator ObjectBinding(RequiredObjectBindingBuilder declaration) Parameters Type Name Description RequiredObjectBindingBuilder declaration The chain. Returns ObjectBinding The handle. Examples Door = Bind.Object().MustExist();
