reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ObjectLif.title: Struct ObjectLifetimeFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ObjectLif.summary: Struct ObjectLifetimeFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Object surface inside Build(): builds the blocks that create, spawn, activate, deactivate and end objects this script owns, and the blocks that hide, show and tint an object and write its material Number properties. public readonly struct ObjectLifetimeFactory Expand Details ... Examples Shield = Define.Object(); On.Ready(Object.Create(Shield)); On.Disabled(Object.Deactivate(Shield)); On.Update(If(Health <= 0.0).Then(Object.Destroy())); Remarks The type is not called ObjectFactory, because UnityEditor.ObjectFactory already exists and this project's editor assembly uses it; two types of that name in scope make the editor assembly fail to compile. The script-facing surface is still written Object, which is what the settled contract-object-lifecycle answer names, and the type name is never written in a script. Self by omission. Omitting the target acts on the object the script runs on. Passing a declared OwnedObject acts on the object this same script produced into it. Two verbs make an object and two end one, in pairs. Create makes a fresh object - an empty one into a declared owned object, or a copy of a prefab - and Destroy(OwnedObject, string, int) ends it for good. Spawn(Pool, string, int) checks a reusable object out of a declared pool, and Despawn(OwnedObject, string, int) returns it. Destroy(OwnedObject, string, int) also ends a pooled object, which takes it out of its pool. Every produced object is owned by the instance that produced it unless its chain wrote SurvivesCaller(), and all of them fill the same declared owned objects, so one owned object is produced by one call and addressed by the rest of this surface. The visual members - Hide, Show, IsVisible, SetColor, ResetColor, MaterialNumber and For - change how the object is drawn and leave it running. They write through the renderer's property block, so no material asset changes. docs/proposals/visual-presentation.md is their contract. The blocks reach the object through IScriptObjectLifetime, never through a UnityEngine.GameObject; AGENTS.md rule 24. A host that does not implement that interface cannot run a script containing these blocks, and the spawn is refused rather than the block failing later. Fields SpawnFromAcquisitionMigration The compile error a call to the removed Object.Spawn(acquisition) produces. public const string SpawnFromAcquisitionMigration = "LunyScript: Object.Spawn takes a pool now. For a fresh copy of the loaded prefab write Object.Create(acquisition) with the same chain." Field Value string SpawnFromPrefabMigration The compile error a call to the removed Object.Spawn(prefab) produces. public const string SpawnFromPrefabMigration = "LunyScript: Object.Spawn takes a pool now. For a fresh copy of the prefab write Object.Create(prefab) with the same chain; to reuse copies, declare Guards = Define.Pool(nameof(Guards)).From(prefab) in Build() and write Object.Spawn(Guards)." Field Value string Properties IsVisible Whether the object this script runs on is drawn: true while its Renderer is enabled, which is the state Hide(string, int) and Show(string, int) write. False when the object has no renderer. public ConditionBlock IsVisible { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Update(If(Object.IsVisible).Then(Seen.Set(true))); Remarks Unity's Renderer.isVisible, whether any camera sees the renderer, is a different reading. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This factory was not obtained inside Build(). Methods Activate(OwnedObject, string, int) Builds a block that activates an object this script owns. public Block Activate(OwnedObject target, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description OwnedObject target The owned object Define.Object() declared. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Enabled(Object.Activate(Shield)); Remarks It acts on the object the owned object holds, and takes effect where it is written, because an owned object runs no LunyScript and raises no observation. An owned object whose slot is empty is left alone. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException target is not an owned object this script declared. An owned object nothing in this script produces is refused when Build() finishes. Activate(string, int) Builds a block that activates the object this script runs on. public Block Activate(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one: it is what records the line of the script this block was written on. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Message(Wake, Object.Activate()); Remarks The block records a LifetimeRequest, and the runner applies it after the current dispatch, which is what delivers On.Enabled between event invocations rather than inside one. Activating an already-active object delivers nothing. Activate(OwnedObject, string, int) activates an object this script owns. Create(Operation<Prefab>, string, int) Starts a fresh copy of a succeeded prefab acquisition. The payload is readable after When.Operation(handle).Succeeded only. A create before Succeeded is refused at run. public CreateBuilder Create(Operation<Prefab> acquisition, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Operation<Prefab> acquisition The typed handle a successful Asset.Load bound. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Examples On.Authority.Gained(isReady.Set(false)); On.Authority.Lost(chargeLevel.Set(0.0)); Remarks Authority is never hidden, and these are how a script reacts to it changing rather than polling for it. AGENTS.md rule 45. The runner raises them when the answer it refreshes at the top of each tick differs from the previous tick's, so an object that is spawned with authority gets Gained(params Block[]) on its first networked tick, and one whose session ends gets Lost(params Block[]). Nothing in this milestone transfers authority at run time. These events exist so that a script written now is written against the change rather than against a value that happens not to move yet; the API that requests a transfer is a later proposal. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.OnFactory.summary: Struct OnFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The On surface inside Build(): registers blocks against the events the runner raises. public readonly struct OnFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(health.Set(100.0)); On.Update(If(health > 0.0).Then(health.Add(-1.0))); Remarks The params array is a build-time allocation and is inside the boundary the allocation rule permits; AGENTS.md rule 33 forbids params on the run-time path, which this is not. No event registration here captures the authored line, and that is a language limit rather than an oversight. C# allows no parameter after a params array, so [CallerFilePath] cannot be added without taking the params sugar away from every call site. The blocks passed in carry their own locations, because the factories that built them are not params methods; see SourceLocation. Properties Application The five application observations: pause, resume, focus and quit. public OnApplicationFactory Application { get; } Property Value OnApplicationFactory Examples On.Application.Paused(Armed.Set(false)); Authority The two authority events: gaining authority over this object, and losing it. public OnAuthorityFactory Authority { get; } Property Value OnAuthorityFactory Examples On.Authority.Gained(isReady.Set(false)); Methods CollisionEnter(params Block[]) Registers blocks that run when this object's collider begins touching another collider. public void CollisionEnter(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. Examples On.CollisionEnter(Score.Add(1.0)); Remarks Unity raises OnCollisionEnter on the object the script is on, so this is On. rather than When.. A script that does not call this, or CollisionStay(params Block[]), CollisionExit(params Block[]), TriggerEnter(params Block[]), TriggerStay(params Block[]) or TriggerExit(params Block[]), is not subscribed to physics callbacks at all. The blocks run against this object. Other is the other collider, the same surface on all six contact events. Unity still allocates the Collision argument it passes into its own callback; LunyScript copies primitives from the other collider and does not store that argument. A Pausable script that Time.Pause() has stopped still runs these blocks, the way Unity sends a collision to a MonoBehaviour that is not updating, so On.CollisionEnter(Time.Resume()) can resume the game. The project setting "Time.Pause pauses contact events" in Edit, Project Settings, LunyScript makes a pause skip them on a Pausable script, as it skips On.Update. A script whose component is disabled runs none of the six. Time.Pause() also stops Unity's fixed step, so a paused game meets a contact only when it steps physics itself. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException blocks is null or contains null. CollisionExit(params Block[]) Registers blocks that run when this object's collider stops touching another collider. public void CollisionExit(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. Examples On.CollisionExit(Touching.Set(false)); Remarks Unity raises OnCollisionExit on the object the script is on. The blocks run against this object; Other is the other collider. See CollisionEnter(params Block[]). Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException blocks is null or contains null. CollisionStay(params Block[]) Registers blocks that run every fixed step while this object's collider is touching another collider. public void CollisionStay(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. Examples On.CollisionStay(Push.Set(Other.WorldPosition)); Remarks Unity raises OnCollisionStay on the object the script is on. The blocks run against this object; Other is the other collider. See CollisionEnter(params Block[]). Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException blocks is null or contains null. Created(params Block[]) Registers blocks that run once, at the first managed binding to a native host. public void Created(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. Examples On.Created(Armed.Set(true)); Remarks Delivered after declared inputs are resolved and before Ready(params Block[]). A pooled respawn onto the same host does not raise it again; a bind to a different host does. It does not promise Unity's Awake timing: a host that is already in the scene still gets it on first bind. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException blocks is null or contains null. Despawned(params Block[]) Registers blocks that run once when the incarnation ends, while the instance and its object are still valid. public void Despawned(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. Examples On.Despawned(Object.Destroy(Shield)); Remarks This is the bounded cleanup the settled contract-dispatch-order answer asks for before the incarnation is invalidated: the instance is still in the runner's live list, its host is still alive, and the objects it created still exist, so these blocks can act on all three. The objects it created are destroyed after they have run. It is not delivered for an instance the scene-unload sweep collects, because that sweep exists for a host that went away without telling LunyScript and these blocks would run against a destroyed object; docs/host-transform-cache.md. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException blocks is null or contains null. Disabled(params Block[]) Registers blocks that run when the instance becomes disabled, having been enabled. public void Disabled(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. Examples On.Disabled(Armed.Set(false)); Remarks Delivered once per transition. An authored Object.Deactivate() produces it, an authored Object.Destroy() or Object.Despawn() produces it before Despawned(params Block[]), and so does Unity's own OnDisable on a managed object. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException blocks is null or contains null. Enabled(params Block[]) Registers blocks that run when the instance becomes enabled, having been disabled. public void Enabled(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. Examples On.Enabled(Armed.Set(true)); Remarks Delivered once per transition: enabling an already-enabled instance delivers nothing. An authored Object.Activate() produces it, and so does Unity's own OnEnable on a managed object, through LunyScriptBehaviour - including the first activation, which is where Unity delivers OnEnable for the first time. It therefore runs before On.Ready on a managed object, the way OnEnable runs before Start. A bare ScriptRunner.Spawn, which a test uses and a managed object does not, delivers none: it writes the enabled state rather than changing it. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException blocks is null or contains null. Event(Event, string, int) Starts a listener for an event: this script's own, or another script's generated descriptor such as DoorScript.Events.Opened. Do names the blocks; From restricts the listener to one sender first. public EventHandlerBuilder Event(Event @event, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Event event The event. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns EventHandlerBuilder The builder whose Do or From finishes the listener. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Operation.title: Enum OperationFailure | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Operation.summary: Enum OperationFailure Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Every failure an operation can produce, classified once by the gateway so that no script and no block ever sees an exception type. See AGENTS.md section 12, rule 51. public enum OperationFailure Expand Details ... Fields CapacityExhausted = 11 An object pool at its hard cap refused a spawn: every entry was in use or still returning. No entry was taken back from another use and no object was created outside the pool; the spawn produced nothing. Denied = 4 The service understood the call and refused it. Not retried. None = 0 No failure. The value while a request is pending and after it succeeded. NotFound = 5 The key or resource does not exist. Not retried. NotSignedIn = 2 The player is not signed in. The request is queued until sign-in completes. Offline = 1 No usable network connection. The request is queued and replayed. RateLimited = 3 The service refused the call because too many were made. Carries a retry delay. Timeout = 6 No answer within the gateway's own deadline. Unknown = 7 A failure the gateway could not classify. Logged with the original text. Unreachable = 10 No route reaches a navigation destination: the route is invalid, or it is partial and the move required a complete one. The actor stopped where it was. Unreadable = 8 A stored document exists and is not a readable document: not UTF-8, not JSON, or not in the document layout. Nothing was applied and the stored copy was not changed. Unsupported = 9 A stored document is readable and cannot become the declared version: it is newer, no migration step starts from its version, a step rejected it, or the migrated result failed validation. Nothing was applied and the stored copy was not changed. Examples On.Update(If(Loading.FailedAs(OperationFailure.NotFound)).Then(Missing.Set(true))); Remarks It is in the script namespace so a script names it without a using line: If(Loading.FailedAs(OperationFailure.NotFound)). IAsyncOperation reports one of these values.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform..summary: Interface IAsyncOperation Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform Assembly ApiSource.dll One in-flight request owned by the services gateway. Script code never sees this type; it sees a status variable and an outcome event. This interface exists so that the gateway has exactly one place that knows how asynchronous work is represented. public interface IAsyncOperation Expand Details ... Remarks .NET 10 seam. The implementation today wraps System.Threading.Tasks.Task, which is what every Unity Gaming Services API returns. The .NET 10 counterparts are System.Threading.Tasks.ValueTask (no allocation for a synchronously completed call), System.Collections.Generic.IAsyncEnumerable for streamed results, and TimeProvider-based timeouts instead of Task.Delay. Replacing: Task, Task<T>, TaskCompletionSource, Task.Delay, async void handlers. Nothing in this codebase awaits on the main thread; the gateway polls IsComplete once per frame. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform..summary: Interface IGameClock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform Assembly ApiSource.dll A clock that drives a running game, so it carries the game's time scale and can be paused as well as read. Time.Scale, Time.IsPaused, Time.SetScale, Time.Pause and Time.Resume reach the clock through this interface. public interface IGameClock : ITimeSource Expand Details ... Inherited Members ITimeSource.DeltaSeconds ITimeSource.ElapsedSeconds ITimeSource.UnscaledDeltaSeconds ITimeSource.UnscaledElapsedSeconds Examples var clock = (IGameClock)runner.TimeSource; clock.Pause(); Remarks Why this is separate from ITimeSource. Every clock can report how much time passed; only a clock that governs a game's speed can be asked to change it. The editor session's clock reports elapsed edit-time seconds and governs no game, so it implements ITimeSource alone and a script that pauses the game cannot run on an editor runner. UnityTimeSource and TestKit.ManualTimeSource implement this one. This clock's pause is a time scale of zero, and resume restores the last positive scale this clock was set to. Time.IsPaused reads the runner flag, not this property: Time.Pause sets the flag and calls Pause(), and Time.SetScale(0) calls SetScale(double) without setting the flag. A scale set outside this clock - Unity's own Time.timeScale written by other code - changes what Scale reports and does not change what Resume() restores, because this clock did not set it. .NET 10 seam. ITimeSource's row in AGENTS.md section 4 is unchanged by this interface: System.TimeProvider replaces the reading half, and the scale and the pause stay the engine's, because no BCL type carries a game time scale. Resuming a clock that is not paused changes nothing. void Resume() SetScale(double) Sets the time scale. A positive value is also what Resume() will restore afterwards. void SetScale(double scale) Parameters Type Name Description double scale The new scale. Zero pauses; a negative or non-finite value is refused. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The scale is negative, NaN or infinite.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform..summary: Interface ITimeSource Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform Assembly ApiSource.dll The only place LunyScript reads the passage of time. Blocks and the runner take an ITimeSource instead of calling UnityEngine.Time or System.DateTime.UtcNow directly. public interface ITimeSource Expand Details ... Remarks .NET 10 seam. The counterpart is System.TimeProvider, which does not exist in .NET Standard 2.1 and therefore cannot be used while Unity 6.7's Mono and IL2CPP backends are targets. When the product drops pre-Unity 7 support, the implementation of this interface becomes a wrapper over a TimeProvider and every caller stays unchanged. Replacing: UnityEngine.Time.deltaTime, UnityEngine.Time.time, System.DateTime.UtcNow, System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch. Four reads, in two pairs. The first pair is the clock a game's own speed is measured on, so a time scale below one slows it and a pause stops it. The second pair is real time, which neither the scale nor a pause changes. A clock that is never scaled, such as the editor session's, answers both pairs with the same numbers, and that is a correct answer rather than a placeholder. IGameClock is what adds the scale and the pause; a clock that only reports time implements this interface alone. A paused game still reports how long its frames take here. double UnscaledDeltaSeconds { get; } Property Value double UnscaledElapsedSeconds Seconds since the run started in real time, which keeps advancing while the game is paused. Implements IRandomSource Examples var first = new XorshiftRandomSource(42); var second = new XorshiftRandomSource(42); var a = first.NextDouble(); var b = second.NextDouble(); Remarks This is the consumer IRandomSource existed without. It does not read UnityEngine.Random, which is a static with hidden global state. It does not use System.Random either: that type's sequence is not the same on Mono, IL2CPP and CoreCLR, so a test that replayed a seed would not replay the draws. Examples [Asset] public Prefab Enemy { get; private set; } public Pool Guards { get; private set; } Guards = Define.Pool(nameof(Guards)).From(Enemy).HardCap(8).Prewarm(4); On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards).Into(Escort)); Remarks The declaration describes storage; Build() creates no object. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Prefab.ht.title: Struct Prefab | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Prefab.ht.summary: Struct Prefab Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A handle to one prefab input of a script. Returned by Bind.Prefab() at build time, or assigned before Build() by [Asset] on the property; what the input holds is an instance read, because the value belongs to the object and not to the script type. public readonly struct Prefab Expand Details ... Examples Sentry = Bind.Prefab(); On.Ready(Object.Create(Sentry).At(new Vector3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)).Into(Guard)); Remarks A prefab input refuses a GameObject that is not a prefab. A scene object assigned to an input a script copies from is a mistake that shows up as a duplicated scene object rather than as a message. A value the host assigned that is not a prefab asset is refused at spawn, and the input then resolves as if nothing had been assigned. A scene object is what ObjectBinding binds. Object.Create and Define.Pool take this type and no other input kind, so passing an AudioClip or an ObjectBinding to them does not compile. The declared name is the input's durable identity: a value stored on a host is matched to an input by that name. A generated property gives the input its member's name, and .As(name) names it explicitly. Renaming it orphans what a scene stored for the old name. A handle is valid only inside the Build that declared it, for the reason Var<T> states: it carries a slot index and nothing that identifies its program. Properties IsDeclared False for a handle Build() never assigned, or one still waiting for its name. public bool IsDeclared { get; } Property Value bool Name The name the script declared, which is what a stored value is matched against and what a diagnostic names. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods ToString() The declared name, for a log line or a failure message. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "Sentry : prefab". Operators implicit operator Prefab(AssetInputBuilder<Prefab>) Declares the prefab input a Bind.Prefab() chain describes. The generated property of the line then gives it the member's name. public static implicit operator Prefab(AssetInputBuilder<Prefab> declaration) Parameters Type Name Description AssetInputBuilder<Prefab> declaration The chain. Returns Prefab The handle. Examples Sentry = Bind.Prefab();

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Process.h.summary: Enum Process Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Whether a script ticks while the runner is paused, and whether it ticks at all. public enum Process Expand Details ... Fields Always = 3 Tick whether the runner is paused or not. Disabled = 4 Do not tick. Lifecycle events still run. The GameObject stays active. Inherit = 0 Walk parents; if none names a mode, Pausable. Pausable = 1 Tick only while the runner is not paused. WhenPaused = 2 Tick only while the runner is paused. Examples SetProcessMode(Process.WhenPaused); Remarks Inherit walks the Unity transform parent chain, skipping GameObjects that have no LunyScriptBehaviour, and becomes Pausable when the walk ends. Pausable ticks only while the runner is not paused. WhenPaused ticks only while it is. Always ticks either way. Disabled never ticks. Lifecycle events still run in every mode. Authored only: SetProcessMode(Process, string, int) in Build() sets the type default, and the Inspector override on LunyScriptBehaviour sets it per instance. There is no runtime verb.

Examples var enemy = EnemyScript.At(Target); When.Var(enemy.Health).Changed(Flash.Set(true)); Remarks The watch follows the target. When the target resolves to a different incarnation than at the previous check, that incarnation's value becomes the baseline and no block runs, so switching targets never looks like a change of value. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ReleaseGa.title: Class ReleaseGate | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ReleaseGa.summary: Class ReleaseGate Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Gate 4. Runs inside a standalone player built without DEBUG and asserts what only that build can show: that operator true and operator false on a condition block still throw, that the [Conditional] contract guards are gone, and that the two guards written out unconditionally are not. public static class ReleaseGate Expand Details ... Inheritance object ReleaseGate Remarks AGENTS.md rule 38 says the two operators throw in release builds as well as debug, and that wrapping them in #if DEBUG is not allowed. Every run the Test Runner can produce defines DEBUG: the Editor does, and Player mode builds a development player. So the rule cannot be checked by a test alone, and this entry point exists instead. The gate is compiled in only when LUNY_RELEASE_GATE is defined, which PlayerBackendSettings.SetReleaseGate does and nothing else does. It quits the player with exit status 0 when every check passed and 1 when any failed, and writes one line per check so the log says which. Its first check is its own premise: it fails when DEBUG turns out to be defined, because a pass under DEBUG would prove nothing about a release build. Two of its checks are a matched pair and neither means much without the other. CodeSmile.LunyScript.ReleaseGate.ContractGuardsAreCompiledOut() passes when a [Conditional] guard does not throw in a build without DEBUG; CodeSmile.LunyScript.ReleaseGate.UnconditionalGuardsStillThrow() passes when the two guards that are deliberately unconditional do throw in that same build. Together they are what makes AGENTS.md rule 71's "a guard may be conditional only where the failure its removal gives up is loud" a measured rule rather than a stated one. Fields LogPrefix Prefix every line this gate logs carries, so a caller can find them in the player log. public const string LogPrefix = "LunyScript release gate | " Field Value string Remarks Tools/run-tests.sh greps the player log for this exact phrase, so it is composed from the one logging surface rather than written out again here; AGENTS.md rule 60. Changing either half changes what gate 4 reports. Methods Run() Runs the checks and returns how many failed. Callable from a test as well, which is what makes the same assertions visible in the Editor and in the development players; only the first check can differ between them, and it is the one the release build exists for. public static int Run() Returns int Number of failed checks. 0 means every check passed. Examples Assert.That(ReleaseGate.Run(), Is.Zero); RunOperatorChecks() Runs only the two operator checks, without the check that DEBUG is absent. A test calls this, because the Editor and every development player define DEBUG and would fail the premise check while the operators themselves behave correctly. public static int RunOperatorChecks() Returns int Number of failed checks. 0 means the implicit bool conversion threw and && constructed an AND node. Examples Assert.That(ReleaseGate.RunOperatorChecks(), Is.Zero);

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ReparentB.title: Struct ReparentBuilder | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ReparentB.summary: Struct ReparentBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What SetParent(...) and Unparent() return: the reparent, which keeps the object's world placement unless KeepLocal() says otherwise. public readonly struct ReparentBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Transform.SetParent(Transform.Root)); On.Ready(Transform.Unparent().KeepLocal()); Remarks The default keeps the object's world position and rotation and writes the closest local scale it can, which is the captain's answer to API-semantics row T06 on 2026-09-13. The scale is the half that can only be approximated: a parent that is rotated and scaled unevenly produces world scales no local scale reproduces, and Unity writes the nearest one. The approximation is not reported anywhere yet. An observation is a value on a finished action's result, and that surface is accepted and not yet built; docs/execution-model.md, "Shared outcomes and concurrent groups". Methods KeepLocal() Finishes the reparent, keeping the object's local position, rotation and scale and letting its world placement move. public Block KeepLocal() Returns Block The finished block. Examples On.Ready(Transform.SetParent(Transform.Root).KeepLocal()); Remarks This is what to pick when the new parent is a socket or a slot and the object should snap to it. Without it the object stays where it is in the scene. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This builder is a default that no SetParent or Unparent call produced. Operators implicit operator Block(ReparentBuilder) Finishes a reparent that said nothing, which leaves the object where it is in the scene. public static implicit operator Block(ReparentBuilder builder) Parameters Type Name Description ReparentBuilder builder The builder to finish. Returns Block The finished block. Examples Block drop = Transform.Unparent(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException builder is a default that no SetParent or Unparent call produced.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Rotation..title: Struct Rotation | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Rotation..summary: Struct Rotation Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll An orientation in three dimensions, held as a unit quaternion. public readonly struct Rotation Expand Details ... Examples var facing = Rotation.Euler(0.0, 90.0, 0.0); var reversed = facing.Inverse; Remarks The four components are readable and none of them is writable. Three of the four are not independent of the fourth: a quaternion that is not of length one is not an orientation, so writing one component alone produces a value that rotates and stretches. The API semantics board ruled on 2026-09-13 that a rotation is changed through its constructors or Compose(Rotation) rather than through its components. An input that names no orientation produces Identity. A quaternion of length zero and one carrying a NaN or an infinity are both refused that way rather than stored, so nothing downstream reads a value that is not a rotation. Euler(double, double, double) takes degrees and applies them in the order Z, then X, then Y, which is the order Unity's own euler-angle rotation uses, so a script that computes an orientation here and one that reads it off a transform agree. Constructors Rotation(double, double, double, double) Builds an orientation from four quaternion components, scaling them to length one. Components that name no orientation - a length of zero, or a NaN or an infinity among them - produce Identity. public Rotation(double x, double y, double z, double w) Parameters Type Name Description double x The first component. double y The second component. double z The third component. double w The fourth component. Examples var upright = new Rotation(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0); Fields Identity The orientation that turns nothing. public static readonly Rotation Identity Field Value Rotation Examples var upright = Rotation.Identity; Properties Inverse The orientation that undoes this one. public Rotation Inverse { get; } Property Value Rotation Examples var undone = facing.Inverse; W The fourth component of the quaternion. public float W { get; } Property Value float Examples var w = facing.W; X The first component of the quaternion. public float X { get; } Property Value float Examples var x = facing.X; Y The second component of the quaternion. public float Y { get; } Property Value float Examples var y = facing.Y; Z The third component of the quaternion. public float Z { get; } Property Value float Examples var z = facing.Z; Methods AngleTo(Rotation) How far apart two orientations are, in degrees, between 0 and 180. public double AngleTo(Rotation other) Parameters Type Name Description Rotation other The orientation to measure to. Returns double The angle in degrees. Examples var offBy = facing.AngleTo(wanted); Remarks An orientation and its four negated components name the same orientation, so the angle between them is zero rather than 360. That is what "antipodal equality" means here, and a tolerance comparison is written a.AngleTo(b) <= tolerance. ApplyTo(Vector3) A spatial value turned by this orientation. The value's length is unchanged. public Vector3 ApplyTo(Vector3 value) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3 value The value to turn. Returns Vector3 The turned value. Examples var worldOffset = facing.ApplyTo(new Vector3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)); Compose(Rotation) This orientation applied after another one. public Rotation Compose(Rotation first) Parameters Type Name Description Rotation first The orientation applied first. Returns Rotation The combined orientation. Examples var combined = yaw.Compose(pitch); Remarks The argument is applied first and this one second, so yaw.Compose(pitch) pitches and then yaws. Equals(Rotation) Whether two values name the same orientation. Four negated components name the same orientation, so they compare equal. public bool Equals(Rotation other) Parameters Type Name Description Rotation other The orientation to compare against. Returns bool True when the components match exactly, or match exactly after negation. Examples var unchanged = facing.Equals(lastFacing); Equals(object) Whether this is an equal orientation of the same type. public override bool Equals(object obj) Parameters Type Name Description object obj What to compare against. Returns bool True when it is a Rotation naming the same orientation. Examples var same = facing.Equals((Object)other); Euler(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock) Builds an orientation expression out of three angle expressions, applied in the order Z, then X, then Y. public static RotationValueBlock Euler(NumberValueBlock xDegrees, NumberValueBlock yDegrees, NumberValueBlock zDegrees) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock xDegrees The angle around the first axis. NumberValueBlock yDegrees The angle around the second axis. NumberValueBlock zDegrees The angle around the third axis. Returns RotationValueBlock An orientation expression. Examples On.Update(Facing.Set(Rotation.Euler(0.0, Heading, 0.0))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Any operand is null. Euler(Vector3) Builds an orientation from three angles in degrees held in one value, applied in the order Z, then X, then Y. public static Rotation Euler(Vector3 degrees) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3 degrees The three angles. Returns Rotation The orientation those three angles name. Examples var facing = Rotation.Euler(new Vector3(0.0, 90.0, 0.0)); Remarks The value's X, Y and Z are the angles around the first, second and third axes: the layout ToEuler() returns, so Rotation.Euler(facing.ToEuler()) names the orientation facing names. Euler(Vector3ValueBlock) Builds an orientation expression out of one spatial expression holding three angles in degrees, applied in the order Z, then X, then Y. public static RotationValueBlock Euler(Vector3ValueBlock degrees) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3ValueBlock degrees The three angles. Returns RotationValueBlock An orientation expression. Examples On.Update(Facing.Set(Rotation.Euler(Heading))); Remarks The same orientation as the three-number form, with the value's X, Y and Z as the three angles. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException degrees is null. Euler(double, double, double) Builds an orientation from three angles in degrees, applied in the order Z, then X, then Y. public static Rotation Euler(double xDegrees, double yDegrees, double zDegrees) Parameters Type Name Description double xDegrees The angle around the first axis. double yDegrees The angle around the second axis. double zDegrees The angle around the third axis. Returns Rotation The orientation those three angles name. Examples var facing = Rotation.Euler(0.0, 90.0, 0.0); GetHashCode() A hash of the orientation, taken from the form whose first non-zero component is positive, so two values that compare equal hash equal. public override int GetHashCode() Returns int The hash. Examples var hash = facing.GetHashCode(); Slerp(Rotation, Rotation, double) An orientation a stated fraction of the way from one to another along the shortest arc. The fraction is not limited, matching scalar Math.Lerp. public static Rotation Slerp(Rotation from, Rotation to, double fraction) Parameters Type Name Description Rotation from Where the fraction 0 sits. Rotation to Where the fraction 1 sits. double fraction How far along to go. Returns Rotation The interpolated orientation. Examples var mid = Rotation.Slerp(from, to, 0.5); ToEuler() The three euler angles in degrees that name this orientation, in the order Unity writes them: Z, then X, then Y. public Vector3 ToEuler() Returns Vector3 X, Y and Z degrees. Examples var degrees = facing.ToEuler(); ToString() The four components, so a log line naming one reads as it was written. public override string ToString() Returns string The components in brackets. Examples var described = facing.ToString();

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.RoundingM.summary: Enum RoundingMode Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll How Math.Round and Number.Round resolve a value exactly halfway between two whole numbers. public enum RoundingMode Expand Details ... Fields AwayFromZero = 1 A midpoint goes away from zero: 0.5 becomes 1 and -0.5 becomes -1. This is what System.MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero does. ToEven = 0 A midpoint goes to the nearer even whole number: 0.5 and 1.5 both become 0 and 2. This is the default, and it is what System.MidpointRounding.ToEven does. Examples On.Ready(Score.Set(Math.Round(2.5))); // 2, midpoint to even On.Ready(Score.Set(Math.Round(2.5, RoundingMode.AwayFromZero))); // 3 Remarks The default is ToEven, which is the rule the API semantics board settled on 2026-09-13: "Round midpoint-to-even unless an explicit mode is supplied". Pass AwayFromZero to get the school rule instead.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.RunnerDia.summary: Class RunnerDiagnostics Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Native diagnostics for one explicitly supplied local runner. Reads execute no authored logic. public sealed class RunnerDiagnostics Expand Details ... Inheritance object RunnerDiagnostics Examples var current = runner.Diagnostics.ReadCurrent(runner.Diagnostics.GetIdentity(instance)); Remarks Caller-owned snapshots allocate only on explicit observation. Current-only Shallow coverage is the default: in the Editor every instance records each block's last outcome, which a snapshot carries in NodeOutcomes. BeginTrace explicitly collects ordered action records; current snapshots do not contain historical values. Preview(DiagnosticNode) computes what a built-in condition that reads only the script's variables says about a snapshot's own copy of them, and runs no script code. In the Editor every instance also records which script, object and block last changed each variable, which a snapshot carries in ValueWrites, and breakpoints set with SubmitBlockBreakpoint(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, bool, int) and SubmitValueBreakpoint(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, bool, int) pause Play Mode. Service work before a runtime provider is ready retains the existing gateway queue contract. Of the commands, only an applied SubmitFireBlock(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, int) runs an authored block. Properties FailedBuildScript Script type associated with the latest failed Build. public string FailedBuildScript { get; } Property Value string Examples var script = runner.Diagnostics.FailedBuildScript; LatestBuildFailure Most recent failed Build, available even though no program or lifetime was created. public DiagnosticFault LatestBuildFailure { get; } Property Value DiagnosticFault Examples var error = runner.Diagnostics.LatestBuildFailure; LatestDriverFailure Latest outer failure. A contained block error appears on its instance snapshot instead. public DiagnosticFault LatestDriverFailure { get; } Property Value DiagnosticFault Examples var error = runner.Diagnostics.LatestDriverFailure; PauseCount How many breakpoint hits have paused the application in this diagnostic session. public long PauseCount { get; } Property Value long Examples var paused = runner.Diagnostics.PauseCount > seen; Methods Apply(DiagnosticCommand) Rechecks admission and applies the command once. A value edit writes backing state without delivering gameplay or editor events; a fire runs its block as described on SubmitFireBlock(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, int). public void Apply(DiagnosticCommand command) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticCommand command Examples diagnostics.Apply(command); BeginTrace(DiagnosticIdentity, DiagnosticBuffer) Starts bounded action capture for a live target at an idle boundary. One attachment per lifetime is permitted. Non-development players require LUNYSCRIPT_TRACE when compiled. public DiagnosticTrace BeginTrace(DiagnosticIdentity target, DiagnosticBuffer buffer) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target DiagnosticBuffer buffer Returns DiagnosticTrace Examples var trace = diagnostics.BeginTrace(target, new DiagnosticBuffer(1024)); GetIdentity(ScriptInstance) Captures the identity before pooling can reuse the instance. public DiagnosticIdentity GetIdentity(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance Returns DiagnosticIdentity Examples var target = runner.Diagnostics.GetIdentity(instance); LiveLifetimes() Copies live lifetimes with their script and object names; discovering them neither builds nor starts scripts. public DiagnosticLifetime[] LiveLifetimes() Returns DiagnosticLifetime[] Examples var targets = runner.Diagnostics.LiveLifetimes(); Remarks Each entry formats its host's description, so this read allocates one string per lifetime. ReadCatalog(ScriptProgram) Returns immutable declarations built with the program, without executing blocks. public DiagnosticCatalog ReadCatalog(ScriptProgram program) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptProgram program Returns DiagnosticCatalog Examples var catalog = runner.Diagnostics.ReadCatalog(program); ReadCurrent(DiagnosticIdentity) Reads coherent stored state at an idle boundary. Busy, ended and failed boundaries report unavailable. public DiagnosticSnapshot ReadCurrent(DiagnosticIdentity target) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target Returns DiagnosticSnapshot Examples var current = runner.Diagnostics.ReadCurrent(target); ReadPauses() Copies the most recent pauses, at most eight, oldest first. public DiagnosticPause[] ReadPauses() Returns DiagnosticPause[] The retained pauses; empty when no breakpoint has hit. Examples var latest = runner.Diagnostics.ReadPauses().LastOrDefault(); Remarks Each copy formats the host descriptions of the lifetimes it names, so this read allocates. Submit(DiagnosticIdentity, int, DiagnosticValue, bool, int) Admits a single typed live edit without applying it. Refusals carry an explicit reason. public DiagnosticCommand Submit(DiagnosticIdentity target, int variable, DiagnosticValue value, bool isLive = true, int major = 1) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target int variable DiagnosticValue value bool isLive int major Returns DiagnosticCommand Examples var command = diagnostics.Submit(target, 0, DiagnosticValue.FromNumber(15.0)); Remarks Admission is synchronous. Up to 64 unapplied receipts can be retained; a full admission queue refuses new work. This is a pending-command bound, not a history retention policy. SubmitBlockBreakpoint(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, bool, int) Admits setting or clearing a breakpoint on one catalog node's block, without setting it yet. Refusals carry an explicit reason. public DiagnosticCommand SubmitBlockBreakpoint(DiagnosticIdentity target, int node, bool enabled, bool isLive = true, int major = 1) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target The lifetime. int node The block's catalog node. bool enabled True sets the breakpoint, false clears it. bool isLive False when the caller's view is paused on history, which refuses the command. int major The caller's protocol major. Returns DiagnosticCommand The receipt, admitted or rejected. Examples diagnostics.Apply(diagnostics.SubmitBlockBreakpoint(target, node.Id, true)); Remarks Once applied, each time the block starts to run in this lifetime the runner records a pause and, when the dispatch it runs in has completed, asks the installed pause to pause the application: in the Editor, Play Mode pauses at the end of that frame, after every script the frame runs. The block and everything after it still run. A breakpoint lasts until it is cleared or the lifetime or the session ends; a pooled respawn starts with none. A block object placed twice breaks in both places, under its OutcomeNode. A condition or a value node has no block and is refused, and so is a runner with no pause installed, which is every runner outside the Editor's debugger. SubmitClearOverride(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, int) Admits returning one forced If to evaluating its condition. A node that is not forced is refused. public DiagnosticCommand SubmitClearOverride(DiagnosticIdentity target, int node, bool isLive = true, int major = 1) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target The lifetime. int node The If's catalog node. bool isLive False when the caller's view is paused on history, which refuses the command. int major The caller's protocol major. Returns DiagnosticCommand The receipt, admitted or rejected. Examples diagnostics.Apply(diagnostics.SubmitClearOverride(target, node.Id)); SubmitFireBlock(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, int) Admits running one catalog node's block once, without running it. Refusals carry an explicit reason. public DiagnosticCommand SubmitFireBlock(DiagnosticIdentity target, int node, bool isLive = true, int major = 1) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target The lifetime. int node The catalog node whose block runs, a Id. bool isLive False when the caller's view is paused on history, which refuses the command. int major The caller's protocol major. Returns DiagnosticCommand The receipt, admitted or rejected. Examples diagnostics.Apply(diagnostics.SubmitFireBlock(target, node.Id)); Remarks Apply(DiagnosticCommand) runs the block at an idle boundary, as a dispatch of its own through the runner's per-action containment, then applies the object lifetime requests it made, records an intervention and, when the block threw, stops the instance as any failed block does. A node whose FireUnavailableReason is not null is refused with that reason. A faulted or disabled instance, a networked instance this peer has no write authority over, and a player built without DEBUG or LUNYSCRIPT_TRACE are refused too. Firing an If runs its condition, or its forced branch, and that branch; firing a watch runs its check once. SubmitOverrideCondition(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, bool, int) Admits forcing one If to take the requested branch, without forcing it yet. Refusals carry an explicit reason. public DiagnosticCommand SubmitOverrideCondition(DiagnosticIdentity target, int node, bool value, bool isLive = true, int major = 1) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target The lifetime. int node The If's catalog node. bool value True forces Then, false forces Else. bool isLive False when the caller's view is paused on history, which refuses the command. int major The caller's protocol major. Returns DiagnosticCommand The receipt, admitted or rejected. Examples diagnostics.Apply(diagnostics.SubmitOverrideCondition(target, node.Id, true)); Remarks Once applied, the If runs its Then branch for true and its Else branch for false every time it runs in this lifetime, and its condition is not evaluated, until SubmitClearOverride(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, int) is applied or the lifetime or the session ends. The If still records the branch it took. Applying records an intervention and reads the forced branch back. A node whose ForceUnavailableReason is not null is refused with that reason. An If object placed twice is forced in both places, under its OutcomeNode. Forcing an already forced If replaces its branch. SubmitValueBreakpoint(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, bool, int) Admits setting or clearing a breakpoint on one declared variable, without setting it yet. Refusals carry an explicit reason. public DiagnosticCommand SubmitValueBreakpoint(DiagnosticIdentity target, int variable, bool enabled, bool isLive = true, int major = 1) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target The lifetime. int variable The variable's declaration id, a Id. bool enabled True sets the breakpoint, false clears it. bool isLive False when the caller's view is paused on history, which refuses the command. int major The caller's protocol major. Returns DiagnosticCommand The receipt, admitted or rejected. Examples diagnostics.Apply(diagnostics.SubmitValueBreakpoint(target, variable.Id, true)); Remarks Once applied, each time the variable's value changes the runner records a pause naming the script, object and block that changed it, and pauses the application the way SubmitBlockBreakpoint(DiagnosticIdentity, int, bool, bool, int) describes. A write that stores the value already held is no change, and a debugger value edit does not pause. A shared variable breaks on a change any script makes to its store, so the pause can name another script on another object. Internal storage is refused, and so is a lifetime that records no value changes, which is every lifetime outside the Editor.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SceneGate.summary: Class SceneGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Owns in-flight Scene.Load and Scene.Unload attempts, the scene identities the runner's scripts declared, and one counter per identity and phase that the When.Scene* watches read. One per ScriptRunner. Script code never sees a Task, an AsyncOperation or an exception type; AGENTS.md rules 50 and 51. public sealed class SceneGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object SceneGateway Examples runner.SceneGateway.UseProvider(new FakeSceneProvider()); Remarks A start may allocate. A tick with nothing in flight, and a tick that only polls, allocate nothing; AGENTS.md rule 31 applied to this gateway. A scene identity is interned once, when an object that declares it spawns. The asset path the host stored becomes a small number that the instance keeps in a hidden slot, so every later read, including every watch on every frame, is an array index. A load whose requester stopped waiting is cleaned up, not rolled back. When the requester cancels, is superseded, times out or despawns while an additive load is still in flight, the native load is allowed to finish and the exact scene instance it produced is then unloaded. That is the settled api-scene-cancel-cleanup answer: the requester observes its own outcome, and a host cleanup owner handles the late completion. A replacement load is never cleaned up: it released every loaded scene when it started, so its destination is the only scene there is. Properties HasProvider Whether a provider has been named. Without one every scene attempt fails as OperationFailure.Denied. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool Methods Tick() Polls once. Called by the runner before any instance runs, so an attempt that completed since the last frame advances its counters now and the watches that react to it run in this same tick. With nothing in flight this returns after three count checks and allocates nothing. public void Tick() UseProvider(ISceneProvider) Names the backend scene loads and unloads talk to. public void UseProvider(ISceneProvider provider) Parameters Type Name Description ISceneProvider provider The backend. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SceneRefe.summary: Struct SceneReference Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A handle to one scene input of a script: the typed scene identity that Scene.Load, Scene.Unload and the When.Scene* watches take. Returned by Bind.Scene() at build time, or assigned before Build() by [Asset] on the property. public readonly struct SceneReference Expand Details ... Examples Arena = Bind.Scene(); On.Ready(Scene.Load(Arena).As(LoadingArena)); Remarks The scene is assigned in the Inspector, not written as a string. The host's declared-input table draws a scene field for this input, stores the scene asset's path and GUID, and the runner resolves that path when the object spawns. A script never names a scene by its file name, which is the settled contract-reference-kinds answer: a typed scene identity, and no UnityEngine.Object cast in script values. An unassigned scene input has no placeholder. Substituting a scene would change what the game is, so the settled binding-default catalog lists a scene reference among the types that get none. The object still spawns, the missing assignment is reported once per script type, and a Scene.Load of it fails as OperationFailure.NotFound. The identity is the scene asset. Two inputs on two scripts that are assigned the same scene name the same identity, so a watch on one observes a load started through the other. Scene.Unload ends the one loaded instance of that asset and refuses when two are loaded, because the asset name alone cannot say which one was meant. A handle is valid only inside the Build that declared it, for the reason Var<T> states: it carries a slot and nothing that identifies its program. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScreenRay.summary: Struct ScreenRay Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Camera.ScreenRay(position) returns: the world ray through a screen position, starting on the camera's near plane and pointing into the screen. Along(ray) on a cast travels along it, and Origin and Direction read it. public readonly struct ScreenRay Expand Details ... Examples var point = Input.Vector2("Point"); When.Input(Input.Button("Click")).Performed( Collision.RayCast().Along(Camera.ScreenRay(point.Value)).Into(Ground)); Remarks A ray is an expression, never a stored value. Each read takes the camera's pose and the position at that moment, so a ray written once in Build() follows the pointer and the camera every frame. A script that keeps one stores ray.Origin and ray.Direction in two Vector3 variables. The position is in screen pixels from the bottom left, which is what the Input System's pointer reports. Without InView(ObjectBinding, string, int) the ray goes through Camera.main; with it, through the camera on the view's object. A position outside that camera's pixel rectangle reads a zero origin and a zero direction without a report. No camera, a view binding that holds no object, an object with no camera and a disabled camera read the same zeros and are reported once per script type and line. A camera that renders into a texture takes the position in that texture's pixels. Cinemachine moves the camera, so the ray follows the live rig and any running blend. docs/proposals/screen-rays.md is the contract. Properties Direction Which way the ray points: a world direction of length one, into the screen, read each time the value is evaluated. public Vector3ValueBlock Direction { get; } Property Value Vector3ValueBlock A spatial value; zero when the ray could not be computed. Examples On.Update(Aim.Set(ray.Origin + ray.Direction * 10)); Remarks An orthographic camera's rays are all parallel to its forward. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This ray is a default that Camera.ScreenRay never made, or another script's Build() made it. Origin Where the ray starts: the point on the camera's near plane under the position, in world space, read each time the value is evaluated. public Vector3ValueBlock Origin { get; } Property Value Vector3ValueBlock A spatial value; zero when the ray could not be computed. Examples On.Update(Aim.Set(ray.Origin + ray.Direction * 10)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This ray is a default that Camera.ScreenRay never made, or another script's Build() made it. Methods InView(ObjectBinding, string, int) The same position through the camera on a view's object instead of Camera.main. public ScreenRay InView(ObjectBinding view, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description ObjectBinding view An object binding, such as LeftView = Bind.Object();. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one: it records the authored line a diagnostic names. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns ScreenRay A ray through that view's camera. Examples var left = Camera.ScreenRay(point.Value).InView(LeftView); Remarks The view is the object carrying the Unity Camera that draws it, the object View.For(view) takes. The ray is unchanged, so one ray can be written with two views. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This ray is a default that Camera.ScreenRay never made, another script's Build() made it, it already names a view, or view was not declared by this script's Build().
