The runner arbitrates focus and activation once per frame, before any script's On.Update; docs/proposals/interaction.md is the family. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Motion Builds blocks that move a kinematic or CharacterController body, push a dynamic body, or relocate the object. Available only inside Build(). protected MotionFactory Motion { get; } Property Value MotionFactory Examples On.FixedUpdate(Motion.MoveTo(Pad).AtSpeed(4.0)); On.FixedUpdate(Motion.AddForce(Thrust).InWorldSpace()); Remarks Motion is not Transform. Transform.MoveBy writes pose immediately, with no physics. Motion.MoveBy is component-directed and refuses a dynamic Rigidbody. Dynamic bodies use AddForce, AddImpulse, SetVelocity and StopMotion. Relocation that is not traversed movement is TeleportTo. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Navigation Moves the object this script runs on, or with For a declared GameObject input, along a route around obstacles, and reports the route, the movement and where the move ended. Each move is an attempt on an operation handle bound with .As. Available only inside Build(). protected NavigationFactory Navigation { get; } Property Value NavigationFactory Examples On.Ready(Navigation.MoveTo(Post).As(Patrol)); When.Operation(Patrol).Succeeded(If(Navigation.Arrived(Patrol)).Then(OnGuard.Set(true))); Remarks Runtime-only. The route comes from the navigation backend the C# code that owns the runner installs, NavMeshNavigationProvider for Unity's NavMesh; with none, every move fails as Denied. Speed, acceleration and stopping distance stay on the actor's agent. Motion.MoveTo is the straight-line move. docs/proposals/navigation.md is the family. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Net The session, authority and message surface. Available only inside Build(). protected NetFactory Net { get; } Property Value NetFactory Examples On.Update(If(Net.HasAuthority).Then(Score.Add(1.0))); Object Creates, activates, deactivates and ends objects this script owns. Available only inside Build(). protected ObjectLifetimeFactory Object { get; } Property Value ObjectLifetimeFactory Examples On.Ready(Object.Create(Shield)); Remarks The member hides System.Object for simple-name lookup inside a Script subclass. That is the settled surface name from the contract-object-lifecycle answer, and a subclass that needs the type writes System.Object, which this codebase does not do on the run-time path anyway. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). On Registers blocks against the runner's events. Available only inside Build(). This surface has no EditorUpdate; that lives on EditorScript. protected OnFactory On { get; } Property Value OnFactory Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Options How this script type runs. Override it with RunAs(Scope.Singleton) to run one instance per game on an object LunyScript creates; leave it alone to run one instance per object that carries the script. protected virtual LunyScriptOptions Options { get; } Property Value LunyScriptOptions Examples protected override LunyScriptOptions Options => RunAs(Scope.Singleton); Remarks Read once per script type, when the runner builds it, just before Build(). A singleton starts when the game starts, on an ordinary GameObject named after the script type, in DontDestroyOnLoad, and a copy of the script on any other object does not run. docs/proposals/singleton-scripts.md is the contract. Other The other collider of the contact event currently running. Available only inside Build(), and the blocks it builds run only inside a contact event. protected OtherFactory Other { get; } Property Value OtherFactory Examples On.CollisionEnter(If(Other.HasTag("Player")).Then(Score.Add(1.0))); On.TriggerStay(HitAt.Set(Other.WorldPosition)); Remarks The same members exist on all six contact events, because they are properties of the other collider. A read outside those events throws when the block runs. docs/proposals/physics-contact-events.md is the surface. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Panel Binds, places and opens UI Toolkit panels. It hides PanelRenderer inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. Available only inside Build(). protected PanelFactory Panel { get; } Property Value PanelFactory Examples var health = Panel.Label("health"); health.BindText(Text.Format("{0}% HP", Health)); Remarks Runtime-only. The supported scene component is PanelRenderer; UIDocument is not probed. A scene-free editor host reports once and writes nothing. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Particles Starts, pauses, stops, clears and bursts the authored Unity ParticleSystem on the object this script runs on, or with For the one on a declared GameObject input, and reads whether it is playing or alive. It hides UnityEngine.ParticleSystem inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. Available only inside Build(). protected ParticlesFactory Particles { get; } Property Value ParticlesFactory Examples On.Ready(Particles.Play()); When.Input(fire).Performed(Particles.For(MuzzleFlash).Emit(12)); Remarks Unity owns the effect's modules and look. A target with no ParticleSystem is reported once per script type and the object still runs. docs/proposals/particles.md is the family. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Progress Saves and loads documents among the user's progress, in local storage. Each save and load is an attempt on an operation handle bound with .As. Available only inside Build(). docs/proposals/local-documents.md is the family. protected ProgressFactory Progress { get; } Property Value ProgressFactory Examples On.Ready(Progress.Load(Career).As(LoadingCareer)); When.Var(BestWave).Changed(Progress.Save(Career).As(SavingCareer)); Remarks A property or field of a script named Progress hides this surface inside that script, so name a document after what it holds, such as Career or Quests. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Scene Loads and unloads Unity scenes named by a typed SceneReference, each as an operation attempt. It hides UnityEngine.SceneManagement.SceneManager inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. Available only inside Build(). protected SceneFactory Scene { get; } Property Value SceneFactory Examples On.Ready(Scene.Load(Vault).Additive().As(LoadingVault)); When.SceneLoaded(Vault).Do(VaultReady.Set(true)); Remarks Runtime-only. A replacement load releases every loaded scene; an additive load releases none. docs/proposals/scene-flow.md is the family. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Sender The script that sent the request running now, as a target. Available only inside Build(), and it names a script only while an On.Request handler runs. protected LunyScriptTarget Sender { get; } Property Value LunyScriptTarget Examples On.Request(Heal, Health.Add(HealerScript.At(Sender).Strength)); Remarks A local request always carries its sender, so a handler can read the sender's public variables with SenderScript.At(Sender) or answer it with a request of its own. Outside a request it names nothing: a read through it returns the default and a request to it fails as NotFound. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Settings Saves and loads documents among the user's settings, in local storage. Each save and load is an attempt on an operation handle bound with .As. Available only inside Build(). protected SettingsFactory Settings { get; } Property Value SettingsFactory Examples On.Ready(Settings.Load(Preferences).As(LoadingPreferences)); When.Var(MusicVolume).Changed(Settings.Save(Preferences).As(SavingPreferences)); Remarks A property or field of a script named Settings hides this surface inside that script, and one named Options hides the property that declares the script's scope, so name a document after what it holds, such as Preferences or Controls. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). SpawnedBy The script whose Object.Create(prefab) or Object.Spawn(pool) made this object, as a target. Available only inside Build(). protected LunyScriptTarget SpawnedBy { get; } Property Value LunyScriptTarget Examples On.Request(Scored, Request(SpawnedBy, ShooterScript.Requests.CountHit)); Remarks Every script the made object carries, its children's included, names the incarnation of the script whose block asked for the copy. A pooled copy names the script of its current checkout. It names nothing on an object no script made, such as one saved in a scene, and after that incarnation ended, such as a pooled spawner that went back to its pool: a read through it returns the default and a request to it fails as NotFound. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Sync Which parts of this object's transform cross the network, and how often each one is sent. Available only inside Build(). protected SyncFactory Sync { get; } Property Value SyncFactory Examples Sync.Position(SyncCadence.EveryTick); Time The running game's clock and its time scale, available only inside Build(). It hides UnityEngine.Time inside a script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform: inside a Script, Time means this one. protected TimeFactory Time { get; } Property Value TimeFactory Examples On.Update(Age.Add(Time.Delta)); Remarks Runtime-only. An explicitly owned editor runner's clock governs no game, so it has no scale to read or stop; EditorTime.Elapsed() is that session's own reading. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Transform Builds blocks that move and rotate the object this script runs on. Available only inside Build(). protected TransformFactory Transform { get; } Property Value TransformFactory Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). View Chooses what a local player sees: which camera rig a view renders, and how much of the screen it takes. Available only inside Build(). protected ViewFactory View { get; } Property Value ViewFactory Examples On.Ready(View.For(Screen).SetCamera(ChaseRig)); Remarks Runtime-only, and routed through Cinemachine: with that package absent no provider is installed and every block on this surface writes nothing and says so once. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Methods Reject(string, int) Refuses the request this script is handling. The sections after the current one do not run, and what already ran stays done. protected Block Reject(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block The block. Examples On.Request(Open, If(Locked).Then(Reject())); Remarks Belongs in the blocks of an On.Request handler. Run anywhere else it does nothing and is reported once. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(). Request(LunyScriptTarget, Request, string, int) Sends a request to the script running on a target's object. Its handlers run inside this block, before the next one. protected RequestBuilder Request(LunyScriptTarget target, Request request, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description LunyScriptTarget target A binding Bind.Object() declared, Object.Owned(owned), SpawnedBy, inside a contact event Other, or inside On.Request, Sender. Request request The receiver's request. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns RequestBuilder The builder, which is a block as it is and takes As. Examples On.Ready(Request(Patient, EnemyScript.Requests.Heal)); On.Ready(Request(Door, DoorScript.Requests.Open).As(Opening)); On.TriggerEnter(If(Other.HasTag("Player")).Then(Request(Other, PlayerScript.Requests.Collect))); Remarks Name the request through the receiver's generated descriptor, such as EnemyScript.Requests.Heal, or this script's own when another object runs the same script. The receiver decides what to do; .As(operation) observes whether it did it. docs/proposals/script-communication.md is the contract. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(); the target names nothing or belongs to another script's Build(); or the request was never declared or has no name yet. RunAs(Scope, string, int) Makes the value the Options property returns. protected LunyScriptOptions RunAs(Scope scope, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Scope scope Scope.Singleton for one instance per game, Scope.Object for one per object. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns LunyScriptOptions The options. Examples protected override LunyScriptOptions Options => RunAs(Scope.Singleton); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called while Build() runs, where it would configure nothing, or given a value that is not a Scope. SendEvent(Event, string, int) Sends one of this script's events to every local script listening to it. Their handlers run inside this block, before the next one. protected Block SendEvent(Event @event, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Event event An event this script declared with Define.Event(). string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block The block that sends it. Examples Opened = Define.Event(); On.Request(Open, IsOpen.Set(true), SendEvent(Opened)); Remarks A script sends only its own events, so a listener hearing DoorScript.Events.Opened knows a DoorScript sent it. docs/proposals/script-communication.md is the contract. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(), or the event was never declared, has no name yet, or is another script's. SetProcessMode(Process, string, int) Sets this script type's default process mode. Inherit, the default, walks the Unity transform parent chain and is Pausable when the walk ends. protected void SetProcessMode(Process mode, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Process mode Whether instances of this type tick while the runner is paused. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Examples SetProcessMode(Process.WhenPaused); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(), called twice, or mode is not a defined Process value.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptBas.title: Class ScriptBase | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptBas.summary: Class ScriptBase Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Shared infrastructure for Script and EditorScript. One instance of a concrete subclass is compiled into one ScriptProgram, once, and every object running that script shares it. [Serializable] public abstract class ScriptBase Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptBase Derived EditorScript Script Examples public sealed partial class CountdownScript : Script { [Variable(3)] public Number Health { get; private set; } [Variable(true)] public Flag Alive { get; private set; } protected override void Build() { On.Update(If(Health > 0.0).Then(Health.Add(-1.0)).Else(Alive.Set(false))); When.Var(Alive).Changed(Health.Set(0.0)); } } Remarks Build() runs once per script type, before any object exists. It cannot read an inspector value, an object name or anything else about a particular object; declare a variable and fill it at spawn instead. AGENTS.md rule 25. Calls made while Build() runs construct the shared Script program once per Script type. The blocks those calls return execute later, per event and per Script instance. Confusing those phases is the largest defect class in this design. AGENTS.md rule 43. Properties Asset Starts and ends content acquisitions. Available only inside Build(). protected AssetFactory Asset { get; } Property Value AssetFactory Examples EnemyContent = Define.Operation<Prefab>(nameof(EnemyContent)); On.Ready(Asset.Load(EnemyPrefab).As(EnemyContent)); Remarks Asset.Load(source).As(handle) is an asynchronous attempt. Declared [Asset] inputs remain spawn-time resolution and are not this factory. Asset.Load does not load a scene. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Bind Declares the inputs this script needs: assets, scenes and objects in a scene. Available during generated asset-input declaration or Build(). protected BindFactory Bind { get; } Property Value BindFactory Examples OpenSound = Bind.AudioClip(); Witch = Bind.Object(); Remarks What an input holds belongs to the object, not to the script type: it is resolved when an object spawns, from what that object assigns, then the input's own declared source, then the default registered for its type. An object binding searches the object's scene instead of using a default. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Debug Blocks that write a line to the Console when they run: Debug.Log, Debug.Warn and Debug.Error. Available only inside Build(). It hides UnityEngine.Debug inside a script the same way Math hides System.Math. protected DebugFactory Debug { get; } Property Value DebugFactory Examples On.Ready(Debug.Log("ready"), Debug.Log(Health)); Remarks Each line is the message and value, then the script and the object it ran on: Health = 15 (Script: PlayerScript, Object: Player). The blocks write only in a build that defines DEBUG, which is the Editor and every development player. docs/proposals/debug-log-blocks.md is the family. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Define Declares this script's variables with the author spelling Round 06 settled. Available during generated variable initialization or Build(). protected DefineFactory Define { get; } Property Value DefineFactory Examples Health = Define.Number(nameof(Health), 100); TeamScore = Define.Number(nameof(TeamScore), 0).Shared(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Math The core numeric functions, available only inside Build(). It hides System.Math inside a script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform: inside a Script, Math means this one. protected MathFactory Math { get; } Property Value MathFactory Examples On.Update(Health.Set(Math.Clamp(Health + Healing, 0.0, 100.0))); Random Draws from a declared randomizer that store a result, available only inside Build(). protected RandomFactory Random { get; } Property Value RandomFactory Examples Loot = Define.Randomizer().Seed(42); On.Ready(Random.Number().From(Loot).In(1.0, 100.0).Into(Roll)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Shared Operations on a shared store. Available only inside Build(). protected SharedFactory Shared { get; } Property Value SharedFactory Examples On.Ready(Shared.Clear()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Text Builds text formats. Inside a script, Text in an expression means this member; in a property declaration it is the Text type. A text variable is declared with Define.Text. Available during generated variable initialization or Build(). protected TextFactory Text { get; } Property Value TextFactory Examples On.Update(Label.Set(Text.Format("{0} hp", Health))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Var Declares this script's variables. Available during generated variable initialization or Build(). protected VarFactory Var { get; } Property Value VarFactory Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). When Registers blocks against a change in state. Available only inside Build(). protected WhenFactory When { get; } Property Value WhenFactory Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Methods AlwaysFails(BehaviorNode, string, int) A behaviour-tree wrapper that reports Failed once its child finishes, whatever the child reported. While the child runs, the wrapper reports Running. protected BehaviorNode AlwaysFails(BehaviorNode node, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description BehaviorNode node The child. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns BehaviorNode The wrapper, as a node. Examples var tryDoor = InOrder(AlwaysFails(Task(Knocks.Inc())), Task(Wait(1))).UntilOneSucceeds(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The child is a node no factory produced, or this was called outside Build(). AlwaysSucceeds(BehaviorNode, string, int) A behaviour-tree wrapper that reports Succeeded once its child finishes, whatever the child reported. While the child runs, the wrapper reports Running. protected BehaviorNode AlwaysSucceeds(BehaviorNode node, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description BehaviorNode node The child. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns BehaviorNode The wrapper, as a node. Examples var chase = InOrder(AlwaysSucceeds(pursue), Check(Caught), Task(Catches.Inc())).UntilOneFails(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The child is a node no factory produced, or this was called outside Build(). Behavior(string, string, int) Opens a behaviour tree: a root node that chooses and runs work, and a handle that starts it and reads its result. protected BehaviorBuilder Behavior(string name, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name What this tree is called in a diagnostic and in the runtime debugger. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns BehaviorBuilder The builder whose Root call takes the root node. Examples var open = Behavior("Open").Root(InOrder(Check(HasKey), Task(Opening.Set(true))).UntilOneFails()); On.Message(Use, open.Start()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The name is null or whitespace, or this was called outside Build(). Build() protected abstract void Build() Check(ConditionBlock, string, int) A behaviour-tree leaf that reads a condition in the advance that reaches it: Succeeded when it is true, Failed when it is false. protected BehaviorNode Check(ConditionBlock condition, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The condition. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns BehaviorNode The Check, as a node. Examples var open = InOrder(Check(HasKey), Task(Opening.Set(true))).UntilOneFails(); Remarks A Check never reports Running, and a composite that moved past it does not read it again. A condition that has to hold while other work runs is read once per frame by Repeat(Check(condition)).UntilFails() placed beside that work in InParallel(...).UntilOneFails(). Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The condition is null, or this was called outside Build(). Choose(Choice, string, int) Opens a scored choice. Highest names the options; optional Bias and Hold follow; used as a block it starts the selector. protected ChooseBuilder Choose(Choice choice, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Choice choice The choice Define.Choice() declared, whose name a diagnostic and the runtime inspector call this selector by. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns ChooseBuilder The builder whose Highest call takes the options. Examples Needs = Define.Choice(); On.Ready(Choose(Needs).Highest( Option(WorkScore).Then(Work), Option(RestScore).Then(Rest)).Bias(0.1).Hold(Seconds(1))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException choice is not a choice this script declared, or another Choose call already opened it. DefineAssets() Assigns generated asset-input handles before Build, after the variables. Source-generated overrides call the base implementation first so inherited declarations keep their order. protected virtual void DefineAssets() Remarks Written by the same generator that writes DefineVariables(). Use [Asset] properties in a partial Script subclass, or declare the inputs with Bind calls inside Build. It is a second hook rather than more lines in the first because the two declare different things: a variable is storage this script owns and an asset input is a value an object supplies. Both run before Build(), which is what lets Build() use either. DefineVariables() Assigns generated variable handles before Build. Source-generated overrides call the base implementation first so inherited declarations keep their order. protected virtual void DefineVariables() Remarks Written by the LunyScript variable generator. Use [Variable] properties in a partial Script subclass, or keep explicit Var.Define calls inside Build. ForEach(HitsResult, string, int) Visits each entry a Collision cast stored, nearest first. Nested ForEach is refused. protected ForEachHitsBuilder ForEach(HitsResult hits, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description HitsResult hits The result to visit. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns ForEachHitsBuilder A builder whose Do takes the visit body. Examples On.Update(ForEach(Pierced).Do(entry => If(entry.Distance < 2).Then(Close.Add(1)))); Remarks The count is read before each entry, so a body that runs a cast into the same result reads the new result. An entry read after the loop ends reads zero and is reported. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The result was never declared or another script declared it, a ForEach is already open, or this was called outside Build(). ForEach(OverlapsResult, string, int) Visits each entry a Collision overlap stored, in Unity's order. Nested ForEach is refused. protected ForEachOverlapsBuilder ForEach(OverlapsResult overlaps, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description OverlapsResult overlaps The result to visit. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns ForEachOverlapsBuilder A builder whose Do takes the visit body. Examples On.Update(ForEach(Nearby).Do(entry => Last.Set(entry.WorldPosition))); Remarks The count is read before each entry, so a body that runs an overlap into the same result reads the new result. An entry read after the loop ends reads zero and is reported. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The result was never declared or another script declared it, a ForEach is already open, or this was called outside Build(). ForEach<T>(ListHandle<T>, string, int) Visits each list entry present at loop entry. Nested ForEach is refused. protected ForEachListBuilder<T> ForEach<T>(ListHandle<T> list, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) where T : struct Parameters Type Name Description ListHandle<T> list The list to visit. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns ForEachListBuilder<T> A builder whose Do takes the visit body. Type Parameters T The list element kind. Examples On.Update(ForEach(Slots).Do(id => Hits.Add(id))); ForEach<TKey, TValue>(MapHandle<TKey, TValue>, string, int) Visits each map pair present at loop entry, in insertion order. Nested ForEach is refused. protected ForEachMapBuilder<TKey, TValue> ForEach<TKey, TValue>(MapHandle<TKey, TValue> map, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) where TKey : struct where TValue : struct Parameters Type Name Description MapHandle<TKey, TValue> map The map to visit. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns ForEachMapBuilder<TKey, TValue> A builder whose Do takes the visit body. Type Parameters TKey TValue Examples On.Update(ForEach(Scores).Do((key, value) => Hits.Add(value))); Hours(double) An elapsed duration of this many hours, for Hold and Wait. protected Elapsed Hours(double amount) Parameters Type Name Description double amount How many hours. Returns Elapsed Examples Hold(Hours(1)) If(CollectionTryBuilder, string, int) Starts a conditional block that owns one collection call: the call runs once each time the block runs, and its own outcome picks the branch. protected IfBuilder If(CollectionTryBuilder attempt, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description CollectionTryBuilder attempt The try, such as Slots.TryAdd(item). This consumes it. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns IfBuilder A builder whose Then names the blocks that run when the call succeeded, and whose Else names the blocks that run when it was refused. Examples On.Ready(If(Slots.TryAdd(item)).Then(Hits.Add(1.0)).Else(ShowFull.Set(true))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException attempt is a default try, or another If, ElseIf or .As already consumed it. If(ConditionBlock, string, int) Starts a conditional block. protected IfBuilder If(ConditionBlock condition, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The condition to test, built from a variable's operators. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one: this is where the whole If chain records the line it was written on, because Then and Else take a params array and C# allows no parameter after one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns IfBuilder A builder whose Then names the blocks to run. Examples On.Update(If(health > 0.0).Then(health.Add(-1.0))); InAnyOrder(params BehaviorNode[]) A behaviour-tree composite that runs its children one after another, in an order shuffled each time the composite is entered, and resumes at the child that reported Running. protected BehaviorCompositeBuilder InAnyOrder(params BehaviorNode[] children) Parameters Type Name Description BehaviorNode[] children The children. Returns BehaviorCompositeBuilder The composite, ready to be used as a node or given an ending clause. Examples var patrol = InAnyOrder(Visit(PostA), Visit(PostB), Visit(PostC)).UntilOneFails(); Remarks The order is drawn from a random stream of the object, seeded the way an unseeded Define.Randomizer() is. The endings are those of InOrder. This factory takes a params array, so it captures no authored line; AGENTS.md rule 72. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The list is null or empty, holds a node no factory produced, or this was called outside Build(). InOrder(params BehaviorNode[]) A behaviour-tree composite that runs its children one after another, in the order they are written, and resumes at the child that reported Running. protected BehaviorCompositeBuilder InOrder(params BehaviorNode[] children) Parameters Type Name Description BehaviorNode[] children The children, in the order they run. Returns BehaviorCompositeBuilder The composite, ready to be used as a node or given an ending clause. Examples var open = InOrder(Check(HasKey), Task(Opening.Set(true)), Task(Wait(1))).UntilOneFails(); Remarks As written, every child runs and the composite succeeds only if every child succeeded. UntilOneFails() and UntilOneSucceeds() end it early. This factory takes a params array, so it captures no authored line; AGENTS.md rule 72. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The list is null or empty, holds a node no factory produced, or this was called outside Build(). InParallel(params BehaviorNode[]) A behaviour-tree composite that advances every child once per advance, in the order they are written. protected BehaviorCompositeBuilder InParallel(params BehaviorNode[] children) Parameters Type Name Description BehaviorNode[] children The children, in the order they are advanced. Returns BehaviorCompositeBuilder The composite, ready to be used as a node or given an ending clause. Examples var guarded = InParallel(Repeat(Check(!IntruderNear)).UntilFails(), patrol).UntilOneFails(); Remarks As written, the composite waits for every child and succeeds only if every child succeeded. UntilOneFails() and UntilOneSucceeds() end it early and cancel the children still running. Given blocks rather than nodes, InParallel is the routine group. This factory takes a params array, so it captures no authored line; AGENTS.md rule 72. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The list is null or empty, holds a node no factory produced, or this was called outside Build(). InParallel(params Block[]) A concurrent group: every child advances each frame, in the order they are written, inside one step of a routine. protected RoutineGroupBuilder InParallel(params Block[] children) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] children The children, in declaration order. Returns RoutineGroupBuilder The group, ready to be used as a routine step or given an ending clause. Examples On.Ready(Routine(Open).Run(InParallel(slideDoor, playSound))); Remarks As written, the group runs every child and waits for all of them, reporting Succeeded only if every child succeeded. UntilOneFinishes() and UntilOneSucceeds() replace that with an early ending, and OthersKeepRunning() follows either of those to keep the unfinished children running under the enclosing routine activation. This factory takes a params array, so C# allows it no parameter after the children and it captures no authored line; AGENTS.md rule 72. The routine step that carries the group is what a diagnostic names. A group belongs in a routine, another group, a Run body or a Choose option's action. Placed inside Then or Else, or directly in an event list, it is refused when the script type is built; inside Then or Else the refusal names the line of the If that holds it. LUNY007 reports the same placement at compile time where the group is written directly in the list. Inverted(BehaviorNode, string, int) A behaviour-tree wrapper that swaps its child's result once the child finishes: Succeeded becomes Failed and Failed becomes Succeeded. While the child runs, the wrapper reports Running. protected BehaviorNode Inverted(BehaviorNode node, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description BehaviorNode node The child. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns BehaviorNode The wrapper, as a node. Examples var pursue = InOrder(Task(Goal.Set(IntruderAt)), Inverted(Check(Caught))).UntilOneFails(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The child is a node no factory produced, or this was called outside Build(). Milliseconds(double) An elapsed duration of this many milliseconds, for Hold and Wait. protected Elapsed Milliseconds(double amount) Parameters Type Name Description double amount How many milliseconds. Returns Elapsed Examples Hold(Milliseconds(500)) Minutes(double) An elapsed duration of this many minutes, for Hold and Wait. protected Elapsed Minutes(double amount) Parameters Type Name Description double amount How many minutes. Returns Elapsed Examples Hold(Minutes(2)) Option(NumberValueBlock, string, int) One scored option of a Choose selector. Then names the action that runs while this option is selected. protected UtilityOptionBuilder Option(NumberValueBlock score, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock score The current score. All finite signed scores are legal; the largest wins. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns UtilityOptionBuilder The builder whose Then call takes the action. Examples Option(WorkScore).Then(Work) Repeat(BehaviorNode, string, int) A behaviour-tree decorator that runs its child again after each finish, starting at most one fresh repetition per frame. protected BehaviorRepeatBuilder Repeat(BehaviorNode node, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description BehaviorNode node The child. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns BehaviorRepeatBuilder The Repeat, ready to be used as a node or given an ending. Examples var arrive = Repeat(Check(Arrived)).UntilSucceeds(); var lookAround = Repeat(Task(Looks.Inc())).Times(3); Remarks As written, the Repeat runs until its owner cancels it and has no result of its own. Times(n), UntilFails() and UntilSucceeds() give it an ending. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The child is a node no factory produced, or this was called outside Build(). RequireContext(string) protected ScriptBuildContext RequireContext(string surface) Parameters Type Name Description string surface Returns ScriptBuildContext Resource<T>(string, string, int) An asset of one kind in a Unity Resources folder, for Asset.Load. protected Resource<T> Resource<T>(string key, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) where T : struct Parameters Type Name Description string key The key, relative to any Resources folder and without a file extension, the way UnityEngine.Resources.Load takes one. Validated here. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Resource<T> The source Asset.Load takes. Type Parameters T The input kind the load produces, such as Texture2D or Prefab. Examples On.Ready(Asset.Load(Resource<Texture2D>("UI/Portrait")).As(PortraitContent)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(), or key is null, whitespace, or carries a file extension or a leading slash. Routine(Routine, string, int) Opens a sequential routine: steps that run in the order they are written, each one finishing before the next begins, over as many frames as they need. protected RoutineBuilder Routine(Routine routine, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Routine routine The routine Define.Routine() declared, whose name a diagnostic and the runtime inspector call this routine by. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns RoutineBuilder The builder whose Run call takes the steps. Examples Patrol = Define.Routine(); On.Ready(Routine(Patrol).Run(walkOut, waitAtPost, walkBack)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException routine is not a routine this script declared, or another Routine call already opened it. Run(Block, Block, params Block[]) Opens independently advanced repeating work whose body has more than one block. This overload takes a params array, so it captures no authored line; AGENTS.md rule 72. protected RunWorkBuilder Run(Block first, Block second, params Block[] more) Parameters Type Name Description Block first The first block of the body. Block second The second block of the body. Block[] more Any further blocks, in order. Returns RunWorkBuilder The builder whose For, Over, Every, Start and Stop finish the chain. Examples var pulse = Run(windUp, Hits.Add(1.0)).Over(3); Run(Block, string, int) Opens independently advanced repeating work. Qualifiers name a repetition count (For), a duration (Over) or a cadence (Every). Start() starts one activation; declaration does not. protected RunWorkBuilder Run(Block body, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Block body The blocks each activation runs, in order. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns RunWorkBuilder The builder whose For, Over, Every, Start and Stop finish the chain. Examples var pulse = Run(Hits.Add(1.0)).Over(3); var tick = Run(Hits.Add(1.0)).Every(3); var burst = Run(Hits.Add(1.0)).Every(3).For(5); var continuous = Run(Hits.Add(1.0)); On.Ready(pulse.Start(), tick.Start(), burst.Start(), continuous.Start()); Seconds(double) An elapsed duration of this many seconds, for Hold and Wait. protected Elapsed Seconds(double amount) Parameters Type Name Description double amount How many seconds. Returns Elapsed Examples Hold(Seconds(1)) Sequence(params Block[]) Several blocks held as one block. It runs them in the order they are written and does what they would do written out in its place. protected Block Sequence(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in the order they run. Returns Block The sequence, as one block. Examples var hop = Sequence(Lift.Set(1), Wait(0.25), Lift.Set(0)); On.Ready(Routine(WarmUp).Run(hop, hop)); Remarks In an event list, a Then or another list that runs every block at once, the sequence runs its blocks in that frame. As a step of a routine, a group, a Run body or a Choose option's action, each of its blocks finishes before the next begins, so a Wait inside it holds that owner, and in a concurrent group the sequence is one child. It reports Failed when one of its blocks did, and runs the rest of them first. Placed a second time it is a copy with progress of its own. (a, b, c), a tuple of 2 to 9 blocks, is the same sequence. Define.Sequence declares one with a name, which the debugger shows. This factory takes a params array, so it captures no authored line; AGENTS.md rule 72. docs/proposals/sequences.md is the contract. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The list is null, empty or holds a null, or this was called outside Build(). Task(Block, string, int) A behaviour-tree leaf that runs a block. An ordinary block runs once and the Task succeeds in the same advance; an action, such as a Wait or a routine group, is advanced once per frame and the Task reports its result. protected BehaviorNode Task(Block action, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Block action The block to run. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns BehaviorNode The Task, as a node. Examples var open = InOrder(Task(Opening.Set(true)), Task(Wait(1)), Task(Opened.Set(true))); Remarks A routine group carrying OthersKeepRunning() is refused in a Task when the script type is built: the clause hands unfinished children to an enclosing routine activation, and a Task is not one. A Task that starts a routine is legal, and the routine runs as script work. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The block is null, or this was called outside Build(). Wait(Elapsed, string, int) A routine step that holds its routine for a duration value, the one Seconds(n), Milliseconds(n), Minutes(n) or Hours(n) makes. protected Block Wait(Elapsed duration, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Elapsed duration How much game time. The value already carries its unit. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block The wait step. Examples On.CollisionEnter(Routine(Flash).Run(Object.SetColor(1, 0.25, 0.25), Wait(Seconds(0.15)), Object.ResetColor())); Wait(NumberValueBlock, string, int) A routine step that holds its routine for this much game time, then lets the next step run. Used as a block the amount is seconds; a unit call names another unit. protected WaitBuilder Wait(NumberValueBlock amount, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock amount How much game time, in seconds unless a unit call follows. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns WaitBuilder The builder, which is a step as it is or takes Seconds, Milliseconds, Minutes or Hours. Examples On.Ready(Routine(Door).Run(Opening.Set(true), Wait(3), Opening.Set(false))); On.Ready(Routine(Blink).Run(Lamp.Set(true), Wait(500).Milliseconds(), Lamp.Set(false))); Remarks The wait counts game time from the moment the routine reaches it, and the amount is read then. Zero finishes at once; a negative amount, NaN or an infinity finishes at once and is reported as a warning. A wait belongs in a routine, a concurrent group or a Run body; placed inside Then or Else, or directly in an event list, it is refused when the script type is built, naming its line, and LUNY007 reports it at compile time where it is written directly in the list.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptBui.summary: Class ScriptBuildContext Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The build-time half of the behaviour tree: each tree a Behavior(name).Root(node) declares, placed once, and where its starts are placed. public sealed class ScriptBuildContext Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptBuildContext Remarks A tree's nodes are placed where Root is written, with one CodeSmile.LunyScript.BlockCloner, the way a Run's body is placed where the Run is declared. A tree whose Start is placed in a state's Enter list belongs to that state: CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptBuildContext.FinishStateMachines() claims it, and the machine advances it instead of the runner. All of this runs once per script type; nothing here runs per frame. docs/proposals/behaviour-trees.md is the contract. Properties ScriptType The script type being built. Named in every diagnostic this build can raise. public Type ScriptType { get; } Property Value Type

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptIns.summary: Class ScriptInstance Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One object's state for one program: the slot arrays the program's layout asked for, and the host the blocks act on. The blocks themselves are shared by every instance of the program and hold no per-object state at all. public sealed class ScriptInstance Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptInstance Examples var instance = runner.Spawn(program, host); instance.SetNumber(health.NumberSlot, 100.0); Remarks "Swapping the context" means passing a different ScriptInstance to the same block object. Nothing is copied and nothing is rebound. See AGENTS.md rule 21 and docs/execution-model.md. An instance is reusable: Rebind(IScriptHost) points it at another host and ResetToDefaults() puts every slot back to its declared starting value, both without allocating. That is what makes pooling a memory copy rather than a spawn. Constructors ScriptInstance(ScriptProgram, IScriptHost) Allocates the slot arrays the layout asks for and copies the declared defaults into them. This is the one allocation the spawn boundary permits, and its size is exactly what SlotBytes predicts plus one array header per SlotArrayCount. public ScriptInstance(ScriptProgram program, IScriptHost host) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptProgram program The program this instance runs. IScriptHost host The object the blocks act on. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException program or host is null. Fields NoLocalPlayer No local player: what LocalPlayer holds for an incarnation bound to nobody. public const int NoLocalPlayer = -1 Field Value int NoNetworkObject What NetworkObjectId holds while this instance is bound to no networked object. public const int NoNetworkObject = 0 Field Value int Properties AssetInputCount How many asset inputs this instance holds, which is how many its script declared. public int AssetInputCount { get; } Property Value int Examples Assert.That(instance.AssetInputCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); CanProcess Whether process events run on this instance given the runner's paused flag and this instance's effective process mode. Cached next to IsEnabled; recomputed when the runner pauses, when this instance is spawned, and when it is reparented, never every frame. public bool CanProcess { get; } Property Value bool HasNetworkAuthority True when this peer holds authority over the object this instance runs on. False for an instance bound to no networked object, and for every peer while there is no session. public bool HasNetworkAuthority { get; } Property Value bool Remarks Refreshed once per tick by ScriptRunner, so every block that reads it within one frame reads the same answer. AGENTS.md rule 45 requires that authority is visible rather than hidden, and an answer that could change between two blocks of one frame would be visible and useless. Host The object this instance's blocks act on. Never a GameObject directly; see AGENTS.md rule 24. public IScriptHost Host { get; } Property Value IScriptHost IsEnabled Whether the runner runs this instance's per-frame blocks. Driven by the host's own enable and disable, which Unity owns; LunyScript re-implements none of it. public bool IsEnabled { get; } Property Value bool IsFaulted True after an action failure, until explicitly re-enabled or respawned. public bool IsFaulted { get; } Property Value bool Examples if (instance.IsFaulted) runner.SetEnabled(instance, true); IsPooled Whether this instance is currently in a pool rather than attached to a live object. public bool IsPooled { get; } Property Value bool IsReady Whether On.Ready has already run for this instance. public bool IsReady { get; } Property Value bool LocalPlayer The local player number this incarnation is bound to, or NoLocalPlayer. Set when the instance spawns: by Object.Create(prefab).ForPlayer(n) or Object.Spawn(pool).ForPlayer(n), or by the Local Player field on the object's LunyScriptBehaviour. public int LocalPlayer { get; } Property Value int Examples var player = instance.LocalPlayer; Remarks Player-less input reads, Input.Vector2("Move"), Input.IsPaired and When.Player(), read this player; docs/proposals/local-player-pairing.md. NetworkObjectId Which networked object this instance is bound to, or NoNetworkObject when it is bound to none. public int NetworkObjectId { get; } Property Value int Remarks Assigned by ScriptRunner.BindNetworkObject, which the Netcode assembly calls when Netcode for GameObjects spawns the object. An instance with no binding takes no part in the network tick: it sends nothing, receives nothing, and its writes are never refused. OwnedObjectCount How many owned-object slots this instance has. public int OwnedObjectCount { get; } Property Value int Examples Assert.That(instance.OwnedObjectCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); PendingLifetime What an authored Object.Activate(), Object.Deactivate(), Object.Destroy() or Object.Despawn() asked for and the runner has not applied yet. public LifetimeRequest PendingLifetime { get; } Property Value LifetimeRequest Examples Assert.That(instance.PendingLifetime, Is.EqualTo(LifetimeRequest.None)); Remarks One request at a time: a later request in the same dispatch replaces an earlier one, because the last thing the script said is what it means. LifetimeRequest states why the request is recorded rather than applied on the spot. Program The program whose blocks run against this instance. public ScriptProgram Program { get; } Property Value ScriptProgram Methods AppendTextSlot<TDestination>(in TextSlot, ref TDestination) Appends one text slot's bytes onto the end of a fixed-capacity buffer, rather than replacing what the buffer holds the way ReadText<TDestination>(in TextSlot, ref TDestination) does. public FormatError AppendTextSlot<TDestination>(in TextSlot slot, ref TDestination destination) where TDestination : unmanaged, INativeList<byte>, IUTF8Bytes Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot slot The text slot to read. TDestination destination The buffer to append onto. Returns FormatError FormatError.None, or FormatError.Overflow when the buffer is too small for what this slot holds. Type Parameters TDestination The fixed-string type of the buffer. Examples var error = instance.AppendTextSlot(slot, ref buffer); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance, or its capacity is not one of the five. CopyTextSlot(in TextSlot, in TextSlot) Copies one text slot into another. Allocates nothing, except the new string a growing destination takes when a fixed source holds different characters. public void CopyTextSlot(in TextSlot destination, in TextSlot source) Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot destination The slot written. TextSlot source The slot read. Examples instance.CopyTextSlot(lastWinner.TextSlot, playerName.TextSlot); Remarks Copying a slot onto itself does nothing and leaves the text as it was. The check is required rather than tidy: SetText reaches FixedString.CopyFrom, which empties the destination before it appends the source, so a self-copy without this early return would clear the variable and report no error. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The source text does not fit in the destination's declared capacity. The destination is left unchanged. GetAsset(in AudioClip) The audio clip one of this script's declared inputs holds on this object. public AudioClip GetAsset(in AudioClip input) Parameters Type Name Description AudioClip input The handle Build() assigned. Returns AudioClip The clip. Examples var clip = instance.GetAsset(script.Shot); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle was never declared, or belongs to another script. Returns AudioMixerGroup The group. Examples var group = instance.GetAsset(script.Effects); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle was never declared, or belongs to another script. GetFlag(in FlagSlot) Reads a Flag slot. public bool GetFlag(in FlagSlot slot) Parameters Type Name Description FlagSlot slot Which slot to read. Returns double The value this instance currently holds in that slot. Examples var current = instance.GetNumber(health.NumberSlot); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is not one of this instance's, which almost always means the handle was declared by a different script type. TSource value The text to store. Type Parameters TSource A Unity.Collections fixed-string type.
