The slot is left unchanged. SetVector2(in Vector2Slot, in Vector2) Writes one two-component spatial slot. public void SetVector2(in Vector2Slot slot, in Vector2 value) Parameters Type Name Description Vector2Slot slot Which slot to write. Vector2 value What to store. Examples instance.SetVector2(slot, new Vector2(1.0, 0.0)); Remarks There is no authority guard here, for the reason SetVector3(in Vector3Slot, in Vector3) states. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance. SetVector3(in Vector3Slot, in Vector3) Writes one spatial slot, or the shared store the slot names. public void SetVector3(in Vector3Slot slot, in Vector3 value) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3Slot slot Which slot to write. Vector3 value What to store. Examples instance.SetVector3(slot, new Vector3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)); Remarks There is no authority guard here, because a spatial variable cannot be synchronised in this version: Var.DefineSynced refuses the two spatial kinds where they are declared, so no spatial slot is ever a synchronised one. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance. TextEquals<TOther>(in TextSlot, in TOther) Whether a text slot holds exactly this text. Allocates nothing. public bool TextEquals<TOther>(in TextSlot slot, in TOther other) where TOther : unmanaged, INativeList<byte>, IUTF8Bytes Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot slot Which slot to compare. TOther other The text to compare against. Returns bool True when the slot's bytes and length match. Type Parameters TOther A Unity.Collections fixed-string type. Examples var expected = new FixedString64Bytes("Player One"); var same = instance.TextEquals(playerName.TextSlot, in expected); TextLength(in TextSlot) How many UTF-8 bytes a text slot currently holds. public int TextLength(in TextSlot slot) Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot slot Which slot to measure. Returns int The slot's current length in bytes, which is 0 for an empty one. Examples var bytes = instance.TextLength(playerName.TextSlot); TextSlotsEqual(in TextSlot, in TextSlot) Whether two text slots hold the same text. Allocates nothing. public bool TextSlotsEqual(in TextSlot left, in TextSlot right) Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot left The first slot. TextSlot right The second slot. Returns bool True when both slots hold the same bytes. Examples var same = instance.TextSlotsEqual(playerName.TextSlot, lastWinner.TextSlot);

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptObs.title: Class ScriptObservation | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptObs.summary: Class ScriptObservation Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One C# observation of one variable of one script incarnation, returned by Observe(in Number, Action<double>) and its siblings. The caller owns it and ends it with Dispose(). public abstract class ScriptObservation Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptObservation Examples m_Watch = player.Observe(player.Definition.Health, ShowHealth); // ... m_Watch.Dispose(); Remarks This is the settled contract-instance-access observation: it has an explicit disposable owner and ends on target invalidation. It ends by itself when the observed incarnation ends, when its callback is a method of a Unity object that has been destroyed, and when its callback throws, which is reported once. The runner checks it once per frame, after every script's On.LateUpdate, and calls the callback only when the value differs from the previous check. The check allocates nothing. Properties IsActive True until the observation is disposed or ends by itself; the callback is called only while it is true. public bool IsActive { get; } Property Value bool Examples if (m_Watch.IsActive == false && player.IsRunning) m_Watch = player.Observe(player.Definition.Health, ShowHealth); Methods Dispose() Ends the observation. The callback is not called again. A second call does nothing. public void Dispose() Examples private void OnDestroy() => m_Watch?.Dispose(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called from a thread other than the runner's.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptPro.title: Class ScriptProgram | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptPro.summary: Class ScriptProgram Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One script type, built. Holds the immutable block tree, the On.* event table and the instance layout, and is shared by every object running that script. public sealed class ScriptProgram Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptProgram Examples var program = runner.GetOrBuildProgram(new PlayerScript()); var instance = runner.Spawn(program, host); Remarks A program is built once per script type, not once per object. The predecessor called Build() once per object, at roughly ninety managed allocations per spawn, which made it unusable for a game that spawns enemies and pickups. AGENTS.md rule 21; docs/execution-model.md has the whole model. Nothing on a program is mutable. Per-object state lives in slots on a ScriptInstance, and running the same block against a different instance is all that "swapping the context" means. Properties AssetInputCount How many asset inputs this script declares. public int AssetInputCount { get; } Property Value int Examples Assert.That(program.AssetInputCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); AuthorityGainedBlockCount Number of blocks On.Authority.Gained registered. public int AuthorityGainedBlockCount { get; } Property Value int AuthorityLostBlockCount Number of blocks On.Authority.Lost registered. public int AuthorityLostBlockCount { get; } Property Value int BehaviorTreeCount Number of behaviour trees this script declared, including one a state machine advances. Each one the runner advances costs one number read per frame per instance while it is not active. public int BehaviorTreeCount { get; } Property Value int Examples var trees = program.BehaviorTreeCount; BuiltScript The one object of ScriptType whose Build() produced this program, and therefore the one object whose variable properties were assigned. Read a variable from this object; every other object of the same script type keeps its variable properties at their defaults, because Build() runs once per script type. public ScriptBase BuiltScript { get; } Property Value ScriptBase Examples var script = (PlayerScript)instance.Program.BuiltScript; var health = instance.GetNumber(script.Health.NumberSlot); Remarks Script returns this object from Awake onward, which is how a component reaches it without holding a program. docs/slice-decisions.md D4.42 records the decision, what it costs, and the one ordering hazard: a component with a negative DefaultExecutionOrder that caches behaviour.Script in its own Awake caches the prototype in the serialized field, because LunyScriptBehaviour.Awake has not run yet. FrameUpdateBlockCount Number of blocks On.Update registered. public int FrameUpdateBlockCount { get; } Property Value int InputActionCount How many input actions this script declared. public int InputActionCount { get; } Property Value int Examples var count = program.InputActionCount; Remarks A declaration belongs to the script type rather than to the object, so this is also how many entries InputGateway.ResolutionsFor produces for this program. IsNetworked True when this script declares at least one synchronised variable, which is what makes an instance of it take part in the network tick at all. public bool IsNetworked { get; } Property Value bool Layout How many slots of each kind every instance of this program owns. public InstanceLayout Layout { get; } Property Value InstanceLayout MessageCount How many distinct message names this script sends or receives. public int MessageCount { get; } Property Value int OwnedObjectCount How many owned objects this script declares, one per distinct name its Object.Create calls use. public int OwnedObjectCount { get; } Property Value int Examples Assert.That(program.OwnedObjectCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); ProcessMode The type default process mode SetProcessMode wrote, or Inherit. public Process ProcessMode { get; } Property Value Process ReadyBlockCount Number of blocks On.Ready registered. public int ReadyBlockCount { get; } Property Value int RoutineCount Number of routines this script declared. Every one of them is advanced once per frame per instance, and a routine whose activation has not started returns on its first line. public int RoutineCount { get; } Property Value int SceneInputCount How many scene inputs this script declares. public int SceneInputCount { get; } Property Value int Examples Assert.That(program.SceneInputCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); Scope How many instances of this script type run: one per object that carries it, or one per game on the object LunyScript creates for it. The script's Options property declares it. public Scope Scope { get; } Property Value Scope Examples if (program.Scope == Scope.Singleton) { } ScriptType The Script subclass this program was built from. public Type ScriptType { get; } Property Value Type StateMachineCount Number of state machines this script declared. Each one runs a pass per instance on its own tick, and a machine that has not started returns on its first line. public int StateMachineCount { get; } Property Value int SyncedTransformChannelCount How many transform channels this script synchronises: at most three, one each for position, rotation and scale. public int SyncedTransformChannelCount { get; } Property Value int SyncedVariableCount How many synchronised variables this script declared. public int SyncedVariableCount { get; } Property Value int TimedWorkCount Number of timed-work declarations this script built. Every one of them is advanced once per frame per instance, and a work whose activation has not started returns on its first line. public int TimedWorkCount { get; } Property Value int UtilityCount Number of utility selectors this script declared. Every one of them is advanced once per frame per instance, and a selector whose activation has not started returns on its first line. public int UtilityCount { get; } Property Value int WatchCount Number of When.Var(x).Changed watches registered. public int WatchCount { get; } Property Value int Methods AssetInputIndex(string) The slot one asset-input name addresses. public int AssetInputIndex(string name) Parameters Type Name Description string name The declared name. Returns int The slot index, or -1 when this script declares no input by that name. Examples var slot = program.AssetInputIndex(nameof(GateScript.OpenSound)); AssetInputNameAt(int) What one asset input is called. The name is what a host's stored value is matched against and what the Inspector derives its label from. public string AssetInputNameAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Its position in declaration order. Returns string The declared name. Examples var name = program.AssetInputNameAt(0); AssetInputTypeAt(int) Which Unity asset type one asset input accepts. The Inspector draws a field of this type, which is what stops an asset of another kind being assigned. public Type AssetInputTypeAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Its position in declaration order. Returns Type The declared type. Examples var type = program.AssetInputTypeAt(0); FindVariable<T>(string) Finds a variable this script declared, by the name it was declared with, and returns its handle. public Var<T> FindVariable<T>(string name) where T : struct Parameters Type Name Description string name The name the script declared, which nameof produced. Returns Var<T> The same handle Build() assigned to the script's own property. Type Parameters T Number, Flag or Text, matching how the variable was declared. Examples var health = program.FindVariable<Number>(nameof(PlayerScript.Health)); Remarks This is the tooling path, not the fix for reading a variable from the wrong object. It exists so that code holding a program and a name - a runtime inspector, a debugging window, a test - can reach a variable without holding a Script object at all. Ordinary code reads the variable from BuiltScript, which Script returns. docs/slice-decisions.md D4.42 records both and which is which. It is never read on the run-time path: a block holds the handle its build gave it. The search is a linear scan over the script's declarations, which number in the tens. The shadow slots a When.Var(x).Changed watch and a synchronised variable add are refused rather than returned. Their names are in angle brackets and no script wrote them, so returning one would hand out a slot the caller cannot have meant. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException No variable of that name was declared, the name belongs to a slot LunyScript added rather than the script, or the variable was declared with a different kind than T. InputActionKindAt(int) What one declared input action produces. public InputValueKind InputActionKindAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Which declaration, in declaration order. Returns InputValueKind The declared kind. Examples var kind = program.InputActionKindAt(0); InputActionNameAt(int) The name one declared input action carries. public string InputActionNameAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Which declaration, in declaration order. Returns string The action's name as the script declared it. Examples var name = program.InputActionNameAt(0); InputActionPlayerAt(int) Which local player one declared input action belongs to. public int InputActionPlayerAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Which declaration, in declaration order. Returns int The local player index. Examples var player = program.InputActionPlayerAt(0); IsObjectBindingAt(int) Whether the input in one slot is an object binding, which the Inspector draws as a field that accepts an object from the Hierarchy. public bool IsObjectBindingAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index The input's position, as AssetInputNameAt(int) takes it. Returns bool True for an object binding. Examples var sceneObject = program.IsObjectBindingAt(0); MessageNameAt(int) The name of one message, for a diagnostic and for the runtime inspector. public string MessageNameAt(int messageId) Parameters Type Name Description int messageId Which message. Returns string The name the script wrote. OwnedObjectIndex(string) The slot one owned-object name addresses. public int OwnedObjectIndex(string name) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name an Object.Create used. Returns int The slot index, or -1 when this script names no owned object by that name. Examples var shield = instance.OwnedObject(program.OwnedObjectIndex("Shield")); OwnedObjectNameAt(int) What one owned-object slot is called. public string OwnedObjectNameAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index The slot. Returns string The name its Object.Create used. Examples var name = program.OwnedObjectNameAt(0); OwnedObjectSurvivesCaller(int) Whether the call that produces one owned-object slot wrote SurvivesCaller(), so the object outlives the instance that produced it and its end only empties the slot. public bool OwnedObjectSurvivesCaller(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index The slot. Returns bool True for a slot whose object outlives its producer. Examples var survives = program.OwnedObjectSurvivesCaller(0); SceneInputNameAt(int) What one scene input is called. The name is what a host's stored scene is matched against and what the Inspector derives its label from. public string SceneInputNameAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Its position in declaration order. Returns string The declared name. Examples var name = program.SceneInputNameAt(0); SyncedTransformChannelAt(int) One transform channel's declaration. public TransformSyncDeclaration SyncedTransformChannelAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Its position in SyncedTransformChannelCount. Returns TransformSyncDeclaration The declaration. SyncedVariableAt(int) One synchronised variable's declaration, by declaration order. public SyncDeclaration SyncedVariableAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Which one, from 0 to SyncedVariableCount minus one. Returns SyncDeclaration The declaration. ToString() One line naming the type and its counts, for a log or a failure message. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "PlayerScript ready=2 frameUpdate=1 watches=1 doubles=2 booleans=1 ...". VariableNames() Names of every variable this script declared, including the shadow slots a watch adds. For diagnostics and the future runtime inspector; never read on the run-time path. public string[] VariableNames() Returns string[] A new array, so a caller cannot change the program. Examples var names = program.VariableNames();

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptRun.title: Class ScriptRunner | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptRun.summary: Class ScriptRunner Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll How one script reaches another on this runner: resolving a target to the instance running on its object, delivering a request to one receiver and an event to its listeners, and the nesting limit both share. public sealed class ScriptRunner Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptRunner Examples var runner = new ScriptRunner(); var program = runner.GetOrBuildProgram(new CountdownScript()); var instance = runner.Spawn(program, new FakeHost(1)); runner.RaiseReady(instance); runner.TickFrameUpdate(); Remarks Delivery is immediate. A request's sections and an event's handlers run inside the sender's block, before the sender's next block, which is what the settled api-local-delivery answer asks for. They run inside the dispatch that is already running, so no public entry point is re-entered. Nothing here allocates on the per-frame path. Resolving a target is a slot read, one dictionary lookup keyed by the object with reference equality, and the incarnation comparison IsLive(ScriptRunner, ScriptInstance, long) makes. An event's listeners are copied into a list kept for each nesting level, which grows once. Filing an instance and adding a listener happen when an instance spawns, which is AGENTS.md rule 31's spawn boundary. docs/proposals/script-communication.md is the contract. Constructors ScriptRunner(int, ScriptContexts) Creates a runner. public ScriptRunner(int expectedInstanceCapacity = 64, ScriptContexts context = ScriptContexts.Runtime) Parameters Type Name Description int expectedInstanceCapacity How many live instances to make room for up front. The list grows past it, at a spawn, which is a boundary where the allocation rule permits allocation; presizing keeps a measured spawn free of that growth. ScriptContexts context Examples var runner = new ScriptRunner(expectedInstanceCapacity: 128); Properties AssetGateway The one gateway this runner's Asset.Load and Asset.Release blocks talk to. Bound Inspector loads do not need a provider. Resources loads need UseProvider(IAssetLoadProvider). Available on runtime and editor runners. public AssetGateway AssetGateway { get; } Property Value AssetGateway Examples runner.AssetGateway.UseProvider(new FakeAssetLoadProvider()); AudioGateway The one audio gateway every instance this runner spawns writes through for one-shots, named bound sources, and mixer writes. Bound playback on the object a script runs on lives on the host instead. public AudioGateway AudioGateway { get; } Property Value AudioGateway Examples var audio = runner.AudioGateway; CameraGateway The one camera gateway every instance this runner spawns writes through. Whoever owns the runner names its backend with UseProvider(ICameraProvider); with none, every camera block writes nothing and says so once. public CameraGateway CameraGateway { get; } Property Value CameraGateway Examples runner.CameraGateway.UseProvider(new FakeCameraProvider()); CloudGateway The one gateway this runner's cloud blocks talk to. Whoever owns the runner names its provider with UseProvider(ICloudSaveProvider); requests made before that are queued, not thrown. TickFrameUpdate() polls it once per frame, before any instance runs, so a completion is observed in the same frame the watches that react to it run in. public CloudSaveGateway CloudGateway { get; } Property Value CloudSaveGateway Examples runner.CloudGateway.UseProvider(new FileCloudSaveProvider(directory)); Context The runner's execution context. Editor Play Mode game runners are Runtime. public ScriptContexts Context { get; } Property Value ScriptContexts Examples var runner = new ScriptRunner(context: ScriptContexts.Editor); Diagnostics Ordinary local observation and control, independent of authored execution. public RunnerDiagnostics Diagnostics { get; } Property Value RunnerDiagnostics Examples var snapshot = runner.Diagnostics.ReadCurrent(target); InputGateway The one input gateway every instance this runner spawns reads through. Whoever owns the runner names its backend with UseProvider(IInputProvider); a script that reads input before that reads the resting value of every action and says so once. public InputGateway InputGateway { get; } Property Value InputGateway Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new FakeInputProvider()); Remarks Resolution happens once per program, at the first spawn of that program, because a declaration names a local player and an action name and both are written in Build(). InstanceCount How many instances this runner is currently running. public int InstanceCount { get; } Property Value int IsPaused True while Time.Pause has set the runner flag. This is what Time.IsPaused reads. It is not whether the time scale is zero. public bool IsPaused { get; } Property Value bool NavigationGateway The one navigation gateway every instance this runner spawns moves actors through. Whoever owns the runner installs its backend with UseProvider(INavigationProvider); with none, every Navigation.MoveTo fails as Denied and says so once. Runtime runners only. public NavigationGateway NavigationGateway { get; } Property Value NavigationGateway Examples runner.NavigationGateway.UseProvider(new FakeNavigationProvider()); NetworkGateway The one netcode gateway every instance this runner spawns talks to. Give it a provider before starting a session. public NetworkGateway NetworkGateway { get; } Property Value NetworkGateway Examples runner.NetworkGateway.UseProvider(new FakeNetworkProvider()); runner.NetworkGateway.StartHost(); Remarks The runner drains this gateway twice per tick: once before the instances run, to refresh authority and apply what arrived, and once after, to send what the cadences say to send. AGENTS.md rule 45 is why the refresh is first: a block that reads Net.HasAuthority reads the answer this tick opened with, and every block in the frame reads the same one. NetworkTicksElapsed How many network ticks this runner has taken, whatever the frame rate is. A tick is counted only on a frame where the session is connected AND at least one instance is bound to a networked object, so a runner that has never had a session reports zero. public int NetworkTicksElapsed { get; } Property Value int Remarks A tick is not one message. One tick produces one stream, sent in as many pieces as the backend's message budget needs, or in none at all when no channel had anything to send. Divide this into a byte total for a per-tick figure; it is not a message count. Read by AGENTS.md rule 47's bandwidth measurement, which divides the bytes a window sent by the ticks that window took. It is a counter rather than a figure derived from elapsed time because the two are not the same: the runner's tick accumulator is driven by its own time source, and a measurement that assumed a tick rate rather than counting ticks would report a per-tick figure for a number of ticks that never happened. That mistake was made and caught on 2026-09-06, by dividing this runner's bytes by a netcode backend's tick count. NetworkedInstanceCount How many instances this runner has bound to a networked object. public int NetworkedInstanceCount { get; } Property Value int ProgramCount How many script types this runner has built. public int ProgramCount { get; } Property Value int RandomSeed The session seed unseeded random streams are derived from. Tests supply one through UseRandomSeed(uint) so a failing run can be replayed. public uint RandomSeed { get; } Property Value uint SceneGateway The scene loads and unloads this runner's scripts start, and the scene phases their When.Scene* watches read. The default runner names UnitySceneProvider; a runner created in code names its own with UseProvider(ISceneProvider). Runtime runners only. public SceneGateway SceneGateway { get; } Property Value SceneGateway Examples runner.SceneGateway.UseProvider(new FakeSceneProvider()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read on an editor runner. TimeSource The clock a rate-capped SyncCadence counts its cooldown down against, and the one the Time surface's blocks read. public ITimeSource TimeSource { get; } Property Value ITimeSource Remarks Time.Scale, Time.IsPaused, Time.SetScale, Time.Pause and Time.Resume need this to be an IGameClock, which UnityTimeSource and TestKit.ManualTimeSource both are; Time.Delta and Time.Elapsed read any clock. UiGateway The one UI Toolkit gateway every instance this runner spawns writes through. Element lookup is spawn-time cache, not per-use Q. public UIGateway UiGateway { get; } Property Value UIGateway Methods BindNetworkObject(ScriptInstance, int) Binds one instance to a networked object, so that it takes part in the network tick: its authority is refreshed every frame, its synchronised variables are sent while it has authority, and messages and updates addressed to that object reach it. public void BindNetworkObject(ScriptInstance instance, int networkObjectId) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance, as Spawn(ScriptProgram, IScriptHost, bool) returned it. int networkObjectId The object's network id, which the netcode backend assigns and which is the same number on every peer. Examples runner.BindNetworkObject(instance, 7); Remarks Called by CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode when Netcode for GameObjects spawns the object, and by a test that pairs two runners by hand. The core knows nothing about how the id is produced; AGENTS.md rule 49. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The instance is null, the id is ScriptInstance.NoNetworkObject, or another live instance already holds that id. Despawn(ScriptInstance) Stops running an instance and keeps it for the next spawn of the same program. public void Despawn(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance to stop. Examples runner.Despawn(instance); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException instance is null. FindNetworkedInstance(int) The instance bound to one network object id, or null when no instance is. public ScriptInstance FindNetworkedInstance(int networkObjectId) Parameters Type Name Description int networkObjectId The id. Returns ScriptInstance The instance, or null. Examples var instance = runner.FindNetworkedInstance(7); GetOrBuildProgram(ScriptBase) Returns the program for this script type, building it the first time it is asked for. public ScriptProgram GetOrBuildProgram(ScriptBase prototype) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptBase prototype An instance of the script type. Build() reads nothing from it, because it is object-independent, but the first object of a script type is the object Build() runs on and the program keeps it as BuiltScript for as long as the program lives; docs/slice-decisions.md D4.42. A later object of the same type reaches nothing: the cached program is returned unchanged. Returns ScriptProgram The one program every object of that script type shares. Examples var program = runner.GetOrBuildProgram(new CountdownScript()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException prototype is null. HasProgram(Type) Whether this runner has already built a program for a script type, without building one. public bool HasProgram(Type scriptType) Parameters Type Name Description Type scriptType The script type to ask about. Returns bool True when GetOrBuildProgram(ScriptBase) would return a cached program. Examples var built = runner.HasProgram(typeof(CountdownScript)); PooledCount(ScriptProgram) How many pooled instances are waiting for a respawn of one program. public int PooledCount(ScriptProgram program) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptProgram program The program to ask about. Returns int The pool's size, or 0 when nothing of that program has been despawned. Examples var pooled = runner.PooledCount(program); RaiseApplication(ApplicationObservation) Delivers one of the five On.Application observations to every enabled instance. public void RaiseApplication(ApplicationObservation observation) Parameters Type Name Description ApplicationObservation observation What Unity reported. Examples runner.RaiseApplication(ApplicationObservation.Paused); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The runner is already dispatching, or it is an editor runner. RaiseCollisionEnter(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.CollisionEnter blocks. Unity raises OnCollisionEnter on the contact component; tests call this without a scene. public void RaiseCollisionEnter(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseCollisionEnter(instance); RaiseCollisionExit(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.CollisionExit blocks. public void RaiseCollisionExit(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseCollisionExit(instance); RaiseCollisionStay(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.CollisionStay blocks. public void RaiseCollisionStay(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseCollisionStay(instance); RaiseReady(ScriptInstance) Delivers Ready once. An action error disables that instance and is reported once. public void RaiseReady(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance Examples runner.RaiseReady(instance); RaiseTriggerEnter(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.TriggerEnter blocks. public void RaiseTriggerEnter(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseTriggerEnter(instance); RaiseTriggerExit(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.TriggerExit blocks. public void RaiseTriggerExit(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseTriggerExit(instance); RaiseTriggerStay(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.TriggerStay blocks. public void RaiseTriggerStay(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseTriggerStay(instance); SetEnabled(ScriptInstance, bool) Turns an instance's per-frame blocks on or off, following the host's own enabled state. Unity owns that state and LunyScript re-implements none of it; AGENTS.md rule 54. public void SetEnabled(ScriptInstance instance, bool enabled) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance. bool enabled Whether its per-frame blocks run. Examples runner.SetEnabled(instance, false); Spawn(ScriptProgram, IScriptHost, bool) Creates or reuses an instance of a program for one host, and starts running it. public ScriptInstance Spawn(ScriptProgram program, IScriptHost host, bool enabled = true) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptProgram program The program to run. IScriptHost host The object the blocks act on. bool enabled Whether the instance's per-frame blocks run from the start. True by default, which is what a test or a direct caller wants. LunyScriptBehaviour passes false and lets Unity's own OnEnable enable it, so that the first activation delivers On.Enabled exactly once and a spawn delivers none. Returns ScriptInstance The instance, enabled and not yet ready. Examples var instance = runner.Spawn(program, new FakeHost(1)); Remarks A fresh instance allocates its slot arrays, which is exactly what SlotBytes predicts plus one array header per SlotArrayCount. A pooled instance allocates nothing: it is rebound to the new host and reset to the program's declared defaults. TickEditorUpdate() Delivers one editor update followed by shared variable watches, without game services. public void TickEditorUpdate() Examples runner.TickEditorUpdate(); TickFixedUpdate() Delivers On.FixedUpdate. Unity runs the fixed step zero to many times per frame, before Update; AGENTS.md rule 54. public void TickFixedUpdate() Examples runner.TickFixedUpdate(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The runner is already dispatching, or it is an editor runner. TickFrameUpdate() Delivers runtime updates. An editor runner must use TickEditorUpdate instead. public void TickFrameUpdate() Examples runner.TickFrameUpdate(); TickLateUpdate() Delivers On.LateUpdate, after every instance's On.Update and its watches have run in the same frame, then checks every C# ScriptObservation once. public void TickLateUpdate() Examples runner.TickLateUpdate(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The runner is already dispatching, or it is an editor runner. UnbindNetworkObject(ScriptInstance) Removes an instance's network binding. Called when the object despawns, and by Despawn(ScriptInstance) for every instance it pools. public void UnbindNetworkObject(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance. Doing this to an instance that has no binding changes nothing. Examples runner.UnbindNetworkObject(instance); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The instance is null. UseRandomSeed(uint) Replaces the session seed used to derive unseeded named streams. A stream declared with an explicit seed ignores this value. public void UseRandomSeed(uint seed) Parameters Type Name Description uint seed The seed a failing test prints so the run can be repeated. Zero becomes 1, because a xorshift state cannot hold zero. Examples runner.UseRandomSeed(42); UseTimeSource(ITimeSource) Replaces the clock this runner reads. A game leaves the default, UnityTimeSource; a test installs TestKit.ManualTimeSource so that a cadence test advances time by a stated amount rather than by however long a frame took. public void UseTimeSource(ITimeSource timeSource) Parameters Type Name Description ITimeSource timeSource The clock. Examples runner.UseTimeSource(new ManualTimeSource()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The clock is null.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptSer.title: Enum ScriptServices | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptSer.summary: Enum ScriptServices Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Services required by composed nodes, independently of their execution contexts. [Flags] public enum ScriptServices Expand Details ... Fields Clock = 8 The owning runner's clock; available in both contexts. EditorPlacementDemo = 32 Provisional selected-placement demo target access; not a general editor service API. EditorUndo = 16 Explicit editor effects with Undo; not provided by the scene-free host. None = 0 Slots and pure calculations need no external service. RuntimeCamera = 512 The runtime camera gateway, which every View and Camera block needs. RuntimeCloud = 2 The runtime cloud gateway, including its pre-provider queue. RuntimeCollision = 8192 Collision queries against a physics world, which GameObjectHost answers from Unity's default physics scene. Every Collision query needs it. RuntimeDocuments = 1024 The runtime document gateway, which every Progress and Settings save and load needs. RuntimeInput = 256 The runtime input gateway, which every Input read and every When.Input watch needs. RuntimeNavigation = 2048 The runtime navigation gateway, which every Navigation block needs. RuntimeNetwork = 4 The runtime network gateway. RuntimeObjectLifetime = 64 Runtime object creation, activation, deactivation and destruction. A host provides it by implementing IScriptObjectLifetime. RuntimeObjectPooling = 4096 Keeps reusable prefab copies in a pool: the host implements IScriptObjectPooler. Object.Spawn needs it. RuntimeObjectSpawning = 128 Runtime object production from a prefab. A host provides it by implementing IScriptObjectSpawner. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Sequence..title: Struct Sequence | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Sequence..summary: Struct Sequence Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A named sequence: several blocks a script declared as one with Define.Sequence, under the name of the property it is assigned to. It converts to a block wherever a block is accepted. public readonly struct Sequence Expand Details ... Examples DodgeRoll = Define.Sequence(Crouch.Set(true), Wait(0.2), Lane.Add(1), Wait(0.4), Crouch.Set(false)); On.Message(Roll, Routine(Dodge).Run(DodgeRoll)); Remarks The name comes from the property. DodgeRoll = Define.Sequence(...) in a partial script's Build() makes the generator write the DodgeRoll property, and that property's setter gives the sequence the name DodgeRoll and the line of the Define call. The debugger shows the sequence as one row with that name, folded, and a diagnostic names it the same way. A sequence does what its blocks would do written out in its place. In an event list, a Then or another list that runs every block at once, it runs its blocks in that frame. As a step of a routine, a group, a Run body or a Choose option's action, each of its blocks finishes before the next begins, and a Wait inside it holds that owner. In a concurrent group it is one child. docs/proposals/sequences.md is the contract. Placed a second time it is a copy, with progress of its own, the rule for every composed block. A Define.Sequence assigned to a local or to a hand-written property has no name, and using it as a block is refused; Sequence(...) is the spelling for a sequence without a name. Methods ToString() The sequence's name, for a log line or a failure message. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "DodgeRoll : sequence of 4 blocks". Operators implicit operator Block(Sequence) The sequence as a block, for any list that takes blocks. public static implicit operator Block(Sequence sequence) Parameters Type Name Description Sequence sequence The named sequence. Returns Block Examples On.Message(Roll, Routine(Dodge).Run(DodgeRoll, Rolls.Inc())); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle was never assigned, or its Define.Sequence line has no name because no generated property received it.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Services..summary: Class UgsCloudSaveProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Services Assembly ApiSource.dll The Unity Gaming Services Cloud Save backend: initialises the services, signs in anonymously, and uploads, downloads and deletes one document per key in the signed-in player's data, all behind IAsyncOperation so the gateway polls and nothing awaits; AGENTS.md rule 51. public sealed class UgsCloudSaveProvider : ICloudSaveProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object UgsCloudSaveProvider Implements ICloudSaveProvider Examples LunyScriptRuntime.DefaultRunner.CloudGateway.UseProvider(new UgsCloudSaveProvider()); Remarks Needs the project to be linked to a Unity Cloud project; the link lives in ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset as cloudProjectId and organizationId. A document is stored as one JSON object under its key, the settled answer "One stored value for the whole document", in the player data a client may write, which Cloud Save calls the Default access class. Every failure is classified once, from RequestFailedException.ErrorCode, into an OperationFailure; a failure that maps to no narrower reason is Unknown and is logged with the original message. The package decides when a request has timed out and reports it as CommonErrorCodes.Timeout; this provider adds no deadline. Methods Delete(string) Starts removing the document stored under a key. public IAsyncOperation Delete(string key) Parameters Type Name Description string key The document's name. Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. It succeeds when no document is stored under the key afterwards, whether or not one was stored before. Remarks Cloud Save reports nothing about a key that holds no data, so a delete of an absent document succeeds. Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines, so that a reader of the Console can tell a real service round trip from a file-based one. Allocates; called only at state transitions, never per frame. public string Describe() Returns string For example: "Unity Cloud Save, signed in as player abc123", or "file-based provider at C:/saves". Load(string) Starts reading the document stored under a key. public ICloudLoadOperation Load(string key) Parameters Type Name Description string key The document's name. Returns ICloudLoadOperation The operation the gateway polls. A key with no stored document completes with OperationFailure.NotFound. Save(string, string) Starts storing one document under its key, replacing any copy stored before. public IAsyncOperation Save(string key, string document) Parameters Type Name Description string key The document's name. The script's build validated it; a provider may refuse a key it cannot store with OperationFailure.Denied. string document The whole document as JSON text. Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. Remarks The JSON text is parsed into an object, so Cloud Save stores the document's fields as fields rather than as one escaped string. SignIn() Starts signing in. Called by the gateway once, when the first request arrives. A provider that needs no sign-in returns an already-completed operation. public IAsyncOperation SignIn() Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SlotKind..summary: Enum SlotKind Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which kind of slot a variable occupies. Fields Color = 8 A colour slot holding a Color: four channels, each stored as Double. Enum = 7 A declared C# enum slot. Storage is the enum's integer code as Int64, not a Number. Flag = 2 A Flag slot. Number = 1 A Number slot. AGENTS.md rule 12: this is the default number type. Rotation = 5 An orientation slot holding a Rotation. Text = 3 A fixed-capacity UTF-8 text slot. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SourceLoc.title: Struct SourceLocation | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SourceLoc.summary: Struct SourceLocation Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Where in a user's script a block was authored: the file and the line of the Build() call that created it. public readonly struct SourceLocation Expand Details ... Examples // Transform.MoveBy captures the caller's file and line, so this block knows it came from here. On.Update(Transform.MoveBy(0.02, 0, 0)); Remarks This is captured at build time and never at failure time, because at failure time the user's line is not on the call stack at all. A block is composed inside Build(), which runs once per script type at launch, and is executed later by ScriptRunner; by the moment it logs or throws, the only frames on the stack are LunyScript's own. [CallerFilePath] and [CallerLineNumber] on the block factory methods are what put the authored line into the block, and this struct is what the block holds. Construction allocates nothing. [CallerFilePath] hands the compiler's own path literal, which lives in the assembly's string table, so this struct stores that reference and an int and does no string work. The project-relative form a user reads is produced by ProjectRelativePath(), which allocates and is called only when a diagnostic is actually produced. That split is what lets every block carry a location without touching the allocation rule; AGENTS.md rule 29. A block built by a C# operator carries Unknown: an operator cannot declare the optional parameters the caller attributes need. health + 1.0 therefore has no location of its own, and the block that consumes it does. Fields Unknown A location that names nothing, which is what a block built by a C# operator carries. public static readonly SourceLocation Unknown Field Value SourceLocation UnknownDescription What Describe() returns for a location that names nothing. public const string UnknownDescription = "an unknown location" Field Value string Properties CompilerPath The path exactly as the compiler recorded it, absolute and unnormalised. public string CompilerPath { get; } Property Value string IsKnown Whether this location names a file and a line. public bool IsKnown { get; } Property Value bool Line The one-based line number of the call that built the block, or 0 when unknown. public int Line { get; } Property Value int Methods Describe() The location as one readable token, for a message a user reads. public string Describe() Returns string Assets/.../SliceScript.cs:45, or a phrase saying the location is unknown. Examples message += $" authored at {location.Describe()}"; Equals(SourceLocation) Indicates whether the current object is equal to another object of the same type. public bool Equals(SourceLocation other) Parameters Type Name Description SourceLocation other An object to compare with this object. Returns bool true if the current object is equal to the other parameter; otherwise, false. Equals(object) Indicates whether this instance and a specified object are equal. public override bool Equals(object obj) Parameters Type Name Description object obj The object to compare with the current instance. Returns bool true if obj and this instance are the same type and represent the same value; otherwise, false. FromCaller(string, int) Builds a location from the caller attributes a factory method declares. Allocates nothing. public static SourceLocation FromCaller(string callerFilePath, int callerLineNumber) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler through [CallerFilePath]. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler through [CallerLineNumber]. Returns SourceLocation The location, or Unknown when the compiler supplied neither. Examples public Block MoveBy(NumberValueBlock x, NumberValueBlock y, NumberValueBlock z, [CallerFilePath] String callerFilePath = null, [CallerLineNumber] Int32 callerLineNumber = 0) => new MoveByBlock(x, y, z, SourceLocation.FromCaller(callerFilePath, callerLineNumber)); GetHashCode() Returns the hash code for this instance. public override int GetHashCode() Returns int A 32-bit signed integer that is the hash code for this instance. ProjectRelativePath() The path with forward slashes and everything above the project's Assets folder removed, which is the form Unity's console resolves to an asset. public string ProjectRelativePath() Returns string The project-relative path, or an empty string when this location is unknown. Examples var path = location.ProjectRelativePath(); // "Assets/CodeSmile/.../SliceScript.cs" Remarks This allocates and is not for the run-time path. It runs when a diagnostic is produced, which is a failure path or a log call, never per frame; AGENTS.md rule 29. A path with no Assets segment is returned with its separators normalised and nothing removed, because a package or a test fixture can legitimately live elsewhere. ToString() Returns the fully qualified type name of this instance. public override string ToString() Returns string The fully qualified type name. ToUnityStackFrame(string) The location written as one Unity stack frame, which is the form Unity's console prints a frame in. public string ToUnityStackFrame(string frameLabel) Parameters Type Name Description string frameLabel What to name the frame, in Unity's Type:Method() shape. Returns string The frame line, or an empty string when this location is unknown. Examples var frame = location.ToUnityStackFrame("CountdownScript:Build()"); Remarks The format is Unity's own, produced by UnityEngine.StackTraceUtility.ExtractFormattedStackTrace: Namespace.Type:Method() (at path:line). Writing the authored location in that format is what lets LunyScriptException present it as the topmost frame, so that the Console prints the user's own line first. It does not move the row's double-click target, which Unity takes from the live call stack at log time; docs/console-navigation.md.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SpawnBuil.title: Struct SpawnBuilder | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SpawnBuil.summary: Struct SpawnBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Object.Spawn(pool) returns: a checkout of one pooled object with no placement of its own yet. Add At(Vector3ValueBlock), ChildOf(string, int), Into(OwnedObject, string, int), ForPlayer(int, string, int) and SurvivesCaller(string, int) in any order, finish with As(Operation) to observe the attempt, or use it as a block. public readonly struct SpawnBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards)); On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards).At(Portal).InRadius(5.0).Into(Escort).As(TakeGuard)); Remarks Where it goes, in order of precedence: the call's own At, then the pool's SpawnAt, then the world position and rotation of the object this script runs on. A call's At replaces the pool's whole placement, spread included, so Object.Spawn(Guards).At(Ambush) is exact and draws no random offset. The use is owned by the instance that spawned it, with or without Into(OwnedObject, string, int), and goes back to its pool when that instance ends. SurvivesCaller(string, int) leaves it with the scene instead. The four builder structs are a typestate, the way the create chain's three are: a shape exists only after At, and a frame modifier only once, so a second At, a shape with no centre and a conflicting frame pair are compile errors. Methods As(Operation) Binds the checkout to an operation handle, so the script can observe whether it succeeded and why it was refused. public Block As(Operation handle) Parameters Type Name Description Operation handle The handle Define.Operation returned. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards).Into(Escort).As(TakeGuard)); Remarks The attempt succeeds when the object is out of the pool and placed, in the drain after this block. It fails as CapacityExhausted when the pool is at its hard cap, and as NotFound when a landmark placement cannot be read; a refused spawn produces nothing and fills no name. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle was never declared, or this builder is a default. At(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock) Places the object at a position given as three numbers, turned the way the prefab is, replacing the pool's own placement. public SpawnPlacedBuilder At(NumberValueBlock x, NumberValueBlock y, NumberValueBlock z) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock x The x of where the object goes. NumberValueBlock y The y of that position. NumberValueBlock z The z of that position. Returns SpawnPlacedBuilder A builder that can take a shape, a frame and the other clauses. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards).At(Column, 0.0, Row)); Remarks The same placement as At(position), with the three numbers as the position's X, Y and Z. They are evaluated where this block runs. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Any number is null, or this builder is a default. At(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, RotationValueBlock) Places the object at a position given as three numbers and turns it, replacing the pool's own placement. public SpawnPlacedBuilder At(NumberValueBlock x, NumberValueBlock y, NumberValueBlock z, RotationValueBlock rotation) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock x The x of where the object goes. NumberValueBlock y The y of that position. NumberValueBlock z The z of that position. RotationValueBlock rotation How it is turned. Returns SpawnPlacedBuilder A builder that can take a shape, a frame and the other clauses. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards).At(0.0, 0.0, 4.0, Rotation.Euler(0.0, 90.0, 0.0))); Remarks The same placement as At(position, rotation), with the three numbers as the position's X, Y and Z. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Any argument is null, or this builder is a default. At(ObjectBinding, string, int) Places the object on a landmark: at its world position and turned by its world rotation, replacing the pool's own placement. The landmark's scale changes nothing. public SpawnPlacedBuilder At(ObjectBinding landmark, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description ObjectBinding landmark An object binding, such as Portal = Bind.Object();. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns SpawnPlacedBuilder A builder that can take a shape, a frame and the other clauses. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards).At(Portal)); Remarks The landmark is sampled where this block runs. A binding that holds no object, and one whose object is inactive, refuses the spawn as NotFound. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException landmark was never declared, another script's Build() declared it, or it is declared as a type with no pose. At(Vector3ValueBlock) Places the object at a position, turned the way the prefab is, replacing the pool's own placement. public SpawnPlacedBuilder At(Vector3ValueBlock position) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3ValueBlock position Where the object goes. Returns SpawnPlacedBuilder A builder that can take a shape, a frame and the other clauses. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards).At(new Vector3(0.0, 0.0, 4.0))); Remarks The expression is evaluated where this block runs. The coordinates are the parent's until InWorldSpace() says otherwise; with no parent the two are the same coordinates. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException position is null, or this builder is a default. At(Vector3ValueBlock, RotationValueBlock) Places the object at a position and turns it, replacing the pool's own placement. public SpawnPlacedBuilder At(Vector3ValueBlock position, RotationValueBlock rotation) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3ValueBlock position Where the object goes. RotationValueBlock rotation How it is turned. Returns SpawnPlacedBuilder A builder that can take a shape, a frame and the other clauses. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards).At(Vector3.Zero, Rotation.Euler(0.0, 90.0, 0.0))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Either expression is null, or this builder is a default. ChildOf(OwnedObject, string, int) Parents the object to an object this script owns. public SpawnBuilder ChildOf(OwnedObject parent, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description OwnedObject parent The owned object Define.Object() declared. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns SpawnBuilder A builder that can still take the clauses it could take before. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Shields).ChildOf(Turret)); Remarks The parent is an owned object this script produced, by Object.Create or Object.Spawn with Into. A parent whose slot is empty when the spawn is applied leaves the object at the scene root and reports it. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException parent is not an owned object this script declared, this chain already names a parent, or this builder is a default. ChildOf(string, int) Parents the object to the object this script runs on. public SpawnBuilder ChildOf(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns SpawnBuilder A builder that can still take the clauses it could take before. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Shields).ChildOf()); Remarks ChildOf cannot parent to itself. ChildOf(OwnedObject, string, int) parents it to an object this script owns instead. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This chain already names a parent, or this builder is a default. ForPlayer(int, string, int) Binds every script the checked-out object starts to one local player. public SpawnBuilder ForPlayer(int localPlayer, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayer The local player number, from 0. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns SpawnBuilder A builder that can still take the clauses it could take before. Examples When.Player(1).Paired(Object.Spawn(Avatars).ForPlayer(1)); Remarks It overrides the Local Player field the prefab's LunyScriptBehaviour carries, for every script that starts an incarnation during this checkout. The binding lasts for that incarnation. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException localPlayer is negative, this chain already names a player, or this builder is a default. Into(OwnedObject, string, int) Holds the checked-out object in one of this script's declared owned objects, so later blocks can deactivate, despawn or destroy it. public SpawnBuilder Into(OwnedObject target, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description OwnedObject target The owned object Define.Object() declared. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns SpawnBuilder A builder that can still take the clauses it could take before. Examples Escort = Define.Object(); On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards).Into(Escort)); Remarks The owned object is an address and nothing else: the use is owned by this instance with or without it, and the object keeps the name the prefab gives it in the scene. When the use ends by any path, the owned object is emptied. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException target is not an owned object this script declared, this chain already names one, another call already produces it, or this builder is a default. SurvivesCaller(string, int) Lets the checked-out object outlive the instance that spawned it: it stays out of the pool until it despawns itself, something ends it, or its scene unloads. public SpawnBuilder SurvivesCaller(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns SpawnBuilder A builder that can still take the clauses it could take before. Examples On.Update(If(Health <= 0).Then(Object.Spawn(Pickups).SurvivesCaller(), Object.Destroy())); Remarks Without it, the use goes back to its pool when this instance ends. With it, Into(OwnedObject, string, int) still addresses the use while this instance runs. A use that survives the caller cannot be a child of the caller, so ChildOf() with this clause is refused while the script type is built. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This chain already says it, or this builder is a default. Operators implicit operator Block(SpawnBuilder) Finishes a spawn that states no placement of its own, so the pool's placement or the caller's pose applies. public static implicit operator Block(SpawnBuilder builder) Parameters Type Name Description SpawnBuilder builder The builder to finish. Returns Block The finished block. Examples Block block = Object.Spawn(Guards); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException builder is a default.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SpawnObje.title: Class SpawnObjectBlock | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SpawnObje.summary: Class SpawnObjectBlock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Object.Spawn(pool) and its chain build: checks one entry out of a declared pool, places it, parents it, and holds it in an owned-object slot when the chain named one. public sealed class SpawnObjectBlock : Block, IScriptNode Expand Details ... Inheritance object Block SpawnObjectBlock Implements IScriptNode Inherited Members Block.Contexts Block.Location Block.ExecuteAll(Block[], ScriptInstance) Block.AdvanceContained(ActionBlock, ScriptInstance) Block.None Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Guards).At(Portal).InRadius(5.0).Into(Escort).As(TakeGuard)); Remarks The block records the spawn; the runner applies it after the current dispatch, for the reason CreatePrefabObjectBlock states: activating an entry runs the scripts it carries, and those re-enter the runner. The placement is evaluated here. The call's own At when it wrote one, otherwise the pool's SpawnAt, otherwise this object's own world position and rotation. A call's At replaces the pool's whole placement, shape included. A disk or sphere draws its random offset when the runner has an entry for the spawn, so a refused spawn draws nothing. A refused spawn produces nothing and fills no name. A pool at its hard cap refuses with CapacityExhausted, and a landmark placement that cannot be read refuses with NotFound. The chain's As(handle) observes that; without it the refusal is reported once per pool and reason. This block itself allocates nothing. It writes one struct into the runner's request list. Properties RequiredServices Services this node requires in addition to its children's requirements. public override ScriptServices RequiredServices { get; } Property Value ScriptServices Examples public override ScriptServices RequiredServices => ScriptServices.Clock; Methods DescribeChildren(NodeDescription) Names the call's placement expressions for the runtime inspector. public override void DescribeChildren(NodeDescription description) Parameters Type Name Description NodeDescription description What to add the children to. Examples block.DescribeChildren(description); Execute(ScriptInstance) Runs this block against one object's state. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SpawnPlac.summary: Struct SpawnPlacement Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Where an authored Object.Spawn puts the object it produces, and in which frame those coordinates are read. public readonly struct SpawnPlacement Expand Details ... Examples var placement = SpawnPlacement.At(new Vector3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), inWorldSpace: true); Remarks A placement carries values, not expressions. The position and rotation expressions are evaluated by SpawnObjectBlock where the block runs, so a placement built from a variable reads that variable at the line the author wrote and not at the moment the runner applies the spawn. The default frame is the parent's. InWorldSpace is false unless the author wrote InWorldSpace(), and a spawn with no parent puts the object at the scene root, where the parent frame and the world frame are the same coordinates. The modifier is spelled the way the settled semantics-t02 answer of 2026-09-13 spells the transform family's, so a script carries one spelling for the frame and not two. A component the author did not name is not written: a spawn that states a position and no rotation leaves the produced object turned the way the prefab is. Properties HasPosition Whether the author named a position. public bool HasPosition { get; } Property Value bool HasRotation Whether the author named a rotation. public bool HasRotation { get; } Property Value bool InWorldSpace Whether the coordinates are world coordinates. False means the parent's frame, which for an object with no parent is the same thing. public bool InWorldSpace { get; } Property Value bool None The placement that names nothing, so the produced object keeps the pose the prefab carries. public static SpawnPlacement None { get; } Property Value SpawnPlacement Examples spawner.SpawnObject(prefab, null, SpawnPlacement.None); Position The position, when HasPosition is true. public Vector3 Position { get; } Property Value Vector3 Rotation The rotation, when HasRotation is true. Never read while HasRotation is false, which is why the placements that name no rotation carry the default value rather than the identity. public Rotation Rotation { get; } Property Value Rotation Methods At(Vector3, Rotation, bool) A placement that names a position and a rotation. public static SpawnPlacement At(Vector3 position, Rotation rotation, bool inWorldSpace) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3 position Where the produced object goes. Rotation rotation How it is turned. bool inWorldSpace True for world coordinates, false for the parent's frame. Returns SpawnPlacement The placement. Examples var placement = SpawnPlacement.At(Vector3.Zero, Rotation.Euler(0.0, 90.0, 0.0), true); At(Vector3, bool) A placement that names a position. public static SpawnPlacement At(Vector3 position, bool inWorldSpace) Parameters Type Name Description Vector3 position Where the produced object goes. bool inWorldSpace True for world coordinates, false for the parent's frame. Returns SpawnPlacement The placement. Examples var placement = SpawnPlacement.At(new Vector3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), false); ToString() What this placement names, for a log line or a failure message. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "at (0, 1, 0) in the parent's frame".

A pool spawn carries its placement in CodeSmile.LunyScript.SpawnRequest.PoolPlacement instead. public SpawnPlacement Placement { get; } Property Value SpawnPlacement PrefabName The input's declared name, or the pool's, which is what a diagnostic names. public string PrefabName { get; } Property Value string PrefabSlotIndex The asset slot the declared prefab input occupies on the instance. public int PrefabSlotIndex { get; } Property Value int SurvivesCaller Whether the produced object outlives the instance that asked for it. public bool SurvivesCaller { get; } Property Value bool

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.State.htm.summary: Struct State Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One state of one state machine. Examples (Phases, Calm, Angry) = Define.StateMachine(nameof(Phases)).WithStates(nameof(Calm), nameof(Angry)); Phases.Initial(Calm); Phases.From(Calm).To(Angry).When(Health < 50); Remarks A state is passed to its machine's calls: Phases.State(Calm), Phases.From(Calm).To(Angry), Phases.To(Defeated), Phases.Initial(Calm) and Phases.IsIn(Calm). reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.StateBuil.summary: Struct StateBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What machine.State(state) returns: the state's Enter, Update and Exit lists, written in that order and each at most once, or an internal transition with When(ConditionBlock, string, int). public readonly struct StateBuilder Expand Details ... Examples Phases.State(Angry).Enter(Speed.Set(3)).Update(Transform.RotateBy(0, 90, 0)).Exit(Speed.Set(1)); Phases.State(Angry).When(HitTaken).Do(HitTaken.Set(false), Flashes.Inc()); Remarks Enter runs when the machine enters the state, and the Routine, Choose or Run it starts belongs to the state: the machine advances that work on its own tick and cancels it when it leaves the state. Update runs once per pass in which no transition is chosen, after that work. Exit runs when the machine leaves the state. Each list runs its blocks at once, so a Wait or an InParallel group in one is refused when the script type is built. Methods Enter(params Block[]) The blocks that run when the machine enters this state, in the call that enters it. public StateEnterDeclaration Enter(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. A Routine, Choose or Run started here belongs to the state. Returns StateEnterDeclaration The state, which may take Update and Exit. Examples Phases.State(Angry).Enter(Speed.Set(3), Routine(Roar).Run(Roaring.Set(true), Wait(1), Roaring.Set(false))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The list is null, empty or holds a null, this state's Enter was already written, or this builder was never obtained from machine.State(state). Exit(params Block[]) The blocks that run when the machine leaves this state, after the work Enter started is cancelled. public void Exit(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. Examples Phases.State(Desperate).Exit(Speed.Set(0)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The list is null, empty or holds a null, this state's Exit was already written, or this builder was never obtained from machine.State(state). Returns StateUpdateDeclaration The state, which may take Exit. The state keeps the work it started, and neither Exit nor Enter runs. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.StateMach.summary: Struct StateMachine Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A flat state machine: one current state per object, transitions read in the order they were written, and the lists each state runs when it is entered, while it is current and when it is left. public readonly struct StateMachine Expand Details ... Examples (Phases, Calm, Angry) = Define.StateMachine(nameof(Phases)).WithStates(nameof(Calm), nameof(Angry)); Phases.Initial(Calm); Phases.State(Angry).Enter(Speed.Set(3)).Exit(Speed.Set(1)); Phases.From(Calm).To(Angry).When(Health < 50); On.Ready(Phases.Start()); Remarks Declared with its states on one line inside Build(); the generator writes a property for the machine and one for each state. Every call on the handle is written inside Build(). Start() and Stop() return blocks, IsIn and IsRunning return conditions, and the rest declare the machine. A pass runs on the machine's tick, the frame update unless InFixedUpdate(string, int) or InLateUpdate(string, int) is written. It reads the transitions first and does the current state's work only when none is chosen. docs/proposals/state-machine.md is the contract. Properties IsDeclared False for a handle Build() never assigned. public bool IsDeclared { get; } Property Value bool IsRunning True while this machine runs: after a Start and before a Stop. public ConditionBlock IsRunning { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Update(If(!Phases.IsRunning).Then(Phases.Start())); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Name The name the script declared, which nameof produced. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods CascadeLimit(int, string, int) The most state changes one pass commits. The default, 1, ends the pass at every change, and the new state's work runs in the next pass. Above 1 the pass continues with the new state, and stops before a change back to a state it already visited. public StateMachine CascadeLimit(int limit, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description int limit 1 to 100, or 0 for the ceiling of 100. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns StateMachine This machine, so another configuration call can follow. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns StateTransitionFromBuilder The transition's source, which takes To. InFixedUpdate(string, int) Runs this machine's pass in each fixed step, after On.FixedUpdate, so a Motion write in a state's Update list is in the step Motion requires. At a time scale of zero no fixed step runs. public StateMachine InFixedUpdate(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns StateMachine This machine, so another configuration call can follow. Examples Movement.InFixedUpdate(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(), or the machine's tick was already written. InLateUpdate(string, int) Runs this machine's pass in the late update, after On.LateUpdate. public StateMachine InLateUpdate(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns StateMachine This machine, so another configuration call can follow. Examples Follow.InLateUpdate(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(), or the machine's tick was already written. Initial(State, string, int) Names the state Start(string, int) enters. Every machine names one, once. public StateMachine Initial(State state, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description State state One of this machine's states. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns StateMachine This machine, so another configuration call can follow. Examples Phases.Initial(Calm); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(), a second time, or with a state of another machine. IsIn(State, string, int) True while this machine runs and the state is current. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns ConditionBlock A condition to pass to If or When. Start(string, int) The block that starts this machine, or restarts it: a running machine leaves its current state the way Stop(string, int) does, then enters the initial state. The initial state's Enter runs in the same call; the machine's first pass is on its next tick. public Block Start(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns StateBuilder The state, which takes Enter, Update, Exit or When. Examples Phases.State(Angry).Enter(Speed.Set(3)).Update(Transform.RotateBy(0, 90, 0)).Exit(Speed.Set(1)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(), or with a state of another machine. Stop(string, int) The block that stops this machine: it cancels the work the current state started and runs that state's Exit. A machine that is not running is left as it is. public Block Stop(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns StateTransitionBuilder The transition, which takes When. Each pass reads the transitions in the order they were written and chooses the first whose source is the current state and whose condition is true. public StateTransition When(ConditionBlock condition, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition Read at most once per pass, and only while no earlier transition was chosen. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler.
