reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Store.htm.summary: Struct Store Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A declared shared-variable store: a group of shared Number, Flag, Vector3 and Text variables that every script on the runner which names the store reads and writes as one slot per name. public readonly struct Store Expand Details ... Examples MatchData = Define.Store(); Score = Define.Number(nameof(Score), 0).Shared(MatchData); Remarks MatchData = Define.Store(); declares one, and .Shared(MatchData) on a Define or Bind line places a variable on it. Another script names the same store through the generated descriptor, MatchScript.Stores.MatchData. Its identity is the script type that declared it and its name, so two scripts that each declare their own MatchData hold two stores. .Shared() with no argument is the default store, which needs no declaration. A store lives as long as its runner. docs/proposals/declared-identity-handles.md is the contract. Properties IsDeclared Whether this handle names a declared store. public bool IsDeclared { get; } Property Value bool Examples if (MatchData.IsDeclared) { } Name The name the store was declared with, or null before it has one. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Examples var name = MatchData.Name; Methods As(string, string, int) Names a store a hand-written property or a local holds, which the generator does not name. public Store As(string name, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name; use nameof of the property. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Store The named store. Examples MatchData = Define.Store().As(nameof(MatchData)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(), on a store that already has a name, or with an empty name or one this script already uses. ToString() How a diagnostic names this store: MatchScript.MatchData. public override string ToString() Returns string The declaring script and the name.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncCaden.title: Struct SyncCadence | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncCaden.summary: Struct SyncCadence Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll How often one synchronised variable is sent. Declared per variable, because AGENTS.md rule 46 says synchronised state is declared one variable at a time and there is no networked struct and no state object to put two variables into. public readonly struct SyncCadence Expand Details ... Examples Health = Var.DefineSynced<Number>(nameof(Health), SyncCadence.OnChangeCapped(10.0), 100.0); Remarks The cadence is a required parameter, not a default. There is no way to declare a synchronised variable without naming what it costs, which is the compile-time half of rule 46: a never-changing player name and a per-tick value cannot share a payload, because there is nowhere to put them together. A rate cap caps sends, not writes. The authority's own value is always current; a peer sees at most MaxPerSecond updates and therefore may hold a stale value between them. That is latency as a state, per rule 45, and it is reported rather than hidden. Fields EveryTick Sent every network tick, changed or not. For a continuously varying value a peer interpolates. public static readonly SyncCadence EveryTick Field Value SyncCadence Kind Which of the three kinds this is. public readonly SyncKind Kind Field Value SyncKind MaxPerSecond The rate cap in sends per second, or 0 for no cap. Only meaningful when Kind is OnChange. public readonly double MaxPerSecond Field Value double OnChange Sent whenever the value changed since the last send. The cadence to reach for, and still written out, because a cadence chosen by omission is a cadence nobody reviewed. public static readonly SyncCadence OnChange Field Value SyncCadence Once Sent once, the first time the value is known, and never again. For a name, a team or a colour chosen when a player joins. public static readonly SyncCadence Once Field Value SyncCadence Properties IsRateCapped Whether this cadence caps its send rate. public bool IsRateCapped { get; } Property Value bool Methods OnChangeCapped(double) Sent when the value changed, and no more often than the cap allows. For a value that can change in a burst, such as health under rapid damage, where every intermediate value is not worth a packet. public static SyncCadence OnChangeCapped(double maxPerSecond) Parameters Type Name Description double maxPerSecond Sends per second. Must be greater than zero. Returns SyncCadence The cadence. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The cap is zero or negative, which would either mean "never send", written as not synchronising the variable at all, or is a sign error. ToString() Names the cadence for a log line and for the Block Inspector. Allocates; called at build time and at state transitions, never per tick. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "OnChange, at most 10 per second".

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncDecla.title: Struct SyncDeclaration | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncDecla.summary: Struct SyncDeclaration Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One synchronised variable, as the script declared it: which slot holds it, how often it is sent, and the bookkeeping slots the cadence and the staleness reading need. Recorded at build time, read by the program, and never changed afterwards. public readonly struct SyncDeclaration Expand Details ... Remarks One of these per synchronised variable, which is what AGENTS.md rule 46 requires: state is declared one variable at a time, and there is no networked struct that could carry two of them. This type is that rule expressed in the build output, and it is deliberately not a grouping: nothing here can hold a second variable. The cadence's own state lives in slots, not in fields on this struct. AGENTS.md rule 23: all per-object state is a slot allocated at build time. One declaration is shared by every object running the script, so "the value I last sent" and "how long until I may send again" are per-object facts and belong in the instance. What this struct carries is the addresses of those slots, which are the same for every object. Constructors SyncDeclaration(string, SlotKind, TextCapacity, int, int, int, int, int, SyncCadence) Builds a declaration. public SyncDeclaration(string name, SlotKind kind, TextCapacity capacity, int slotIndex, int shadowSlotIndex, int sentSlotIndex, int cooldownSlotIndex, int stalenessSlotIndex, SyncCadence cadence) Parameters Type Name Description string name The variable's name. SlotKind kind Which kind of slot holds the value. TextCapacity capacity How many bytes a text slot holds; ignored for the other kinds. int slotIndex Which slot of that kind holds the value. int shadowSlotIndex Which slot of that kind holds the last sent value. int sentSlotIndex Which Flag slot records that a send has happened. int cooldownSlotIndex Which Number slot counts down to the next permitted send, or -1 when the cadence carries no rate cap. int stalenessSlotIndex Which Number slot counts seconds since the last received value. SyncCadence cadence How often the value is sent. Fields Cadence How often the value is sent. public readonly SyncCadence Cadence Field Value SyncCadence Capacity How many bytes the text slot holds, for Text. Unused and default for the other two kinds. public readonly TextCapacity Capacity Field Value TextCapacity CooldownSlotIndex Which Number slot counts down the seconds until a rate-capped cadence may send again, or -1 when the cadence carries no rate cap. public readonly int CooldownSlotIndex Field Value int Kind Which kind of slot holds the value. public readonly SlotKind Kind Field Value SlotKind Name The variable's name, for diagnostics and for the Block Inspector. public readonly string Name Field Value string SentSlotIndex Which Flag slot records that this peer has sent the value at least once since the last peer joined. It is what makes the first send happen even when the value still equals its declared default, and what a join resets so that a late joiner receives a SyncCadence.Once value it was not there for. public readonly int SentSlotIndex Field Value int ShadowSlotIndex Which slot of that kind holds the value this peer last sent. Compared against the value to decide whether SyncCadence.OnChange has anything to send. public readonly int ShadowSlotIndex Field Value int SlotIndex Which slot of that kind holds the value the script reads and writes. public readonly int SlotIndex Field Value int StalenessSlotIndex Which Number slot counts the seconds since this peer last received a value for the variable. Read by Net.SecondsSinceUpdate, and held at zero on the peer with authority, whose own value is never stale. public readonly int StalenessSlotIndex Field Value int Remarks AGENTS.md rule 45: latency is a state a script may read, not an exception it handles. A rate-capped or Once variable is stale between sends by design, and this is where a script can see by how much rather than having to assume. Properties CooldownSlot The slot counting down to the next permitted send. Only meaningful when IsRateCapped is true. public NumberSlot CooldownSlot { get; } Property Value NumberSlot FlagSlot The value slot, for a Flag variable. public FlagSlot FlagSlot { get; } Property Value FlagSlot NumberSlot The value slot, for a Number variable. public NumberSlot NumberSlot { get; } Property Value NumberSlot SentSlot The slot recording that the value has been sent at least once. public FlagSlot SentSlot { get; } Property Value FlagSlot ShadowFlagSlot The last-sent slot, for a Flag variable. public FlagSlot ShadowFlagSlot { get; } Property Value FlagSlot ShadowNumberSlot The last-sent slot, for a Number variable. public NumberSlot ShadowNumberSlot { get; } Property Value NumberSlot ShadowTextSlot The last-sent slot, for a Text variable. public TextSlot ShadowTextSlot { get; } Property Value TextSlot StalenessSlot The slot counting seconds since the last received value. public NumberSlot StalenessSlot { get; } Property Value NumberSlot TextSlot The value slot, for a Text variable. public TextSlot TextSlot { get; } Property Value TextSlot Methods ToString() Names the declaration for a diagnostic. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "Health (Number, OnChange, at most 10 per second)".

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncFacto.title: Struct SyncFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncFacto.summary:
Struct SyncFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Sync surface: which parts of an object's transform cross the network, and how often each one is sent. public readonly struct SyncFactory Expand Details ... Examples protected override void Build() { Sync.Position(SyncCadence.EveryTick); Sync.Rotation(SyncCadence.OnChange); Sync.Scale(SyncCadence.Once); } Remarks One call per channel, each with its own cadence, which is AGENTS.md rule 46 applied to the transform. There is no "synchronise the transform" switch, for the reason rule 46 gives for there being no networked struct: a scale that never changes would otherwise share a payload with a position that changes every tick, and the cost of the second would be paid for the first. What the channels carry crosses as one stream per authority per network tick, not as one message per object; rule 47, and docs/netcode-bandwidth.md is the measurement that rule requires. Methods Position(SyncCadence) Synchronises the object's world position. public void Position(SyncCadence cadence) Parameters Type Name Description SyncCadence cadence How often it is sent. Required, so that a position whose cost nobody chose cannot be synchronised. Examples Sync.Position(SyncCadence.EveryTick); Remarks The position is sent as the change since the last one sent, in 6 bytes, and as an absolute position in 12 whenever the change is too large to encode or a peer has just joined. Only the authority may move an object whose position is synchronised; a move on any other peer is refused, and the diagnostic names what to write instead. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The cadence is unset, or this script already declared this channel. Rotation(SyncCadence) Synchronises the object's world rotation. public void Rotation(SyncCadence cadence) Parameters Type Name Description SyncCadence cadence How often it is sent. Examples Sync.Rotation(SyncCadence.OnChange); Remarks Sent as a quaternion compressed into 4 bytes: the two-bit index of its largest component and the other three at ten bits each. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The cadence is unset, or this script already declared this channel. Scale(SyncCadence) Synchronises the object's local scale. public void Scale(SyncCadence cadence) Parameters Type Name Description SyncCadence cadence How often it is sent. Examples Sync.Scale(SyncCadence.Once); Remarks Sent as three half-precision values, 6 bytes. A scale that is chosen once and never changed is declared with SyncCadence.Once and then costs nothing per tick.

Each axis must be between -65504 and 65504, which is what the 16-bit encoding holds. This channel sends the value rather than a change, so unlike a position it has no second form to fall back to: an object scaled outside that range has its scale sent to nobody, every peer keeps the last scale that was inside the range, and the runner writes one warning naming the object, its scale and the bound. That warning is written once for an object and not again: a scale that leaves the range later is refused the same way and in silence, because composing the message on a path that repeats would allocate.

Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The cadence is unset, or this script already declared this channel.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncKind..title: Enum SyncKind | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncKind..summary: Enum SyncKind Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The three kinds of cadence. A rate cap is a property of OnChange rather than a fourth kind, because a capped and an uncapped OnChange send on the same condition and differ only in how often. public enum SyncKind Expand Details ... Fields EveryTick = 3 Sent every network tick. None = 0 Not synchronised. The value a default SyncCadence reads as, so an unset cadence cannot be mistaken for Once. OnChange = 2 Sent when the value changed, optionally rate capped. Once = 1 Sent once and never again.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Text.html.title: Struct Text | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Text.html.summary: Struct Text Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A text variable of a script: a handle to one text slot. Build() declares it, and its methods build blocks. public readonly struct Text Expand Details ... Examples PlayerName = Define.Text(nameof(PlayerName)); On.Ready(PlayerName.Set("Player One")); Remarks A Text is a handle, not the characters. Each object running the script keeps its own slot. Declared without a byte count, the slot is one System.String that grows with what is written into it: writing the characters it already holds allocates nothing, and writing different characters allocates the new string. Declared with a TextCapacity, the slot is a fixed string that never allocates and refuses text that does not fit. A String literal is written into it with Set("..."); a String never converts to a handle on its own, so Debug.Log("msg" + variable) cannot become a block (AGENTS.md rule 40). A partial script declares text on one line inside Build(), and the generator writes the property: Label = Define.Text(nameof(Label));. Fields MaxLiteralBytes Largest text literal a script can write into a fixed text, compare with one, or place in a Text.Format, in UTF-8 bytes: such a literal is stored in a FixedString512Bytes inside the block. A literal written into or compared with a growing text has no such limit. public const int MaxLiteralBytes = 509 Field Value int Properties Capacity How many bytes this variable holds when it was declared with a byte count. Zero, which is no TextCapacity member, for a text that grows; TextSlot.IsAllocating is true for one. public TextCapacity Capacity { get; } Property Value TextCapacity Examples var capacity = PlayerName.Capacity; Kind Which slot array on the instance this variable lives in: Text, or Undefined before Build() assigns the handle. public SlotKind Kind { get; } Property Value SlotKind Examples var kind = PlayerName.Kind; Name The declared name, used in diagnostics and by the runtime debugger. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Examples var name = PlayerName.Name; TextSlot This variable's slot, including its declared capacity. public TextSlot TextSlot { get; } Property Value TextSlot Examples var slot = PlayerName.TextSlot; Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle is unassigned. Methods Clear(string, int) Builds a block that empties this variable. public Block Clear(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Ready(Log.Clear()); Equals(object) True when both handles address the same slot. public override bool Equals(object obj) Parameters Type Name Description object obj A Text or a Var<Text>. Returns bool Whether the handles are equal. Format(string, params TextArgument[]) Builds a text value out of a format and the values that fill its holes, for a text variable's Set. public static TextFormat Format(string format, params TextArgument[] arguments) Parameters Type Name Description string format The text to write, with {0} where the first value goes, {1} the second, and so on. A number hole may ask for a fixed number of decimal places, written {0:2}. A literal brace is written {{ or }}. TextArgument[] arguments One value per hole: a number, a flag or a text variable. Literals of those kinds convert on their own. Returns TextFormat The parsed format, which a text variable's Set takes. Examples On.Update(Label.Set(Text.Format("{0:1}/{1} hp", Health, MaxHealth))); Remarks What a number hole prints. With no decimal count, up to six decimal places with trailing zeros removed, so a whole number prints with no decimal point at all. With a count, exactly that many places, rounding a midpoint to the nearer even digit the way Math.Round does. NaN prints as NaN and an infinity as Infinity or -Infinity. A magnitude at or above 9,000,000,000,000,000,000 is printed through Unity's own single-precision formatter, which is the one case where the printed digits are not the Double's. What a flag hole prints is true or false. A text hole copies the variable's bytes in. The format is parsed once per script type, inside Build(). Writing the result per frame appends into a buffer the size of the destination variable and allocates nothing; text that does not fit the destination is refused the same way Set refuses a literal that is too long. Inside a script, Text.Format reaches the same call through the script's Text member. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The format is null or malformed, an argument is null or carries no value, or a hole names an argument that was not passed. GetHashCode() Returns the hash code for this instance. public override int GetHashCode() Returns int A 32-bit signed integer that is the hash code for this instance. Join(string, string, int) Starts a text built from parts, each written while its condition holds, for a text variable's Set: a sentence whose wording depends on several values, written as one block in place of one If branch per combination of those values. public static TextJoinBuilder Join(string separator, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string separator The text written between two written parts, such as ", "; "" writes the parts next to each other. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one: this is the line this call's refusals name. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns TextJoinBuilder A builder whose Part adds the first part. Examples On.Update(Augments.Set(Text.Join(", ") .Part(RingVolley, "Ring volley") .Part(MineLayer, "Mine layer") .Else("none"))); Remarks Each time the block that writes the join runs, it tests every part's condition once, in the order the parts were written, and writes the text of each part whose condition holds, with the separator between two written parts. Else names the text written when no condition holds; without it, the empty text is written then. A part's text is a literal, written as it is, or a Text.Format or another join, whose values are read when the part is written. Writing a join into a fixed text allocates nothing, and writing one into a growing text allocates only when the composed characters change, as for Text.Format. Inside a script, Text.Join reaches the same call through the script's Text member. A join is started while a script's Build() runs, from the script or from a helper it calls, because Build() refuses a join that was started and never finished with Else or by being used as a text. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException separator is null or longer than MaxLiteralBytes UTF-8 bytes, or no script's Build() is running. Set(CollectionRead, string, int) Builds a block that writes one collection entry into this variable. public Block Set(CollectionRead value, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description CollectionRead value A list or map text read. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Update(Label.Set(Labels.At(0))); Set(InputControlText, string, int) Builds a block that writes the control path an input action or part uses now into this variable, such as <Keyboard>/space, for a settings row. public Block Set(InputControlText value, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description InputControlText value An action's or a part's BoundControl. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Writing it every frame allocates nothing. Examples On.Update(FireKey.Set(Fire.BoundControl)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException value is a default one no BoundControl produced. Set(Text, string, int) Builds a block that copies another text variable into this one. public Block Set(Text other, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Text other The text variable to copy. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Ready(Shown.Set(PlayerName)); Set(TextFormat, string, int) Builds a block that writes a formatted text into this variable. public Block Set(TextFormat format, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description TextFormat format A format from Format(string, params TextArgument[]). string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Update(Label.Set(Text.Format("{0} hp", Health))); Set(UiText, string, int) Builds a block that writes a Label or TextField's current text into this variable. public Block Set(UiText value, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description UiText value The UI text to read. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples When.UI(nameField).ValueChanged(PlayerName.Set(nameField.Text)); Set(string, string, int) Builds a block that writes a literal into this variable. public Block Set(string value, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string value The characters. Null writes the empty string. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Ready(PlayerName.Set("Player One")); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This is a fixed text and the literal needs more than MaxLiteralBytes UTF-8 bytes. ToString() Returns the fully qualified type name of this instance. public override string ToString() Returns string The fully qualified type name. Operators operator ==(Text, Text) Builds a condition that is true when two text variables hold the same characters. It does not compare handles; Equals(object) does. public static ConditionBlock operator ==(Text left, Text right) Parameters Type Name Description Text left A text variable. Text right A text variable. Returns ConditionBlock A condition block. Examples On.Update(If(Typed == Answer).Then(Solved.Set(true))); operator ==(Text, string) Builds a condition that is true when this variable holds exactly these characters, compared ordinally. public static ConditionBlock operator ==(Text left, string right) Parameters Type Name Description Text left The text variable. string right The literal. Returns ConditionBlock A condition block. Examples On.Update(If(PlayerName == "Admin").Then(Admin.Set(true))); operator ==(string, Text) The literal-first spelling of the equality condition. public static ConditionBlock operator ==(string left, Text right) Parameters Type Name Description string left The literal. Text right The text variable. Returns ConditionBlock A condition block. Examples On.Update(If("Admin" == PlayerName).Then(Admin.Set(true))); implicit operator Text(Var<Text>) Converts a handle from the generic factory to the same variable's Text handle. public static implicit operator Text(Var<Text> variable) Parameters Type Name Description Var<Text> variable The generic handle. Returns Text The same variable. Examples Text label = program.FindVariable<Text>(nameof(Label)); operator !=(Text, Text) Builds a condition that is true when two text variables differ. public static ConditionBlock operator !=(Text left, Text right) Parameters Type Name Description Text left A text variable. Text right A text variable. Returns ConditionBlock A condition block. Examples On.Update(If(Typed != Answer).Then(Solved.Set(false))); operator !=(Text, string) Builds a condition that is true when this variable does not hold exactly these characters. public static ConditionBlock operator !=(Text left, string right) Parameters Type Name Description Text left The text variable. string right The literal. Returns ConditionBlock A condition block. Examples On.Update(If(PlayerName != "").Then(Named.Set(true))); operator !=(string, Text) The literal-first spelling of the inequality condition. public static ConditionBlock operator !=(string left, Text right) Parameters Type Name Description string left The literal. Text right The text variable. Returns ConditionBlock A condition block. Examples On.Update(If("" != PlayerName).Then(Named.Set(true)));

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TextArgum.title: Struct TextArgument | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TextArgum.summary: Struct TextArgument Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One value a Text.Format call fills a hole with. Returns TextArgument The argument that carries it. Examples Label.Set(Text.Format("{0}", Alive.IsTrue())); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException value is null. implicit operator TextArgument(Number) Takes a number variable as a format argument. public static implicit operator TextArgument(Number variable) Parameters Type Name Description Number variable The variable to read. Returns TextArgument The argument that carries it. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TextCapac.summary: Enum TextCapacity Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll How many bytes a text variable can hold. Declared per variable at build time, because the five capacities are five distinct Unity.Collections.FixedString types and a text variable is stored in exactly one of them. public enum TextCapacity Expand Details ... Fields Bytes128 = 128 A FixedString128Bytes slot: 128 bytes of storage, 125 usable. Bytes32 = 32 A FixedString32Bytes slot: 32 bytes of storage, 29 usable. Bytes4096 = 4096 A FixedString4096Bytes slot: 4096 bytes of storage, 4093 usable. Bytes512 = 512 A FixedString512Bytes slot: 512 bytes of storage, 509 usable. Bytes64 = 64 A FixedString64Bytes slot: 64 bytes of storage, 61 usable. Examples var playerName = Var.DefineText("playerName", TextCapacity.Bytes64); Remarks AGENTS.md rule 15: Var.DefineText defaults to Bytes64, because 64 bytes is a common cache-line size, and that default is what a caller gets when the content has no known size. Choosing a different capacity deliberately is still the right thing when the content is known to be shorter or longer than the 61 usable bytes of Bytes64; what the enum exists to prevent is one size being imposed on every text variable with no way to change it. Above Bytes4096 there is no fixed string, and that case needs a fallback that is allowed to allocate and allowed to be non-networked. Define.Text(name).Allocating(maxBytes) is that fallback. The usable payload of each size is three bytes less than the name says: two bytes hold the length and one holds a terminating zero. UsableBytes(TextCapacity) returns the usable figure rather than the name's figure.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TextLengt.title: Enum TextLength | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TextLengt.summary: Enum TextLength Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Named byte bounds for each Text entry in a list or map. Declared per collection side at build time, because the five sizes are five distinct Unity.Collections.FixedString types and every entry on that side uses exactly one of them. public enum TextLength Expand Details ... Fields L = 512 512 storage bytes, 509 usable UTF-8 bytes. Fits 509 one-byte characters or 127 four-byte characters. M = 128 128 storage bytes, 125 usable UTF-8 bytes. Fits 125 one-byte characters or 31 four-byte characters. S = 64 64 storage bytes, 61 usable UTF-8 bytes. Fits 61 one-byte characters or 15 four-byte characters. XL = 4096 4096 storage bytes, 4093 usable UTF-8 bytes. Fits 4093 one-byte characters or 1023 four-byte characters. XS = 32 32 storage bytes, 29 usable UTF-8 bytes. Fits 29 one-byte characters or 7 four-byte characters. This is the default for a collection Text side that omits KeyLength or ValueLength. Examples Scores = Define.Map<Text, Number>(nameof(Scores), 8).KeyLength(TextLength.S); Labels = Define.List<Text>(nameof(Labels), 4).ValueLength(TextLength.M); Remarks The default is XS, the smallest step. Each step documents both its storage byte count and how many UTF-8 characters fit: one-byte characters fill the usable payload, four-byte characters fill a quarter of it. Usable payload is three bytes less than storage: two bytes hold the length and one holds a terminating zero. Collection text uses these named steps through KeyLength and ValueLength. Variable text still uses TextCapacity.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TimeFacto.title: Struct TimeFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TimeFacto.summary: Struct TimeFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Time surface a script reads the game clock through, and the one place a script changes how fast that clock runs: Delta, Elapsed, Scale, IsPaused, SetScale(NumberValueBlock, string, int), Pause(string, int) and Resume(string, int). public readonly struct TimeFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Update(Age.Add(Time.Delta)); On.Update(If(Health <= 0.0).Then(Time.Pause())); Remarks The scaled clock is the default and real time carries the word. Time.Delta is game time, so a game running in slow motion sees a smaller number and a paused game sees zero; Time.Delta.Unscaled() is real time, which neither the scale nor a pause changes. The modifier follows the verb and only the unusual case is written out, which is the same grammar a transform verb's frame uses. It applies to both readings and to nothing else here: a scale has no clock to choose, so Time.Scale and Time.IsPaused return types that carry no Unscaled and Time.Scale.Unscaled() does not compile. Pausing sets the runner flag and zeros the time scale. Time.IsPaused reads the flag. Pausable scripts skip process events while it is set, apart from the six contact events, which reach them unless the project setting "Time.Pause pauses contact events" is on; WhenPaused and Always scripts keep ticking. On.FixedUpdate still does not run at scale zero, because Unity's fixed step is driven by game time. A pause menu declares SetProcessMode(Process.WhenPaused) and reads Time.Delta.Unscaled(). docs/execution-model.md, "Pause and the game clock", is the whole contract. The scale is the game's, not this object's. One script pausing pauses everything, because that is what a time scale is. Nothing here is per object, and nothing here is synchronised: a peer that pauses its own game pauses only its own, and the network keeps ticking while it is paused, because the other peers are still playing. This is the running game's clock. Every member is runtime-only, so a script built for an explicitly owned editor runner cannot use them; that runner's clock governs no game and has no scale to read or stop. EditorTime.Elapsed() is the editor session's own reading, and docs/editor-foundation.md owns that boundary. Properties Delta How many seconds the previous frame took, in game time. public TimeReadBlock Delta { get; } Property Value TimeReadBlock Examples On.Update(Age.Add(Time.Delta)); Remarks Scaled, so it is smaller in slow motion and zero while paused. Write Time.Delta.Unscaled() for the real-time frame length, which a pause does not change. This is the number a per-second rate is written with: Health.Add(-Drain * Time.Delta) loses Drain health per second whatever the frame rate is. Elapsed How many seconds of game time have passed since the run started. public TimeReadBlock Elapsed { get; } Property Value TimeReadBlock Examples On.Update(If(Time.Elapsed > 60.0).Then(Overtime.Set(true))); Remarks Scaled, so it stops advancing while the game is paused and advances at half speed at a scale of one half. Write Time.Elapsed.Unscaled() for real time, which keeps advancing while paused. IsPaused True while the runner paused flag is set, which is what Time.Pause writes. public ConditionBlock IsPaused { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.Update(If(!Time.IsPaused).Then(Score.Add(1.0))); Remarks This is a condition, so it goes into If(...) and is negated with !. It reads the runner flag rather than testing whether the time scale is zero: Time.SetScale(0) stops the clock and does not set the flag. Scale How fast game time runs against real time: one at ordinary speed, one half in slow motion, zero while paused. public NumberValueBlock Scale { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.Update(If(Time.Scale < 1.0).Then(ShowSlowMotionBadge.Set(true))); Methods Pause(string, int) Builds a block that stops game time, remembering the scale to come back to. public Block Pause(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Update(If(MenuOpen.IsTrue()).Then(Time.Pause())); Remarks Pausing an already paused game changes nothing. Pausable scripts skip process events while the flag is set; see this surface's own remarks and docs/execution-model.md. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This factory was not obtained inside Build(). Resume(string, int) Builds a block that restarts game time at the last positive scale it was set to. public Block Resume(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Update(If(!MenuOpen.IsTrue()).Then(Time.Resume())); Remarks Resuming a game that is not paused changes nothing, so a resume written on every frame does not cancel a slow-motion scale another script set. The scale it comes back to is one when nothing set another. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This factory was not obtained inside Build(). SetScale(NumberValueBlock, string, int) Builds a block that sets the game's time scale. public Block SetScale(NumberValueBlock scale, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock scale The new scale: zero stops game time, one is ordinary speed, and a value above one runs the game faster than real time. A positive value is also what Resume(string, int) comes back to afterwards. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one: it is what records the line of the script this block was written on. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Update(If(Bullets == 1.0).Then(Time.SetScale(0.25))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException scale is null, or this factory was not obtained inside Build(). A scale that is negative, NaN or infinite is refused when the block runs, because an expression's value is not known until then.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TimeReadB.summary: Class TimeReadBlock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Time.Delta and Time.Elapsed return: a number expression reading one of the runner's two clocks, and the one place the clock choice is written. public sealed class TimeReadBlock : NumberValueBlock, IScriptNode Expand Details ... Inheritance object NumberValueBlock TimeReadBlock Implements IScriptNode Inherited Members NumberValueBlock.DescribeChildren(NodeDescription) NumberValueBlock.Equals(object) NumberValueBlock.GetHashCode() Examples On.Update(Age.Add(Time.Delta)); On.Update(RealAge.Add(Time.Delta.Unscaled())); Remarks This block type is public because Unscaled() is part of the authored grammar, not because a test needs it: a script writes Time.Delta.Unscaled(), so the type Time.Delta returns has to carry that method. Its constructor is internal like every other block's, so a script still cannot build one directly. The scaled clock is the default and real time carries the word. That is the same grammar a transform verb's frame uses - the modifier follows the verb, the common case is the default, and the unusual case is the one that is written out. It is applied to both readings and to nothing else on the Time surface: Time.Scale and Time.IsPaused are not clock readings and return types that carry no Unscaled at all, so Time.Scale.Unscaled() does not compile rather than meaning nothing. Evaluating one reads two properties - the runner's clock and one of its four values - and allocates nothing. Both clock choices cost the same; there is no cast and no branch on anything but the two readonly fields. Must allocate nothing after warm-up; AGENTS.md rule 29. public override double Evaluate(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Returns double The value this expression has for that object right now. Unscaled() The same reading taken from the real-time clock, which the game's time scale and a pause do not change. public NumberValueBlock Unscaled() Returns NumberValueBlock A number expression reading real time. Calling it on a read that is already unscaled returns an equivalent block rather than refusing, because the sentence Time.Delta.Unscaled() means the same thing however many times it is written. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Struct TransformFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Transform surface inside Build(): where the object a script runs on is, how it is turned and scaled, what is above and below it in the hierarchy, and what it is parented to. public readonly struct TransformFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Update(Transform.MoveBy(Step, 0.0, 0.0), Transform.RotateBy(0.0, 1.5, 0.0)); On.Ready(Transform.SetScale(2.0)); On.Ready(If(Transform.HasParent).Then(Transform.Unparent())); Remarks The blocks reach the object through IScriptHost, never through a UnityEngine.Transform; AGENTS.md rule 24. Every number parameter is a NumberValueBlock and every spatial parameter a Vector3ValueBlock, so a literal, a variable and an expression all work, through the implicit conversions those types declare. Every verb that takes three numbers also takes one spatial value. MoveBy(Step) and MoveBy(Step.X, Step.Y, Step.Z) build the same block; a Vector3 carrying degrees holds them in the layout Rotation.ToEuler() returns. A displacement is in the object's own frame and an absolute value names its frame in the verb. MoveBy(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) and RotateBy(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) act along the object's own oriented axes unless the builder they return is given InWorldSpace(); SetWorldPosition(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) and SetLocalPosition(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) say which frame they mean in their names. That is the captain's answer to API-semantics row T02 on 2026-09-13, and TransformSpace states why one word covers two frames. Parent, Child(NumberValueBlock, string, int) and Root aim the same verbs at one step of the hierarchy around the object. They offer no further navigation of their own; TransformTargetFactory says why. An object with a Rigidbody, kinematic or dynamic, refuses every verb that writes its position or rotation: the write changes nothing, the line is reported once per script type as an error naming the Motion call to use in On.FixedUpdate, and the rest of the event runs. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Struct TransformOffsetBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What MoveBy and RotateBy return: the displacement, in the object's own frame unless a modifier says otherwise. public readonly struct TransformOffsetBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Update(Transform.MoveBy(0.02, 0.0, 0.0)); // along the object's axes On.Update(Transform.MoveBy(0.02, 0.0, 0.0).InWorldSpace()); // along the scene's axes Remarks The default is the object's own oriented axes, which is the captain's answer to API-semantics row T02 on 2026-09-13 and what the previous version of LunyScript did; docs/verification/transform-space-spelling.md is the reading of it. A move of one unit along X goes one world unit along the direction the object faces, unaffected by its own or its parent's scale, and a turn composes after the rotation the object already has. InWorldSpace() selects the scene's axes and InLocalSpace() states the default. Each returns a type that offers neither, so a second space clause does not compile; that is the typestate API-semantics row T08 asks for and AGENTS.md rule 41 requires. The conversion to a block is what AGENTS.md rule 42 asks for: a builder either converts or registers, so an unmodified MoveBy cannot silently drop its behaviour. Methods InLocalSpace() Applies the amounts along the object's own oriented axes, which is what they do without this clause. public SpacedTransformOffsetBuilder InLocalSpace() Returns SpacedTransformOffsetBuilder The finished displacement, which takes no second space clause. Examples On.Update(Transform.MoveBy(1.0, 0.0, 0.0).InLocalSpace()); Remarks Present so a script can say the frame it means at a call site where leaving it out would read as an oversight. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This builder is a default that no verb produced. InWorldSpace() Applies the amounts along the scene's axes instead of the object's own. public SpacedTransformOffsetBuilder InWorldSpace() Returns SpacedTransformOffsetBuilder The finished displacement, which takes no second space clause. Examples On.Update(Transform.MoveBy(1.0, 0.0, 0.0).InWorldSpace()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This builder is a default that no verb produced. Operators implicit operator Block(TransformOffsetBuilder) Finishes a displacement that named no frame, which is the object's own. public static implicit operator Block(TransformOffsetBuilder builder) Parameters Type Name Description TransformOffsetBuilder builder The builder to finish. Returns Block The finished block. Examples Block step = Transform.MoveBy(1.0, 0.0, 0.0); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException builder is a default that no verb produced.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Enum TransformPart Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which of the three values of a transform a verb reads or writes. public enum TransformPart Expand Details ... Fields Position = 0 The position. Rotation = 1 The rotation, in euler degrees. Scale = 2 The scale. World reads Unity's lossy scale and cannot be written; see IScriptHost.WriteTransform. Examples host.ReadTransform(TransformRelation.Parent, 0, TransformSpace.World, TransformPart.Scale, out var x, out var y, out var z); Remarks Rotation is carried as euler degrees here, because that is what a script author writes and reads. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Enum TransformRelation Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which object a transform verb acts on, named relative to the object the script runs on. public enum TransformRelation Expand Details ... Fields Child = 3 One of that object's children, by index. Refused when the index is outside the child count. None = 0 No object. As a reparent destination this is the scene root, which is what Transform.Unparent() asks for; as a verb's target it resolves to nothing and is refused. Parent = 2 That object's parent. Refused when it has none. Root = 4 The topmost object of that object's hierarchy, which is the object itself when it has no parent. Self = 1 The object the script runs on. Examples host.ReadChildCount(TransformRelation.Self, 0); Remarks The hierarchy vocabulary is one step deep by design: Parent, Child and Root are reached from the object the script runs on and offer no further navigation of their own, so a chain cannot walk an arbitrary path. That is the "bounded hierarchy queries" of docs/positioning.md item C14 applied to this family. A named or bound object of any kind is not a relation and is not part of this version; it arrives with C14 itself.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.title: Enum TransformSpace | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Enum TransformSpace Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which frame a transform verb's numbers are in. public enum TransformSpace Expand Details ... Fields Local = 1 The object's own oriented axes for a displacement, and the parent's frame for an absolute value. The default for MoveBy and RotateBy. World = 0 The scene's frame. Examples host.ReadTransform(TransformRelation.Self, 0, TransformSpace.Local, TransformPart.Position, out var x, out var y, out var z); Remarks Local names two different frames, and which one it is depends on the verb. That is deliberate and it is the captain's answer to API-semantics row T02 on 2026-09-13, which is also what the previous version of LunyScript did; docs/verification/transform-space-spelling.md is the reading of it. For a displacement - MoveBy and RotateBy - Local is the object's own oriented axes, which is Unity's Space.Self. A move of one unit along X goes one world unit along the direction the object faces, unaffected by its own or its parent's scale; a turn composes after the rotation the object already has. For an absolute value - a read or a set of a position, a rotation or a scale - Local is the parent's frame, which is Unity's localPosition, localEulerAngles and localScale. World is the scene's frame for both, and for a turn it composes before the rotation the object already has. An object at the scene root with no rotation of its own cannot tell the two apart, which is why a test that separates them gives the object both; AGENTS.md rule 56 names that as the plausible-looking wrong result.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.title: Class TransformStreamInbox | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Class TransformStreamInbox Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Holds the transform streams that arrived since the last tick drained them, in one buffer the inbox owns. Every INetworkProvider uses one, so that the receive side of the stream is written once rather than once per backend. public sealed class TransformStreamInbox Expand Details ... Inheritance object TransformStreamInbox Remarks Why this exists rather than a queue of byte arrays. A stream arrives on every tick of every peer that is not the authority. Handing back a fresh array per stream would allocate on every one of those ticks, which AGENTS.md rule 29 forbids and which none of rule 31's six relaxations covers. The arriving bytes are copied into one buffer instead, and TryDequeue(out byte[], out int, out int) hands back the offset and length of a stream inside it. How the buffer is reused. The write cursor returns to the start on the first append after the queue has been drained. That is deliberately not "on the last dequeue": a caller reads the bytes after TryDequeue(out byte[], out int, out int) has returned, and resetting there would let the next arriving stream overwrite them while the caller was still reading. Resetting on the next append instead means a view stays readable until new bytes arrive, and a view that old is stale in any case. What it assumes about threads. Nothing here is thread safe. Both providers append from the netcode backend's own receive callback and drain from ScriptRunner.TickFrameUpdate, and both of those run on the main thread in separate phases of one frame. Fields HeaderBytes How many bytes of a payload IsStreamHeader(byte, byte, byte) reads. public const int HeaderBytes = 3 Field Value int Properties Count How many streams are waiting. public int Count { get; } Property Value int Methods Append(byte[], int, int) Copies one arrived stream in. public void Append(byte[] payload, int offset, int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The buffer the stream arrived in. int offset Where the stream starts in it. int length How many bytes it occupies. Clear() Drops everything waiting. Called when a session ends, so that a stream from the previous session cannot be applied in the next one. public void Clear() IsStreamHeader(byte, byte, byte) Whether the first three bytes of an arriving payload are a transform stream's. public static bool IsStreamHeader(byte first, byte second, byte third) Parameters Type Name Description byte first The payload's first byte. byte second Its second byte. byte third Its third byte. Returns bool False for a payload some other system sent. Examples if (TransformStreamInbox.IsStreamHeader(first, second, third) == false) return; Remarks A stream travels as an unnamed message, which carries no name of its own, so a provider is handed every unnamed payload in the session including ones this product did not send. This is what lets a provider drop those before copying them: without it, another system's large payload grows the provider's receive buffer and this inbox's buffer to its size, and neither ever shrinks. It is three byte comparisons and not a parse. The reader checks the same three bytes again when it decodes; that is not a duplicate for the sake of it, because a payload can also arrive through a provider that never saw it as an unnamed message. TryDequeue(out byte[], out int, out int) The next waiting stream, as a view into the inbox's own buffer. public bool TryDequeue(out byte[] payload, out int offset, out int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The inbox's buffer. int offset Where this stream starts in it. int length How many bytes it occupies. Returns bool False when nothing is waiting.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Struct TransformSyncDeclaration Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One Sync.Position, Sync.Rotation or Sync.Scale as the build recorded it: which channel, at which cadence, and which slots hold the per-object bookkeeping the network tick needs. Built by ScriptBuildContext and read by ScriptRunner; a script never sees one. public readonly struct TransformSyncDeclaration Expand Details ... Remarks The shadow slots are the one part worth reading twice, because they mean two things at once and that is deliberate. On the peer with authority they hold the last value it put in the stream. On every other peer they hold the last value it took out of one. Both are the same fact - the value the two ends agree on - which is exactly what a change is measured against, so the position channel's change encoding needs no second set of slots to decode with. The rotation channel uses one shadow slot, not three, and what it holds is not a coordinate. A rotation is sent whole rather than as a change, so the only thing the authority needs to remember is the 32 bits it last sent, and ShadowSlotX holds exactly those, as a Number, which carries a 32-bit integer without rounding. ShadowSlotY and ShadowSlotZ are CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptBuildContext.NoShadowSlot there: a negative index cannot address a slot, so a path that read one by mistake fails its bounds check rather than reading an unrelated variable. Set once and never cleared, so the report is made once for an object and not again. Only the scale channel has one: it is the only channel that sends a value rather than a change, so it is the only one with no second form to fall back to. public FlagSlot UnencodableReportedSlot { get; } Property Value FlagSlot Methods ToString() How a diagnostic names this declaration. public override string ToString() Returns string

Examples On.Update(Transform.MoveTo(3.0, 0.0, 0.0).Over(2.0)); Remarks This builder converts to no block. A duration interpolator without a duration would be an immediate write, which SetWorldPosition, SetWorldRotation and SetScale already are. Over is required; AGENTS.md rules 41 and 42. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns TransformToDurationBuilder The duration, which is a block in seconds as it is or takes Seconds, Milliseconds, Minutes or Hours. Examples On.Update(Transform.MoveTo(3.0, 0.0, 0.0).Over(2.0)); On.Update(Transform.ScaleTo(2.0).Over(500).Milliseconds()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException amount is null, or this builder is a default that no verb produced.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.UIGateway.title: Class UIGateway | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.UIGateway.summary: Class UIGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The core's one entry point to UI Toolkit. Resolves declared names to VisualElement once per instance at spawn and again on panel reload, and answers the writes, reads and occurrence tests the UI blocks make. public sealed class UIGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object UIGateway Remarks A per-use Q is a defect. Blocks store interned names and declaration indices because the shared script tree cannot hold an element. This gateway holds the resolved element per instance. The per-frame path never queries the visual tree. The supported scene component is PanelRenderer. UIDocument is not probed. Close writes display = None and keeps this cache. Destroy is should-have and is not in this version. This file names VisualElement and VisualTreeAsset. PanelRenderer lookup lives on GameObjectHost. Blocks never name either type.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.UnityScen.summary: Class UnitySceneProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The scene provider the default runner uses: Unity's SceneManager, loading and unloading scenes that are in the build. public sealed class UnitySceneProvider : ISceneProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object UnitySceneProvider Implements ISceneProvider Examples runner.SceneGateway.UseProvider(new UnitySceneProvider()); Remarks This file and the runner's driver are the two that name SceneManager. No block names it; a scene block reaches Unity only through SceneGateway and this provider, which is the arrangement docs/proposals/scene-flow.md states. A scene that is not in the build fails as NotFound, in the Editor as well as in a player. Unity's Editor can load a scene that is not in the build through an Editor-only call, and using it would make an example work in the Editor and fail in the built game. The check is SceneUtility.GetBuildIndexByScenePath, before anything starts. A replacement load is LoadSceneMode.Single, which releases every loaded scene; an additive load is LoadSceneMode.Additive. An unload names the exact Scene it ends, never a scene name, because two additive copies of one scene asset share a name. Properties LoadedSceneCount How many scene instances are loaded now. public int LoadedSceneCount { get; } Property Value int Methods CountLoaded(string) How many loaded scene instances were loaded from this asset path. public int CountLoaded(string scenePath) Parameters Type Name Description string scenePath The scene asset's path. Returns int Zero when none is loaded. Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines. Allocates; called only when the provider is installed. public string Describe() Returns string For example: "Unity SceneManager" or "in-memory scene provider". Load(string, bool) Starts loading one scene asset. A replacement load releases every loaded scene; an additive load releases none. public ISceneLoadOperation Load(string scenePath, bool additive) Parameters Type Name Description string scenePath The scene asset's path. bool additive True to load alongside the loaded scenes. Returns ISceneLoadOperation The operation the gateway polls. A scene that is not in the build completes at once as OperationFailure.NotFound, and nothing starts. LoadedScenePathAt(int) The asset path of one loaded scene instance. public string LoadedScenePathAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index From zero to LoadedSceneCount minus one. Returns string The path. May allocate; the gateway reads it only when a replacement load starts. Unload(ISceneLoadOperation) Starts unloading the exact instance one completed additive load produced. This is how a load whose requester stopped waiting is cleaned up. public IAsyncOperation Unload(ISceneLoadOperation load) Parameters Type Name Description ISceneLoadOperation load An operation this provider's Load(string, bool) returned, completed successfully. Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. Unload(string) Starts unloading the one loaded instance of this asset path. The gateway calls it only after CountLoaded(string) returned one. public IAsyncOperation Unload(string scenePath) Parameters Type Name Description string scenePath The scene asset's path. Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. When that instance is the only loaded scene, it completes at once as OperationFailure.Denied, because a game always has one scene loaded.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Var-1.htm.title: Struct Var<T> | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Var-1.htm.summary: Struct Var<T> Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A handle to one variable of a script. Returned by Var.Define at build time; the operators and methods on it build blocks. public readonly struct Var<T> where T : struct Type Parameters T What the variable holds: Number, Flag, Text, Vector3, Rotation, Vector2, Color or a declared C# enum. AGENTS.md rule 12 makes Number the number type, so there is no Var<Int32> and no Var<Single>. Expand Details ... Examples var post = Var.Define<Vector3>("post", new Vector3(3.0, 0.5, 0.0)); On.Update(If(post.Y > 1.0).Then(post.Set(post.WithY(0.5)))); Remarks The handle is an index, not a value: it says where the variable lives on every instance of the program, and the same handle reads a different number on every object running the script. A handle is valid only inside the Build that declared it. It carries a slot index and a kind and nothing that identifies its program, so a handle from one script used in another script's Build addresses that other script's slot of the same index. Take a ScoreScript holding static Number Score at index 0, and a PickupScript whose own first variable is cooldown: writing On.Ready(ScoreScript.Score.Add(10.0)) inside PickupScript.Build adds 10 to every pickup's cooldown and never moves the score. Where the borrowed index is past the end of the borrowing program's array, ScriptInstance throws LunyScriptUsageException naming this cause; where it is within range, as here, nothing detects it. Declare each script's variables in its own Build. A kind's operations are members of its handle. A Number, Flag or Text variable is declared as that handle type, which carries the arithmetic, ordering, truth and text members of its kind. This generic handle carries what Vector3, Vector2, Rotation and enum variables use, with Set and ==, so Here.Add(1.0) and Here + There on a Var<Vector3> are compile errors. A member it shares between those kinds, such as Z on a Var<Vector2> or == on a Var<Vector3>, compiles and throws LunyScriptUsageException while the script type is built, because C# 9 cannot restrict a member of a generic type to one instantiation of it. Build runs once per script type at launch, so a script that can throw one of these throws it on the first run. The Var<Number> that Var.Define<Number> returns converts to the Number handle, and so do Flag and Text: Number health = Var.Define<Number>("health", 100.0);. docs/slice-decisions.md D4.3 records the history. operator == on a handle builds a condition block; it does not compare handles. Use Equals(object) to compare two handles. A value of no length normalizes to zero rather than to a NaN. public Vector3ValueBlock Normalized { get; } Property Value Vector3ValueBlock Examples On.Update(Heading.Set(Offset.Normalized)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This is not a Vector3 variable. The C# operators are the one part this cannot cover. Spawn * 2.0 does not compile, because operator lookup also runs on the operands' own types and neither is a spatial expression. Put the variable in a local of the expression type first - Vector3ValueBlock spawn = Spawn; - and the operators are available on it. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.VarFactor.summary: Struct VarFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Var surface inside Build(): declares a script's variables and hands back the typed handles the blocks are built from. public readonly struct VarFactory Expand Details ... Examples protected override void Build() { var health = Var.Define<Number>("health", 100.0); var playerName = Var.DefineText("playerName"); } Remarks This is a build-time surface. Every call runs once per script type, before any object exists, and constructs part of the shared Script program, which is why it may allocate. The blocks returned during that build execute later, per event and per Script instance. AGENTS.md rule 43; rule 25 forbids reading anything about an object here. Methods DefineAllocatingText(string, int) Declares a growing text variable with a bound: a System.String of at most maxBytes UTF-8 bytes. This variable cannot be synchronised. public Text DefineAllocatingText(string name, int maxBytes) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name, which should come from nameof. int maxBytes How many UTF-8 bytes it may hold, from 1 to 1048576. Returns Text The typed handle. Examples Log = Var.DefineAllocatingText(nameof(Log), 16384); DefineSyncedText(string, SyncCadence, TextCapacity) Declares a text variable that every peer sees. public Text DefineSyncedText(string name, SyncCadence cadence, TextCapacity capacity = TextCapacity.Bytes64) Parameters Type Name Description string name The variable's name, which should come from nameof. SyncCadence cadence How often it is sent. Required, per AGENTS.md rule 46: a synchronised variable whose cost nobody chose cannot be written. Text carries a managed string on the wire, so EveryTick is refused for it and Once is the usual choice. TextCapacity capacity How many bytes it holds. Defaults to Bytes64, which is one cache line. A synchronised text is always fixed: its size is what it costs on the wire, and a growing text is not networked. Returns Text The handle. Examples PlayerName = Var.DefineSyncedText(nameof(PlayerName), SyncCadence.Once); Motto = Var.DefineSyncedText(nameof(Motto), SyncCadence.OnChange, TextCapacity.Bytes512); Remarks The cadence comes before the capacity, which is the opposite of the order the proposal wrote. C# allows no required parameter after an optional one, so a defaulted capacity and a required cadence can only be written in this order. It is also the order DefineSynced<T>(string, SyncCadence, T) already uses: the name, then the cadence, then the one thing that has a sensible default. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The cadence is unset, the cadence is EveryTick, or the name is taken. DefineSynced<T>(string, SyncCadence, T) Declares a variable that every peer sees, with the cadence that says what it costs. The cadence is required, so a synchronised variable whose cost nobody chose cannot be written; AGENTS.md rule 46. public Var<T> DefineSynced<T>(string name, SyncCadence cadence, T defaultValue = default) where T : struct Parameters Type Name Description string name The variable's name, which should come from nameof. SyncCadence cadence How often it is sent. T defaultValue What it starts from. Returns Var<T> The handle, which reads and writes exactly like an unsynchronised one. Type Parameters T Number or Flag. Use DefineSyncedText(string, SyncCadence, TextCapacity) for text. Examples Score = Var.DefineSynced<Number>(nameof(Score), SyncCadence.OnChange, 0.0); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The cadence is unset, or the name is taken. Returns Text The typed handle. Examples var chatLine = Var.DefineText("chatLine", TextCapacity.Bytes512); // 512 bytes, 509 usable Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The name is already taken. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.VarWatchB.summary: Struct VarWatchBuilder<T> Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What When.Var(x) returns. Its only method is Changed(params Block[]), which registers the watch with the build. public readonly struct VarWatchBuilder<T> where T : struct Type Parameters T Expand Details ... Examples When.Var(playerName).Changed(score.Set(0.0)); Remarks A watch is polled once per frame, after the frame-update blocks. It compares the variable against a second slot of the same kind, allocated at build time, that holds what the variable was the last time the watch ran. A value that changes and changes back within one frame therefore does not fire. That is the semantic, stated rather than hidden; docs/execution-model.md and docs/slice-decisions.md record why polling was chosen over notifying on write. Methods Changed(params Block[]) Registers the blocks that run when the variable's value differs from what it was the last time the watch ran. public void Changed(params Block[] blocks) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks, in order. Examples When.Var(health).Changed(alive.Set(health > 0.0)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException blocks is null or contains null, or the variable's kind is not one LunyScript can watch.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vector2.h.summary: Struct Vector2 Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A two-component spatial value: a stick deflection, a screen offset, a planar direction. [Serializable] public struct Vector2 Expand Details ... Examples var stick = new Vector2(1.0, 0.0); var raised = stick.WithY(1.0); Remarks The name is Unity's, and the namespace is LunyScript's. This type is CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vector2, kept apart from UnityEngine.Vector2 by its namespace, for the reason Vector3 gives. The components are Single while Number is Double. That is the precision split the API semantics record carries, applied the same way Vector3 applies it. Every constructor, method and operator here takes and returns Double at its edges, so a script never writes an f suffix; the component fields hold the Single itself. The components are public fields, so Unity saves them, for the reason and with the Single write Vector3 states: stick.Y = 0.5f. A script variable of this type is written whole. WithX and WithY return a copy with one component changed, which is what the variable's Set takes; the variable handle has no writable component. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vector3.h.summary: Struct Vector3 Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A three-component spatial value: a position, a direction, a displacement or a scale. [Serializable] public struct Vector3 Expand Details ... Examples var spawn = new Vector3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0); var raised = spawn.WithY(2.5); Remarks The name is Unity's, and the namespace is LunyScript's. This type is CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vector3, kept apart from UnityEngine.Vector3 by its namespace, so a Unity user reads a name they already know. A script imports no engine namespace, so Vector3 in a script names this type. A file that imports both CodeSmile.LunyScript and UnityEngine sees two types named Vector3, and the compiler refuses the bare name with CS0104 until one of them is written with its namespace, such as UnityEngine.Vector3 in host code. The components are Single while Number is Double. That is the precision split the API semantics record carries: scalars use double, and spatial payload and spatial math use float, narrowing at the destination that declares it. Every constructor, method and operator here takes and returns Double at its edges, so a script never writes an f suffix, and the narrowing happens in the constructor. The component fields below hold the Single itself. The components are public fields, so Unity saves them. A field of this type in a ScriptableObject, or in a [Serializable, LunyScriptData] struct such an asset holds, keeps the three components the Inspector wrote through a save and a reload, and Bind.Data copies them into the script's variables unchanged. A value is a copy: writing a component of a local changes that local only. C# that writes a fractional literal into a component writes the f suffix, offset.Y = 2.5f, because the field holds a Single; WithY(2.5) takes a Double. A script variable of this type is written whole. WithX, WithY and WithZ return a copy with one component changed, which is what the variable's Set takes, and the variable handle has no writable component. Constructors Vector3(double, double, double) Builds a value from three numbers, narrowing each to the component's single precision. public Vector3(double x, double y, double z) Parameters Type Name Description double x The first component. double y The second component. double z The third component. Transform.Forward is the object's own forward in world space, so a local query or a local MoveBy takes this constant and a world one takes that read, and the object's orientation is never applied twice. One The value whose three components are one. public static readonly Vector3 One Field Value Vector3 Examples var unscaled = Vector3.One; Right The unit value along the first axis, (1, 0, 0): right in Unity's convention. public static readonly Vector3 Right Field Value Vector3 Examples On.Update(Transform.MoveBy(Vector3.Right * 0.1)); Up The unit value along the second axis, (0, 1, 0): up in Unity's convention. public static readonly Vector3 Up Field Value Vector3 Examples On.FixedUpdate(Collision.RayCast().InLocalSpace().Towards(-Vector3.Up).Length(1.1).Into(Ground)); X The first component. A public field, which is what Unity saves. public float X Field Value float Examples var x = offset.X; Y The second component. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ViewFacto.title: Struct ViewFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ViewFacto.summary: Struct ViewFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The View surface inside Build(): what a local player sees, and which camera rig it renders. public readonly struct ViewFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(View.For(Screen).SetCamera(ChaseRig)); Remarks A view and a camera rig are two objects, not one. The view is the thing that draws part of the screen; the rig is the authored Cinemachine configuration that decides where the shot is. Keeping them separate is what lets one rig serve a group view and four separate views serve four local players, which is the accepted design's own reason for the split. Both are declared asset inputs, assigned per object in the Inspector. The core cannot name a Camera or a Cinemachine type, so a view and a rig reach the camera adapter as the object a declared input resolved to, and the adapter is what knows whether the object is one. An object that is not is reported and nothing is written. The camera family is routed through Cinemachine and nothing else. That is the captain's answer on the camera family, 2026-09-13. With the Cinemachine package absent, CodeSmile.LunyScript.Cinemachine does not compile in, no provider is installed, and every block on this surface writes nothing and says so once. This surface's shape is provisional. It implements the recorded recommendation of the open decision contract-view-routing, which keeps the view separate from its rig and its target group. The alternative that decision holds open makes the player the entry point instead. Nothing below this surface depends on which is chosen. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.VisualTre.summary: Struct VisualTreeAsset Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A handle to one VisualTreeAsset input of a script: a UXML document the object's Inspector assigns. Returned by Bind.VisualTreeAsset() at build time, or assigned before Build() by [Asset] on the property. public readonly struct VisualTreeAsset Expand Details ... Examples Portrait = Bind.VisualTreeAsset(); var first = Panel.Place(Portrait).At(Anchor.TopLeft); Remarks This is LunyScript's type, with Unity's name. A script imports only CodeSmile.LunyScript, so VisualTreeAsset there is this handle and the script compiles without an engine reference. The Inspector field accepts a UnityEngine.UIElements.VisualTreeAsset, and C# on the object reads the assigned asset with LunyScriptBehaviour.GetAsset. A file that imports both namespaces writes UnityEngine.UIElements.VisualTreeAsset for Unity's type. The declared name is the input's durable identity. A value stored on a host is matched to the input by that name. A generated property gives the input its member's name, and .As(name) names it explicitly. Renaming it orphans what a scene stored for the old name. An object that assigns none gets an empty document as its asset placeholder, which is reported at warning severity because nothing about it is visible. A handle is valid only inside the Build that declared it, for the reason Var<T> states: it carries a slot index and nothing that identifies its program. Properties IsDeclared False for a handle Build() never declared, or one still waiting for its name. public bool IsDeclared { get; } Property Value bool Name The name the script declared, which is what a stored value is matched against and what a diagnostic names. Null until the declaration has its name. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods ToString() The declared name and kind, for a log line or a failure message. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "Portrait : VisualTreeAsset". Operators implicit operator VisualTreeAsset(AssetInputBuilder<VisualTreeAsset>) Declares the input a Bind.VisualTreeAsset() chain describes. The generated property of the line then gives it the member's name. public static implicit operator VisualTreeAsset(AssetInputBuilder<VisualTreeAsset> declaration) Parameters Type Name Description AssetInputBuilder<VisualTreeAsset> declaration The chain. Returns VisualTreeAsset The handle. Examples Portrait = Bind.VisualTreeAsset();

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.WaitBuild.title: Struct WaitBuilder | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.WaitBuild.summary: Struct WaitBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Wait(amount) returns: a routine step that holds its routine for that much game time. Used as a block it waits that many seconds; Seconds(), Milliseconds(), Minutes() and Hours() name the unit. public readonly struct WaitBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Routine(Door).Run(Opening.Set(true), Wait(3), Opening.Set(false))); Remarks Seconds is the default unit, so Wait(3) and Wait(3).Seconds() are the same wait. The wait counts game time from the moment the routine reaches it, and the amount is read then. Zero finishes at once; a negative amount, NaN or an infinity finishes at once and is reported as a warning. docs/proposals/wait-step.md is the contract. Methods Hours() The amount is hours of game time. public Block Hours() Returns Block The wait step. Examples On.Ready(Routine(Harvest).Run(Wait(1).Hours(), Ripe.Set(true))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This builder is a default that no Wait call produced. Milliseconds() The amount is milliseconds of game time. public Block Milliseconds() Returns Block The wait step. Examples On.Ready(Routine(Blink).Run(Lamp.Set(true), Wait(500).Milliseconds(), Lamp.Set(false))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This builder is a default that no Wait call produced. Minutes() The amount is minutes of game time. public Block Minutes() Returns Block The wait step. Examples On.Ready(Routine(Shift).Run(Wait(2).Minutes(), ShiftOver.Set(true))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This builder is a default that no Wait call produced. Seconds() The amount is seconds of game time. The same wait as using the builder as a block. public Block Seconds() Returns Block The wait step. Examples On.Ready(Routine(Door).Run(Opening.Set(true), Wait(3).Seconds(), Opening.Set(false))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This builder is a default that no Wait call produced. Operators implicit operator Block(WaitBuilder) Finishes the wait in seconds, the default unit, so Wait(3) is a routine step without a unit call. public static implicit operator Block(WaitBuilder builder) Parameters Type Name Description WaitBuilder builder The wait. Returns Block The wait step. Examples On.Ready(Routine(Door).Run(Opening.Set(true), Wait(3), Opening.Set(false))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException builder is a default that no Wait call produced.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.html.title: Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.html.summary: Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Classes ActionBlock A block whose objective can take more than one frame, and which therefore reports ActionResult rather than simply running to completion. ActivateObjectBlock What Object.Activate() and Object.Activate(name) build: activates the object the script runs on, or one the script created.
