AdapterAdmission The package and version admission table for extension blocks and optional adapters. AssetAttribute Declares an asset input whose handle is assigned before Build, in declaration order. AssetGateway Owns in-flight Asset.Load attempts and owner-acquisition records for one ScriptRunner. Bound Inspector loads complete from the instance's already resolved input. Resources loads go through IAssetLoadProvider. Script code never sees a Task or an exception type; AGENTS.md rules 50 and 51. AssetInputFileSources The file sources of the two input kinds LunyScript can decode from a file: Bind.Texture2D() reads a PNG and Bind.AudioClip() reads a PCM WAV file. Any other kind has none of these methods, so Bind.Prefab().FromStreamingAssets(...) does not compile. AssetLoadBlock What Asset.Load(source).As(handle) builds: starts one asynchronous content acquisition bound to an operation handle. Completion yields an owned typed asset on that handle, or a classified failure. Failure does not fall through to an asset placeholder. AssetPlaceholders The asset placeholder every asset type falls back to when an input of that type is left unassigned, and the two ways one is configured. AssetReleaseBlock What Asset.Release(acquisition) builds: relinquishes this owner's acquisition. Bound consumers retain content they still need. Release does not destroy them and does not promise immediate physical reclamation. AudioGateway The runner-owned audio service: pooled one-shot voices, named bound-source control, and mixer writes. Bound playback on the object a script runs on lives on IScriptHost instead. Block One step of behaviour in a script. A block object is created once, when its script type is built, and is then shared by every object running that script; the per-object state it reads and writes lives in slots on the ScriptInstance passed to Execute(ScriptInstance). CameraGateway The core's one entry point to the camera. Owns the ICameraProvider, passes each authored operation to it, and reports a refused one once. CloudSaveGateway Owns every cloud upload, download and delete of a document one ScriptRunner's scripts start: signs in when the first request arrives, queues requests in the order their blocks ran, sends one request per document at a time, polls each operation once per frame, and completes each request's attempts with its classified outcome. No script and no block ever sees a Task or an exception type; AGENTS.md section 12. ColorValueBlock The root of every colour expression: something that produces a Color when the block holding it runs. A Color value and a colour variable both convert to one, so a call that takes a colour takes either. CompilationFacts What the compiler was told when this assembly was built. Read by tests and by the release gate, so that a claim about release behaviour can name the compilation it was measured in. ConditionBlock A block that answers true or false for one object. Passed to If(...) and combined with &, | and !. CreateObjectBlock What Object.Create(name) builds: creates a new, empty, active object owned by the instance that runs this block, and records it in the owned-object slot the build assigned to that name. CreatePrefabObjectBlock What Object.Create(prefab) and its chain build: produces a fresh copy of a declared prefab input, places it, parents it, and holds it in an owned-object slot when the chain named one. DataSchema The schema of one LunyScriptDataAttribute struct: which fields it has, and how a value of it becomes a script's variables. Scripts pass it to Bind.Data as WeaponStats.Schema, the static property the generator writes into the struct. DataSchema<TValue, THandle> The schema of the struct TValue, whose script variables are the generated handle THandle. DeactivateObjectBlock What Object.Deactivate() and Object.Deactivate(name) build: deactivates the object the script runs on, or one the script created. DespawnObjectBlock What Object.Despawn() and Object.Despawn(name) build: returns a pooled object to the pool it came from. DestroyObjectBlock What Object.Destroy() and Object.Destroy(name) build: permanently ends the object the script runs on, or one the script produced. DiagnosticBuffer Fixed-capacity, ordered storage shared by console and trace readers. DiagnosticCatalog Immutable catalog for one built program. DiagnosticCommand Caller-owned receipt. Terminal results survive target closure and are never replayed. DiagnosticFault Observed contained error or failed outer boundary, separate from enabled state. DiagnosticLifetime One live lifetime and the two names a person finds it by: its script and its object. DiagnosticNode Immutable declaration metadata; never contains a live block or delegate. DiagnosticPause One breakpoint hit that paused Play Mode. DiagnosticProtocol Local diagnostics protocol version. Current snapshots and optional action records are separate observations. DiagnosticSnapshot Caller-owned current state from an idle main-thread boundary, never execution history. DiagnosticTrace Explicit action capture for one instance lifetime. Disposal changes no script state. DiagnosticVariable One immutable declared variable, including whether it is internal storage. DiagnosticWrite The last change of one variable's value: which script, object and block changed it, and when. DocumentFields The stored fields of one document while a DocumentMigration step converts them. Reads and writes a copy: nothing here reaches a script's variables or the stored file. DocumentMigration One consecutive step of a document's schema: converts a stored document of FromVersion into version FromVersion + 1. Written in C#, registered in Build() with Define.Document(...).Migration(step). EditorScript The editor entry: a subclass whose Build() composes blocks that run in an EditorScriptSession. Game scripts subclass Script instead. A concrete EditorScript identifies the editor role without an attribute. EnumValueBlock The root of every enum expression: something that produces an integer code when the block holding it runs. FakeAssetLoadProvider An in-memory asset-load backend for tests: keys map to objects a test registered, a missing key fails as NotFound, and a registered object of another type fails as Denied. No Resources folder is required. AGENTS.md rule 52's shape applied to assets. FakeCameraProvider A camera backend that records what it was asked to do, with no Cinemachine package, no camera and no scene. FakeInputProvider An input backend that holds its actions and their values in memory, with no device, no window and no Input System package. FakeNavigationProvider A navigation backend with no navigation mesh: each registered actor has a position, a speed and a stopping distance, and moves in a straight line to the end of the route a test chose. FakeNetworkProvider A netcode backend that runs entirely in this process, with no network, no Editor and no Netcode for GameObjects. Two instances are paired with Pair(out FakeNetworkProvider, out FakeNetworkProvider) and each one's sends arrive in the other's queues. FakeSceneProvider An in-memory scene backend: a list of scene paths that count as in the build, a list of loaded scene instances, and loads and unloads that complete when the gateway ticks or when a test says so. It reports the native Loaded and Unloaded phases the way Unity's callbacks do. FileCloudSaveProvider The file-based Cloud Save provider: one file per document, under a directory the caller names. A first-class part of the product, not a test fixture; AGENTS.md rule 52. It is how every failure branch is tested without a network, and what makes the automated suite runnable with no credentials. FileLoadBlock What Asset.Load(file).Into(destination).As(handle) builds: starts reading one declared text or JSON file and, when the read and the decoding succeed, writes the destination in one step. FlagValueBlock A block that produces a Flag for one object: a variable read or a literal. GameObjectHost The Collision queries of a GameObject's host: Unity's buffer-taking physics queries on the default physics scene, with each result copied into a CodeSmile.LunyScript.RawCollisionHit. InputGateway The core's one entry point to player input. Owns the IInputProvider, resolves each program's declared actions once, and answers the value reads and the occurrence tests the input blocks make. InstanceLayout How many slots of each kind one instance of a program owns, and what value each slot starts from. Built once per script type and never changed afterwards. InteractionStyle How a target's visual moves while players focus it: how far it rises, how much it grows, how fast it turns and how long it takes to blend in and out. An asset an Interaction.Target(...).Visual(child) script's Inspector assigns to its InteractionStyle input. LunyScript Finds the script an object runs, for ordinary C# code outside a script. The result is a LunyScriptReference<TScript> to one incarnation of that script. LunyScriptAssemblyAttribute Declares what the scripts of an assembly are for, so that a game start runs the singleton scripts of its production assemblies and none of a sample's or a test's. LunyScriptBehaviour Assigns one GameObject to one script type. This is the component a user adds; the script is named by an explicit field rather than by a type name written as a string. LunyScriptContactBehaviour Unity physics callbacks for one managed object whose script declared at least one of the six contact events. LunyScriptBehaviour adds this component only in that case, so an object whose script declares none of them is not subscribed. LunyScriptContractException Thrown when LunyScript observes that the lifecycle ownership contract was broken: the object running a script was destroyed, reparented or otherwise changed by native Unity API rather than by a LunyScript block. LunyScriptDataAttribute Marks a partial struct as a LunyScript data schema: a value shape a script declares its own copy of with Define.Data, binds from an Inspector-assigned asset with Bind.Data, and loads from a JSON file. LunyScriptDataFieldAttribute Marks a public field a script may read through a data input, or states the capacity of a text field in a LunyScriptDataAttribute schema. LunyScriptDriverBehaviour Ticks one ScriptRunner once per frame, and sweeps instances whose object a scene unload took away. Lives on a hidden object that LunyScriptRuntime creates; a user never adds this component. LunyScriptException The root of every exception LunyScript throws. Catch this to catch everything the product raised and nothing else. LunyScriptInternalException Thrown when LunyScript's own invariant was broken on a path a user cannot reach: a null or an impossible value inside the product's internals. LunyScriptLog The one place LunyScript writes to the Unity console. Unity log lines are formatted here; the LunyScript console reads the retained structured fields. LunyScriptLogAreas The area names the product's own log records carry, so that a reader and a debugging window see the same set of words rather than one spelling per call site. LunyScriptRuntime Holds the one ScriptRunner that LunyScriptBehaviour components share, and the hidden object that ticks it once per frame. LunyScriptSingletonCatalog The singleton scripts a player starts, which the build writes into its first scene on a hidden object. LunyScriptUsageException Thrown when script code asks LunyScript for something the API does not offer: a C# if around a condition block, an arithmetic operator on a text variable, a builder finished twice. NavigationGateway The core's one entry point to navigation. Owns the INavigationProvider, one record per actor with the attempt that drives it and whether it is paused, and polls every driven actor once per frame before any instance runs. One per ScriptRunner. NetworkGateway The core's one entry point to netcode. Owns the INetworkProvider, refuses the session calls that are a user mistake, and drains the provider's two queues once per tick. AGENTS.md rules 44 to 49. NodeDescription Collects named child nodes while building immutable program metadata. NumberValueBlock A block that produces a Number for one object: a variable read, a literal, or an arithmetic expression over other value blocks. ReferencedColorBlock A read of another script's Color variable. ReferencedEnumBlock A read of another script's enum variable. ReferencedFlagBlock A read of another script's Flag variable, which is also a condition. ReferencedNumberBlock A read of another script's Number variable. ReferencedRotationBlock A read of another script's Rotation variable. ReferencedVector2Block A read of another script's Vector2 variable. ReferencedVector3Block A read of another script's Vector3 variable. ReleaseGate Gate 4. Runs inside a standalone player built without DEBUG and asserts what only that build can show: that operator true and operator false on a condition block still throw, that the [Conditional] contract guards are gone, and that the two guards written out unconditionally are not. ResourcesAssetLoadProvider The Resources backend for Asset.Load of an Resource<T> key. The read happens inside the provider call, which is a start boundary, and the gateway observes the completed operation on its next poll. Blocks never name UnityEngine.Resources. RotationValueBlock The root of every orientation expression: something that produces a Rotation when the block holding it runs. RunnerDiagnostics Native diagnostics for one explicitly supplied local runner. Reads execute no authored logic. SceneGateway Owns in-flight Scene.Load and Scene.Unload attempts, the scene identities the runner's scripts declared, and one counter per identity and phase that the When.Scene* watches read. One per ScriptRunner. Script code never sees a Task, an AsyncOperation or an exception type; AGENTS.md rules 50 and 51. SceneLoadBlock What Scene.Load(scene).As(handle) and Scene.Load(scene).Additive().As(handle) build: starts one scene load bound to an operation handle. The handle succeeds when the destination is loaded and active, and fails with a classified reason otherwise. SceneUnloadBlock What Scene.Unload(scene).As(handle) builds: starts unloading the one loaded instance of a scene, bound to an operation handle. The handle succeeds when Unity has unloaded it. Script The runtime entry: a subclass whose Build() composes blocks that run on a game object. Editor workflows subclass EditorScript instead. ScriptBase Shared infrastructure for Script and EditorScript. One instance of a concrete subclass is compiled into one ScriptProgram, once, and every object running that script shares it. ScriptBuildContext The build-time half of the behaviour tree: each tree a Behavior(name).Root(node) declares, placed once, and where its starts are placed. ScriptInstance One object's state for one program: the slot arrays the program's layout asked for, and the host the blocks act on. The blocks themselves are shared by every instance of the program and hold no per-object state at all. ScriptObservation One C# observation of one variable of one script incarnation, returned by Observe(in Number, Action<double>) and its siblings. The caller owns it and ends it with Dispose(). ScriptProgram One script type, built. Holds the immutable block tree, the On.* event table and the instance layout, and is shared by every object running that script. ScriptRunner How one script reaches another on this runner: resolving a target to the instance running on its object, delivering a request to one receiver and an event to its listeners, and the nesting limit both share. SpawnObjectBlock What Object.Spawn(pool) and its chain build: checks one entry out of a declared pool, places it, parents it, and holds it in an owned-object slot when the chain named one. TextCapacities Facts about TextCapacity that both the layout and the blocks need. TextFormat A text built at build time for a text variable's Set, or a Label's SetText or BindText: a parsed Text.Format call, which holds the literal pieces of the format, which value fills each hole and how many decimal places each number hole asks for, or a Text.Join of parts, each written while its condition holds. TextLengths Facts about TextLength that collection storage needs. TimeReadBlock What Time.Delta and Time.Elapsed return: a number expression reading one of the runner's two clocks, and the one place the clock choice is written. TransformStreamInbox Holds the transform streams that arrived since the last tick drained them, in one buffer the inbox owns. Every INetworkProvider uses one, so that the receive side of the stream is written once rather than once per backend. UIGateway The core's one entry point to UI Toolkit. Resolves declared names to VisualElement once per instance at spawn and again on panel reload, and answers the writes, reads and occurrence tests the UI blocks make. UnitySceneProvider The scene provider the default runner uses: Unity's SceneManager, loading and unloading scenes that are in the build. VariableAttribute Declares a variable whose handle is assigned before Build, in declaration order. Vector2ValueBlock The root of every two-component spatial expression: something that produces a Vector2 when the block holding it runs. Vector3ValueBlock The root of every spatial expression: something that produces a Vector3 when the block holding it runs. Structs AdapterRegistration One extension block type an adapter registered, with the Unity package and minimum version that type needs. AimedLookAtBuilder A facing whose up direction has been named. It converts to a block and takes no further clause. AnimatorFactory The Animator surface inside Build(): typed handles to the parameters of the Animator Controller on the object the script runs on. It hides UnityEngine.Animator inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. AnimatorFlag A handle to one Bool parameter of the Animator on the object a script runs on. Returned by Animator.Flag(name) at build time. The product word for Unity's Bool is Flag. AnimatorInteger A handle to one Int parameter of the Animator on the object a script runs on. Returned by Animator.Integer(name) at build time. AnimatorNumber A handle to one Float parameter of the Animator on the object a script runs on. Returned by Animator.Number(name) at build time; the members on it build blocks. AnimatorTrigger A handle to one Trigger parameter of the Animator on the object a script runs on. Returned by Animator.Trigger(name) at build time. AnyPlayerInputFactory What Input.AnyPlayer() returns: a shared button, read across every local player number the backend holds. AssetFactory The Asset surface inside Build(): starts and ends content acquisitions. Unity owns the asset. LunyScript owns the attempt, the owner-acquisition, and consumer retention. AssetInputAssignment One row of the declared-input table a host component serializes: the name of a declared input and the asset this object assigns to it, or, for a scene input, the scene. AssetInputBuilder<TInput> What Bind.Prefab(), Bind.Texture2D(), Bind.AudioClip(), Bind.AudioMixer(), Bind.AudioMixerGroup() and Bind.VisualTreeAsset() return: an input declaration that is complete once it is assigned or named. AssetLoadBuilder What Asset.Load(source) returns: an unfinished acquisition that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds the operation handle. An unbound Load is refused when Build() finishes. AudioClip A handle to one AudioClip input of a script: an audio clip the object's Inspector assigns. Returned by Bind.AudioClip() at build time, or assigned before Build() by [Asset] on the property. AudioFactory The Audio surface inside Build(): one-shot play, bound source control, and named mixer writes. It hides UnityEngine.AudioSource inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. AudioListenerHandle What Audio.Listener returns. AudioListenerTargetBuilder What Audio.Listener.SetTarget(target) returns. AudioListenerTargetDurationBuilder What Audio.Listener.SetTarget(target).Over(amount) returns: a transition whose amount is seconds unless a unit call names another unit. AudioMixer A handle to one AudioMixer input of a script: an audio mixer the object's Inspector assigns. Returned by Bind.AudioMixer() at build time, or assigned before Build() by [Asset] on the property. AudioMixerGroup A handle to one AudioMixerGroup input of a script: a group of an audio mixer the object's Inspector assigns. Returned by Bind.AudioMixerGroup() at build time, or assigned before Build() by [Asset] on the property. AudioMixerHandle What Audio.Mixer(mixer) returns: named exposed-parameter writes. AudioPlacedOneShotBuilder A one-shot whose placement has been named. It converts to a block and takes no further placement clause. AudioPlayOneShotBuilder What Audio.PlayOneShot(clip) returns: a 2D one-shot, or one placement. AudioSourceHandle What Audio.For(source) returns: bound-source control on that object. AudioVoice A declared voice: one tracked one-shot per instance, which Audio.PlayOneShot(clip).Into(voice) fills and which Stop, Pause, Detach, SetVolume and When.Audio(voice) address. AudioVoiceVolumeBuilder What voice.SetVolume(value) returns. AudioVoiceVolumeDurationBuilder What voice.SetVolume(value).Over(amount) returns: a fade whose amount is seconds unless a unit call names another unit. AudioWatchBuilder What When.Audio(voice) returns. Each method registers blocks for one end of that tracked playback. BehaviorBuilder What Behavior(name) returns. Its one call, Root(BehaviorNode), takes the tree's root node and declares the tree. BehaviorCompositeBuilder What InOrder(...), InParallel(...) and InAnyOrder(...) return when their children are behaviour-tree nodes: a composite with no ending clause yet. BehaviorNode One node of a behaviour tree: a leaf made by Task or Check, a composite made by InOrder, InParallel or InAnyOrder, or a wrapper made by Inverted, AlwaysSucceeds, AlwaysFails or Repeat. BehaviorRepeatBuilder What Repeat(node) returns: a node that runs its child again after each finish, with no ending yet. BehaviorTree A declared behaviour tree. Start(string, int) starts or restarts one activation, Stop(string, int) interrupts it, and four conditions read what it reached. BindFactory The Bind surface inside Build(): declares the inputs a script needs - assets, scenes and objects in a scene - and hands back the typed handles that read them. BindingWatchBuilder What When.Binding(binding) returns: names the blocks that run when a LiveRebind() binding's object or availability changed. BodyFactory The Body surface inside Build(): observations of what physics actually did to the object this script runs on, and the switch of its Rigidbody between kinematic and dynamic. BoxCastBuilder What Collision.BoxCast() returns: a box cast that takes its clauses in any order, each once, and is finished by Into. BoxOverlapBuilder What Collision.BoxOverlap() returns: a box overlap that takes its clauses in any order, each once, and is finished by Into. CameraFactory The Camera surface inside Build(): what one camera rig tracks. It hides UnityEngine.Camera inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. CameraGroupBoundsBuilder What Camera.FollowGroup().Bounds(width, height) returns: the limited group follow, finished with For(ObjectBinding). CameraGroupFollowBuilder What Camera.FollowGroup() returns: a rig's target group that follows every local player's object, finished with For(ObjectBinding), optionally limited with Bounds(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock) first. CameraRigBuilder What Camera.For(rig) returns: the rig's two tracking targets and its target group. CameraTargetsBuilder What Camera.For(rig).Targets returns: the five operations on a rig's group of tracked objects. CapsuleCastBuilder What Collision.CapsuleCast() returns: a capsule cast that takes its clauses in any order, each once, and is finished by Into. CapsuleOverlapBuilder What Collision.CapsuleOverlap() returns: a capsule overlap that takes its clauses in any order, each once, and is finished by Into. Choice A declared choice: the name of one scored selector, which Choose(handle).Highest(...) opens and which a diagnostic and the runtime inspector call it by. ChooseBiasedBuilder A Choose chain that already has Bias. Optional Hold(Elapsed, string, int) follows. ChooseBiasedHoldAmountBuilder A Choose chain that has Bias and a Hold amount: the amount is seconds unless a unit call names another unit. Used as a block it starts the selector. ChooseBuilder What Choose(choice) returns. Its one call, Highest(params UtilityOption[]), names the scored options. ChooseCompleteBuilder A Choose chain that has both Bias and Hold. Used as a block it starts the selector. ChooseHeldBuilder A Choose chain that already has Hold. Optional Bias(double, string, int) follows. ChooseHighestBuilder A Choose(choice).Highest(...) chain. Optional Bias(double, string, int) and Hold(Elapsed, string, int) follow; used as a block it starts the selector. ChooseHoldAmountBuilder A Choose(choice).Highest(...).Hold(amount) chain: the Hold amount is seconds unless a unit call names another unit. Optional Bias(double, string, int) follows; used as a block it starts the selector. CloudDeleteBuilder What Cloud.Delete(document) returns: a delete of the cloud copy that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds the operation handle. An unbound delete is refused when Build() finishes. CloudFactory The Cloud surface inside Build(): uploads a declared document to the signed-in player's Cloud Save data, downloads it back, and deletes the cloud copy. Each start is one attempt on an operation handle, bound with .As(handle), which is required; the outcome arrives through When.Cloud(handle) and When.Operation(handle). AGENTS.md rule 50. CloudLoadBuilder What Cloud.Load(document) returns: a download that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds the operation handle. An unbound download is refused when Build() finishes. CloudSaveBuilder What Cloud.Save(document) returns: an upload that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds the operation handle. An unbound upload is refused when Build() finishes. CollectionRead A typed read of one collection entry: either At(index) or the current ForEach item. Each use reads the entry addressed by that expression, so a replacement of the current element is visible to the next read in the same body. CollectionResult The read-only, named outcome of one synchronous collection call. Declared with Define.CollectionResult(nameof(X)) inside Build() and produced by exactly one Slots.TryAdd(item).As(X). Used as a condition, it stands for Succeeded. CollectionTryBuilder What Slots.TryAdd(item) returns: one synchronous collection call whose own outcome is read. It has two kinds of consumer and takes exactly one: If(Slots.TryAdd(item)), or ElseIf(Slots.TryAdd(item)) in an If chain, branches on the outcome, and As(CollectionResult, string, int) stores it in a CollectionResult. CollisionFactory The Collision surface: seven verbs that ask the physics world what is in front of an object or around it, each writing into a result the script declared. Color A colour: red, green, blue and alpha channels, each from 0 to 1, as Unity's Color holds them. ColorSlot Where one Color variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. CreateBuilder What Object.Create(prefab) returns: a fresh copy of a prefab with no placement yet. Add At(Vector3ValueBlock), ChildOf(string, int), Into(OwnedObject, string, int), ForPlayer(int, string, int) and SurvivesCaller(string, int) in any order, or use it as a block, which creates the copy at the prefab's own pose. CreateFramedBuilder What a frame modifier returns: a create whose placement and frame are both stated. It offers no second frame clause, which is what makes a conflicting pair uncompilable. CreatePlacedBuilder What Object.Create(prefab).At(...) returns: a create whose placement is stated and whose frame is still the default, the parent's. CursorInputFactory What Input.Cursor returns: lock mode and visibility as two independent writes on the machine cursor. Four local players share one cursor; this surface is not on Input.ForPlayer. DataDeclaration Which Define.Data or Bind.Data declaration a generated Variables handle belongs to. DataDefineBuilder<TValue, THandle> What Define.Data(value) returns: this script's own copy of a LunyScriptDataAttribute struct, complete once it is assigned or named. Every object running the script starts from value, and a JSON load into it starts from value again. DataFileBuilder<THandle> What Bind.Data(schema).From...(path) returns: a JSON file of that schema, complete once it is assigned or named. DataFileLoadBuilder<THandle> What Asset.Load(dataFile) returns: a JSON load waiting for the Define.Data it fills. Into(THandle, string, int) names it. DataFile<THandle> A JSON file of one data schema, which Asset.Load(file).Into(data) reads into a Define.Data of that schema. DataInputBuilder<TValue, THandle> What Bind.Data(schema) returns: an Inspector data input, or with a From... call a JSON file of that schema. DebugFactory The Debug surface: blocks that write a line to the Console when they run. Log(string, string, int) writes an ordinary entry, Warn a warning and Error an error. DefineFactory The Define surface inside Build(): declares a script's variables, operations and collection results, and hands back the typed handles the blocks are built from. DiagnosticConditionOverride One If a debugger forced in one lifetime, and the branch it takes while forced. DiagnosticIdentity Identifies one lifetime independently of pooled object reuse. DiagnosticNodeOutcome What one catalog node's block last did in one lifetime, recorded when the block ran. Reading it re-evaluates nothing. DiagnosticPreview What one condition or value node says about a snapshot's stored values, or why a snapshot cannot say. Preview(DiagnosticNode) computes it from the snapshot's own copy of the values, without running any block or script code. DiagnosticValue A typed diagnostic value. Text is a caller-owned managed representation. Document A handle to one declared document: a named, versioned set of variables that Progress.Save and Progress.Load, or Settings.Save and Settings.Load, keep in the user's local storage, and Cloud.Save, Cloud.Load and Cloud.Delete keep in the signed-in player's Cloud Save data. Declared with Define.Document(nameof(X)) inside Build(). DocumentDefineBuilder What Define.Document(name) returns: a document being declared, which takes its version, its fields and its migration steps, then converts to the Document handle. DocumentLoadBuilder What Progress.Load(document) and Settings.Load(document) return: a load that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds the operation handle. An unbound load is refused when Build() finishes. DocumentSaveBuilder What Progress.Save(document) and Settings.Save(document) return: a save that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds the operation handle. An unbound save is refused when Build() finishes. Elapsed An elapsed duration written with a unit constructor: Seconds(1), Milliseconds(500), Minutes(2) or Hours(1). EnumSlot Where one declared C# enum variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. Event An event a script sends: a notification that something happened on its object, which every local script listening to it hears at once. EventHandlerBuilder A listener On.Event(event) started: Do(params Block[]) names its blocks, and From(LunyScriptTarget, string, int) restricts it to one sender first. EventSourceHandlerBuilder A listener restricted to one sender by From: Do(params Block[]) names its blocks. FakeCameraProvider.TargetGroupEntry One object in a rig's target group, with the weight and radius it was given. FileLoadBuilder What Asset.Load(file).Into(destination) returns: a load that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds its operation handle. Flag A true-or-false variable of a script: a handle to one slot backed by bool storage, or a constant. Build() declares it, and its methods and operators build blocks. FlagBindBuilder What Bind.Flag returns. It converts to no handle; Shared is required. FlagDefineBuilder What Define.Flag returns: an object-local flag unless Shared is called. FlagSlot Where one Flag variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. ForEachHitsBuilder What ForEach(hits) returns: Do(Func<HitEntry, Block>) takes the body run once per stored entry, nearest first. ForEachListBuilder<T> What ForEach(list) returns. Its only method is Do(Func<CollectionRead, Block>). ForEachMapBuilder<TKey, TValue> What ForEach(map) returns. Its only method is Do(Func<CollectionRead, CollectionRead, Block>). ForEachOverlapsBuilder What ForEach(overlaps) returns: Do(Func<OverlapEntry, Block>) takes the body run once per stored entry, in Unity's order. Gate A declared gate: a named hold on input or camera for every script on the runner, which Gate.Open(gate, categories) opens and Gate.Close(gate) closes. GateFactory The Gate surface: named, nested, runner-wide masks of suppressed categories. HitEntry One entry of a HitsResult: what hits.At(index) and a ForEach(hits) body's entry read. HitResult The nearest collider one cast touched: what Define.Hit declares and a cast's Into(hit) writes. HitsDefineBuilder What Define.Hits(name) returns: a declaration that takes the project's default capacity, or states its own with Capacity(int, string, int). HitsResult Every collider one cast touched, up to a capacity, nearest first: what Define.Hits declares and a cast's Into(hits) writes. IfBuilder What If(condition) and ElseIf(condition) return. Its only method is Then(params Block[]), so a condition without a consequence does not compile. IfThenBuilder What If(condition).Then(...) and ElseIf(condition).Then(...) return: add an ElseIf(ConditionBlock, string, int), add an Else(params Block[]), or use it as a block, which the implicit conversion does. InputBindingOverride One binding override a backend reports for a local player's actions, or applies to them: which binding, and the control path it uses instead of the action asset's. InputButton A handle to one pressed-or-not action of one local player. Returned by Input.ForPlayer(player).Button(name) at build time; the members on it build blocks. InputControlText The control path an action or a part uses now, for FireKey.Set(fire.BoundControl). Returned by handle.BoundControl. InputFactory The Input surface inside Build(): names the local player whose actions this script reads. It hides UnityEngine.Input inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. InputNumber A handle to one single-axis action of one local player. Returned by Input.ForPlayer(player).Number(name) at build time. InputPart A handle to one part of an action's composite binding, such as the Up key of a W A S D Move. Returned by handle.Part(name) at build time. InputRebindBuilder What handle.Rebind() returns. Bind it with .As(operation) before Build() returns, or Finish refuses the chain naming this type and the authored line. InputVector2 A handle to one two-axis action of one local player. Returned by Input.ForPlayer(player).Vector2(name) at build time. InputVector3 A handle to one three-axis action of one local player. Returned by Input.ForPlayer(player).Vector3(name) at build time. InputWatchBuilder What When.Input(action) returns. Its three methods register the blocks that run on a frame where the action reported that occurrence. InteractionFactory The Interaction surface inside Build(): declares this object a target players can focus and use, or a focuser that looks for targets for the local player its object is bound to, and reads and changes both. InteractionFocus What Interaction.Focus(activate) returns: this object as a focuser for the local player it is bound to. Each clause is optional and written once. InteractionTarget What Interaction.Target(prompt) returns: this object as a target, whose prepared parts the three clauses name. Each clause is optional and written once. LayerMask A set of the project's layers that a Collision query searches: what Define.LayerMask makes and a query's Layers(mask) takes. ListDefineBuilder<T> What Define.List returns: an empty list of the declared capacity. ListHandle<T> A handle to one fixed-capacity list declared with Define.List<T>. Occupancy starts at zero. The C# type is not List<T>, because that name collides with System.Collections.Generic.List. LiveObjectBindingBuilder What Bind.Object().LiveRebind() returns: a binding that searches again while it has no object. LookAtBuilder What LookAt returns: the facing, about the world up unless WithUp(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) names another direction. LunyScriptLogRecord One thing LunyScript has to say, as structured fields rather than as a finished string. LunyScriptOptions How a script type runs, which its Options property declares: RunAs(Scope.Singleton) for one instance per game, or nothing for one per object. LunyScriptReadSource What a generated reader such as EnemyScript.Reader reads from: the script type it expects and the target, checked when EnemyScript.At(target) ran inside Build(). LunyScriptReference<TScript> One incarnation of a script, referenced from ordinary C# code: its compiled definition, reads of the variables it declared, and observations of their changes. Find<TScript>(LunyScriptBehaviour) returns it. LunyScriptTarget Which object a read of another script, a request or an event filter is about: a declared object binding, an object this script holds under a name, the script that sent the request running now, the object on the other side of the contact event running now, or the script whose create or spawn made this object. MapDefineBuilder<TKey, TValue> What Define.Map returns: an empty map of the declared capacity. MapHandle<TKey, TValue> A handle to one fixed-capacity map declared with Define.Map<TKey, TValue>. Occupancy starts at zero. Existing-key assignment replaces the value and keeps insertion order. MaterialNumber What Object.MaterialNumber(name) returns: one Float or Range property of a renderer's materials, declared by the name in the shader's Properties block. The members build the blocks that write it into the renderer's property block and remove it again. MathFactory The core numeric functions, written as Math.Abs(...) inside a script's Build(). Every member returns an expression that is evaluated each time the block holding it runs; none of them writes anything. Message A declared message: a name without a payload that this script's On.Message handlers run on. A script sends it to its object's authority with Net.Send.ToAuthority(message), and C# on the object sends it with behaviour.Send(message). MigrationResult What one DocumentMigration step returns: the document was converted, or it was rejected with a reason. MotionDisplacementBuilder What Motion.MoveBy returns: a displacement along the object's own axes unless InWorldSpace() is written. MotionExplosionBuilder What AsExplosion returns: an explosion pushing straight away from its centre. Converts to a block, or takes Upwards(NumberValueBlock, string, int) first. MotionExplosionUpwardsBuilder An explosion whose upwards modifier has been named. Converts to a block. MotionFaceTowardsBuilder What Motion.FaceTowards returns. Incomplete until DegreesPerSecond(NumberValueBlock, string, int). MotionFaceTowardsRatedBuilder A FaceTowards whose rate has been named. Converts to a block. MotionFactory The Motion surface inside Build(): component-directed movement, force and relocation for the object a script runs on. MotionFlockBuilder A Motion.FlockChildren() with its goal. It converts to a block, and takes each of AtSpeed(NumberValueBlock, string, int), Within(NumberValueBlock, string, int) and Separation(NumberValueBlock, string, int) at most once, in any order. MotionFlockChildrenBuilder What Motion.FlockChildren() returns. Incomplete until Towards(ObjectBinding, string, int) names the goal. MotionFollowBuilder What Motion.Follow(target) returns: a follow of another object, incomplete until WithinDistance(NumberValueBlock, string, int), AtSpeed and As are written, in that order. MotionForceBuilder What Motion.AddForce and Motion.AddImpulse return: object-local axes unless InWorldSpace() is written. MotionLeadBuilder What Motion.Lead(follower) returns: a lead toward a destination, incomplete until To(Vector3ValueBlock, string, int) names the destination, then WithinDistance, AtSpeed and As. MotionLeadToBuilder A lead whose destination is named. It takes WithinDistance(NumberValueBlock, string, int). MotionMoveToAtSpeedBuilder A MoveTo whose rate has been named. Converts to a block. MotionMoveToBuilder What Motion.MoveTo returns. Incomplete until AtSpeed(NumberValueBlock, string, int). MotionMoveToDurationBuilder A MoveTo whose duration amount has been named. Seconds unless a unit call names another unit: used as a block, or given Ease(Easing, string, int), the amount is seconds. MotionMoveToTimedBuilder A MoveTo whose duration and unit have been named. Converts to a block, or takes Ease(Easing, string, int) first. MotionRangeBuilder A follow or a lead whose range is named. It takes AtSpeed(NumberValueBlock, string, int). MotionRangeSpeedBuilder A follow or a lead with its range and rate. It is incomplete until As(Operation) binds it to an operation handle. MotionRotateToBuilder What Motion.RotateTo returns. Incomplete until DegreesPerSecond(NumberValueBlock, string, int). MotionRotateToDurationBuilder A RotateTo whose duration amount has been named. Seconds unless a unit call names another unit: used as a block, or given Ease(Easing, string, int), the amount is seconds. MotionRotateToRatedBuilder A RotateTo whose rate has been named. Converts to a block. MotionRotateToTimedBuilder A RotateTo whose duration and unit have been named. Converts to a block, or takes Ease(Easing, string, int) first. MotionStrengthBuilder What Motion.AddForce(strength) and Motion.AddImpulse(strength) return: a strength with no direction. Incomplete until AsExplosion names the explosion's centre and radius, which give the direction. MotionTeleportBuilder What Motion.TeleportTo returns: a position write, or WithRotation(RotationValueBlock, string, int) first. MotionTeleportOrientedBuilder A teleport whose orientation has been named. Converts to a block. MotionVelocityBuilder What Motion.SetVelocity returns: object-local axes unless InWorldSpace() is written. NavigationActorCompleteMoveToBuilder A move of a declared GameObject input that refuses a partial route. It is incomplete until As(Operation). NavigationActorMoveToBuilder A move of a declared GameObject input. It takes RequireComplete() once and is incomplete until As(Operation). NavigationCompleteMoveToBuilder A move that refuses a partial route. It takes For(ObjectBinding, string, int) once and is incomplete until As(Operation). NavigationCompleteRangeBuilder A routed follow or lead that refuses a partial route. It is incomplete until As(Operation). NavigationControlBuilder What Navigation.Stop(), Pause() and Resume() return: the control applied to the object the script runs on when it is used as a block, or to a declared GameObject input after For(ObjectBinding, string, int). NavigationFactory The Navigation surface inside Build(): moves an actor along a route around obstacles, holds and stops it, and reads the route, the movement and where a move ended. NavigationFollowBuilder What Navigation.Follow(target) returns: a follow along routes, incomplete until WithinDistance(NumberValueBlock, string, int) and As are written. NavigationLeadBuilder What Navigation.Lead(follower) returns: a lead along a route, incomplete until To(Vector3ValueBlock, string, int) names the destination, then WithinDistance and As. NavigationLeadToBuilder A routed lead whose destination is named. It takes WithinDistance(NumberValueBlock, string, int). NavigationMoveToBuilder What Navigation.MoveTo returns: the move toward a destination, incomplete until As(Operation) binds it to an operation handle. NavigationRangeBuilder A routed follow or lead whose range is named. It takes RequireComplete() once and is incomplete until As(Operation). NavigationReading What a navigation backend reports about one actor when NavigationGateway polls it once per frame: whether it can navigate, its route, whether it moves, and whether it reached the end of its route. NavigationRoute What Navigation.Route(operation) returns: four conditions on the route of the latest attempt a Navigation.MoveTo bound to that handle started. NetFactory The Net surface a script reads the session through: who has authority, whether there is a session, how many peers, how far behind a value is, and the one way to ask the authority to do something. NetSendFactory Net.Send: the one way a peer without authority asks the authority to do something. NetworkMessage One received message: which object it is about, which message it is, and which peer sent it. Sender is carried because rule 45 forbids hiding ownership, and a script that reacts to a message usually needs to know who asked. NetworkValue One value crossing the network, typed rather than boxed. NetworkVariableUpdate One received variable update: which object, which synchronised variable, and the value. Number A number variable of a script: a handle to one slot backed by double storage, or a constant number. Build() declares it, and its methods and operators build blocks. NumberBindBuilder What Bind.Number returns. It converts to no handle; Shared is required. NumberDefineBuilder What Define.Number returns: an object-local number unless Shared is called. NumberFieldBuilder What Bind.Number().FromDataField(field) returns: a number input, complete once it is assigned or named. NumberInputBuilder What Bind.Number() returns: a number input waiting for the data field it copies. FromDataField(string, string, int) completes it. NumberSlot Where one Number variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. ObjectBinding A handle to one object in a scene that a script binds to: the target Object.For, Camera.For, Audio.For, Particles.For, Panel.For, Navigation.For and a landmark take. Returned by Bind.Object() at build time. ObjectBindingBuilder What Bind.Object() returns: an object binding that is complete once it is assigned or named. WithTag and Named set what the scene search looks for; MustExist and LiveRebind each end the choice of what happens when nothing is found. ObjectHandle What Object.For(target) returns: the renderer on one declared GameObject input, with the visual members the Object surface has for the object the script runs on. ObjectLifetimeFactory The Object surface inside Build(): builds the blocks that create, spawn, activate, deactivate and end objects this script owns, and the blocks that hide, show and tint an object and write its material Number properties. OnApplicationFactory On.Application: what Unity reported about the application as a whole, rather than about one object. OnAuthorityFactory On.Authority: the two events a script gets when this peer starts or stops being the one that may write the object's synchronised variables. OnEditorFactory The On surface on EditorScript: Ready, Created, Enabled, Disabled, Despawned, and EditorUpdate. Update, physics and application events live on Script. OnFactory The On surface inside Build(): registers blocks against the events the runner raises. Operation A handle to one observable attempt. Declared with Define.Operation(nameof(X)) inside Build(); family start blocks bind it with .As(handle). OperationWatchBuilder What When.Operation(handle) returns: registers blocks against one attempt's classified outcomes. Each registration declares a hidden counter-shadow variable at build time and is polled once per frame after On.Update, the same shape When.Var(x).Changed has. Operation<T> A typed operation handle. The attempt, generation, deadline and classified outcome are the same surface as Operation. A typed payload is filled by a later family that owns the result type. OrbitPointBuilder What RotateAround(point) returns: the pivot, waiting for the rotation to apply about it. OrbitRotationBuilder What RotateAround(point).By(rotation) returns: the orbit, waiting for the one thing a caller has to say about it. OtherFactory The Other surface inside Build(): the other collider of the contact event currently running. OverlapEntry One entry of an OverlapsResult: what overlaps.At(index) and a ForEach(overlaps) body's entry read. OverlapsDefineBuilder What Define.Overlaps(name) returns: a declaration that takes the project's default capacity, or states its own with Capacity(int, string, int). OverlapsResult Every collider one overlap found, up to a capacity: what Define.Overlaps declares and an overlap's Into(overlaps) writes. OwnedObject A declared owned object: one slot on every instance of the script that holds an object the instance produced, with Object.Create(handle), Object.Create(prefab).Into(handle) or Object.Spawn(pool).Into(handle), and that the rest of the Object surface addresses. PairingInputFactory What Input.Pairing returns: the machine's pairing window. While it is open, a button press on a device no local player holds pairs that device with the host while nobody holds the host, and with the lowest free guest number, from 2, after that. Local player numbers 0 and 1 both name the host, who stays. PanelCloseBuilder What Panel.Close(menu) returns. ForPlayer is required. PanelFactory The Panel surface inside Build(): typed binds, Place of a UXML fragment, and Open/Close of a menu. It hides PanelRenderer inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. PanelHandle What Panel.For(panel) returns: typed elements on that panel's document. PanelOpenBuilder What Panel.Open(menu) returns. ForPlayer is required. ParticleSystemHandle What Particles.For(system) returns: the ParticleSystem on one declared GameObject input, with the same commands and readings the Particles surface has for the object the script runs on. ParticlesFactory The Particles surface inside Build(): starts, pauses, stops, clears and bursts an authored Unity ParticleSystem, and reads whether it is playing or alive. Its own members target the system on the object the script runs on; For(ObjectBinding, string, int) targets the system on a declared GameObject input. ParticlesStopBuilder What Stop() returns: the stop that ends emission and lets living particles die, when it is used as a block, or the stop that also removes them after AndClear(). PlaceAtBuilder What Panel.Place(uxml) returns. At is required; In is optional. PlayerInputFactory What Input.ForPlayer(player) returns: one method per kind of value an action produces, each declaring one action and handing back the typed handle that reads it. PlayerWatchBuilder What When.Player(n) and When.Player() return. Its four methods register the blocks that run when this script sees a local player pair, leave, lose a device or get it back. Pool A handle to one declared object pool of a script: which prefab it reuses, how many entries it may hold, how many it prepares in advance, and where a spawn from it goes when the call names no placement. Returned by Define.Pool inside Build(); Object.Spawn takes it. PoolBuilder What Define.Pool(name).From(prefab) returns: a pool declaration that converts to its Pool handle, or takes a hard cap, a prewarm count and a default placement first. PoolDefineBuilder What Define.Pool(name) returns: a pool declaration that still needs the prefab it reuses. PoolFramedBuilder What a frame modifier returns on a pool declaration: a default placement whose frame is stated, which can still take a hard cap and a prewarm count. PoolPlacedBuilder What SpawnAt returns: a pool declaration with a default placement, which can still spread over a disk or a sphere, take a frame, and take a hard cap and a prewarm count. PoolShapedBuilder What a shape returns on a pool declaration: a spread default placement, which can still take a frame, a hard cap and a prewarm count. Prefab A handle to one prefab input of a script. Returned by Bind.Prefab() at build time, or assigned before Build() by [Asset] on the property; what the input holds is an instance read, because the value belongs to the object and not to the script type. ProgressFactory The Progress surface inside Build(): saves a document among the user's progress in local storage, and loads it back. Quest flags, counters, unlocks and the best wave belong here; Settings keeps configuration. RandomChoiceBuilder What Random.Choice returns. Incomplete until From(Randomizer, string, int). RandomChoiceFromBuilder A choice that has named its randomizer. Incomplete until Into(Number). RandomFactory The Random surface inside Build(): draws from a declared randomizer that store a result. A draw consumes one sample when the block runs; later reads of the result reuse it. Define.Randomizer() declares the randomizer. RandomIndexBuilder What Random.Index() returns. Incomplete until From(Randomizer). RandomIndexCountBuilder An index draw that has named its count. Incomplete until Into(Number). RandomIndexFromBuilder An index draw that has named its randomizer. Incomplete until In(NumberValueBlock, string, int). RandomNumberBuilder What Random.Number() returns. Incomplete until From(Randomizer). RandomNumberFromBuilder A number draw that has named its randomizer. Incomplete until In(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) and its Into, or until Into(Number), which draws from 0 up to but excluding 1. RandomNumberRangeBuilder A number draw that has named its range. Incomplete until Into(Number). RandomStreamSlot Where one named random stream's state lives on every instance of a program. RandomWeightedBuilder What Random.Weighted returns. Incomplete until WithWeights(params NumberValueBlock[]). RandomWeightedFromBuilder A weighted choice that has named its randomizer. Incomplete until Into(Number). RandomWeightedWeightsBuilder A weighted choice that has its weights. Incomplete until From(Randomizer, string, int). Randomizer A declared randomizer: a sequence of draws whose state lives on each instance of the script, which Random.Number().From(randomizer) and the other draws consume one sample of each time they run. RangeWatchBuilder What When.Motion(handle) and When.Navigation(handle) return: registers blocks against the range of the Follow or Lead run bound to that handle. RayCastBuilder What Collision.RayCast() returns: a ray cast that takes its clauses in any order, each once, and is finished by Into. ReferencedWatchBuilder A watch on another script's variable that When.Var(reader.Member) started: Changed(params Block[]) names the blocks that run when the value changes on the same target. ReparentBuilder What SetParent(...) and Unparent() return: the reparent, which keeps the object's world placement unless KeepLocal() says otherwise. Request A request a script accepts: work another script asks this script's object to do, which this script's On.Request handlers perform, check or refuse. RequestBuilder A request Request(target, request) started: used as a block it sends the request, and As(Operation, string, int) binds an operation that observes the outcome. RequiredObjectBindingBuilder What Bind.Object().MustExist() returns: a binding the script cannot start without. Resource<T> An asset of one kind in a Unity Resources folder, which Asset.Load loads. Rotation An orientation in three dimensions, held as a unit quaternion. RotationSlot Where one Rotation variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. Routine A declared routine: the name of one sequential routine, which Routine(handle).Run(steps) opens and which a diagnostic and the runtime inspector call it by. RoutineBuilder What Routine(routine) returns. Its one call, Run(params Block[]), takes the steps the routine runs in order and produces the block that starts an activation of it. RoutineGroupBuilder What InParallel(...) returns: a concurrent group with no ending clause yet. RoutineGroupEndingBuilder A concurrent group that carries an early-ending clause. Its one further call decides what happens to the children that had not finished when the group published its result. RoutineGroupSurvivorBuilder A concurrent group whose unfinished children the enclosing routine activation owns after the group publishes its result. The routine advances those children during its following steps and cancels them when that routine activation ends or is cancelled. RunCadenceBuilder A cadence that has named its unit. Start(string, int) runs it indefinitely; For(NumberValueBlock, string, int) adds a count bound and Over(NumberValueBlock, string, int) a duration bound. RunEveryAmountBuilder A Run(body).Every(amount) chain: a cadence in seconds unless a unit call names another unit. Start(string, int) runs it indefinitely; For(NumberValueBlock, string, int) and Over(NumberValueBlock, string, int) add a count or a duration bound. RunForAmountBuilder A Run(body).For(count) chain: a repetition count. The count is the finished bound as it is; Times() states it. RunHandle A finished Run chain. Start(string, int) starts or restarts one activation; Stop(string, int) interrupts it. RunOverAmountBuilder A Run(body).Over(amount) chain: an elapsed-time bound, in seconds unless a unit call names another unit. RunWorkBuilder What Run(body) returns. Qualifiers name a repetition count, a duration or a cadence; Start(string, int) starts one activation and Stop(string, int) interrupts it. SceneAdditiveLoadBuilder What Scene.Load(destination).Additive() returns: an additive load that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds the operation handle. SceneFactory The Scene surface inside Build(): loads and unloads Unity scenes named by a typed SceneReference, each as an operation attempt. SceneInputBuilder What Bind.Scene() returns: a scene input declaration that is complete once it is assigned or named. SceneLoadBuilder What Scene.Load(destination) returns: a replacement load that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds the operation handle, or an additive load after Additive(). An unbound load is refused when Build() finishes. SceneReference A handle to one scene input of a script: the typed scene identity that Scene.Load, Scene.Unload and the When.Scene* watches take. Returned by Bind.Scene() at build time, or assigned before Build() by [Asset] on the property. SceneUnloadBuilder What Scene.Unload(scene) returns: an unload that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds the operation handle. SceneWatchBuilder What When.SceneLoading(scene), When.SceneLoaded(scene), When.SceneUnloading(scene) and When.SceneUnloaded(scene) return. Its only method is Do(params Block[]), which registers the watch with the build. ScreenRay What Camera.ScreenRay(position) returns: the world ray through a screen position, starting on the camera's near plane and pointing into the screen. Along(ray) on a cast travels along it, and Origin and Direction read it. Sequence A named sequence: several blocks a script declared as one with Define.Sequence, under the name of the property it is assigned to. It converts to a block wherever a block is accepted. SettingsFactory The Settings surface inside Build(): saves a document among the user's settings in local storage, and loads it back. Volume, sensitivity, difficulty and other configuration belong here; Progress keeps what a player earned. SharedFactory The Shared surface inside Build(): operations on a shared store rather than on one variable. SourceLocation Where in a user's script a block was authored: the file and the line of the Build() call that created it. SpacedBoxCastBuilder A Collision.BoxCast() whose frame has been named: every clause but a second space clause. SpacedBoxOverlapBuilder A Collision.BoxOverlap() whose frame has been named: every clause but a second space clause. SpacedCapsuleCastBuilder A Collision.CapsuleCast() whose frame has been named: every clause but a second space clause. SpacedCapsuleOverlapBuilder A Collision.CapsuleOverlap() whose frame has been named: every clause but a second space clause. SpacedMotionDisplacementBuilder A Motion displacement whose frame has been named. It converts to a block and takes no further clause. SpacedMotionForceBuilder A force or impulse whose frame has been named. SpacedMotionVelocityBuilder A velocity whose frame has been named. SpacedRayCastBuilder A Collision.RayCast() whose frame has been named: every clause but a second space clause. SpacedSphereCastBuilder A Collision.SphereCast() whose frame has been named: every clause but a second space clause. SpacedSphereOverlapBuilder A Collision.SphereOverlap() whose frame has been named: every clause but a second space clause. SpacedTransformOffsetBuilder A displacement whose frame has been named. It converts to a block and takes no further clause. SpawnBuilder What Object.Spawn(pool) returns: a checkout of one pooled object with no placement of its own yet. Add At(Vector3ValueBlock), ChildOf(string, int), Into(OwnedObject, string, int), ForPlayer(int, string, int) and SurvivesCaller(string, int) in any order, finish with As(Operation) to observe the attempt, or use it as a block. SpawnFramedBuilder What a frame modifier returns: a checkout whose placement and frame are both stated. It offers no second frame clause, which is what makes a conflicting pair uncompilable. SpawnPlacedBuilder What Object.Spawn(pool).At(...) returns: a checkout with its own exact placement, which can still spread over a disk or a sphere and take a frame. SpawnPlacement Where an authored Object.Spawn puts the object it produces, and in which frame those coordinates are read. SpawnRequest One authored Object.Create(prefab) or Object.Spawn(pool) that has run and has not been applied yet: which prefab input or pool to produce from, where the produced object goes, what it is parented to, and which owned-object slot holds it. SpawnShapedBuilder What a shape returns: a checkout spread over a disk or a sphere, which can still take a frame. SphereCastBuilder What Collision.SphereCast() returns: a sphere cast that takes its clauses in any order, each once, and is finished by Into. SphereOverlapBuilder What Collision.SphereOverlap() returns: a sphere overlap that takes its clauses in any order, each once, and is finished by Into. State One state of one state machine. Declared on the machine's own line, so a state exists only in the machine that declared it. StateBuilder What machine.State(state) returns: the state's Enter, Update and Exit lists, written in that order and each at most once, or an internal transition with When(ConditionBlock, string, int). StateEnterDeclaration A state whose Enter list is written. Update and Exit may follow. StateMachine A flat state machine: one current state per object, transitions read in the order they were written, and the lists each state runs when it is entered, while it is current and when it is left. StateMachineDefineBuilder What Define.StateMachine(name) returns. Its one call, WithStates, names the machine's states and returns the machine and the states together, so one line declares all of them. StateTransition A registered transition. Its one call, Do(params Block[]), adds the blocks that run between the old state's Exit and the new state's Enter, or alone for an internal transition. StateTransitionBuilder A transition with its source and destination. Its one call, When(ConditionBlock, string, int), names the condition, and registers the transition in the order it was written. StateTransitionFromBuilder What machine.From(state) returns. Its one call, To(State, string, int), names the state the transition enters. StateUpdateDeclaration A state whose Update list is written. Exit may follow. Store A declared shared-variable store: a group of shared Number, Flag, Vector3 and Text variables that every script on the runner which names the store reads and writes as one slot per name. SyncCadence How often one synchronised variable is sent. Declared per variable, because AGENTS.md rule 46 says synchronised state is declared one variable at a time and there is no networked struct and no state object to put two variables into. SyncDeclaration One synchronised variable, as the script declared it: which slot holds it, how often it is sent, and the bookkeeping slots the cadence and the staleness reading need. Recorded at build time, read by the program, and never changed afterwards. SyncFactory The Sync surface: which parts of an object's transform cross the network, and how often each one is sent. Text A text variable of a script: a handle to one text slot. Build() declares it, and its methods build blocks. TextArgument One value a Text.Format call fills a hole with. Numbers, flags, text variables and literals of those kinds all convert to it, so a call site writes the value and never this type's name. TextBindBuilder What Bind.Text returns. It converts to no handle; Shared is required. TextCapacityDefineBuilder What Define.Text(name, capacity) returns: an object-local fixed text slot of that capacity, which never allocates and refuses text that does not fit, unless Shared is called. TextDefineBuilder What Define.Text(name) returns: an object-local text that grows with what is written into it, one System.String per object, unless Allocating or Shared is called. TextFactory Builds text formats: Text.Format and Text.Join. Inside a script, Text in an expression means this member; in a declaration it is still the Text type. A text variable is declared with Define.Text. TextFile A UTF-8 text file, which Asset.Load(file).Into(text) reads into a Text variable. TextFileBuilder What Bind.TextFile().From...(path) returns: a text file, complete once it is assigned or named. TextFileInputBuilder What Bind.TextFile() returns: a text file declaration waiting for the folder it is read from. FromStreamingAssets, FromUserData or FromTemp completes it. TextFileLoadBuilder What Asset.Load(textFile) returns: a text load waiting for the Text it fills. Into(Text, string, int) names it. TextJoinBuilder What Text.Join(separator) returns. Its only member is Part, so a join with no part does not compile where a text is expected. TextJoinPartBuilder What Text.Join(separator).Part(...) returns: add a Part, add an Else, or use it as a TextFormat, which the implicit conversion does. TextSlot Where one text variable lives on every instance of a program, and how it is stored: in a fixed-capacity array selected by Capacity, or as one System.String per object when IsAllocating is true. Texture2D A handle to one Texture2D input of a script: a texture the object's Inspector assigns. Returned by Bind.Texture2D() at build time, or assigned before Build() by [Asset] on the property. TimeFactory The Time surface a script reads the game clock through, and the one place a script changes how fast that clock runs: Delta, Elapsed, Scale, IsPaused, SetScale(NumberValueBlock, string, int), Pause(string, int) and Resume(string, int). TransformFactory The Transform surface inside Build(): where the object a script runs on is, how it is turned and scaled, what is above and below it in the hierarchy, and what it is parented to. TransformOffsetBuilder What MoveBy and RotateBy return: the displacement, in the object's own frame unless a modifier says otherwise. TransformSyncDeclaration One Sync.Position, Sync.Rotation or Sync.Scale as the build recorded it: which channel, at which cadence, and which slots hold the per-object bookkeeping the network tick needs. Built by ScriptBuildContext and read by ScriptRunner; a script never sees one. TransformTargetFactory One step of the hierarchy around the object a script runs on: what Transform.Parent, Transform.Child(n) and Transform.Root return. TransformToBuilder What MoveTo, RotateTo and ScaleTo return: the destination, waiting for the duration. TransformToDurationBuilder What MoveTo(...).Over(amount), RotateTo(...).Over(amount) and ScaleTo(...).Over(amount) return: a timed interpolation whose amount is seconds unless a unit call names another unit. UiActivatedWatchBuilder What When.UI(button) returns. Activated is pointer click plus keyboard and gamepad submit. UiButton A handle to one named Button. UiGroup A handle to one named Group, for showing or hiding a cluster already in the panel UXML. Not a Place target. UiLabel A handle to one named Label. Returned by Panel.Label at build time. UiOffsetPlacement What Offset(x, y, z) returns: the name scope of a world-anchored clone that already has its offset, so a second Offset does not compile. UiPlacement A Place fragment: the name scope for elements inside a cloned UXML, and a block so On.Ready(Panel.Place(...).At(...)) still compiles. Placement itself runs at spawn. UiProgressBar A handle to one named ProgressBar. UiSlider A handle to one named Slider, the UI Toolkit control a player drags to choose a number between the low and high values its UXML sets. UiText The current text of a Label or TextField, for PlayerName.Set(nameField.Text). UiTextField A handle to one named TextField. UiToggle A handle to one named Toggle. UiValueChangedWatchBuilder What When.UI(toggle), When.UI(bar) and When.UI(field) return. UiWorldPlacement What Panel.Place(uxml).Over() and At(position) return: a clone kept over a world point, and the name scope for elements inside it. Offset is optional and written once. UtilityOption One scored option of a Choose selector: a score expression and the action that runs while that option is selected. UtilityOptionBuilder What Option(score) returns. Its one call, Then(params Block[]), names the action that runs while this option is selected. VarFactory The Var surface inside Build(): declares a script's variables and hands back the typed handles the blocks are built from. VarWatchBuilder<T> What When.Var(x) returns. Its only method is Changed(params Block[]), which registers the watch with the build. Var<T> A handle to one variable of a script. Returned by Var.Define at build time; the operators and methods on it build blocks. Vector2 A two-component spatial value: a stick deflection, a screen offset, a planar direction. Vector2Slot Where one Vector2 variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. Vector3 A three-component spatial value: a position, a direction, a displacement or a scale. Vector3BindBuilder What Bind.Vector3 returns. It converts to no handle; Shared is required. Vector3DefineBuilder What Define.Vector3 returns: an object-local Vector3 unless Shared is called. Vector3Slot Where one Vector3 variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. ViewBuilder What View.For(view) returns: the two things a script does to a view. ViewFactory The View surface inside Build(): what a local player sees, and which camera rig it renders. VisualTreeAsset A handle to one VisualTreeAsset input of a script: a UXML document the object's Inspector assigns. Returned by Bind.VisualTreeAsset() at build time, or assigned before Build() by [Asset] on the property. WaitBuilder What Wait(amount) returns: a routine step that holds its routine for that much game time. Used as a block it waits that many seconds; Seconds(), Milliseconds(), Minutes() and Hours() name the unit. WhenFactory The When surface inside Build(): registers blocks against a change in state rather than against an event the runner raises. Interfaces IAssetLoadOperation A load in flight. Adds the loaded object to IAsyncOperation. The object is meaningful only once the operation completed successfully. IAssetLoadProvider What an asset-load backend provides to AssetGateway: one load of a provider-qualified key, returned as an operation the gateway polls once per frame. Script code never sees this type; it sees Asset.Load and When.Operation. ICameraProvider What a camera backend provides to the CameraGateway: choosing which rig a view renders, sizing that view, and writing a rig's tracking targets. Script code never sees this type; it sees the View and Camera surfaces. ICloudLoadOperation A load in flight. Adds the loaded document to IAsyncOperation; the document is meaningful only once the operation completed successfully. ICloudSaveProvider What a Cloud Save backend provides to the CloudSaveGateway: sign-in, and the upload, download and delete of one whole document, each returned as an operation the gateway polls once per frame. Script code never sees this type; it sees start blocks and outcome events. AGENTS.md section 12. IInputActionHandle The one thing every input action handle has in common: whether Build() produced it, and where its declaration sits in the program. IInputProvider What an input backend provides to the InputGateway: the resolution of a declared action name to something the backend can read, the four value reads, the start of each frame's occurrences and the three occurrence tests, interactive rebind start, cancel and poll, the bound control path, binding reset, the binding overrides a Settings document saves and loads, and local player pairing. Script code never sees this type; it sees the Input surface, When.Input, When.Player, handle.Rebind().As, handle.BoundControl, handle.ResetBinding() and .Bindings(Input.ForPlayer(n)). Cursor lock and visibility are not on this interface. ILunyScriptDataSource What the generator implements on a class that carries LunyScriptDataFieldAttribute fields, so that a data input copies them without reflection. ILunyScriptDataVariables What every generated Variables handle answers: which declaration its variables belong to. ILunyScriptData<TValue, THandle> What the generator implements on a LunyScriptDataAttribute struct, so that Define.Data(new WeaponStats ) finds the schema and the handle type from the value alone. INavigationProvider What a navigation backend provides to the NavigationGateway: sending an actor toward a destination, reading its route and movement, holding it in place, and clearing its route. Script code never sees this type; it sees the Navigation surface. INetworkProvider What a netcode backend provides to the NetworkGateway: a session to start and end, the connection facts a script is allowed to read, and two queues the gateway drains once per tick. Script code never sees this type; it sees the Net and Sync surfaces. AGENTS.md rule 49. IPackageVersionSource Answers which Unity package versions this project currently has installed. Adapter admission queries it at spawn, never per frame. ISceneLoadOperation A scene load in flight. Completion means the destination is loaded and active, its objects have run Awake and OnEnable, and Unity has reported it loaded. ISceneProvider What a scene backend provides to SceneGateway: starting a load of one scene asset, ending one loaded instance, and reporting which scene instances are loaded. Script code never sees this type; it sees Scene.Load, Scene.Unload and When.Operation. IScriptAssetInputs The part of a host that carries the assets an author assigned to one object, so that two objects running the same script can hold different assets. IScriptHost The object a script runs on, as the blocks see it. Blocks reach the object through this interface and never through a GameObject, a Transform or a Component. IScriptHostCapabilities Optional explicit host capability declaration. Legacy hosts remain runtime hosts. IScriptNode Build-time requirements and child declarations for actions and expressions. IScriptObjectLifetime The part of a host that can activate, deactivate, create and destroy objects. A host that provides it declares RuntimeObjectLifetime by implementing this interface; a host that does not cannot run a script containing an Object block, and the spawn is refused with a message naming the missing service. IScriptObjectPooler The part of a host that can keep reusable copies of a prefab: a storage object in its scene, inactive entries under it, and the move of one entry out into the scene and back. A host that provides it declares RuntimeObjectPooling by implementing this interface; a host that does not cannot run a script containing an Object.Spawn block. IScriptObjectSpawner The part of a host that can produce a new object from a prefab. A host that provides it declares RuntimeObjectSpawning by implementing this interface; a host that does not cannot run a script containing an Object.Spawn block, and the spawn of that script is refused with a message naming the missing service. IScriptSceneInputs The part of a host that carries the scenes an author assigned to one object's scene inputs, so that two objects running the same script can name different scenes. IScriptSceneObject The object in the scene a script runs on, as the Unity object an adapter acts on. A host that has one implements this interface. IScriptTrackingTarget The one thing a camera needs from the object a script runs on: something it can be told to follow or aim at. A host that can supply one implements this interface. IUiElementHandle The one thing every UI element handle has in common: whether Build() produced it, and where its declaration sits in the program. Enums ActionResult What an action reports about the objective it was given: still pending, finished having met it, or finished having failed to meet it. Anchor One of the nine reserved HUD regions a Panel.Place call can occupy: four corners, four edges, and the centre. ApplicationObservation Which of the five application observations a runner is delivering: what Unity reported about the application as a whole, rather than about one object. ArithmeticOperator Which arithmetic a CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberArithmeticBlock performs. AssemblyUsage What an assembly's scripts are for, which LunyScriptAssemblyAttribute declares. AssetPlaceholderSource Which configuration named the asset placeholder a type resolves to. AssetProvider Which provider finds an asset that a script names. CameraOperationResult What happened when the camera gateway asked its provider to do something. CameraTargetOperation What one target-group operation does to a camera rig's group of tracked objects. CameraTracking Which of a camera rig's two tracking targets an operation writes. ComparisonOperator Which comparison a CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberComparisonBlock performs. DataFieldRead The outcome of one read of an annotated field. DiagnosticCommandKind What one command asks the runner to do to one lifetime. DiagnosticCommandState Admission and terminal application states for one submitted command. DiagnosticPauseKind Which kind of debugger breakpoint paused Play Mode. DiagnosticRecordKind The observation represented by a console or trace record. DiagnosticWriteSource What changed a variable's value the last time it changed. DiskPlane The two axes a spawn's InRadius disk lies on. The default is XZ, the ground plane of a 3D scene; XY is the plane a 2D scene draws on. Easing The curve an eased timed move follows: how far along its path the object is at each point of the duration. Written in Ease(...) after Over(amount), or after its unit call such as Over(amount).Seconds(), on Motion.MoveTo and Motion.RotateTo. GateCategory Systems a named gate may suppress for every script on the runner. Only input and camera exist as mute-able gateways in this version.
